If you're unfamiliar with the borderlands series, the main idea of the game is loot. Borderlands is all about gear variation. Each item that drops is made up of different "parts" from different manufacturers.
So you can get the same item, but it have completely different  stats due to the parts on it (the make of the gun is actually just the "body" part of the gun, the rest of the parts, barrel, grip, stock, sights may all be different manufacturers). Such as a Hyperion sniper rifle with a "Jacobs" manufacturer grip increasing damage, but greatly increasing reload delay, where as a "Tediore" grip might cause much faster reload speed, but actually decrease the weapon's damage.
Borderlands two is great for end game play, and is where the bulk of the experience is - Ultimate Vault Hunter mode, and overpower levels. It's all about getting to know the gear, and finding the right gear for your build and playstyle. Borderlands 2 is also great for supporting different levels of skill: from Salvador the Gunzerker; who's Gunzerking ability makes the game much easier; but still fun, to Zero who requires a lot of skill to play.
If you're in it for the story, you probably won't find it here though I'm afraid. Borderlands 2 has more plot holes than a beach has grains of sand. Almost nothing makes any sense, and you'll commonly find yourself laughing at the absurdity of what just happened (but I guess that's enjoyable in its own way?). This game is about the loot, not the story. Go out, kill baddies, get gear, kill badder baddies.
Sadly the 'gore' has been turned down quite a bit from Borderlands 1, and it can be hard to really "feel" how much damage your doing. In Borderlands 1, if you have an "average" sniper rifle, a headshot causes a blood splat, a "higher" sniper rifle will cause the head to explode and give a hilariously satisfying geyser of blood (sounds worse than it is... maybe), where a really overpowered sniper rifle would simply instantly gib the target. In Borderlands 2, you might be lucky to get a decap and a splat with a stupidly overpowered sniper rifle.
On that note, the guns also don't really feel as good as borderlands 1 to use. A lot of them feel like rubber band guns, with no real "kick" to them, but that's just personal preference perhaps. There is great variety, even if limited by manufacturer specialities.
Which brings us to the next item. Manufacturer specialities. In Borderlands 1, each manufacturer was better at "something" than other manufactures. Jacobs had higher damage, Hyperion had more accuracy, Vladof had fire rate. In borderlands 2, each manufacture instead has a "trait". ALL Torque guns shoot explosive rounds. ALL Hyperion guns have ramping accuracy/recoil control, ALL Tediore weapons are disposable reload, and ALL bandit guns are garbage (that's their trait, I swear. It's not larger clips, it's just to suck).
As such it's possible you may have a poor experience randomly, simply because you may not know what guns are better, or just have bad luck with drops. But if you stick with it, you can find some really cool items, and awesome combinations (Bee shield + sandhawk SMG anyone?). As a tip for the early game for new players, I recommend keeping an eye out for TMP's, "Assassin"s, and Anarchies. All are machine pistols, high damage, easy to use, though have fun and try everything out.
This is a game that pays off from sticking with it. If you're into end game, and farming for not only the best items, but the best versions of the item, this game is one of the best out there, you will not be disappointed for sticking with it. If you like to just drop a few hours into a game, don't expect to get much out of this game unfortunately. It's not for the mild investment. The community is very large, and very helpful. There's tons of information out there if you want to take a quick look.

I had been recommended to play this game quite a few times, though I was also told that it was "severely overrated", which certainly made me keep on postponing it. Then, on a mellow Friday afternoon, someone I love told me it would be a good idea to play it together. I couldn't say no, obviously.
I immediately fell in love with the old-fashioned graphics. It was plain that it had drawn much of its essence from Earthbound: from the design of the sprites to the antics of the enemies that spawned in the overworld. Undertale's Tsunderplane is nothing but a reflection of what Earthbound's New Age Retro Hippy would have been if the game had been designed in the 00s.
It was quite easy to be enthralled by its bizzarre, surreal humour (in a way, alike to the one seen in FF VI), with dialogues displaying silly jokes and puns galore; all of which were exhibited under the embrace of a fitting soundtrack which, unbelievably, was composed and arranged by the same person who developed the entire game.
It is but an understatement to say the game is a work of art: a fine example of what an RPG can and should make its players experience.

Graphics are good.  Game mechanics in terms of gun modeling and taking damage, etc. are good.  The control scheme constantly reminds you that you are playing a console game on PC.  Infuriatingly clumsy character movement, particularly with regard to running.  Where this game really falls down, however, is the story.  The story is loosely based on the movie Apocalypse Now, which in turn was loosely based on the book Heart of Darkness, by Joseph Conrad.  The nuance and underlying message of the original, however, are completely missing here.  The story attempts to go for that artsy "moral grey area" stuff, and instead just railroads you into killing american soldiers and commiting atrocities against civilians.  And by railroad, I mean, if you don't do it, the game doesn't progress.  Because of this, I stopped enjoying the game about 1/4 of the way into it, and kept playing in the hopes that the story would get better and find some redeeming end.  It doesn't.
Even on sale, this game is a turd.  Don't buy it.

Great successor to the first Life is Strange.  Some of the dialog timings could have been better, but the story immerses you enough that you just tune out the oddities.  As long as they keep up the great story telling, Life is Strange will be a series I continue to subscribe to. With the release of the second episodes, Life Is Strange: Before The Storm continues to impress me. It definitely is a faithful adaptation to Dontnod's original creation, Deck Nine definitely put as much care into this game as Dontnod did to theirs. The soundtrack, the art, the voice acting, and the writing are just as strong. Before The Storm, despite having a huge number of callbacks (or call-forwards?) to Season 1 of Life Is Strange, still manages to keep itself independent. I can definitely say for sure that BTS is an amazing game in its own right. You don't need to have played Life Is Strange to love it. You can love it as it is and that's what makes an exceptional prequel.

I'm re-writing my review to go more in depth as to why this is not a hunting sim and more of a hunting arcade game. I will also list some reasons why the game is "broken" and not getting good reviews at this time. This game fails at being a simulator for many reasons and I'm sure I will not list all of them but I will do my best to point out the biggest issues my friends and I had.
Animals & AI- There are just too many animals honestly for this to be a simulator. They are EVERYWHERE! A hunting simulator should require a bit of patience and planning on the hunters behalf ,however, in this game you can just sprint around and wait until you hear a "warning call" from an animal then go into stealth mode and call it in or stalk it. The worst thing about the AI I feel is that you can shoot at an animal and the other animals around it and yourself only run away a short distance and can be called right back after a very short time. By very short I'm talking less than 10 seconds in some instances. The game needs a longer "spook" timer and range. Animals should run further away and be gone for 10-30 minutes. There are also cases of animals running in circles right in front of you.
Weapon system/ballistics and shot placement- Something that gets me personally is that the ballistics in this game are completely made up and garbage, let me explain. Animals in the game have an integrity bonus which is there to stop you from using larger more powerful weapons on smaller animals which is fine but the weapons they have that can cause you to get that 0% bonus are very off. For example using a .270 on deer will give you 0% integrity bonus. This seems very silly to me as many people hunt deer with a .270 and many even use a 30-06 these are both extreamely common deer hunting rifles. Yet at the same time you can take that .270 and shoot an elk in the head and have it bleed at a "very low" rate and have to track it for 10 minutes. This should obviously be a critical wound. Another big issue I have with this is that if you shoot an animal in the legs or any bone used in walking and it doesn't stop the animal from running. I have shot a deer with that .270 which they claim is just so overpowered for deer and gives you a 0% integrity bonus in 3 different legs and the pelvis bone and it was able to RUN from me. Now for shot place-ment. The game is overly picky about where you shoot an animal. Taking that same overpowered .270 that just ruins your deer to the point you get a 0% integrity bonus and shooting near the heart should drop the deer dead in it's tracks if it were so damaging but it doesn't and the deer will still run off and force you to track it. You must shoot a direct shot into the heart to get that instant kill.  In theory you should be able to take one of the biggest guns either the 7mm or the .338 and shoot a deer in the neck and drop it on the spot but you can't you will still have to track it. Finally shooting doesn't place bullet holes on animals. It just doesn't make sense to me and it seems like they took everything they learned while making The Hunter Classic and tossed it out the window on this game.
Night Hunting- Night hunting should not be in the game. It is illegal in most places as well as hunting with artificial light. They could fix this by not allowing you to shoot before/after certain hours in game while still allowing you to travel or track an already shot animal. They could allow you to shoot an animal at night if you are attacked by it while traveling or tracking.
Bugs- The game has a lot of bugs currently. Some of them are minor and some are in my opinion game breaking. A few bugs I can think of are a small window pop up that is blank and says Press F1 for more info. The box blocks some of your view and is more of an annoyance than anything. Weapons, callers, and such will disappear from your hands randomly. This is really bad when you're changing from a caller to your rifle to kill that animal you just spent 20 minutes calling in only to find out your rifle is randomly missing. Sometimes you will crouch to sneak around and just randomly die. You might shoot an animal only to have it freeze in place this sounds silly but really breaks immersion. You might kill an animal only to have it disappear in front of you. You might shoot an animal to have it stop bleeding in the middle of tracking it. At times you will buy something from the shop and it won't be in your storage or inventory, I feel this one sucks because things in the game are pretty expensive to begin with. Your flashlight has no effect on animals. Panning while looking in binoculars if very slow whiled zoomed out. There are areas on the map which are bugged and will cause large mixed herds of animals to spawn at times there may be a mix of 50 animals in one area again this one breaks immersion. In multiplayer only the host can interact with landmarks, claim outposts, and build stands. Entering a stand while another player is in it will kill you. Desync issues where people who join your game can't see animals and at times can see and shoot them but when they collect the animal they recieve no xp or money. This is by no means a full list of bugs but it's long enough and I pointed out some of the more crucial ones that I am aware of.
Now for the most heated and debated topic yet. Microtransactions/DLC. This company said back in the beggining they would not have "microtransactions". Which was great as The Hunter Classic had a ton and really turned people off. They said this game would be a one time pay game. So what happens shortly after launching the game? They put out "DLC" instead. You get people who say that microtransactions and DLC are two different things. Myself and others will agree that they are the same thing under a different name when it comes down to it. Paying for additional content. Some say that microtransactions are typically small and/or temporary and are usually cheap and may give an advantage during gameplay and DLC is usually a fair amount of content like a new map or missions and once you pay for them they are permanent and can be pricey. Now from my personal experience I have seen things from one category fall into the other countless times. Skins, cosmetics, teleport stones, pets, and access to new areas in a game all permanent and being sold as microtransactions. I have seen DLC sold anywhere from a large new map full of creatures and content (Ark: Scorched Earth for example) to a few weapons or skins in a pack. So what do we have for "DLC" in The Hunter: Call of the Wild? Tents and blinds for $3.99 which basically breaks down to $1.99 each. I would hardly call it a "large" amount of content, it does give players an advantage to quickly be in an area, and also change the time of day so they can be in spawn zones when they spawn without much downtime. This leads to my conclusion that if it looks like a duck and quacks like a duck, then it's a duck. The issue here is that either one can be called the other. I am quite sure the company knew they would be releasing DLC and should have said so. You may call it what you like. You may buy it if you like. Many others will not.
Long story short I suggest people stay away from this one for another 6 months or a year and check back to see if this company has got itself together. Hopefully that is long enough as they have been very slow at bug fixes and seem to have no troubles getting out "DLC". We would all like to see this game succeed but it's currently in a questionable state.

Okay, so the map is like 1/7 scale or so, and time flies to compensate. Sorting out which mod is causing your game to crash can also be some work.
But the other somewhat annoying quirks of the game -- speed cameras and gas stations never being where you want them to be (that is, on your road and not on your road, respectively), idiots overtaking you on roundabouts only to end up under your trailer, heavy trailers causing your front wheels to lift off the ground, making steering useless, slight steering mishaps at 60 mph causing huge mayhem -- those things are just like real life, I guess.
I always knew truck driving was harder than driving a car, but experiencing it fir-- well, second-hand, has only increased my respect for truck drivers. If I'm pulling my trailer out of the English Channel (figuratively speaking) after just 20 minutes of driving, why would I complain if a real-life truck driver nudges onto my lane for a few inches? For all I know, he's been on the road for 20 days.
Enough ranting. Do I endorse this game? Definitely. The only serious drawback it has for me so far: it's highly addicting.

enjoy this chicken stir fry recpie
- Serves 4
- 10 mins to prepare and 10 mins to cook
- 325 calories / serving
- Healthy
INGREDIENTS:
- 1 orange, zested and juiced
- 2tbsp soy sauce
- 2tbsp sesame oil
- 250g (8oz) tender stem broccoli
- 5cm (2in) piece root ginger
- 1tbsp sunflower oil
- 1 garlic clove, finely sliced
- 1 red pepper, deseeded and thinly sliced
- 150g Straight To Wok Noodles
- 400g (13oz) chicken fillet, cut into thin slices
METHOD
Step 1 - Mix together the orange zest and juice, soy sauce and sesame oil and set aside.
Step 2 - Blanch the broccoli in boiling water for 2 minutes, then drain well and set aside.
Step 3 - Finely shred the ginger. Then heat a large frying pan or wok, add the sunflower oil, heat it until sizzling, and fry the ginger till it's crisp.
Step 4 - When it's done, remove with a slotted spoon. Add the chicken and garlic, and stir-fry until just browned. Remove the meat using a slotted spoon and set aside.
Step 5 - Add the red pepper and broccoli and stir-fry for around 2-3 minutes until it's just tender. Add the soy sauce mixture, bring it to the boil then return the chicken to the pan

I had been recommended to play this game quite a few times, though I was also told that it was "severely overrated", which certainly made me keep on postponing it. Then, on a mellow Friday afternoon, someone I love told me it would be a good idea to play it together. I couldn't say no, obviously.
I immediately fell in love with the old-fashioned graphics. It was plain that it had drawn much of its essence from Earthbound: from the design of the sprites to the antics of the enemies that spawned in the overworld. Undertale's Tsunderplane is nothing but a reflection of what Earthbound's New Age Retro Hippy would have been if the game had been designed in the 00s.
It was quite easy to be enthralled by its bizzarre, surreal humour (in a way, alike to the one seen in FF VI), with dialogues displaying silly jokes and puns galore; all of which were exhibited under the embrace of a fitting soundtrack which, unbelievably, was composed and arranged by the same person who developed the entire game.
It is but an understatement to say the game is a work of art: a fine example of what an RPG can and should make its players experience.

Initially, I was sceptical if this game would deliver, since I was a huge fan of the initial Life is Strange (and still am), so when another studio, D9, came along, which actually is pretty experienced in games, just was under another name, so I never heard of D9. However, what also initially made me even more sceptical, was the all-new cast of voice actors, since Ashly Burch and Hannah Telle, etc. just did a phenomenal job of capturing their characters. The new cast was actually due to a strike of the respectible VA network, so they would´ve loved to get some known voices in there, but they just couldn´t. Ashly burch, though, is helping on the writing of the game, which is awesome. She also has a good track record with writing on Adventure Time, for example. Thankfully, the new VA are all doing a phenomenal job acting out their characters. Especially, the protagonists (Chloe´s) VA, Rhianna DeVries, she´s a natural Chloe. The music is phenomenal, breathtaking. It´s mostly music by Daughter, they crafted the soundtrack, but there´s also music from other artists, like Lanterns on the Lake or Speedy Ortiz. Don´t worry if you don´t know them yet, you´ll love the music, trust me. I still listen to this game´s music on my phone. So, you might say "that´s cool and all, but what about the story?", and that´s probably the most important question with games like these. So, the first episode proved my scepticism wrong, big time and I had a blast playing it, had some good chuckles, and maybe even shed a tear or two, don´t judge me ;). The game does such a nice job pulling you into this world and let´s you experience Chloe´s hardships and you´ll find yourself wanting to get to know all the people around you, well, not all of them, but that´s intentional. Ok, so how can you top all, this? Well, with episode two, for sure. It manages to top the great, and transforms this game into something truly special and heartmelting. The second half of episode two is the greatest storytelling I´ve probably ever experienced in my life, I won´t lose any more words on that episode, since that´s what you should experience for yourself. I´m writing this before the release of episode three, so I can´t give you anything about that, but if it´s just remotely as good as the prior episodes, I probably will have never played something more endearing and masterful. Some other things to mention are the comments on this game being cringy, or awkward, from youtubers, but also from people criticizing the game. While there is truth to that, be aware that this is a game about teens and Chloe is kind of a dork, but that, as I see it makes her just more sweet and likeable. If you can´t get over some teenage-angsty weirdness, (which is a welcome part of this game for me) over a great story, great soundtrack, great voice actors, great world building, and just a lot of charme, this game won´t be for you, your loss. One last question the reader of this would maybe have is, if you need to have played the initial Life is Strange to have a good experience. While it´s nice for a player of LiS1 to see returning characters, but also new ones being introduced, it will be nice for those people, you´ll also have just as a blast playing Before the Storm first, which gives you an entirely different perspective on the first game, which must be really nice, too. In short: Buy this game, except you just wanna shoot stuff of have another michael bay-esque action game, or gameplay focused games.
Just one more thing and I´ll let you go. I played this at least double the time as the record says, just in offline mode, so that itself speaks for this game´s quality and replayability and .. ok I´m done. (Love this game so much)

Spec ops is at first glance a typical shoot-cover third person shooter. What tells it apart is focus on storytelling and somehow realistic portrayal of action and consequences in war.
You take the role of Martin Walker, Delta Force captain and the leader of a 3 man squad tasked with investigating what is going on in war-torn Dubai. 6 months earlier a massive sandstrom hit Dubai and a battalion of US Marines, the Damned 33rd, was send to commence evacuation. As its mission failed, they disobeyed orders to leave the city and stayed in. The commander of the 33rd is man named Konrad, a legendary commander.
As you travel through the city it becomes apparent that the city is in total chaos and it is impossible to tell who the bad guys are - Konrad and 33rd, the CIA and the insurgents or maybe Delta itself. Every player will make up their own explanation and that is quite a achievement - I love good stories that make you think.
The Gameplay is, well, quite a chore to be exact. The enemies seem to have considerably bigger forces than 1,300 advertised (I think I've heard characters say that) and have access to seemingly unlimited resources. Typical mission consists of going from one place to another and killing everyone moving. Some of the checkpoints are badly placed, you might not notice if you stay alive but if by mistake you get shot you might have replay large portions of levels. In the second play through I figured out that even on suicide (hard) difficulty level you can stay in cover almost indefinitely and your teammates can easily take care of most enemies. The game is almost entirely linear, only giving you choice at 2-3 times. The decision you can make doesn't matter much and other are made for you even if you do not agree. This makes replayability very low, although as with all shooter, it's enjoable to shoot the baddies all over again.
Beacuse killing bad guys is so easy, the developers give us wave after wave of enemies. This make it quite unbelievable because during the course of the game you easily dispatch 500 people. One can argue that it is like any other shooter but here narrative tells you that the characters dodn't even take a break for a nap. I just can't understand how one trained soldier can kill so many soldiers with the same trainning. They are Delta, not Robocops.
The game is suppose to show the horrors of war but what limits the impact is depiction of gore. It hardly looks authenthic, enemies loose heads to show their badly textured necks and their corpses disappear quickly. The corpses you find along the way look more like wax figures then something that would shock you.
Visuals are quite good although I couldn't tell one office building covered in sand from another. Some of the places (chapter The Edge) look like parts of Dubai collapsed into a giant hole as you can't realisticly expect any sandstorm rise the sand level by 100 floors. Apart from that I like the bright environment's and fighting in sand (granades make a temporary sand clouds upon explosion)
Overall I enjoyed the first half of the game but the last 2 hours where exausting. I wanted to see how the story unveils but combat became so mundane that it was hardly satisfying. For people who enjoys shooters it is reccomended but otherwise I'd give it a pass.

This game was not for me and I understand I am in the minority, so please don't read this if you just want to be grumpy about a negative review. Read this if you are interested in the game but don't believe the hype. //
Advertised as: UNDERTALE! The RPG game where you don't have to destroy anyone. - And that's mostly true. I have been starving for more RPGs and I was interested in Undertale's "unique" alternative to combat but the problem is - you still have to do all of the combat! Even if you don't choose the "fight" option (which I never did until *SPOILER?* the game forces you) you still have to do the little shmup-mini-game in every battle, which get progressively more tedious. In fact, almost everything about the game was tedious. Just getting from one room to the next is often tedious. The game says "You have to solve a puzzle to proceed. ...Oops there's no puzzle this time... But there's probobly a puzzle that will solve itself in the next room! Go see!" and then the GAME continues to delay me from JUST PLAYING THE GAME. I read about 20 reviews before writing my own and I disagree with all of them. Most people spoke about how emotionally invested they were in the game and it's characters. I had no emotional investment in this game and the game often TELLS YOU HOW YOU FEEL. "You feel determined" - How about you let ME actually feel something and not tell me. That would be good game design. In regards to how memorable and fun the characters are, only about 4 of the characters were even memorable for me... And they're only memorable because they are constantly shoved down my throat the entire time. Hindering my progress with bad jokes. Even writing this review makes me realise how tedious everything was, from the combat to the characters... the pacing... the dialog... I've lost interest in writing about this anymore. I have more enjoyable games to play.

Reminds me of my younger days.  Unfiltered basketball.
EDIT::
There WAS multiple channels for this game to kep skill based matchmaking fair.
Rookie 1 Channel / 1-11
Completely for newcomers)
Rookie 2 Channel / 1-11
(For high level experienced players starting a new character or very good rookie 1 players who pick up the game fast.  You are forced to play in rookie 2 if you fit the criteria.)
Major Channel / 12-24
(Where rookie 2 and rookie 1 players merge.  It's overall balanced here because rookie 1 players should get the gist of the game by now.)
Pro Channel 1 / Level 24-39
Nothing much to say here.
Pro Channel 2 / 24-50
Pro 1 players can come here but I highly don't recommend it.
-----------------
As you near the max level you will realize that the game is ultimately Pay 2 Win, or at the very least pay to have a ridiculous advantage.
Example:  Buying a level 1 SPC (Special Character) is about $15 while the same SPC character at level 40 is up to $50.  With this SPC you get 40 extra stat points.  Now to explain stat points - there are attributes such as 3pt shots, rebounding, passing, short lay-ups, long lay-ups, stealing, and more.
The higher the stat the better the succes rate.  You get 2 points each time you level up. Then you go to level your attributes. Each attribute to level up has 4 segments of 5 bars to fill.  At first it cost 1 point to level up.  So 5 points to level up the first 5 bars which is the first segment.  Then is cost 3 points to level up in segment two.  So a total of 15 points to level the next 5 bars to get to segment three.  Segment three; which is 5 points to level up one bar totaling 25 points to fill up segment 3.
(I think segment four is 7 per bar, going by a pattern)
Now let me repeat. SPC's get 40 extra stat points to spend on the attributes. Starting at level 1.
----------
Now granted it is pretty fun and you dont really notice the pay-to-win players until you get to the Pro channel's.  But now it's worse.  A recent update -which is why I'm making this new review- has merged The two rookie channels into one rookie channel, and same for the pro channels.  Think for a moment on what you just read and you'll see how unbalanced that gets very quickly. New players facing SPC users, and new pro players that don't pay to win at level 24 being matched up with full-on level 50 SPC users with those 40 extra stat points.  Good luck.  The wall the gave this game and players some idea of what little fairness was there to begin with has now gotten completely demolished.
----------
Do I thumbs the game up? Yes. Why? Because it can still be fun, and you have a choice to play with computers, for an extreme amount of lowered XP per match.  Do I think people should play it? With this recent update? No.
I say Gamekiss should make two servers.  One for people who are free-to-play and one for the combined community; free to play and not.  The matchmaking has gotten too unbalanced.  If it was a shooting game bullets can make a person go down easy, so pay to win doesnt mean much. But this is a basketball game.  Every, dunk, block, and turnover means all that much more with higher stats over the course of a long 5 minutes per game.   The community is also very toxic, often times for no good reason.

Life is Strange : Before The Storm Complete Season Review (มีสปอย)
" Goodbye to my Santa Monica dream "
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Presentation - เนื่อเรื่องตัวเอก Chloe สก๊อยฝึกหัด ที่พ่อตาย(แม่งยังตามมาหลอกหลอนในฝัน มาเตือนสติลูกตัวเอง) เพื่อนสนิททิ้งหายเข้ากลีบเมฆ พ่อเลี้ยงหัวดอ อยากหนีจากทุกสิ่งทุกอย่าง หนีไปไกลๆแต่ติดที่ไม่มีตังค์ ดั้นนนนนนนไปเป็นเพื่อนสนิทกับ Rachel บ้านรวย อาร์ตในแม่ ดาวโรงเรียนแม่งทำไรก็เก่ง ทั้งคู่พัฒนาความสัมพันธ์จนตั้งใจว่าจะหนีออกจากเมือง แต่มันไม่ง่ายอย่างที่คิด
ตอนที่เล่น Life is strange อารมณ์ของเกมนี้มันจะคล้ายๆกับRoller coaster มันจะขึ้นๆลงๆ หลอกให้เราตายใจว่าเกมนี้มัน ดราม่าตามประสาวัยรุ่น แต่เมื่อเราเล่นนานไปๆ ตัวเกมก็จะรุม กระหน่ำซ้ำเติมความรู้สึกผู้เล่นอย่างหนัก แต่มันไม่ใช่กับ Before the Storm เพราะภาคนี้มีแค่ 3 EP มันเลยทำให้ผู้พัฒนาไม่สามารถเขียนบทให้พีคแบบในภาค 1 ได้ แหงละ เพราะภาค 1 มีตั้ง 5 EP อ่านมาถึงตรงนี้คงรู้ว่าปัญหาคืออะไร คือมันไม่สุด อารมณ์มันไปได้อีก เหมือนขี้ไม่สุดอะ กำลังเบ่งขี้อยู่ จะออกๆ ละมีคนมันพังประตูส้วม คือแม่งมันหดหนีไปเลย แต่มันยังดีที่มีmoment ที่น่าจดจำเยอะมาก มันก็เลยทดแทนกันได้ และตัวเลือกภาคนี้ตัวเลือกที่มีผลต่อเนื้อเรื่องเยอะเหมือนเดิม (แต่ไม่มีผลกับตัวเลือกฉากจบ) เนื้อเรื่องบางเวลามันน่าเบื่อไปนิด เพราะมีแค่ 3 EP Dev เลยจัดหนักบทสนทนาให้เราได้ดื่มด่ำไปกับการพัฒนาความสัมพันธ์ของตัวละคร ชนิดที่ว่ากูนั่งอ่านซับมากกว่าจับจอยบังคับตัวละคร
Gameplay - ภาคนี้ตัวเอก Chloe ไม่มีพลังพิเศษเหนือธรรมชาติอะไรทั้งนั้น มีแค่พลังปากหมาที่เรียกกว่า Backtalk เรียกให้ดีก็คือ การพูดโน้มน้าวใจโดยใช้คำพูดกวนตีน ฮ่าๆๆ โดยที่Backtalk จะเกิดขึ้นกับบางเหตุการณ์ บางตัวละครเท่านั้น เราเลือกได้ว่าจะBacktalk รึเปล่า โดยถ้าเราทำสำเร็จมันจะช่วยให้เราทำ Quest นั้นได้ง่ายขึ้นมาหน่อยนึง หรือแค่ทำเอาสะใจ ถถถถ
Environment - ฉากและNPC เป็นจุดเด่นของซีรีย์นี้ แต่กลับทำได้ไม่ค่อยดีในภาคนี้ ความมีชีวิตชีวายังสู้ภาคแรกไม่ได้ เพราะฉากใหญ่ๆ มีแค่ไม่กี่ที่ เช่น Junkyard , หน้าโรงเรียน .... แค่นี้แหละ แต่Soundtrack สร้างบรรยากาศประกอบฉากและเหตุการณ์ทำได้ดีมากๆ
Overall ให้ 8 / 10
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Advertised as: UNDERTALE! The RPG game where you don't have to destroy anyone. - And that's mostly true. I have been starving for more RPGs and I was interested in Undertale's "unique" alternative to combat but the problem is - you still have to do all of the combat! The game says "You have to solve a puzzle to proceed. ...Oops there's no puzzle this time... But there's probobly a puzzle that will solve itself in the next room! Go see!" and then the GAME continues to delay me from JUST PLAYING THE GAME. I read about 20 reviews before writing my own and I disagree with all of them. Most people spoke about how emotionally invested they were in the game and it's characters. I had no emotional investment in this game and the game often TELLS YOU HOW YOU FEEL. "You feel determined" - How about you let ME actually feel something and not tell me. That would be good game design. In regards to how memorable and fun the characters are, only about 4 of the characters were even memorable for me... And they're only memorable because they are constantly shoved down my throat the entire time. Hindering my progress with bad jokes. Even writing this review makes me realise how tedious everything was, from the combat to the characters... the pacing... the dialog... I've lost interest in writing about this anymore. I have more enjoyable games to play.

Let's be honest, if you played the original LIS then you already own this game but I thought I'd just make sure the reviews remain overwhelmingly positive. The new story stands out from the original game and uses a formula that works to do it's own thing with the franchise whithout using the previous game as a crutch which is wonderful. The graphics are about on level with the previous game (personally not a fan of the Unity engine but thats just me) and stays true to the incredible art style created by dontnod. The soundtrack is my absolute faviourite thing about this game and I personally loved it. That being said - If you don't like Daughter then it may not be for you as there's a significant lack of diversity in artists in the BTS OST which is dissapointing but they nailed it for me so I'm not compalining. Both old and new characters feel diverse and interesting, expanding on the universe of Arcadia Bay. Finally the new 'backtalk' mechanic, this felt far too easy for me - I never felt like it was a real challenge. That being said, I liked it as a substituaiton for the rewind mechanic and it suited Chloe's character well while providing something to the gameplay.
I know I compared this a lot to the original LIS to judge it but taken as an individual release it's still an amazing game - it just falls slightly short of it's predecessor.

Also the game has an amazing soundtrack once again, but the new voice actors are iffy to say the least, such as Samuel or David. They seem out of place, but Chloes VA did a good job so I can't complain. Definitely worth the buy

Overall: Please buy this game if you are in for a mystic, dramatic, coming of age story. Please buy this game if you are longing for an LGBT+ friendly game, that doesn't dance around sexualities and gets right to it. Please buy this game if you want something that makes your descisons really matter.

Cons are that after a while it seems much to grindy. By this I mean there reaches a point where the gold requirements for each new upgrade (be it buying new equipment or perks or skills) seems too high. By this time I had started a few new characters to try and optimize the build and it got overly repetative (despite the level always changing things start to seem familiar). That being said this was after about 10 hours. Given that on sale you can pick this up for about $3 or so the value for money is quite good.
Overall recommend the game if you enjoy Mega-man type experiences. Controller recommened (I used my PS3 controller by using the Motion Joy D3 tool).

Whenever I watch a movie and the protagonist turns me into a reluctant helpless witness to him/her making absolutely horrible avoidable bad decisions one after another then watch him/her deal with completely predictible consequences then go on to the  next bad decision until I pull all the hair out of my head, I get frustrated, but I wave it off to lazy writing and decide to watch less movies in the future. When it happens in a game with a high immersion value, I find that unforgivable.
The reason why game protagonists nowadays shut up for the most time is for you, the player, to lend them your personality and feel that they are you. Most protagonists in computer games are big voids of personalities that the player can fill with themself or with their imagination. Mad Max lets you do that just fine because he's a grumpy loner quiet kind of dude with just enough mystery and depth and inner pain to make him fully relatable and immersion-inducing, but he does not stay that way. He will take over from time to time just long enough each time to really mess things up to the point where I raise my voice at my computer screen, then recedes to his hole letting you once again deal with the predictible and soul-killing aftermath.
The world of the game is horrendous enough for unavoidable drama to just happen unavoidably. The fact that the main character breaks immersion just to screw things up and steer the story into every possible wall towards the end is just... bad.
With that out of the way,  the game plays kind of nicely until you defeat the 3rd identical boss out of a long list and realize that was the whole game. Now you are playing it all over again. And again. And again. I stopped around 60 hours. There was enough stuffing to get closer to 70 or 80, but there was no incentive to bother. Even my OCD cracked under the pressure of pointlesness and just let it go.

If you're considering buying "Rogue Legacy" remember it's a 2D platformer first and rogue-like second...or is that third, fourth or fifth. Yes, you have perma-death and randomly generated maps, staples of rogue-like gaming, but in itself it is not very Rogue like. This is as it describes, rogue-"LITE" and not rogue-like.
Certainly I find the idea of passing on a 'legacy' to your decendants very novel and kinda fun. Also the ideas of the genetic flaws and how they influence the game fun too. But I remember flaws coming from the curses of gods (good and evil) in the Rogue-like games of days past.
So buying this as a Rogue-like game? Don't. Buying a 2D platformer with good humour, novel and creative ideas? Go for it!

I wish I could buy and own Mario, Zelda, Metroid and Castlevania games for Windows. A very good Mad Max game, with some excellent bits but also some issues. The setting is great, car combat is incredibly fun - there's a good sense of freedom and the main missions are pretty good, but the story is quite flat (even though the ending is great), the fighting system is nothing more than decent and the optional stuff becomes pretty repetitive.

Although this game can get repetitive with the hand to hand combat and the driving around, the big open world with numerouse locations to discover and the upgrading mechanics  in the game makes up for it. You have two playstyles in the game. 1. You can play through the storyline with the necessities required to do the storyline tasks but it may get hard as you face stronger enemies out there. Or 2. You can focus on grinding  for scraps by liberating places, collecting scrap metal whenever possible and clearing a region of any enemy influence to upgrade your character, car, the ally's fort and of course, your shotgun. After doing so, completing the next region through the storyline is a breeze.
Overall, I expected this game to be a few days worth of entertainment as I had guessed the game would follow the events in the movie. I am glad to say I was wrong and had multiple days, maybe even weeks on this one game.

The game has much potential.  Graphically, it is great.  The two biggest issues that drove me away:
1) Animal population density (i.e. too many animals in too small of an area) leading to a very small TBK (time between kills).  I get that people have short attention spans, but to me, hunting should involve more time spent calling in and stalking than this game presents.  You can currently bag 10+ animals in an hour of playing.  This drastically takes away from the immersion and reward of each kill.
2) Bugged animals.  I don't expect perfection in any game these days.  But when 50% of the animals I track down run into each other, or get stuck on environmental obstacles (e.g. running endlessly into the side of a tree or mountain) this removes most of the reward in the hunt, and again, removes most all of the immersion.
Properly fix those two issues and this would likely be one of the best hunting games ever made.

This game has beautiful graphics, but it's just not a good game. I am sorry, because I really wanted to like this and invested 30 hours into it until I decided it's enough.
As I said, the graphics are great, sound is good, but not awesome, This basically is a stealth game where you have to develop a good situation awareness. It's about footsteps you hear, animal calls - the whole game crys for heaphones all the time. Why you don't have proper binaural sound but only pretty shabby stereo is acutally pretty mind boggling. Other than that, some sounds were obviously recorded in real nature, with some noise in the background. But I guess that's okay and somehow adds to the game's authenticity.
What's makes the game fall apart is the gameplay or the absence of any. Okay, I get it. This is a hunting sim. It's not your casual shooter, not your fancy Thief like stealth game, it takes time, you have to be patient, I get it.
But this game just does not ask for any real strategy.
There is a mechanic that you're making more noise depending on where you walk - but I honestly never found out how that worked. It seemed pretty much random to me.
Also there is no real way to plan or strategize. You can't really provoke a certain behaviour from the animals. If call them, they stop and listen, maybe come closer and then either walk away again or they see you and run away.
You can mark them FarCry-style, but only for a few seconds. You don't have any chance to circumvent them or something like that before you don't know where they are anymore. With bigger animals like deer and bisons this is ok, because you wont lose them so easily. But hunt a fox or a roe deer and they get out of sight pretty quickly.
So the only real strategy is this one: You go into the woods until you find some tracks. Sometimes they are fresh,so you follow them. Sometimes you hear an animal call and you follow it. You'll eventually spot an animal, take out your gun and shoot it. To make things easier, you can buy animal callers to attract your game. That's basically it.
Oh, you can build lookout points, too. But then you sit in the lookout point for a long, long, long time without anything happening. Yeah, it's a hunting game but maybe a fast forward button to accelerate time would have been nice here. See, I'm not playing anything when I sit on my lookout point and wait for an animal to come by. And waiting will be long even if you got to know certain animals will pass by at a certain time of day (you'll find need zones to get this kind of information). In fact, you'll be a lucky ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, IF they come by at all. So, just don't build lookout points. (Yeah, you have to buy every single one of them.)
You can also do missions. These range from trivial (I once completed one by accidentally pressing the E-key) to just friggin impossible. I quit this game after I repeatedly tried to hunt that damn fox with that stupid bow. These little fellas have ears that hear you across at least 50 meters. They are clever and always cautious. And they are small so they hide perfectly in the undergrowth and higher grass. With your ♥♥♥♥♥♥ standard bow you have to get close. Very close. I invested several hours into that stupid mission - now I won't anymore.
It wouldn't be so bad if I could just pimp my equipment, buy a new bow, maybe a new sight, some fox spray so he can't smell me. You know, handy stuff like that which is actually in the game - but blocked behind an xp barrier. So get some stupid binoculars, I have to be level 20 or 30 or something. I hate mechanics like that! Why can't I just buy that ♥♥♥♥ing better bow if I have the money for it? It doesn't make sense! "No, no, you have to be an epxerienced hunter to use this spray can, my padawan."
And that too wouldn't be so bad, if progress would be at an acceptable pace. But it isn't. Maybe I'm stupid, but I invested 30 hours into this game and I'm level 13 now. 13 is nothing. 13 in this game means a little bit better than your starting equipment. After 13 hours of play!! And no, I am notallowed to buy the better bow or the fox spray.
Why is progress so slow, you might ask? Well, it's a hunting game and it takes some time to hunt stuff. I just hunted that damn fox for an hour and got zero xp and zero money for it. Your average deer gives something about 100 to 150 xp. You can get more for harder and rarer species or for specimens with high trophy ratings - but it's more or less a lottery whether or not you'll find them. So, with 150 xp per kill you have to kill about 15 specimens to get from level 13 to 14, f.e. You can assume that you'll need about 15 minutes for a kill - at least. You can do the math yourself. And that's the playstyle that incorporates stupid, mindless grinding. If you want to properly play the game, explore the word, find good game etc., double or triple that time.
How much time would I have to invest to buy my better bow and the spray so hunting that stupid fox would be a bit more fun and I could end this story mission? A few hours. Maybe six, maybe more.
And that's not fun.
I'm sorry, I really wanted to like this game, it's brautiful to look at, but your game designers need a kick in their butts.

It's hard to recommend this game. It's hard to enjoy it and even harder to like it. Why the thumbs up then? Because it's bad for all the right reasons. Let me elaborate:
MILD SPOILERS AHEAD!
The game starts as a typical military shooter but as you go about shooting "bad guys" things get F.U.B.A.R. real fast. Your character is forced to commit a series of war atrocities, each worse than the last one. The gameplay in between is dull and repetitive but this is a very conscious design decision on the developer's part. While you get bored your mind wanders and you can't help but think about what your character has done. As you try to rationalize his actions you go through some of the same psychological changes that shape his mind during the game. These changes are further pointed out by the exceptionally good voice acting.
This game leads you on at first, reinforcing your childish, video-game/action-movie inspired expectations. And then it shows you what killing hundreds of people in a single day actually does to a person's mind. It gets in your head and hammers the point home by breaking the fourth wall and messing with you, goading you to simply stop playing. You're not supposed to have fun while playing this and the game itself is perfectly aware of that. If you do decide to play it to the bitter end it will simply leave you feeling drained and dirty.
Spec Ops fails as a game on purpose to prove a point and teach you a lesson. I can't help but respect that.

This is an ok game for $10 though its easy to see that the developers didn't do much research on the military during the game's creation. The Seargent in the game is portrayed as the goof ball newbie, though in the real world he would have more time in service than the Leiutenant and Captian combined. the M4 has 2 rear iron sights and one is on backwards. A squad is 8-12 people not 3, in fact 3 isn't even a fireteam. And the US military would not send in 3 guys if they lost contact with an entire regiment.
Gameplay is like gears of war, but much more restrictive. One plus is the number of weapons you can find and the different abilities of each weapon.
The story is on the same level as the Mass Effect series. Its a huge shame this game didnt get the spot light it deserved. Just play the story without any spoilers.

Most horrific storytelling (In a good way) since Silent Hill 2. Generally when looking for amazing storyline, you need to go with small indie games, this provides a heavy storyline with decent gameplay. Don't play it if you're looking just to blow off some steam, but next time you want to play the videogame equivelent of Apocalypse Now or even Jacob's Ladder, this is the game.

Whenever I watch a movie and the protagonist turns me into a reluctant helpless witness to him/her making absolutely horrible avoidable bad decisions one after another then watch him/her deal with completely predictible consequences then go on to the  next bad decision until I pull all the hair out of my head, I get frustrated, but I wave it off to lazy writing and decide to watch less movies in the future. When it happens in a game with a high immersion value, I find that unforgivable.
The reason why game protagonists nowadays shut up for the most time is for you, the player, to lend them your personality and feel that they are you. Most protagonists in computer games are big voids of personalities that the player can fill with themself or with their imagination. Mad Max lets you do that just fine because he's a grumpy loner quiet kind of dude with just enough mystery and depth and inner pain to make him fully relatable and immersion-inducing, but he does not stay that way. He will take over from time to time just long enough each time to really mess things up to the point where I raise my voice at my computer screen, then recedes to his hole letting you once again deal with the predictible and soul-killing aftermath.
The world of the game is horrendous enough for unavoidable drama to just happen unavoidably. The fact that the main character breaks immersion just to screw things up and steer the story into every possible wall towards the end is just... bad.
With that out of the way,  the game plays kind of nicely until you defeat the 3rd identical boss out of a long list and realize that was the whole game. Now you are playing it all over again. Even my OCD cracked under the pressure of pointlesness and just let it go.

Rogue Legacy is a highly addicting procedurally-generated rogue-like that is definitely worth playing. You battle your way through a castle, unraveling it's mysteries, and upon your death, your child succeeds you in your quest. You have your pick from three children every time, each one unique in that it may have positive or negative mutations. You also get to continuously upgrade your armor/weapons/skills/stats after death with the gold collected in your previous run. The upgrading mixed with the simple but fun platforming makes Rogue Legacy a delightfully addicting game. It is a great choice for anyone who enjoys rogue-likes and definitely worth picking up.

Ghosts 'n Goblins + Castlevania + Metroid = Rogue Legacy.   This game is nothing short of intense. If you were raised on the NES like me you will appreciate every second of this game. If you you think things like Halo are the best game "EVAR" then stay away.
In this game you start off relatively weak compared to the enemies.  You venture into a foreboding castle where inevitably you will die, and quickly. Death is permanent in this game, but fear not!  Once you die you chose one of your 3 children. Each heir has a randomized class, spell, and between 0 and 2 traits.  Classes are as follows:
Knave / Assassin: Low stats, but higher critical hit chance / Turn to mist to avoid enemies
Knight / Paladin: Well balanced stats / Shield that blocks all damage
Barbarian / Barbarian King: Low damage but high HP / Shout that pushes enemies back
Mage / Archmage: Low HP, high MP, absorb MP on enemy kills / cycle between 3 different spells.
Spellthief: Smaller sword based on magic damage, absorbs mana from hit enemies / Stronger version of your spell
Lich/Arch Lich: Low starting HP but adds +1 Max HP per enemy killed / Trade Max HP for Max MP
Miner / Spelunker: Low Stats, but 30% increased gold collection / Treasure chests shown on unexplored map areas
Ninja / Hokage: Low HP and no critical hits, but normal attack is very high / Quickly teleport a short distance
Dragon: No sword or jump, and can only cast dragonfire, but your MP regenerates rapidly and you have unlimited flight
The gold you managed to collect before you were killed stays with you wen you die. You can spend it on various stats, weapons, and rune upgrades to make you stronger for your next play through. Spend as much as you can though, because once you re-enter the Castle you must pay Charon all of your remaining gold (you can keep up to 50% if you buy the necessary upgrades)
The castle is completely randomized each play through (unless you have the engineer lock it down, but at a cost of a huge gold penalty).  Rooms, enemies, treasure is different every time. Your ultimate goal is to defeat the 4 bosses in the 4 different areas of the Castle to open the last boss room and defeat him. It sounds simple, but the vast majority of the game involves getting gold and powering up before you can face the later areas without getting killed in one shot. The initial play through offers between 20-30 hours for expert players.
The game has a few flaws.  The controls all feel delayed and floaty.  You must swing your weapon well in advance or the enemy will likely damage you well before you connect. Jumping is not delayed, but the floaty feel makes some of the precision platforming required tricky at times.
Overall a great game that can offer up to 60 hours of quality gameplay (its not over just because you beat the boss!)

Okay, if you've ever heard of this game, it's likely you've heard both good and bad things about this game. Let me make one thing clear - the gameplay /is/ pretty much like every other FPS out there.
The writing is not.
It STARTS out like every other FPS (except perhaps the beautiful scenery) but things get very, very different. Is it worth playing? Only if you're interested in dark stories and tredging through samey gameplay as all of the other shooters out there.
Now, /I/ like shooting stuff if I'm promised interesting story, but perhaps you're not. Watching this on Youtube or something is a valid option, as only the very end of the game has differing choices that affect the end.
If you can get past the mildly boring combat the story in this game is mind blowing.

Spec Ops: The Line is a prime example of ho-hum gameplay, but a powerful and engaging story. This game will make you feel like a monster at the end. You'll see the destruction you caused, the violence you inflicted on people, and the deterioration of your soldier's mind.
The gameplay in Spec Ops is really nothing special. It's a Gears of War-type shooter. You're in third person, you shoot enemies, you hide behind cover, you make things go boom, so and so forth. Playing a demo of this game will not do you justice. Sampling a portion of this full course will either make you crave more and throw it away. If it needs to be experienced, it needs to be experienced in it's entirety. Through out the 14 chapters, the gameplay stayed mainly consistent, with turret sections and tons of cover shooting. It's simple, and can get repetitive very quickly. There's nothing special about this gameplay. Some scripted sequences are definitely pretty cool, but other than that, you're going to be shooting and hiding behind cover for most of the time.
Spec Ops is all about story, though. You might think that story has no impact on a generic military shooter like this, but you would be wrong. The story in this game is incredible; it's like a good book you can't put down. It's very well written, and in the end, you'll transform into a hurly, burly tough man into a hollow shell of a human being.
I highly recommend playing this game. First time I played this, I felt that it was just a simple third person shooter with nothing to offer. After friends told me about it further, I tried it again and realized it was about the story. I was super impressed with this game. If you do choose to play it, make sure you don't look up any info of the story on the internet, it will give stuff away. You'll want to experience it for yourself.

Probably one of the more disturbing games I've played, but the story is unquestionably good in large part due to the depressing storyline. Very thrilling and exciting at parts, and disturbing in others, overall very fun and gives some food for thought on the consequences of war.

Beneath this otherwise standard third-person shooter, there lies a deep storyline with choices that are likely to trigger some
and give you second thoughts about playing any other shooter title. Multiplayer was a feature put into this game against the developer's preference, and you should only really consider this purchase if you're looking for a single player experience.
Achievement hunting in this game is enjoyable for the most part. You gain achievements for getting a certain number of kills with a particular class of weapon, and for the choices you make during the storyline, motivating you to play through the game a second time. There are also typical "Beat Game on 'X' Difficulty Setting" achievements, which I wouldnt recommend for ragequitters, as completing the game on 'Fubar' difficulty is largely based on luck. Sequences that don't even involve shooting will be seemingly impossible, but if you keep patiently throwing yourself at the next checkpoint like I did, you'll get there.

A very good Mad Max game, with some excellent bits but also some issues. The setting is great, car combat is incredibly fun - there's a good sense of freedom and the main missions are pretty good, but the story is quite flat (even though the ending is great), the fighting system is nothing more than decent and the optional stuff becomes pretty repetitive.

Although this game can get repetitive with the hand to hand combat and the driving around, the big open world with numerouse locations to discover and the upgrading mechanics  in the game makes up for it. You have two playstyles in the game. 1. You can play through the storyline with the necessities required to do the storyline tasks but it may get hard as you face stronger enemies out there. Or 2. You can focus on grinding  for scraps by liberating places, collecting scrap metal whenever possible and clearing a region of any enemy influence to upgrade your character, car, the ally's fort and of course, your shotgun. After doing so, completing the next region through the storyline is a breeze.
Overall, I expected this game to be a few days worth of entertainment as I had guessed the game would follow the events in the movie. I am glad to say I was wrong and had multiple days, maybe even weeks on this one game.

This game has beautiful graphics, but it's just not a good game. I am sorry, because I really wanted to like this and invested 30 hours into it until I decided it's enough.
As I said, the graphics are great, sound is good, but not awesome, This basically is a stealth game where you have to develop a good situation awareness. It's about footsteps you hear, animal calls - the whole game crys for heaphones all the time. Why you don't have proper binaural sound but only pretty shabby stereo is acutally pretty mind boggling. Other than that, some sounds were obviously recorded in real nature, with some noise in the background. But I guess that's okay and somehow adds to the game's authenticity.
What's makes the game fall apart is the gameplay or the absence of any. Okay, I get it. This is a hunting sim. It's not your casual shooter, not your fancy Thief like stealth game, it takes time, you have to be patient, I get it.
But this game just does not ask for any real strategy.
There is a mechanic that you're making more noise depending on where you walk - but I honestly never found out how that worked. It seemed pretty much random to me.
Also there is no real way to plan or strategize. You can't really provoke a certain behaviour from the animals. If call them, they stop and listen, maybe come closer and then either walk away again or they see you and run away.
You can mark them FarCry-style, but only for a few seconds. You don't have any chance to circumvent them or something like that before you don't know where they are anymore. With bigger animals like deer and bisons this is ok, because you wont lose them so easily. But hunt a fox or a roe deer and they get out of sight pretty quickly.
So the only real strategy is this one: You go into the woods until you find some tracks. Sometimes they are fresh,so you follow them. Sometimes you hear an animal call and you follow it. You'll eventually spot an animal, take out your gun and shoot it. To make things easier, you can buy animal callers to attract your game. That's basically it.
Oh, you can build lookout points, too. But then you sit in the lookout point for a long, long, long time without anything happening. Yeah, it's a hunting game but maybe a fast forward button to accelerate time would have been nice here. See, I'm not playing anything when I sit on my lookout point and wait for an animal to come by. And waiting will be long even if you got to know certain animals will pass by at a certain time of day (you'll find need zones to get this kind of information). In fact, you'll be a lucky ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, IF they come by at all. So, just don't build lookout points. (Yeah, you have to buy every single one of them.)
You can also do missions. These range from trivial (I once completed one by accidentally pressing the E-key) to just friggin impossible. I quit this game after I repeatedly tried to hunt that damn fox with that stupid bow. These little fellas have ears that hear you across at least 50 meters. They are clever and always cautious. And they are small so they hide perfectly in the undergrowth and higher grass. With your ♥♥♥♥♥♥ standard bow you have to get close. Very close. I invested several hours into that stupid mission - now I won't anymore.
It wouldn't be so bad if I could just pimp my equipment, buy a new bow, maybe a new sight, some fox spray so he can't smell me. You know, handy stuff like that which is actually in the game - but blocked behind an xp barrier. So get some stupid binoculars, I have to be level 20 or 30 or something. I hate mechanics like that! Why can't I just buy that ♥♥♥♥ing better bow if I have the money for it? It doesn't make sense! "No, no, you have to be an epxerienced hunter to use this spray can, my padawan."
And that too wouldn't be so bad, if progress would be at an acceptable pace. But it isn't. Maybe I'm stupid, but I invested 30 hours into this game and I'm level 13 now. 13 is nothing. 13 in this game means a little bit better than your starting equipment. After 13 hours of play!! And no, I am notallowed to buy the better bow or the fox spray.
Why is progress so slow, you might ask? Well, it's a hunting game and it takes some time to hunt stuff. I just hunted that damn fox for an hour and got zero xp and zero money for it. Your average deer gives something about 100 to 150 xp. You can get more for harder and rarer species or for specimens with high trophy ratings - but it's more or less a lottery whether or not you'll find them. So, with 150 xp per kill you have to kill about 15 specimens to get from level 13 to 14, f.e. You can assume that you'll need about 15 minutes for a kill - at least. You can do the math yourself. And that's the playstyle that incorporates stupid, mindless grinding. If you want to properly play the game, explore the word, find good game etc., double or triple that time.
How much time would I have to invest to buy my better bow and the spray so hunting that stupid fox would be a bit more fun and I could end this story mission? A few hours. Maybe six, maybe more.
And that's not fun.
I'm sorry, I really wanted to like this game, it's brautiful to look at, but your game designers need a kick in their butts.

This game was developed with collaboration between the Mad Max director, George Miller, and God of War developer Cory Barlog. A history that goes back to 2008 ! See -
... This game has to mark the end of bad games based on good films, and vica versa. As Miller and Barlog point out, up until now we've had film directors and game developers. Film directors, once they made their mark, could go to the media companies and say "I want to make this", "I want this creative on board". But the game developer was owned by Sony or Microsoft and could not ask to make a particular thing or work with some particular creative. But now ? The wondrous has happened ! Film people have been talking to game people ("workshopping" as Miller puts it) and we have this monster of a game. It's so perfect in many ways it almost scares me. From the Avalanche engine that is doing things that I always wished they'd put in Just Cause. To the sound design where the engine sounds are really dirty, I mean really UGLY sounding beat up engines running on bad fuel, spurting fumes and fire. Madness !

Fantastic hunting simulator. Large open world. Beautiful graphics. Immersive audio and weather systems. Realistic mechanics. Optional quests and rewards. Hidden lore and loot to find. More than fair price range, with additional free content being added. More additional content in the form of dlc. Some bugs, but nothing game-breaking or to detract from the overall gameplay in my experience thus far, and the devs are working on it. The devs have honed their skills in previous games to bring us this one. It's not their first rodeo.
So, all this begs the question, why the low review rating? I mean, what's not to love here?
If you read through many of the "not recommended" reviews, they generally read something like this: "Fantastic game! But..." or "I love this game! But..." or "Best hunting sim ever! But..." and so on. The "but" is an almost universal gripe about a tiny, optional content dlc that reviewers think should have been part of the base game. They consider the dlc a sign, contrary to initial projections, that there will be micro-transactions on the horizon. So the result we see here is an ugly trend in the community to try and bully the devs into compliance, with negative reviews. The negative reviews on the game are almost entirely reviews of the dlc, not the base game. This is unfair, and akin to journalistic terrorism in my opinion. As a result, it has put the devs and mods on hyper-defensive in the forums. The low reviewer rating that has resulted from the negative reviews will cause less people to buy the game, in turn lowering the revenue for the devs, thusly diminishing the likelihood of quality updates and additions in the future. I understand that the reviewers are trying to force the devs to make positive changes to what they see as a poor business model, but the actual effect that it has, in reality, is only to hurt the game and the chances of getting the improvements they want. I'm all for freedom of expression, but there are forums for communicating with the devs, positive ways to get the message acrosss, without attacking a game that they admittedly love because they didn't like something about one dlc. The next content addition has been announced and will be free. But has that made the reviewers change their reviews back to positive? Of course not. Hence the often learned lesson: never negotiate with terrorists.

I won't spoil the plot by revealing what the story is based upon, but know that it is based on one of the most important works of literature ever concieved. It is well voice-acted and the gameplay is fun even if unremarkable. Graphically, the lighting is impeccable and environments ooze detail. Seriously, these are some of the best environemnts since Bioshock. Character models are sub-par but the rest of the textures are phenomenal. The true value of this game lies in its story and remarkably deep symbolism. I would definitely recommend this game to anyone looking for a little more substance in thier shooter. P.S. Just completed the game, and was not terribly impressed. The plot is entirely warrior fantasy shaming. While you'll probably be playing the game for some form of escapism, for example a hero fantasy, but this game spends its whole plot bluntly trying to shame you into feeling bad about playing it. "do you feel like a hero yet"? I'm aware that the casualties of war are many and grevious, but making the plot of a videogame make the player feel bad about playing it doesnt make the game better.
Worse, the actual combat is bad. Usually you'll run out of ammo from full in the first minute or so, and have to run about the battlefield like a headless chicken trying not to die to collect some more. Enemies become bigger and bigger bullet sponges through the game, taking more and more direct hits to the face to kill them, meaning you end up running out of ammo almost immediately in every fight at the end of the game. The 'Heavy' enemies can take two grenades and multiple headshots to kill them on normal difficulty, It makes no sense and isn't fun. Combine that with enemies coming in by waves, blocking you from getting anything from their fallen comrads, and you just have a really badly balanced game.

This game was developed with collaboration between the Mad Max director, George Miller, and God of War developer Cory Barlog. A history that goes back to 2008 ! See -
... This game has to mark the end of bad games based on good films, and vica versa. As Miller and Barlog point out, up until now we've had film directors and game developers. Film directors, once they made their mark, could go to the media companies and say "I want to make this", "I want this creative on board". But the game developer was owned by Sony or Microsoft and could not ask to make a particular thing or work with some particular creative. But now ? The wondrous has happened ! Film people have been talking to game people ("workshopping" as Miller puts it) and we have this monster of a game. It's so perfect in many ways it almost scares me. From the Avalanche engine that is doing things that I always wished they'd put in Just Cause. To the sound design where the engine sounds are really dirty, I mean really UGLY sounding beat up engines running on bad fuel, spurting fumes and fire. Madness !

If fast-paced FPS are your thing, this is not the game for you. A refreshingly slow and steady wins the race ethos that impregnates this game rewards the patient and punishes the hasty.
The first thing you notice is my goodness, it looks good. Scenery will almost certainly draw you in and walking vast distances (somthing we'll some onto later) is always a pleasure. Certain aspects like grass clumped together in neat lines as you prone towards your targets may be a let-down, but ultimately everything else make up for that shortfall by looking nothing less than amazing.
Weapon selection seems well balanced and above all, realistic. Telescopic sights are not clear as day like most games would have you believe, which encourages you to make use of your trusty binoculars.
Getting around the vast map can be a chore in the early days of the game. But part of this games genius is that you'll set off with a certain task in mind, find a track and here we go on a completely different mission. The number of different animals to hunt is good enough but I would have liked to be rewarded if I do decide to take down the smaller game you see rustling about as you progress through the game.
The reward system seems fair and proportional keeping you immerced and eager to keep loading up  the game to progress even more for that new bit of kit, skill or perk.
You're kept going throughout the game with missions not always involving getting a kill. You're equipt with a camera and often asked to help out authors getting the right shot. I like this aspect and lends to the more realistic day-to-day activities of the professional hunter.
The sounds on this game are fantastic and really contribute to its success. One thing I have noticed is a peircing top-end when plodding through water which could be improved on easily. My ears start ringing every time I even think about going in water.
All in all a fantastic game for an amazing price. If steady skill based FPS games float your boat this is definitely one you don't want to miss out on!

In contrast to the original theHunter this game can be classed as an arcade hunting game. Sure, you'll be doing A LOT of walking in order to get to the look-out points and the camps, but you'll be having a wonderful view while doing so.
I really like this game. The graphics are absolutely stunning and is really what caused me to buy it on top of the classic theHunter.
However - there are a few things that kind of break the deal for me:
- It's very hard to determine the distance to an animal's footsteps. They're very loud already when you first hear them, and the animal could be over 100 meters away but the sounds makes you think they're right in front of you. Would be nice to actually determine how far away they are if you don't see them.
- The UI is still kind of clunky and doesn't feel like it's been worked on a whole lot. The feedback when you move around the menus is kind of lacking.
- A game with linear progression like this one shouldn't have "New game" on the main menu as you rarely want to reset your progress unless you're right at the beginning and want to start over with a fresh load of ammo. When the game launched "New game" didn't reset your progress and instead let you think that you were simply starting a new session with your previously played/leveled character. After the first patch that was not the case and I lost about 10 hours of exploration. (say your little brother decides to play on your character and selects New Game, that will reset your entire character. New Game or Reset Profile should only be located in the game options or similar so that it can't be selected by accident.)
- Multiplayer won't let you explore the game as much as single-player. The host of the game is the only player allowed to "discover" new locations to be able to fast-travel there at a later time. This kind of defeats the purpose of exploring in multiplayer if you're not the host.
- In comparison to theHunter Classic I find it hard to know if my hit is going to be a vital one or not, you can be on point with a double lung shot or a heart shot and the animal will still run away and give you a quite low bonus for hit location. I guess distance to the target will lower the impact of the shot, but it just feels less fun that in the original game.
Overall I'd say this game is a 7/10 as it has quite a few bugs that will impact your immersion. Let's hope that future patches will straighten those out and improve the gameplay experience even further.

Just completed the game, and was not terribly impressed. The plot is entirely warrior fantasy shaming. While you'll probably be playing the game for some form of escapism, for example a hero fantasy, but this game spends its whole plot bluntly trying to shame you into feeling bad about playing it. "do you feel like a hero yet"? I'm aware that the casualties of war are many and grevious, but making the plot of a videogame make the player feel bad about playing it doesnt make the game better.
Worse, the actual combat is bad. Usually you'll run out of ammo from full in the first minute or so, and have to run about the battlefield like a headless chicken trying not to die to collect some more. Enemies become bigger and bigger bullet sponges through the game, taking more and more direct hits to the face to kill them, meaning you end up running out of ammo almost immediately in every fight at the end of the game. The 'Heavy' enemies can take two grenades and multiple headshots to kill them on normal difficulty, It makes no sense and isn't fun. Combine that with enemies coming in by waves, blocking you from getting anything from their fallen comrads, and you just have a really badly balanced game.

This game asked me to do something which, no doubt, violated some part of the Geneva Convention. I hated myself for allowing it to happen, since the game lets you avoid this part with some intense combat. However, there comes a point on the harder difficulties when the fighting starts to hurt you emotionally as you go on and on; I quickly came to regret how many young soldiers - all following orders to save people - I had to viciously mow down, and cringed as I stepped over their writhing bodies, their last words lost to the blood that clogged their throats as they slipped away into nothingness. At a certain point, you just execute them, just to save your ears from hearing their pained last breath or two before they die. I didn't want to deal with that.
So I committed an atrocity, and after a cutscene showed me just how horrible of an act I had committed, I averted my eyes, ran past it all and went to the next chapter. The loading screen, which usually told me things like how to jump over barriers or how to look out for environmental hazards, then told me "You are a good person", and despite all evidence to the contrary in my day-to-day life, I couldn't help but disagree with it.
This game can make you physically sick, and will evoke emotions that few games have ever been able to even think of getting out of their audience. If you value an excellent storyline that analyzes what's wrong with the modern shooter market, along with gameplay that brings the story out and lets you be part of the carnage that unfolds, then you must play this game.
