At face value, this seems like another generic FPS with a loosely stringed together plot/ story, with a few 'nice' features. Firstly, the two weapon only rule, yes a lot of games use that now but in addition to this, the limited supply of ammo (which adds welcome realism) and the variety of weapons and situations means the choice of which weapon to pick up isn't as straightforward as usual.
Yes, you can go for the BFG, but with its limited ammo capacity, what happens when you run out of ammo, are pinned down and have no way of obtaining or swapping weapons? Or, with its limited range, you find yourself in a dessert, with little cover between you and the enemy and no practical way to return fire?
These are not the only choices you make through the game either, but there are also story-altering choices to be made, which certainly adds an extra sense of control to the game and makes it a lot more immersive than most FPS'.
The graphics are really quite good, from sandstorms to explosions to the detail put into the main characters' appearances but this takes a back seat the more you play. As you progress through the game, the sense of realism is layered on. First physically, with cuts, scratches, dried blood stains, etc... Then mentally, with the situations having an obvious effect on the three main characters.
This progresses as your character does, and adds an extra layer of dimensionality to what would otherwise be a very straightforward game. Half way through this game, I took a three month break and ended up going back to find that I could remember the plot perfectly, possibly because it’s so simple, but fortunately, the aforementioned aspects of the game doesn’t mean that simple is boring. Quite the opposite.
And whilst I did enjoy playing through the game, the pièce de résistance for me was the ending. I was very surprised (and more than pleasantly so) with it and could not recommend this game enough, for that reason alone.
I would highly recommend getting this game!

In contrast to the original theHunter this game can be classed as an arcade hunting game. Sure, you'll be doing A LOT of walking in order to get to the look-out points and the camps, but you'll be having a wonderful view while doing so.
I really like this game. The graphics are absolutely stunning and is really what caused me to buy it on top of the classic theHunter.
However - there are a few things that kind of break the deal for me:
- It's very hard to determine the distance to an animal's footsteps. They're very loud already when you first hear them, and the animal could be over 100 meters away but the sounds makes you think they're right in front of you. Would be nice to actually determine how far away they are if you don't see them.
- The UI is still kind of clunky and doesn't feel like it's been worked on a whole lot. The feedback when you move around the menus is kind of lacking.
- A game with linear progression like this one shouldn't have "New game" on the main menu as you rarely want to reset your progress unless you're right at the beginning and want to start over with a fresh load of ammo. When the game launched "New game" didn't reset your progress and instead let you think that you were simply starting a new session with your previously played/leveled character. After the first patch that was not the case and I lost about 10 hours of exploration. (say your little brother decides to play on your character and selects New Game, that will reset your entire character. New Game or Reset Profile should only be located in the game options or similar so that it can't be selected by accident.)
- Multiplayer won't let you explore the game as much as single-player. The host of the game is the only player allowed to "discover" new locations to be able to fast-travel there at a later time. This kind of defeats the purpose of exploring in multiplayer if you're not the host.
- In comparison to theHunter Classic I find it hard to know if my hit is going to be a vital one or not, you can be on point with a double lung shot or a heart shot and the animal will still run away and give you a quite low bonus for hit location. I guess distance to the target will lower the impact of the shot, but it just feels less fun that in the original game.
Overall I'd say this game is a 7/10 as it has quite a few bugs that will impact your immersion. Let's hope that future patches will straighten those out and improve the gameplay experience even further.

This is the most fun I've ever had with a platformer or rogue-like game.  The difficulty is handled well and is based off your skill at the game rather than being unfair.  That said, the game is pretty hard, but still enjoyable if you don't like difficult games.
The upgrade system is very well done.  The premise is that your family is trying to take back a castle.  The castle itself is procedurally generated, meaning that certain areas in the castle are in the same general area every time, but each room in the area is randomized.  You can also forfeight a big chunk of the gold you earn during a run to keep the castle the same as your last run instead of having it randomize after death.  Every time you die, your next of kin takes your place in trying to reclaim the castle.  Any gold you earn (dropped from monsters and chests) you can spend at the beginning of your child's run to buy upgrades like increased health or damage.  You can also use gold to unlock more classes.  Each character you play as has a class like paladin, barbarian, mage, etc and they each have a different class ability.  You also get a random spell and random traits.  The traits can range from making your character larger or smaller to turning the entire game world upside down or sepia.  I got tired of the gimmicky ones pretty quick and you are almost never forced to take a bad trait since you choose one of three next of kin after you die.  So at least with me, I found a class that I liked and I try to always select that.
The actual gameplay is smooth and fun.  The controls are simple, but intuitive.  You can get upgrades like double jumping and dashing to help with your platforming.  The enemies make the game into an almost "bullet hell" game and the bosses are definitely in "bullet hell" territory.  The enemy types are varied and there are several variations of each type of enemy.  So a fire mage might shoot a fireball, but a black fire mage will shoot five large fireballs.
Honestly, I don't have any nitpicks about the game.

This sim is merely potential... It is missing A LOT of fundemental gameplay elements to really be considered a respectable hunting sim. The graphics are amazing as far as environmental quality and yes, the maps are sufficient in size, but there is no ethics system...  I don't like hunting games that suggest that players just kill everything in sight. In most cases, real world hunting is mired heavily in rules and regulations. To really get a respectable real world account of things, there must be a licensing system... season system... area code so as to ba allowed to hunt in your designated area etc..
further more it should incude field dressing, more extensive weapon and gear set up... like scope mounts that allow use of sights via high mount, see through rings. Picatinny rail mounts and quick release, Bipods and bipod sticks,  rain gaurds, glare gaurds, butt stock ammo carriers (players should only be allowed to carry as much as they could in real life) slings, workbenches and tools. That brings me to my next subject. Game needs to include gun maintenence such as cleaning and bore sighting. It would also be soooo much more immersive if you'd incude vehicles and camping gear-tents for rest and save points, campfres and cooking and all other types of survival gameplay. Also, more complete subsumption system for game (animal) NPC. I recomend only because its a good foundation but needs a lot of work.

This is two games. The gameplay, the parts in between the story, is a cover shooter, no better than any other made since gears of war popularized the genre. The rest of the game is what Call of Duty ought to be. In my opinion, the story brings the rest of the game up with it. You care about what's happening, because its not some mindless power fantasy. The decisions you make (actual decisions, not 'Press A to decide') impact the game. Frankly I understand why the CoD series storylines are garbage: because if they were any good, you'd have to feel something about the hordes of people you kill.

People rant and rave about how great this game is. How it has an amazing story line that just makes all other shooters feel generic. Well I can say that this game is nothing special. 90% of the story is lackluster, dealing with a soldier who {spoilers ahead} is dealing with PTSD. The PTSD adds an interesting facet to the game. And the ending is rather good, if predictable. But the rest of the game is not worth playing for all of the time that it takes to get to the ending. The game is of standard length for a shoot, sitting at between 5 and 10 hours, depending on difficulty and ability. However, that time can be better spent on a multitude of other games, this game is not really worth the $8 I paid for it.
Mostly my complaint lies in the game mechanics. It is a 3rd person shooter, but the use of angled terrain meant I could only play this game for about an hour and a half at a time before feeling nauseous, leading me to stop for 30 minutes before continuing. The graphics are subpar, for example when using a scoped sniper rifle you can easily see the enemies 200 feet away, and even with the zoom the enemies are little more that grey human shaped blobs, I could tell you the color of the guys eyes at that range with the scopes provided but the game does not bother adjusting the LOD to match the zoom.
Another thing is the horrendous cover system. It uses the sticky cover system, but often it would be more bugged or finicky to use that it was worth. And it did not even matter because the enemy have grenades that can fly right through cover to land behind you, constantly causing you to have to run from cover to cover. But wait, most combat areas only have 2 or 3 pieces of cover to use. So you spend most of your time dodging grenades.
I did play this game on hard difficulty, but given that I often found the game just plain unfair. For example, while hidding behind cover the enemy are constantly suppressing you with full auto weapons from at least 6 different locations, try to pop up and shoot them and your character ends up standing in the open trying to slug fest 6 v 1, it rarely goes well. Also the AI is telepathic, they inexplicable dive for cover if you aim for them, almost as if they know your going to shoot at them, meanwhile the other 5 AI are going full auto into your head and chest with Olympic levels of precision. At 50 feet the enemy will hit you with a pistol about 70% of the time, factor in the fact that it takes about 3 to 6 bullets to kill you (depending on weapon and enemy type) and the fact that your against 6 opponents, well you die very fast, and a lot.
Oh and your AI allies are useless, 20% accuracy unless you use the special attack command, and they feel like their shooting tennis balls not bullets.
All in all, watch the lets play on youtube, you will get all the story line and none of the frustration. The game is not worth the money.

Spec Ops is a surprisingly intelligent game camouflaging itself as a typical third person military shooter. There are so many layers to the plot - the surface plot with twists and turns and surprises, the subplot with its own messages, then at the deepest layer is the subtext which in my opinion is what the game is *really* about.
It's difficult to convey what the game does subtextually, but suffice to say that normally a violent game like this would be steeped with what some pretentious game reviewers call ludonarrative dissonance - a strong disconnect between the plot and the gameplay. On the contrary, the narrative and gameplay in this game are tied together - they comment on each other. The purpose of this game and the messages it attempts to convey are the sum of the narrative and the gameplay.

How does one describe what seems to be a freeform, open environment hunting game?
In a word: Frustrating.
To be fair, I'm not a hunter.  I'm only a moderate firearms geek, and I was looking for something that I could play as a 'relaxed shooter'.  That's what I got.  No twitch reflexes, no tea-bagging online players, no insane aimbots that can pick you off in an eye-blink's reaction time from half way across the map.  Just, something that gave me the satisfaction of finding and shooting moving targets with the relaxation of not having to worry about winning matches, or any other bits of shooter game culture.
I picked up this game knowing it was going to thrust me into simulated hunting conditions, maybe with pointers, maybe not.  I walked into this knowing tracking was going to require patience, and good kills were going to be worked for.
I was right, and I enjoy it.  Even when the game is frustrating with a half-hour long chase for a shot that only caused minor injury to the animal, I find myself relaxed, but alert and thinking.  And learning a little.
The game sports a wonderful environmental engine that immerses you in the gameplay world, placing you in an absolutely colossal area that takes hours to traverse by foot.  You may have looked at screenshots that show pretty landscapes, that's what you get.  Keep in mind the various landscapes are also shot from, at the time of this review, one of two primary maps.
But you're not here for screenshots, you're here to hunt.  Like I said, I'm not a hunter.  But I get to experience some of what it's like to BE a hunter, albeit with some helpful HUD overlays (which can be disabled if you so desire), and a virtual 'Huntermate' GPS phone device that seems to operate on an RTG battery (Never recharge your phone again!).  Also, I'm not bogged down with licensing fees, hauling a heavy carcasses back to a truck, or regulated kill limits.  I load up, I stalk, I shoot anything I want, and I call it a day (or night).  No muss, no fuss.
I've burned away hours of free time, averaging 20 minutes between animal takedowns and enjoying shots ranging from surprise buckshot, to 300+ yard love taps.  All at my own pace.  No quotas, no time limits, no pressure.
The game includes a semi-RPG ish earning system, giving you skills, perks, and money over the course of your hunting to purchase gear and improve your in-game avatar.  So far, it's pretty simple to grind with, so long as you aren't impatient about it.  The animals look nice, if a bit dumb at times, but are actually a bit of a task to reliably approach for good shots.  Not the best AI in existence, but I don't exactly expect sapience.
The game IS however full of bugs at this time.  The interface is clunky, the map interacts with the scope zoom settings, and even some of your tools in the game don't want to play nice at times.  Mostly, these don't get in the way too much, but for many of you who aren't tolerant of buggy release practices rampant among independent developers these days, you may want to wishlist this and wait.  Luckily, the devs seem to be moving constantly, even if nobody can agree on what the Dev's priority should really be  (Releasing a paid DLC while a savegame wiping crash bug is still being reported is a bad PR move in anyone's books).
But if you're patient, tolerant, and want a casual shooter hunting experience with the freedom of an open world sandbox, don't be afraid to pick this up.  Heck, if you want, this game even makes for a good 'sounds of nature screensaver' since there are no  time pressures to speak of.
I look forward to promised additional features in the future, and the cleanup of bugs.

Prisoner's are delicate flowers, don't satsify their needs and they will be unhappy which can lead to destruction of property, prisoners attacking one another or staff and even murder, riots and escapes! Forget the critics, this is an excellent game. Immersion is great; very faithful to the mad max universe. Stretch of desolate wasteland, vehicular combat with large displacement machines, twisted characters, constant scarcity of resources (not so much in game mechanic terms as it is thematically), pretty much all of the elements of a mad max movie are there. All of it is convincingly depicted via terrific audio and visual aesthetics. The desert feels hot and dry and electric storms feels dangerous. I'm no audiophile but the way the game audio adds an extra 'oomph' when max's fist connects with someones face is so damn satisfying, more so than many brawlers out there.
Speaking of brawling, the combat is pretty simple. It uses the same ol' single button attack another for counter system popularized by Batman Arkham series. Even though it can get tiresome if repeated too often, on foot combat portion is spaced out far enough that I personally had no issue with it. The previously mentioned brutal aesthetic of fights does alleviate the monotomy of it somewhat. Plus outside of clearing out fortications, you do have the option of simply running enemies over with a car.
The other part of combat is the vehicular combat. Vehicles control is good and as expected. Didn't say tight and responsive since different cars under different circumstance will expectedly exhibit varying degree of control and responsiveness. In fact, it's surprising to me how realistic the cars control considering how bad I thought the vehicles in Avalanche's Just Cause were. Granted, it's no Colin Mcrae Rally but it does a suffient job of convincing me that there's a car running on a solid surface. When the game is running on all 8 cylinders and you find yourself in the middle of a hostile convoy at full speed, it's a realization of the movie video game cliche of "being in the movie" even if it's fleeting.
It's equally solid gameplay wise, even if it is not particularly original or innovative. Despite having nothing to do with Ubisoft, the game is actually pretty reminiscent of the typical Ubi open world games. You get to an observation point (maybe solve a simple puzzle) and reveal different cookie cutter activities in an area. And then there are "strongholds" in the area you have to clear out to reduce influence of the hostile factions. Rinse and repeat. I think most of the negative reviews are based on this aspect of the game. And that criticsm isn't without warrant; it does make the game feel recycled. But I feel like there are so many other things that this game does right that that lack of originality in overarching game structure can be easily overlooked. In any case, the game is at least worth a try at ~$30 especially if you are a mad max fan.

This was a surprisingly engaging game. It looks generic, but Nolan North's voice acting is a nice touch and the story is a change from other military shooters. It's not original by any means, but the characters are interesting enough to play this one until the end. It takes about 8 hours to complete, and the game is well optimized so high frame rates can be achieved if V-Sync is turned off. The graphics are amazing, as well as the audio. The gameplay is a standard third person cover game, but it works perfectly so that's not necessarily a bad thing. Ammo is scarce at times, so you'll find yourself picking up enemy weapons a lot in order to have a functional weapon.
I'd recommend buying this game, it's not a Call of Duty ripoff - but instead more character focused... a story based around the effects of war and the hard choices that are made. What is right and what is wrong?
Truly, even with the "generic" gameplay, a good story that made me play the game in one sit, 10 hours of gameplay. MP isn't even needed.

So this game has been on my wishlist since it launched many years ago. Every time I thought about buying it I would be bombarded with the always overwhelmingly negative reviews and that high price tag of 35 bucks (for a non AAA title that is). That would put me off for another 6 months. Then I'd come back 6 months later hoping something had changed, it had not. STILL negative, STILL expensive, STILL early access alpha. I'm not bagging early access games in fact I think they are better than AAA titles at times but DayZ just isn't one of them. There really is no excuse for the slow rate of development considering this is a TEAM that is working on this game, not just 1 guy or something. Bohemia Interactive is a studio of multiple devs supposedly "working" on this game but I genuinely question what they do at work every day because it doesn't seem to me like they've been all that busy in the past 3 or so years or however long this has been in early access for I've forgotten now. Either way, the game in its current state really isn't very impressive, yes it has some good functional mechanics like a unique inventory system (although I've found to be quite buggy and just uncomfortable to use at times) and solid graphics (nothing ground breaking but definitely not the worst I've seen in a game like this). Still however, the good does not out weigh the bad. When I eventually bought the game a few days ago after many years of waiting I hoped it wasn't going to be as bad as people had been saying. They were right. Upon loading up the game, straight away I found a bug. My character did not display in the Main Menu screen like it should or at least I thought it should have as there were many UI queues that made out it was supposed to be there. So I couldn't see my guy to customise him. Okay, I guess that can be excused since the game is early access after all albeit skating on very thin ice with its fans while continuing to be in this state. So I went on to connect to a server with the lowest ping I could find which was 50 so thats decent at least. I spawned in an open field not knowing what to do. There is no tutorial, no assistance at all in the game which means you need to source information from wikis or youtube or other people who you know already play the game. I think adding some sort of basic tutorial would be helpful in my opinion. Anyway after talking to some friends who knew the game already I quickly found I needed to make a knife and a bunch of other basic tools which could be done by finding a rock in the ground. After searching for some rocky ground I eventually found some and thats when a big old line of text just appeared in the middle of my screen in a really really ugly font. I mean this font is not what I would call a good font to be using in your game, it just doesn't look neat and tidy it looks basic like it was just thrown in there regardless of how bad it looks. There is only so much you can forgive an early access game for, thats at least 1 and a half strikes now in my book. So upon pressing the action key to search for a rock the text changes to say cancel action by pressing the action key again. It just feels clunky and robotic like the game is telling you exactly what it is doing all the time which I don't need to know. That leads me onto the animations. They aren't all that bad to be honest. I've seen far worse but of course much better also. The animation used when you search for items in the ground however really needs some work. It is not aligned it looks as though your character is waving their hands in the air. It's not that hard to change the animation to have the character kneel down or something and perform the same arm and hand movement down at ground level where they should be doing it. Little things like this can put people off a game if there are enough of them and they're not hard things to fix trust me I've made my own game I know how much effort goes towards certain things. One animation, a new neat looking font and a tweak of some code to show the player in the main menu screen should be but an afternoons work especially if there is more that one person working on the issues. You might be thinking "Oh shut up you've only played 2 hours of the game you can't say any of that!" well, firstly, it doesn't take more than a few hours to suss out a game and find its flaws (there's always at least 1 in any game) if you know what to look for and DayZ is no different. Secondly being in early access does give you a lot of leeway in the community and excuses you from some of the more minor faults in your game but particularly being in early access for so long couple with the fact it seems a lot of the old issues still persist to this day being unresolved entirely despite many reports from the community really doesn't garner a lot of respect from me as a consumer towards Bohemia. So, the verdict? In its current state 35 bucks is ridiculous to be charging for an early access title. This behaviour is typical of developers known across the lands as "money grabbing a-holes" which I really hope isn't the intentions of Bohemia but I can't be sure. I am aware the beta is coming "soon" but how long is "soon"? For all I know "soon" could mean 6 months maybe a year or more! They have long exhausted any trust they had to start with in the community, if they want to recoup any of their loses at all they need act right now and very very fast. I think for as long as this game stays around everyone is going to remember the early access days and never let Bohemia forget it, and rightly so, this is by far the worst the absolute worst early access progression I have ever seen in a game hands down. It has got so bad there are memes about it like this...
"2020:
Call of duty 21
Half-life 3
Battlefield 7
...
...
DayZ Early Access"
When your game gets its own memes usually thats representative of the community liking it. However, in the case of DayZ that is the complete opposite. Bohemia, get a grip and get your act together please. The amount of effort it took to write this review must mean that I still care about this game and have some hope left for it, however little that may be at this point...

DLC
-------------------------------
Let me make it clear though that this is a ONCE OF PURCHASE. There is NO micro transactions like in the Classic Version, but there will be DLC.
So far we got 2 free DLC, and one cheap DLC which enalbes the use of tents and blinds. Tents and blinds is not needed at all, it will just make the game less tedious in a way that instead of spawning and walking to said destinstion for hunting, you can now spawn directly to the place you wanted to walk too.
For me the DLC helps in a way that I walk around A LOT and FAR AWAY from Safe Houses, so when I quit my game, I put down a tent first so next time I spawn back in where I stopped, otherwise I need to spend another 30min to reach my destination next time I start the game up again.....
Bugs
---------------------------------
Now, for the game in itself. There is a few annoying bugs still around, but it will get fixed. The bows are still broken in this game, but still usable .. just not for silent hunting. The bows are broken in a way that they suffer accuracy issues. Sometimes your arrow will hit, sometimes it will not. The bows also have the same spook radius as a Rifle, which is odd.
Animals & Equipment
-----------------------------------
There is also MUCH fewer animals in comparison to Classic, the same could be said for weapons in comparisson to Classic. This game has MANY things short in comparison to Classic to call it a "complete" game. Your weapon choice is VERY limited and I never feel like a Hunter and look at my Store and be like "Man, so many choices, where do I start??" Instead I feel like "This is it ..... Really??".
Gameplay
--------------------------------------
The gameplay in itself is fun and addictive. Even given the amount of limited things, the game still manages to glue me to my seat, and get that fancy bow kill or long shot kill. At the core it is more like a watered down version of Classic for now, with more too come. Given the flaws, it still remeains one of the best Hunting games out there.
Devs
------------------------------------
So far they have been pushing big updates weekly, also with a few hot fixes inbetween. They are well aware of the broken game they gave us, and they intend to fix it. With bugs getting squashed weekly, this game will get better than it already is and I will gladly support it. The Devs are active in the Forums at times and they listen too our feedback.
Conclusion
-----------------------------------
Overall this is a Hunting game that still lacks features and equipment to call it a "complete" game, but at its core it still remains one of the better Hunting games out there and I gladly support it.

My review below:
Years ago I tested theHunter - free to play game. I didn't like it, I was younger & playing totally different games. Now that simulators and games that require patience are mostly the games I play, I'm in love with this. First day I bought this I played freaking 12 hours straight, I haven't played a game that long when I was a teenager.
theHunter - Call of the Wild is a steal at this price in my opinion. The visuals & landscape is stunning and immersive. I had no problem running this game around 100 FPS @ Ultra. No stuttering, quick loads and 0 crashes. I'm stunned that there's even a game like this out. Audio design, holy hell, it's perfect. Hearing the thunder roar startled me for the first time, rain fall from the sky and all the sounds of the forest. It is absolutely the best sound design I've heard in years. Everything ranging from weather, guns to animals.
Gameplay is simple to learn but some elements such as sneaking and being the perfect stalker & ambusher is hard to master. It's mostly about trial and error. There are some elements I really MISS such as free look (please, give me a reason to press Alt). Gunplay is a disappointment though, what this game needs is proper zeroing. Having to adjust your scope & sights with just a simple Pg Up or Pg Down button would be great. I know there's a skill for it but it only gives two ranges, short & long. This really in my opinion makes the rangefinder useless. I hope in the future patches they improve upon this.
AI of the animals is pretty 50/50 at this point. They sometimes (really rare) get stuck on the rocks and become an easy kill at this point. If you kill at one area, the animals will avoid it, I don't know how long the timer is but it's usually marked with purple color on the map. I've had a spot for two days where I killed 4 fallow deers and I haven't seen any animals anymore around the area. They avoid it like a plague. Aggressive animals are sometimes pretty confusing such as the european bison, surely it would attack or be more aggressive towards you if they notice you & you shoot them. The AI needs to be MORE dangerous!
Content itself, if you buy this game, what will you do? You can do the story & side missions. You can even disable them if you just want to hunt, progress on levels & skills and unlock new weapons. Love photography? You can take AMAZING screenshots in this game. This game is more for mature audience than your average mainstream gamer. Try to find the rarest animals, albinos, get best scores or medals on kills. This game is pure trophy hunting and improving your skills. Trial and error. Don't lose your patience, it took me a whole day just to do the mission where you have to kill a red fox with a bow. It felt so good when I got the shot.
Few things that annoyed me though in the beginning were the skill trees and the perks. Some of the skills & perks are so obvious in hunting that they should be on first tiers or at tier 0. The tiers atm are kinda messed up imo, they could look into this and fix them.
A quick note about the multiplayer. Me and my friend tried it. There's no desync problems or anything, it works smooth, you can hop in and out easily. There was something wrong though that the user interface started bugging for both of us. Stucked messages that only occurred in multiplayer. At this point, I really don't have an opinion about the multiplayer side of this game. Mostly I could not see myself playing this game with anyone else though, it's my own zen simulator. Hunting has always fascinated me and the patience it needs. I think I have found a new gaming genre which also to follow along with milsims & survival games.
Future hopes that the devs will actually do:
- More maps
- More animals
- More guns (give me a Mosin Nagant!!)
- Winter landscape
- Desert landscape? Would be interesting!

theHunter: Call of the Wild takes the previous dated installment riddled with microtransactions and puts it all into a single package with massively updated graphics that are truly impressive.
The game in it's current state has it's fair share of bugs and the recent small dlc caused has caused much outrage as it was widely believed that there would be no form of additional paid content - (for better or for worse I believe it is likely there will be more paid dlc content in the future but for what you get in the base game I feel the game is worth it especially in comparison to it's predacessor)
Despite this I am thoroughly enjoying this game largely in part due to the stellar graphics, music, weather and maps. Clearly, the people in the visual department are light years ahead of the rest of the team - every area in each map has it's own distinct "feel" and I regularly come across awe inspiring scenery rich with colour, light and animation.
(Unfortunately the antialiasing method implemented ingame causes much blur and the only real way to fix this is to disable it and downsample from 2/4k. (if you have the hardware to do this I highly suggest doing so).)
In regards to the actual core hunting ingame, there is plenty to be desired - somewhat buggy ai, menu glitches, audio issues - the list goes on. However I gloss over much of these issues (which don't happen often) and have a fairly enjoyable experience irrespective. The level progression/ingame money is fairly distributed and gives you plenty to work for. There is also a mission based system ingame in which main and side objectives will be given to you.
Make no mistake however that this isn't a slow paced game - if you are looking for regular action or are not willing to put in the time for reward this is not the game for you. Patience is virtue.
tldr;
- Absolutely stunning graphics if you have the hardware to run at 2k plus maxed settings.
- Hunting leaves alot to be desired (better ai) but is fully functional.
- Seemingly regular updates and much content to be added in the future whether paid or free.
- Plenty of bugs slowly being fixed
In the end I wanted a current hunting game that offered a true(er) to life experience and this suited my needs and more.

Platforming, hack and slash, Metroidvania-esque map generation; this game is a throw back to everything games used to be. I'm biased, but this is exactly what I look for in a game. I'm about 16 hours in, 2 bosses, and I'm loving every minute. About to fire it up to try and beat the 3rd area.

Mad Max is a very polarizing game. Although the Metascore is very solid, the individual critic reviews can range from positive to negative. But I've never found myself more satisfied by and more addicted to a game than Mad Max! This game, in a nutshell, is "scrumptious", and you'll come back for more if you love open world games that have lots of objectives to fulfill.
Here's a summary of the positives (+) and negatives (-) so far, which will be added to as gameplay time goes on:
+ Extremely well optimized and beautiful. This is one of the very few games that won't make your PC feel substandard and ancient if you had mid range hardware. Breathtaking all around, with a few average textures here and there that barely hurt the visuals. It's smooth as butter, with an excellent selection of video options.
+ Very cool progression system. Leveling up in Mad Max is a joy filled with lots of fun rewards! His appearance even evolves over the course of the game!
+ "Car porn" are two words to describe Mad Max. There's a ton of customization and ways to make your vehicle truly yours. Vehicle combat is high octane and adrenaline pumping, but only after you unlock higher level harpoons and other weapons!
+ Excellent characters that are often quite interesting, especially a few of the main characters and villains. Chumbucket is funny, and a charming companion for your journey. Griffa has an excellent aura of mysticism and mystery.
+/- The game IS a collect-a-thon, but is that a really bad thing? It encourages exploration around the various beautifully desolate locales. Yeah, it's not like Banjo Kazooie or something of the sort, but I don't understand why this aspect of open world games is considered so bad. Maybe to critics who tend to hate random busywork, it's bad, but for the average gamer who loves to fill up meters to 100%, collecting is quite fun in Mad Max! Many items actually affect things, such as scrap which is used as currency.
+/- Ground combat can be a mixed bag. I personally enjoy it a lot. The sound effects have impact, especially when your fist meets the faces of your many foes, but the cinematic combat is really just two or three buttons you push the whole time. Is that a bad thing? Perhaps, but it feels satisfying as hell to see how one button can cause so many varied and cinematic attacks to appear on screen. I don't agree that it's better than let's say, Devil May Cry, but I do like how it aggregates fancy combos into one button, and it's always fun to parry attacks then counter at the right time. Special finishers, weapons, and moves help add flavor to it.
- Ran into at least one gamebreaking bug that forced me to shut the game off, and the other bugs are minor. The most useful and strange bug caused enemies to vanish entirely during battle. Mostly random encounters on the road.
- There might be TOO MUCH to do, it's easy to get sidetracked for hours on end, spoiling the narrative flow. If you want to get to the heart of Mad Max, you'll have to skip a lot of the side content which makes up a majority the game in general.
- Some side objectives are repetitive as hell, but somehow I still enjoy them. But the game does indeed borrow heavily from other open world games... especially the "vantage points".
- Game does tend to lose performance in some car battles, or when there's a large number of enemies on the screen. Dense areas will lose some performance.
- Car combat is weak at the beginning of the game.
- Progression on Max, and his vehicle, is very linear. There is no reason to choose previously unlocked equipment... but baffingly, you can, which hurts your stats. Some vehicle customization options will lower stats, such as top speed or acceleration, giving some depth to it, but there is zero repercussions for using any upgrade for Max.
- The thunderpoon is an overpowered car weapon that is the definition of "dominant strategy"... in the end game. There is no reason to use the awkward harpoon or any other weapon when you can just one hit kill every enemy vehicle with a fully upgraded thunderpoon.
- The currency, Scrap, becomes pointless in the end game. There is no reason to aquire it besides for fun when everything is upgraded and bought.

Spec Ops: The Line is a psychological war thriller masquerading as a Tom Clancy-esque third-person modern military shooter. A better comparison for the game would be to that of Apocalypse Now, the film inspired by Joseph Conrad's Heart of Darkness. While an average game when compared to its contemporaries in the shooter genre, this game defies expectations and delivers an remarkable narrative experience. Play this game if you want to have your preconceptions about the military shooter genre challenged. Play this game if you want to have a brush with PTSD. Play this game if you want to experience a refreshing commentary on the glorification war.

I've been a shooter more or less all my life, my father taught me how to shoot with a crappy .177 air rifle when I was about 6 and I've been hooked ever since. As such, hunting games have always been something I've craved, so when I saw The Hunter: Call of the Wild up on steam for £30, I couldn't resist.
I'm going to address the negatives first because I want to end this review on a positive note, given that I am recommending the game.
The DLC. Yes, the £2.79 tent DLC. I know a lot of people have been laying into the game for this and I can understand why. I played The Hunter Classic for about an hour, then I dropped it because I didn't like the payment model. I know of people who have put over a thousand dollars into Classic and quite a few who have put hundreds in, so I think the reaction to the tent DLC is understandable. However, I also believe a lot of the negativity this game is getting comes down to people being annoyed that the game they put hundreds of dollars into is now available, in full, for £30, albeit a slightly reduced version of the game (the online is nowhere near as sophisticated), but every bit as fun and atmospheric at least.
The simulation aspect. This is where my main grip with the game comes from. On the one hand, the game takes the hunting aspect very seriously. Damage modelling is excellent (I know, I hit a red deer in the leg and it limped off before I quickly delivered the coup de grace) and the tracking and calling mechanics are top notch. Some people say this game makes tracking too easy. To them I say visit the options menu. From there, you can tweak the tracking to make it as easy or as realistically difficult as you want to. The ballistics are well modelled, to a point, and this is where the game lets itself down in the simulation aspect. The accuracy statistic. It is, to be blunt, nonsense. What should be the most accurate rifle in the game and the go to weapon for long shots (it's the go to weapon for snipers in both the US and UK militaries) is in fact the least accurate rifle in the game. I am of course referring to the .338. With an accuracy rating of 10/100, it's a joke. I'm baffled as to why the developers have done this. In fact, I'm baffled as to why each weapon has an accuracy rating at all. Just model the ballistics of each calibre as accurately as possible and the "accuracy rating" will sort itself out. The accuracy with bows is not what I would expect, although I say that as a bow shooter and a pretty decent one at that. The accuracy you'll get out of the bows is probably about on par with what you would see from somebody who's had an hour or two of practice, having never shot with a bow before. This is a difficult one to balance I guess and it does stop you from taking "pot shots" at long rage with the bow. It's best to think of bows as a close quarters weapon, which they are in real life anyway, but I was a tad disappointed when a shot I took from about 15 yards ended up hitting the deer in the back leg, rather than the lungshot I was going for.
Bugs. There are a few of these, although they mostly relate to the UI. There's a very irritating bug where a blank tutorial hint will stay on the screen until you quit the game and restart (quitting to the main menu doesn't fix it!). After you know your way around the game, you can thankfully turn these hints off which stops the hint from appearing and thus fixes the problem, but still. Also the directional indicator for the tracking mechanic will sometimes send you in the opposite direction that it should, although if you're paying attention to the animals footprints this isn't too big of an issue. The game also occasionally crashes when resting at an outpost, it has done this twice in 64 hours of play so nothing too drastic, but does need sorting. These are the main issues I've encountered and nothing else comes immediately to mind. None of them game breaking, just mild irritants.
The animal models are all the same as far as I can tell. Every buck/stag has the same wonderful looking rack, there are no 2.1's here, and they could use some more variety in both the size of the animal for both male and female animals and the quality of the rack for the males.
So, what do I like, no love about the game? Well, pretty much everything else.
The visuals are beautiful. From the dense foliage, the swirling mists that get blown by the wind to the sunlight/moonlight breaking through the trees and shimmering off the leaves, it really does do everything it can to make you feel like you're really there. The weather effects are great, although I was a little disappointed that my weapon didn't get wet when it rained, but that's just nit picking really, but overall the graphics are stunning.
The sound effects are top notch too, although the audio mixing at night could do with a little tweaking, the crickets can be deafening at times. The animal calls and their movements through the foliage are excellent and you can pinpoint their locations just by listening. The rifle reports are great, as is the twang of the bow and the shnick of the arrow as it finds its mark.
The story missions are fun, well voiced and there's plenty of them, some of which are quite challenging (like shooting a fox from 167 yards!).
Overall, the audio/visual presentation creates an unrivalled atmosphere and a real sensation of "being there". I've played most hunting games, from the original Deer Hunter series to the Cabella's (Their Big Game Hunter: Pro Hunts is well worth checking out too, for a slightly more "arcade" experience) but Call of the Wild tops the lot for sheer atmosphere and immersion. It's the absolute best hunting game I've played so far, by a long way. I hope the developers continue to update the game, fixing the bugs and providing more content (more animal models please devs!) because they've got an absolute winner on their hands here, no doubt.

Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

I purchased DayZ back in May 2014 when it was on sale for EUR 20.39. At that time the latest release was 0.45. The game still had a ton of serious issues I knew I wouldn't want to deal with, but back in 2014 I was very naive when it came to survival games and Early Access in general. So I bought it nevertheless, telling myself that I'll wait with playing it until version 0.50 comes out, assuming at that point DayZ will be a lot more polished, serious bugs fixed, so overall being a solid, enjoyable experience.
0.50 was released to "stable" in November 2014. The forums were full of the same kind of reports about bugs and glitches that already were an issue half a year earlier. So I decided to postpone my first DayZ session once again.
Fast forward to today,
later.
And guess what. The game is still plagued by the very same issues it had years ago. In addition to that the game starts to look dated as well, despite their recent efforts of improving the graphics.
I've been waiting for 0.63 for what feels like a year. These guys sold almost 4 million copies of DayZ, yet it feels like there's only 4 people left working on the game. Status report after status report, but hardly any substantial progress for months, even years when looking at the bigger picture.
Why the review now, you might wonder.
It's simple. I'm at the end of my patience. I'm sick of reading these hollow status reports while at the same time this seems like a dead game, abandoned a long time ago with just a few geeks still working on it in their spare time.
DayZ had monumental potential. But looking back from today's point of view, it's nothing but just another failed Early Access crap that is so common in today's gaming industry.

theHunter: Call of the Wild can be dubbed the “ground-breaking open world hunting simulator” you’ve been waiting for. You can expect realistic animal behavior, different weather conditions and ballistics. If you are expecting an extensive tutorial, you won't find it here. What you will find at the beginning of the game is being dropped into the hunting world with a gun and a map. Do expect some limited initial voice overs and tips, but expect to be pretty much left to your own devices.
We've found the tracking mechanics to be both frustrating and exciting at the same time. theHunter creates an immersive experience that feels very real. Also, be forewarned to be on the edge at all times because many of the animals can turn and attack you at a moment’s notice. We must say, it was very exciting once we finally lined up that shot and pulled the trigger. Accuracy matters a whole lot as the ballistics really alter the success of each shot based off distance and trajectory.
The issues that we found with the game are as follows: We found theHunter to be sometimes laggy, due to the sheer size of the map and it being rendered all at once. We noticed that while in the prone position, that the grass does not connect to the ground, which caused clipping and obstructed the path at times. Note that the most noteable glitch during our gameplay was a moose that was stuck in a hillside that just would not die until it was shot five times. This is a big deal when ammo is limited and weapons are difficult to unlock in the beginning. There is also an auto walk feature, which is nice when walking great distances, but problematic when collecting trophies. This is because when doing so the game does not pause and you can walk off a cliff, be attacked by a bear, or both in our case.

The best looking walking simulator you'll likely ever play.
3/10 - mostly for graphics.

I don`t play Free To play Online games, they`re a penny pinching con. And I don`t like always being stuck Online either.  However, some of them do look good and have interesting themes. So when The Hunter: Call of the Wild came out where you pay one fee for the whole game, I was really interested.
I`m a fan of very realistic games especially if based off... reality. So, tentatively, I bought it.
I liked how the game (after you choose a character: Man, of any colour, or woman), you`re plonked straight down in a field with a pad in your left hand and a rifle. Some lady says hello and gives a few instructions on your first hunt... What? now?
Soon, I see a deer- Way down the road. I go prone, aim, shoot and miss. The deer bounds away into the trees, laughing at my noobiness. I try to find the deer, never found it. Hmmm... Better check my settings.
I was glad to see that the options are extensive, you can have as many help icons on or none at all. I immediately got rid of X-ray vision and as I went through my first hunt gradually dropped most icons leaving only the tracking arc. This way the game gets really realistic.
But this game simply would`ve failed if it wasn`t for the incredibly good graphics and sound. It HAD to be good in this game\sim since you`ll spend most of your time staring at trees and foliage ;maybe squirrels getting stuck on the environment(more on that later). Everything looks almost photorealistic and the animation is top notch, trees sway, leaves fall about, You can hear the wind blowing and the sounds of wildlife about you just like in my own countryside in reality. Rain, fog and storms really are authentic. I was particularly impressed when the wind blew through the high grass and you could actually see the grass moving to the wind in a motion all the way ahead just like the real thing. Nicely done.
Hunting animals is VERY well done. Once you get to where there might be some deer, you have to go slow, kneel in cover to keep out of sight then use your Binocs to try and spot animals. You need to listen to sound cues and it isn`t long before you start to understand what a warning is from an animal or what a mating call is.
You really need patience not to spook them because they`re gone if you do. It takes time to get in a good firing position then you have ONE shot before they all scarper everywhere. Sometimes you`re not sure if you hit the creature until you find its body a bit later.
An example: I found an area with 4 deer. It took me about 10 minutes creeping and crawling before I got really close, a little to my own surprise. As I prepared for a shot, one of them called a warning and they all started walking away. They knew something was wrong. In a rush not to lose them after all my efforts I fired and hit one, but they all bounded away in different directions, but somehow keeping together.
Then I had to TRACK them to find the one I shot. The game has a rather cool tracking system that highlights as much of the scene as possible so you can find their tracks (but the highlights can all be turned off), then when you find a track and press a button to check it, it leads to another track and another. Sometimes its blood or stools (they always poop themselves when being shot at! lol). This could really be used for hunter skills in rpgs such as Skyrim or FallOut.
The tracks zig zagged all over the place and took ages of me following, but it was actually pretty cool. I felt like the Human version of the Predator, methodically following my doomed, bleeding prey.
I found them, I was way closer than expected and they darted off right past me and I fired again, but way too hectic to hit anything... and again I was tracking. The deer I`d hit was only slightly wounded so still able to flee fast...
This will not suit everyone, especially finger twitch people who must have flash and boom in their face constantly. Think of this as very realistic Farcry 4 except everything is far less explosions, shooting and story. There are tasks you get given every now and then though.
There are outposts where you can rest and buy more weapons and animal hunting kit with money earned from kills and you also gain experience to increase your skills with.
There are a variety of animals you can hunt, but not all of them are timid deer, some fight back and I noticed there is a health meter which means you could most probably die if an animals does an Arnold Shwarzenegger!
Bad things? Not much really... Saw a couple of squirrels and one got caught in the grass somehow and was running on the spot even while I was right next to it. To be honest it was the only thing that took me out of my immersion, like the cat walking in the same spot twice in the Matrix, hope they fix that. I notice map markers took a while to update in the world itself. When changing graphic resolutions clicking apply don`t work, you have to go back to the label that says `resolution` and click that which confused me for a while.
I saw there was a cheap DLC which I haven`t bought yet.
I really like the game, it`s slow, methodical and realistic- and needs PATIENCE. You`re a mean, practical, no holds-barred hunter who isn`t a snowflake ♥♥♥♥♥ about shooting an innocent animal dead and isn`t afraid to chase around terrified defenceless animals for hours in stunning terrain before shooting them and taking a trophy, Predator style, baby!
Recommended.

If you play this game it's gonna be frustrating if you don't have people to play & coordinate with on your team.
You have a team of 3 & you only control 1 character.  The other 2 are based on either AI mechanics that you have no say over, or other players in your party.  You can ask the AI to pass you the ball but they don't always comply due to the situation.  This game would be a lot better if you could control the AI members of your party.  Don't expect a normal single player B-Ball gaming experience for that very reason.  You need to make a team of real people to actually win games easily.  The AI won't do more advanced manuevers often like the ones they show you in the tutorial either.  They just dribble, pass, shoot.  Sometimes they won't even go for the ball when it's loose & they'll get it stolen when they have it.
Controller support is also lacking.  No D-Input support, so you better have an X-Input controller.  Even then it's still confusing as hell because the game is based purely on Keyboard & you have to look up the button maps online to know what button does what.
Graphics are good, the game is half-court basketball with official rules.  So it's a decent half court b-ball sim game.
The music is probably the best part of the game.  "We be ballin'!"  I gotta say this soundtrack is really catchy & fits the game almost perfectly for an outside half-court b-ball game.
Overall after playing this game a few hours (outside of Steam) it's a good game IF you have 2 other people to play it with, but since I don't have 2 friends to play with my experience was sour. The AI is mediocre at best & difficult to coordinate with.  If you play this game definitely play with friends.  If you don't have friends interested in playing it with you then you might as well not play it at all.

This game is a good game for its time! I have heard that people liked some improvements this game made over its predecesor but I never played Borderlands 1. Something I should bring up is that if you are a liberal, aproach this game with caution! This game possibly has to be the second most unpolitically correct ever made (the first one being Postal 2). Yeah, this is a game I don't talk about in public considering there are enemies in the game called Midgets and Psychos. Okay so what about this game is good? Well everyone who has even heard little bits about Borderlands would know that it has a lot of adult and crude humor behind it. that is very true! Initially when I staarted playing, the humor didn't feel right for me at first because the humor felt better suited to an adult cartoon on Adult Swim. But as the game progressed on, I started to enjoy the humor a bit more. Something to look forward to is the fact that there is an abundance of firearms that you can find. Plus every gun has a specific manufacture and every manufacurerer has their little gimmick that comes with every firearm. The Teidore has to be my favorite company because their guns have the best reload mechanic out there. Instead of a long and tedious reload animation like in your standard Call of Duty Teidore firearms explode when reloaded, so you can throw your shotgun at a bullymong charging in at high speed and what will happen is that the shotgun you just threw exploded and caused harm to the very beast that tried to eat you. In this game, you are going to have a favorite manufacture even though you won't have a favoirte gun. Plus the game is a multiplayer and the mulitplayer was actually handedled better than I though. It's decent but it works. So the multiplayer is an online co-op where someone hosts the game and everyone can decide on their own class. So whenever you create a charcter for multiplayer, you can always use that same charatcer for another mulitplayer or single player if you want to so you can essentailly have a roster of charcters for whatever game you want to play. In my honest opinion, single-player is more fun, because it adds more tension in gameplay than in multiplayer where you knwo when someone has your back. Plus there is the shield items. Shields in this game are a must-have for your charcter. What the shields do is they absorb all of the damage for you, but the shield has a limited amount of punishment it can take before it becomes disabled. The sheild will regenerate the energy over time when you haven't taken any damage but when the sheild goes down, you will not only be vunerable, you will feel vunerable as well so you will spend time trying to find cover to wait for you sheild to go back online. Plus the four classes presented in the game lack varitety but that all have their own special power, the comando has a deployable Sentry that will automatically target enemies for a limited ammount of time, the gunzerker can temporarly dualweild any weapon at his disposal, the siren has this supernatrual ability to crush enemies in this gravitational sphere, and the assassin has the abilitty to create a false-image of himself to disoreint the eneimes. Overall I recomend this game but I recomend you have your own oppionion on this game than simply taking my word for it. The reason why is because this game is good in my oppinion and even though I have never seen anyone not like this game, I can understand why someone wouldn't like this game especially since trying to make a game funny is a lot more dificult than trying to write an episode of South Park. Comedy is the second hardest genere to write and even though this game is funny, the fact that it's a game outs it at a disadvantage. Overall the best advice I can give you about this game is to take a gander at this game over a period of about a week, not a couple days, not a couple hours, you need to give this game at least a week.

Ignore everyone who says the game is terrible.
The dev team of this game is incredibly small in comparison to others as far as I know; about 70-80. Most of which are 3D modellers from Thailand as far as I know. So all the people stating the money factor of this game are a little slow - the progress they've made is slow, yes. But it's in line with the amount of people working on the game. Everyone comparing it to PUBG and Arma 3 are just.. not the brightest, let's say.
The game, right now (12/09/2017) is solid. Difficult, but solid. The new engine lets me play the game on Ultra settings, which wasn't even possible without instantly crashing before, and looks rather fresh, and less like the Arma titles.
Basebuilding is on the way, possibly even by the end of the year. There's a large range of guns and armour and clothing. The map has several new locations and towns, and most buildings are lootable/enterable. Zombies are in. They do not clip through walls, they have animations, and you can now stealth by them, and they are a problem, so you can't just sprint through towns after spawning; consider your actions.
The loot is scarce enough that it's actually difficult - no more lee enfields spawning in every barn on the coast - bullets are rare, guns are rarer down south. Protection from the elements is vital as you can freeze to death now. Most of the manchildren in the review think that's 'stupid', but hey.
If you hate slow updates and progress that rounds the game out bit by bit and not a chunk at a time, go for it, don't play it, don't buy it.
If you enjoy playing every now and then for about 4-5 hours a day, or three, once every few months to see how the game's going, making slow progress and actually building a character on a server (beards soon o:) and all your loot having value, buy it.

Early access done right - Prison Architect is an early access game that is actually updating and has a team supporting it. There are consistent updates that actually add major features and improve the game, and this has been going on for a long time already. As it is an alpha, there are some bugs, which are actually being fixed. But aside from that, on to the game itself.
Players in Prison Architect are set to manage a prison, which as the name implies they get to design themselves. Once the facility is constructed, in part or completely - Your choice, the player can allow in prisoners and manage day to day operation. Arrange for the prisoner's schedules for when they work, eat, sleep and so on. But keep in mind, the prisoners don't want to stay in prison. Some may not try it unless you just plain allow them to walk out the front gate, but others are more active about their attempts to escape or make life suck less. They arrange for tools and drugs to be thrown in over your outer walls, they take knives from the kitchen if they can get to them, and they'll try to dig tunnels to get out.
Special attention is to be paid to the possibility of a riot. Prisoners can decide to start taking over, they can raid the armoury, knock down guards to take their stuff, or kill eachother. They aren't friendly people, most of the time.
And you need to make sure they don't fall right back into their criminal habits after they're released.
Teach them carpentry, send them to a basic education, treat their addictions...And make sure they don't think of your prison as a comfy hotel, it's not a vacation for them, it's a punishment.
Time for the sentences appears to pass at a rate of one year per ingame day, and while this may not sound like it will have prisoners last long enough to do anything, many of them are in for 20 or more years, and some may show up with part of their sentence already done.
Your income, as money does not grow on trees, comes from a few sources. A basic daily income, plus an income per prisoner, and income from the workshop. When you're teaching these prisoners a skill, you may as well profit from it, but of course, not all of them are bright enough to be able to learn workshop safety classes.
I have mentioned money does not grow on trees, but that was only partially correct. The trees are money, as the wood is cut into boards and sold, or taken to the advanced carpentry stations for prisoners to create furniture out of. While probably not intentional, you can play Logging Station Architect instead. You just never take any prisoners and just plant trees to sell the logs. It's a slow way of earning money, and it is not anywhere near as fast or satisfying as running a prison, but the option is there. You can also sell off a prison you already made and use the money to start a new one, which allows you to continue playing the sold prison as well, though you can only sell it once.
The graphics may take some getting used to, but they fit the game and make things easy enough to see what is going on and where things are. The graphics aren't bad, but they aren't shiny 3d models as most games use these days.
In the end, Prison Architect is a great management/prison simulation game with great support by a great developper, and I would recommend it for anyone who is interested in management or simulation style games

This game is surprisingly good!
These days, the word 'simulator' at the end of a game is often a bad thing, but not here.
DETAILED
The game is really detailed - you have control over your truck in a way I've never seen in a driving simulator. lights, high beams, seat adjustment, mirror adjustment, realistic gearbox, windscreen wipers, cruise control, manual ignition. if the function exists in a real truck, you can likely do it in this game. Not to mention truck customization and company management.
The world is detailed too. I live in stockholm, and I can actually recognize the roads and landmarks I drive past in game. I keep going "holy crap, I've been here!" - the game even features a radio system that will livestream actual webradio stations into your game, so you can listen to what's actually airing on the road where you're driving. Add to that countless little things that pop up in the landscape for you to see on your journey
CHALLENGING
It's actually a bit of a challenge. You have to keep your cargo safe and drive legally, so you can't just barrel down the road like a maniac. You need to check your mirrors, mind the traffic and follow road signs. Trying to reverse a long haul truck with cargo is also much more difficult than it looks and delivering cargo to a shipping dock often involves a lot of patience and relearning how to drive, in a sense.
RELAXING
Let's face it, there's no assault rifles in this game, and nothing explodes. Most of the time you're just on a highway going form A to B - but that's actually nice. If you just wanna take 20 minutes to step away from it all (or a few hours), it's very very relaxing to just let the road roll by. Like all the most addictive flash games, it's not super exciting or crazy awesome - it just keeps you hooked and happy.

This is a game about driving trucks between real locations in Europe; a difficult parking job is about as action-packed as it gets. For the most part, you'll just be cruising, listening to the radio (which streams live over the internet), and relaxing. It's very therapeutic, and an oddly rewarding experience.
You either 'get' Euro Truck Simulator 2, or you don't, but it's worth trying it just to see what you might be missing out on.

Rogue Legacy is an absolutely fantastic game.  I purchased this almost a year ago for next to nothing during a sale and never played it until a week ago.  I wish I would have started playing it sooner.
The game gives you one life to complete as much as you can of the four wings of the castle.  While this may sound harsh, when you die, your next of kin gets to spend all the gold on upgrades that will forever be applied to all of your future new characters so technically you level up by dying after collecting gold.  When you die, the bosses you have killed stay dead too so you can get more powerful and slowly grind away at the castle.
The best advice I can give is don't get discouraged with dying very early on when you first start playing.  I think I died in the first or maybe second room on my first try.  The second, third and fourth attempts did not get much farther.  As you get more upgrades for your character as well as more skill in the game and learn the enemies attacks, you will eventually clear the whole first wing before dying, then the first and half of the second, etc.
One of my favorite features here is the replayability.  Once you finish the game, you can enter the castle again on a new game +.  This continues infinitely with the monsters getting more powerful each time.  As others have said in reviews and such, make sure you are ready before advancing the NG+ counter since the bump in difficulty each time is extreme.  From NG+ to NG++ was insane.
Overall this game is a solid 8/10+ and a very fun experience.  For the price, you really cant go wrong.

This game is surprisingly good!
These days, the word 'simulator' at the end of a game is often a bad thing, but not here.
DETAILED
The game is really detailed - you have control over your truck in a way I've never seen in a driving simulator. lights, high beams, seat adjustment, mirror adjustment, realistic gearbox, windscreen wipers, cruise control, manual ignition. if the function exists in a real truck, you can likely do it in this game. Not to mention truck customization and company management.
The world is detailed too. I live in stockholm, and I can actually recognize the roads and landmarks I drive past in game. I keep going "holy crap, I've been here!" - the game even features a radio system that will livestream actual webradio stations into your game, so you can listen to what's actually airing on the road where you're driving. Add to that countless little things that pop up in the landscape for you to see on your journey
CHALLENGING
It's actually a bit of a challenge. You have to keep your cargo safe and drive legally, so you can't just barrel down the road like a maniac. You need to check your mirrors, mind the traffic and follow road signs. Trying to reverse a long haul truck with cargo is also much more difficult than it looks and delivering cargo to a shipping dock often involves a lot of patience and relearning how to drive, in a sense.
RELAXING
Let's face it, there's no assault rifles in this game, and nothing explodes. Most of the time you're just on a highway going form A to B - but that's actually nice. If you just wanna take 20 minutes to step away from it all (or a few hours), it's very very relaxing to just let the road roll by. Like all the most addictive flash games, it's not super exciting or crazy awesome - it just keeps you hooked and happy.

This is a game about driving trucks between real locations in Europe; a difficult parking job is about as action-packed as it gets. For the most part, you'll just be cruising, listening to the radio (which streams live over the internet), and relaxing. It's very therapeutic, and an oddly rewarding experience.
You either 'get' Euro Truck Simulator 2, or you don't, but it's worth trying it just to see what you might be missing out on.

Rogue Legacy is an absolutely fantastic game.  I purchased this almost a year ago for next to nothing during a sale and never played it until a week ago.  I wish I would have started playing it sooner.
The game gives you one life to complete as much as you can of the four wings of the castle.  While this may sound harsh, when you die, your next of kin gets to spend all the gold on upgrades that will forever be applied to all of your future new characters so technically you level up by dying after collecting gold.  When you die, the bosses you have killed stay dead too so you can get more powerful and slowly grind away at the castle.
The best advice I can give is don't get discouraged with dying very early on when you first start playing.  I think I died in the first or maybe second room on my first try.  The second, third and fourth attempts did not get much farther.  As you get more upgrades for your character as well as more skill in the game and learn the enemies attacks, you will eventually clear the whole first wing before dying, then the first and half of the second, etc.
One of my favorite features here is the replayability.  Once you finish the game, you can enter the castle again on a new game +.  This continues infinitely with the monsters getting more powerful each time.  As others have said in reviews and such, make sure you are ready before advancing the NG+ counter since the bump in difficulty each time is extreme.  From NG+ to NG++ was insane.
Overall this game is a solid 8/10+ and a very fun experience.  For the price, you really cant go wrong.
