If you're reading this, chances are you're looking at this game because either, you're looking for a good shooter, or you've heard the story is amazing and you're interested in that.
The simple answer is, yes. With no qualifiers or reservations, I say, you should buy this game. If you need no further explanation, then enjoy. For everyone else, I continue.
On the surface,
doesn't look like anything special. It's a cover-based third-person shooter, where you move from shooting location to shooting location, looking for the right moments to take down your targets. In this way, it is the same as countless other games. As is the norm these days, when you're hurt, just hide long enough and you'll be back to full soon. Your squad can be commanded with simple commands, and shockingly, they're generally very competent. The gameplay is fun, smooth, and I can find no fault with it--this is not written as a ringing endorsement, simply a fact: the game plays well.
The story, likewise, appears unassuming. American military, Middle-Eastern conflict. If you threw in a nuke and maybe a cameo from the Covenant it'd be as formulaic as they come. It doesn't take long, however, before matters start falling apart, and the story leaves you guessing what's really going on. The way the storyline develops is a very strong point to the game, staying interesting, dare I say gripping, from beginning to end. On the merits of the strong story alone, I would recommend it.
But many video games tell a good story. Whether they emulate a book or a movie, showing you the storyline from checkpoint to checkpoint as it unfolds. Video games have been criticized and defended over whether or not they are an art form. I have always believed that they had the potential to be, but very, very few games lived up to that potential; it isn't enough to simply tell a good story, a game must utilize interactivity to tell its story. Whether that means choice, or even the illusion of choice, the difference is it is you, the player, that drive things forward, as part of the story, not a player-character that completes objectives in the right order. Very, very few games accomplish this.
Spec Ops: The Line is one of those few. This game is not about what happens, it is about what you make happen, and even as a linear game with only a few possible conclusions, it is a game where I felt that I created the outcome more than the most expansive sandbox RPG I've ever played. In the words of a certain famous madman, killing is making a choice, and this game puts the gun in your hand and makes you make that choice.
This is a game that demands to be played, do yourself a favor and play it.

Released only a few months after the movie franchise reboot "Mad Max: Fury Road", Mad Max isn't just another one of those movie-adaptation video games to follow the same background and story, but instead it takes inspiration from the entire movie franchise to create a unique experience, as the game is more like prequel to Fury Road, introducing you to the world of Max Mad without the need for any prior knowledge about the series. Mad Max aims for a story about a pointless existence of murder and regret, which does have its moments in situations where your actions will end up messing up other people's lives as well as your own, but just like many other games of its kind the stories that will stay with you afterwards are the ones you make yourself on the road to the finale. The story follows Max, who is once again left with nothing after Scabrous Scrotus took his car, on his journey for revenge accompanied by Chumbucket, a lonely blackfinger whose only goal is to build to ultimate ride. Along this journey you will meet all different kinds of insane people, starting with the Stronghold leaders, which will give you different side quests to complete across the wasteland and ending with all the stranger encounters that will sometimes give you scrap as a token of their gratitude for your fight against Lord Scrotus or useful information to help you take over a camp, such as the location of a secret entrance or different weaknesses in the structure that you can take advantage of. The story missions are only a small part of what Mad Max has to offer, as there are plenty of things to distract you along the way and on that side of things, the game gives you plenty of things to do to spice up your adventures, with camps to take over, scavenging locations to complete and many more; the order in which you complete those is totally up to you and completing different activities along the way is what makes Mad Max an enjoyable experience, even when it does come with its flaws.
If you have played some of the major open world games released in the past year such as Middle-earth: Shadow of Mordor, you will most likely find similarities in Mad Max's gameplay mechanics. On foot, the main combat element is brawling, as you will use simple attack and counter attack movements to defeat various types of enemies along the way, as the only weapon in your arsenal while on foot is your loyal shotgun, which does have limited ammo, so using it carefully between punches to defeat a more dangerous enemy approaching you is key. Driving your Magnum Opus things change, as the ultimate goal is upgrading your car to make it the best ride across the wastelands, as you will unlock new car bodies, engines, suspensions and many more customizable elements; with that being said, your Magnum Opus is equipped with a Harpoon that can be used to drag and pull different objects or structures, as well as a Thunderpoon and Side Burners. In addition to the weapons that can be attached to the Magnum Opus, the car itself can be used as a weapon, as different upgrades such as Boarder Spikes, Armour or Boost will come in handy if you want to be more aggressive and slam into other vehicles. While the main missions will give you an idea of how harsh the world of Mad Max is and introduce you to different elements of the game, the best way to experience what Mad Max has to offer is by going out to explore the different events and locations on your own, as there are numerous races to complete, camps to take over and scavenging locations filled with scrap and upgrade parts for your projects in the Strongholds. As large in scale as it is, Mad Max feels really limited when it comes to movement freedom, as you will often head for a cliff that looks easy to reach only to find out that there is no way for you to get there, as the movement mechanic only allows you to climb marked locations. On top of that, the game does come with the occasional bugs and glitches, but those are minor enough not to influence your experience too much.
For a deserted wasteland, the world of Mad Max is quite beautiful in its own gloomy way, with detailed locations and memorable places; contributing to that world are the insane characters you will meet along the way, each with its unique personality and level of madness. The weather effects have a significant impact on the world, as nights will make the desert look even more lonely and storms will reduce the visibility to a point where looking ahead of you will become your main objective. Animations can be a bit clunky at times and there are some texture popping issues, the number of them varying from one platform to another, but those are only minor issues that barely distract you from the massive world that lies ahead of you.
Bren Foster is the voice of Max and does a great job narrating every dramatic moment of Max's adventures, accompanied by other noted actors such as Travis Willingham voicing Lord Scrotus and Jason Spisak providing the voice of Chumbucket. The sound effects are okay and even though they can feel a bit repetitive at times, there is enough variety in action to make sounds feel distinct and take you on an emotional ride from one dramatic moment to the next one and straight back into the chaotic action afterwards.
You can probably finish the story within 15 hours if you go straight forward from one mission to the next one and complete only what is necessary, but with so many things around you that will probably not be the case, so with all the races, camps and locations to explore you can easily spend 50 hours with Mad Max, add even more if you're willing to complete every challenge.
Mad Max is an excellent open world adventure no matter if you're a fan of the movies or not, as the game does a great job introducing you to the world of the franchise and tell you an interesting story without sacrificing too much on the fun, chaotic gameplay that will keep you hooked for hours. If you want a game to keep you preoccupied for a long period of time, Mad Max is definitely a must try as it provides more than enough content and variety to entertaining you for a couple of days.

I want to compare it to something like Super Castlevania, but as a Rogue-Like game.
The game mostly revolves around exploring an ever-changing castle, searching for treasure and enemies, until you die. When you die, you can spend the gold you earned on upgrading your family tree, and buying better weapons/armor/abilities. Unfortunately, every time you re-enter the castle, you lose ALL your gold. So you can't save your gold through multiple runs of the castle to buy an expensive upgrade; you have to get it all in one go. I would have preferred if this wasn't the case, but it doesn't ruin the game.
Some of the level design feels kind of dickish (I can't tell you how many times an enemy forced me to make a leap of faith to avoid their attack, only to jump right into ANOTHER enemy), but I guess that just comes with the procedurally-generated territory?
Speaking of 'dickish'ness, all of the bosses really got on my nerves. There was only one which I kind of enjoyed, at that was just because the previous boss forced me to grind for upgrades, so I was overleveled for the next portion.
The Final Boss REALLY annoyed me, because his attacks were all very powerful and erratic, so I couldn't get a feel for how to take him down. I wound up giving up after learning that the final boss has TWO forms, when just one form is hard enough. [Note: I have beaten the original Castlevania, Mega Man 2-5, and Super Mario Bros 3. I'm not the type who gives up easily on a difficult game.]
That said, if the game looks interesting to you, then check it out. It's decent enough, just, it could have been a LOT better if they had made it easier to upgrade your characters [I had to spent a majority of the gametime grinding to upgrade my characters], and maybe spent more time integrating the theme of the family.

I have to say after playing a lot of shooters, and a being a fan of story, morality, and all around mind ♥♥♥♥ery.
Spec Ops: The Line really takes the cake. One made of White Phosphorus, and mental instability from one's actions.
As a shooter goes, Spec Ops: The Line brings a decent amount to the table. Some things generic and typical, some surprisingly done well.
Cover system (which is locked into running through holding the space bar, where running is pressing the space bar) is not surprisingly meh, it needed polish on what you could clip to and perhaps making the sprint button another button all together, but this seems rather a norm in cover shooters with clipping and all.
The weapons were simple and typical, yet had that nice touch to the ammo, where you actually felt a need to place shots some what, and caused you to carry either what was practical and you could 'mostly' find ammo for through scavenging dead people after firefights, or carry something that was good yet would probably be used in particular situations.
(such as the Bolt Action .50 BMG you find near the end of the game that 3 shot heavies on Hard, or the grenade launcher which worked like it should, and murders a crowd of enemies with one decently placed shot)
AI for the enemies had it's♥♥♥♥♥♥worthy moments, but they were relatively intellegent for most situations.
Your allies though are wowing on the fact that 90% of the time, you can actually depend on them for killing enemies, killing something you ordered killed (like Lupo braining someone with his rifle, that always brought a feeling of joy knowing the AI was well worked, and wouldn't butt ♥♥♥♥ itself into a corner or get you killed *cough* Sheva *cough*)
But the crowning point of this game is the story, morality of war, 4th wall breaking, and over all feel of regret and acceptance of actions.
SPOLIERS AHEAD IN BLACK. READ AT OWN RISK OF SPOLING! *duh*
Most games generally give you a simple situation of moral dilemma.
Good or Bad?
Blue or Red?
Paragon or Renagade?
Spec Ops: The Line's first instance of moral dilemma, may be forced, but it does make you generally be bothered on a choice 'you' made.
Some will call it a guilt trip because it's forced. But it's a moral point that war is a very ugly thing, and horrible things are done in the name of it. Too many shooters make war out to be cool, and that you're always the good guy, always the hero. You aren't the good guy, from what we've been taught...good guys don't melt people accidentally because they were in the way. It happens though in War. People getting caught in a cross fire. And people who accidentally kill those people...live with those actions and consequences, much like Walker (The character you play) and the player do.
Many of the people who bring up that parts of the game are forced moral trips will see that near the end, the game beings breaking the 4th wall in a very unique way. Such as the load screens saying
"This is all your fault."
"To kill for yourself is murder. To kill for your government is heroic. To kill for entertainment is harmless."
"How many Americans have you killed today?"
"If you were a better person you wouldn't be here."
The choice the player ultimately can make is to play or not play. You didn't have to continue on, you chose to keep playing, regardless if the morality bothered you or not. The General you're chasing till the end of the game even brings it up that Walker didn't have to come into Dubai and chase after him. Those weren't his orders. He chose to continue and in a sense enter the heart of darkness.
I will state the twist at the end was...maybe a tad predictable, but the sense of a shattered mentality of the character after walking through a literal hell (and through speculation, possibly Walker's perception of either hell or purgatory) and a player left wondering if games haven't made them a little desensatisted and possibly brainwashed into how some games make warfare into a cool thing. Is probably some of the best story telling you can do in a game market filled with the same ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t storytelling.
All in all, I give this game an 8 out of 10.

I don't know if I can say it's the best third person shooter ever, but it's quite possibly the best genre deconstruction that I've seen in a video game.
You play as a three man squad of gung-ho US armed forces members, whose leader is voiced by Nolan North. It almost feels like the game wants the player to groan at the casting choice and setup right out of the gate. Where it takes you is through the muckiest of the sins committed during war, with the player truly being taken on a mind-numbing trip with the lead character. Aside from solid gameplay, the plot takes every normal schtick of the third person shooter and turns it on its head. I truly believe that (along with GTA IV, Bioshock Infinite, and Castlevania: Lords of Shadow) this is one of the games of the last four years that MUST be played through at least once, if for no other reason than to understand its contribution to the art form.

I should start out with saying that I am a massive mad max fan, I love the movies, the cars, the whole story and this game is no exception. I adore this game, I got it and then spent the next 4 days glued to it, litterally played nothing else and did almost nothing else.
+ Fantastic story, embodies the Max we know and love almost perfectly, compelling and fun storyline.
+ Good graphics, its nothing outstanding, but they have managed to create a beautiful game.
+ Excelent optimisation, no frame rate drops, no problems at all. (Ran on max settings with i5-4570 / 2GB GTX770 / 8GB RAM)
+ The combat in this game is great, infantry combat is very satisfying and the vehicle combat is a real "blast", but the vehicle combat can get repetetive if you are taking things slow.
- The side missions and other activities in the game get boring after a while. To be fair this only really matters if you are going for 100%.
- The difficulty, it starts out fairly challenging and gets easier to the point at the end when you feel like a god. Also, some bosses are easy and some are very hard.
- Sounds, as a car lover I cannot approve of some of the engine and general car sounds. The V6 with twin turbos has no turbo sound at all, and the supercharged V8's barely whine at all.
All in all, this was a great game, I loved playing it and hopefully I find more time to spend in the wasteland and 100% Mad Max. If you are a fan of the movies, buy it on sale or not, you will love it. If you just want a great singleplayer game, buy it anyway.

I would say this 'game' is first- nicely produced, second- only a fair simulator of truck driving, third- has a large amount of places that are not accurate representations, and fourth- a large collection of customizations for your truck (like paint jobs).
One of the main reasons that prevented me from enjoying this game was the steering:
Steering the truck does not have a realistic feel to it. The steering is not smooth (even when trying and making many different adjustments via the options screen). Steering required constant tweaking back and forth to keep the truck in the lanes and in no way did I ever feel like I was steering a real vehicle. Driving a real vehicle I don’t have to constantly keep ‘on top’ of my steering wheel like you do in this ‘game’. I never felt like I could ever relax like I do when driving on a real road trip.
Other factors for giving this game a thumbs down:
There was not a wide variety of roads; after a while the road design repeated types of roads I had already driven in other locations.
Even though there is a large amount of locations, the locations were not even close to true representations and the location design started repeating just like the roads.
For me, there are way more fun and enjoyable games out there than to waste time on this one.
Also, I wonder if a large portion of the favorable reviews for this game are fabricated in order to drive up profits; note the metacritic reviews average a good amount lower than the steam reviews.

If you're a fan of basketball and always wanted to play one of the NBA games online against other people, this is as close as it gets and boy is it done well but, keep in mind nothing is ever perfect!
Lets start off with what the game offers well right when you start it up. You are free to create a character from any position (Center, Power Forward, Shooting Guard, Point Guard or Small Foward), each having their own strengths and weaknesses just like in real life: A center is good at defense and going up against other players however he's bad at shooting and is not as fast etc... There are special paid characters that gain a boost in their stats (you also gain stat points when you level up like an RPG) but it's still not a Pay to Win aspect as the game itself is more team based. 1 man will NEVER win a game alone no matter how good he is.
Now lets talk about the pros and cons of the game:
PROS:
- Very entertaining and fun to play (will keep you coming back again and again and again)
- Soundtracks that are in the game are perfect and definitely put you in the mood for a basketball game (there are a lot of tracks)
- Not Pay to Win by any means
- Complete control over how to play your position (you can be a Center but still spend your stat points on shooting and increasing your speed if you wanted to!)
- A not so bad community! Some people say the community is toxic that's only because many of them are bad players, if you prove yourself as a good asset to the team everyone will pass to you even the selfish shooter (not always though).
- There is a rank system to prevent pros from going to crush noobs, there are 3 channels: Rookie, Major and Pro with a level cap for each.
- Cool Celebrations after scoring... You get 4 free celebrations when you start the game but anything else requires payment either by ingame currency or real life money (can't blame them though, how else would they make money out of the game)
- Badass dunking and other shooting forms you unlock as you play!
Now for the Cons:
- Very little diversity in the voice acting of characters (it's not going to bother you that much in the actual game though)
-  Clothes in the game are more less too expensive... Throughout your playthrough from Rookie to the Major channel you will most likely be able to buy 1 set of clothes for your character, basically 1 shoe, shirt and trousers and that's it (maybe some other cosmetics too but that's it) and you'll be running out of ingame currency faaaast.
- Although not that common sometimes server start lagging but it doesn't last long and it's not something that could get you to rage quit a game.
And that's it really, there is truly no good reason not to try out this game, no pay to win aspects, a fun gameplay that is not going to get boring anytime soon and if that isn't enough to try out a game these days I don't know what is.
If I had to rate this game I'd give it an 8.0/10... It's solid but could use some extra help in the system of ingame curreny

I am reviewing this as a single player title.  I have no interest in the multiplayer content, and have not tried it to provide feedback on it.
Before the good, I need to be clear on something many might view as bad.  I finished this game in one sitting last night of about six hours.  Some people hate short games, but this game is surprisingly deep, keeps you wanting to stay and play more, and I already am thinking about playing through again as its obvious there are different ending possibilities.  I view the shortness of this game as the one standout thing against it.
Moving on though... there was a lot I liked.
This game is about people who are in very dark situations, confronted by nothing but dark and challenging choices.  You are not either saving the damsel, or killing her dog.  I once read a review that seemed intriguing.  It said that once you realize whats going on you will be hooked and want to see the rest of the game through.  I got there.  I was hooked.  I had to see how it ends.
The gameplay was good, and by the time I realized why -- I was actually surprised.  Too many games have cover systems that aren't necessary.  Enemies that could fire 1000 bullets and maybe hit your water canteen once.  Etc...   Spec Ops:  The Line is not such a cake walk.  The enemies can hit you accurately, and they will.  Your AI team mates will be a necessity, but they will also be vulnerable.  There are times where you will run out of ammo and even if you don't like this gun or that based on your own style... you will think its a god send to have a way to fight off the enemy, and play accordingly.  I found myself using cover at every possible avenue.  Grenades were not an afterthought.  It was FUN.
I've played numerous shooters dating back to Wolfenstein 3D and Duke Nukem.  I've played Medal of Honor, Call of Duty, Battlefield, Halo, and more.  I have to say this game really felt different and drew me in how many AAA games have.
When everything was said and done, it was the story and presentation that blew my mind.  Mature modern story in a believable setting.
Random number score system? 9/10.  I was that impressed.

Where to begin with this game?
Well, it's a third-person cover shooter with pretty basic mechanics, but that's not all. The main selling point of this game is that the story is something you might never see in most shooters. You play as Captain Walker of Delta Squad, with your two mates, Lugo and Adams. Your mission is to rescue a man from Dubai, but that's just the beginning. This game makes you question the moral consequences of shooting your enemies and also makes you question just who the enemy is. Without giving too much away or spoiling the whole plot, it is by far one of the greatest plots I've seen in a shooter. It draws inspiration from Heart of Darkness/Apocaplyse Now, and expands on it. By the end of this game, you will be morally torn in a way you never thought you would be in a shooter.
Since it is part of the game, I figured I should touch on multiplayer. I have yet to play the multiplayer myself, but from what I've heard, it's not much to write home about. Give it a try if you're interested, but multiplayer isn't what this game is made for.
Overall, I would definitely recommend this game for story alone. It's thrilling, makes you question your reasons for killing, and makes you think quite a bit. Buy this game. It's worth it.

I got this game as a Christmas present from a friend in 2015, and sort of played it for a bit before just letting it go off to the wayside for a while. I eventually came back to play it earlier this year (2017), and have completed the game at least twice now since.
I thought this was overall a pretty fun, well-thought out game. The characters are quirky, the locations are fairly creative, the music is incredible, and the story (this includes all the different outcomes for completion and the lore) can range anywhere from funny to somewhat thought-provoking, from tearjerking to heartwarming, and from scary to exciting. I feel kind of silly now that I essentially just left the game untouched for about a year, but things happen.
In terms of mechanics, being unfamiliar with Earthbound-style RPGs and Touhou-style bullet hell games, I can't draw comparisons. But I can say that I find the idea of blending the two genres to be a fairly interesting idea, and I'll definitely say that the experience is unique. The only complaint I really think I have is one smallish plothole, but that one seems really more like a nitpick, so I guess I'll just skip to this:
I'd give Undertale around five stars out of five, and a recommendation. Pick it up if you can.

When I completed the original Life is Strange series, my aching thought was "No game will ever again, be able to pull me in like that. No game will ever be able to tear apart my inner being and play with every emotion like that. No game will ever allow me to connect with characters like that. No game will ever give me an experience like that again."
I have never been more happy in my life to have been wrong.
After spending around 8 hours in the first episode, I feel the same way I did when I found the first Life is Strange game. Absolutely fantastic. This game pulls you in, severing the link to reality and really places you in the shoes of Chloe Price. I was smiling, yelling at my screen, fist pumping, crying, and all kinds of other emotional things that few games have ever been able to make me feel (and I have played a lot of games). I sat here, pondering what decision I would make, for extended periods of time; weighing possible outcomes and really struggling over what I wanted to do. I kept saying to myself "I will just play until the next checkpoint, then I'm going to bed." I started saying this around 11:45PM. I am writing this review at 1:55AM, having completely finished episode 1. Ever since I finished the original Life is Strange, I have been very much longing for a game that could give me, even a similar experience, and Life is Strange: Before the Storm goes above and beyond expectations for a riveting, immersive, story-telling experience.
Props to the new devs, Deck Nine, and publisher Square Enix for continuing an epic franchise and one of my favorite games of all-time. I had extremely high expectations for this game and it did not disappoint. If you liked the original Life is Strange, if you like getting emotionally attached to all the characters in a story, if you like feeling sucker punched in the feels (both very happy and sad), if you like having options that really matter and effect outcomes and dialogue much later in the story, if you like playing tabletop RPGs with computer-animated teenagers, this game is for you.

This may be a game of perfection. I highly recommend it to anyone as it is a solid game for any player. This is a rogue-like, randomly generated dungeon crawler that forces you to fight your way through rooms of enemies, solve puzzles to open chests, and defeat bosses in four sections of the castle.
The beauty of this game is that death is accepted, when you die you simply choose one of three randomly generated characters, cash in on the gold you found, and fight through another castle. At first you are likely to die many times without many kills, but as you learn the enemies and buy upgrades you will slowly find the game getting easier. Learning enemies is essential in this game. They will start out simple, but as you progress they get more difficult with more health, more shots fired, or new variations on enemies previously fought.
A good chunk of this game is about fighting to find treasure. You will mostly collect gold which can be used to buy more health, mana, armor; or you can buy new classes to play as, have a better chance to land a critical hit, or make your spells the hardest hitting in the land. You will also find armor and "runes" (which will add more variety and strategy to each playthrough) in which you must purchase with the gold you earn.
As you select a new class to play you will find random traits your characters may have. Some may only be able to see in black and white, some may be flexible (allowing them to change direction mid-swing), or maybe they have terrible memories (good luck navigating without a map!). The spells you can cast are random as well, some spanning from a simple projectile, to a giant sword wall to keep enemies away.
Absolutely amazing, worth every penny! Controls are tight, graphics are that of the Super Nintendo era, with a great polish. The music can get a bit redundant, but never takes away from the game as most the time you will find yourself focused on not dying. I have heard there may be a secret room to take away from that problem, if you happen to find it, may I recommend "The Fish and the Whale". ENJOY!

A metroidvania type platformer. I loved this game. At first i didn't think too much of it, but the more I played, the more I enjoyed it. You'll die a lot, but with each new descendant you'll be able to progress further and further in the castle and unlock/defeat the bosses. This game has an interesting gimmick in that you have no lives, you play until you get killed and your descendant continues, in another randomly generated castle. What's funny though (and humor is a huge part of this game) is that your descendants will have random genetic "defects". For example, your character can end up having IBS (Irritable Bowel Syndrome) and will roam the castle endlessly passing gas. To cut this review short, I loved this game and I definitely recommend it, despite how frustrated it made me feel. 4/5

Before the good, I need to be clear on something many might view as bad.  I finished this game in one sitting last night of about six hours.  Some people hate short games, but this game is surprisingly deep, keeps you wanting to stay and play more, and I already am thinking about playing through again as its obvious there are different ending possibilities.  I view the shortness of this game as the one standout thing against it.
Moving on though... there was a lot I liked.
This game is about people who are in very dark situations, confronted by nothing but dark and challenging choices.  You are not either saving the damsel, or killing her dog.  I once read a review that seemed intriguing.  It said that once you realize whats going on you will be hooked and want to see the rest of the game through.  I got there.  I was hooked.  I had to see how it ends.
The gameplay was good, and by the time I realized why -- I was actually surprised.  Too many games have cover systems that aren't necessary.  Enemies that could fire 1000 bullets and maybe hit your water canteen once.  Etc...   Spec Ops:  The Line is not such a cake walk.  The enemies can hit you accurately, and they will.  Your AI team mates will be a necessity, but they will also be vulnerable.  There are times where you will run out of ammo and even if you don't like this gun or that based on your own style... you will think its a god send to have a way to fight off the enemy, and play accordingly.  I found myself using cover at every possible avenue.  Grenades were not an afterthought.  It was FUN.
I've played numerous shooters dating back to Wolfenstein 3D and Duke Nukem.  I've played Medal of Honor, Call of Duty, Battlefield, Halo, and more.  I have to say this game really felt different and drew me in how many AAA games have.
When everything was said and done, it was the story and presentation that blew my mind.  Mature modern story in a believable setting.
Random number score system? 9/10.  I was that impressed.

text:
Where to begin with this game?
Well, it's a third-person cover shooter with pretty basic mechanics, but that's not all. The main selling point of this game is that the story is something you might never see in most shooters. You play as Captain Walker of Delta Squad, with your two mates, Lugo and Adams. Your mission is to rescue a man from Dubai, but that's just the beginning. This game makes you question the moral consequences of shooting your enemies and also makes you question just who the enemy is. Without giving too much away or spoiling the whole plot, it is by far one of the greatest plots I've seen in a shooter. It draws inspiration from Heart of Darkness/Apocaplyse Now, and expands on it. By the end of this game, you will be morally torn in a way you never thought you would be in a shooter.
Since it is part of the game, I figured I should touch on multiplayer. I have yet to play the multiplayer myself, but from what I've heard, it's not much to write home about. Give it a try if you're interested, but multiplayer isn't what this game is made for.
Overall, I would definitely recommend this game for story alone. It's thrilling, makes you question your reasons for killing, and makes you think quite a bit. Buy this game. It's worth it.

In terms of mechanics, being unfamiliar with Earthbound-style RPGs and Touhou-style bullet hell games, I can't draw comparisons. I'd give Undertale around five stars out of five, and a recommendation. Pick it up if you can.

My Game of the Year for 2015 Mad Max is a thrilling joyride through beautiful terrain with brutal combat, amazing car chases / races, and an authentic look inside the mind of madness. I bought the game at full price, 60 bucks, and got every penny's worth.
Done by the Just Cause guys, the world is almost overly massive. I didn't get too deeply into Just Cause because I felt like there was just too much crap I had to do. It can get a little repetetive crawling around abandoned bases trying to find that last piece of scrap metal to fully complete an area, but it manages to do the GTA thing where its fun just to drive around. The Combat is lifted from the Batman / LOTR games, but this game definitely does the style the best of those 3 titles.
It achieves the rarely achievable "It's awesome to kill somebody every single time you do it". Brutal crunching sounds and primal screams, awesome animations and satisfying finishers. I found myself getting out of the car and baiting dudes just so I could punch their faces with Max's spiked gauntlets.
The Car, the Magnum Opus, is the real star of the game, and yes, you do level up Max, but the car is the real main character. So many times I was supposed to play for "just a little bit" and then I kept going because I wanted to get the next engine upgrade. Cleverly tied to clearing the map, the car upgrading system - and the fact that, there isnt a "BEST" configuration, just a configuration that best suits your style of play - is the main hook that will keep you coming back.
At this point im taking a slow burn on finishing it completely because I love it that much. The game is like a 6 pack of high quality imported beer - as tempted as I am to chug the rest of it, I'll keep it for when I really need to have some fun.

Wow... just... WOW!  I cannot remember the last time I was so violently enthralled with a game from the very get go.  I was not expecting this to fully capture the FEEL of the mad max movies as incredibly well as it has done!  Though I am not very far into it at this point, it has been pure pleasure since the very beginning!
The visuals are absolutely amazing, and optimization... holy sh*t!  I don't think I have ever seen a game that looks so good and runs so flawlessly!  This is probably one of, if not THE best looking games in my library and it runs on my 3440x1440 ultrawide smooth as silk on ultra settings!
They did an amazing job giving you a huge wasteland to roam and explore, yet while the area is so vast, so far it has definitely not suffered from the traditional "open world sandbox travel through miles of nothing to get to the patches of content" syndrome.  Or at least it hasn't felt like it.  Maybe that's because the gameplay itself is just so d*mn much fun!  (did I mention how well it captures the feel of the films? :D)
The "on foot" combat is very very much, the tried and true assassins creed, batman, shadows of mordor formula as many have stated, with the very refreshing alteration of being more brute strength and rage based then graceful cat like ninja.  You're not leaping all over hell and back, doing fancy spin kicks and back flips, it's more the "walk up to someone, grab em by the neck and smash their face into a table" type.  Absolutely LOVE it!
Vehicular combat... this is the crème de la crème feature of this game, the grand masterpiece!  OMFG it is so much fun!  It's... well... it's something you really just have to experience for yourself, but... ya... wow!  I have seen a few reviewers complaining about the driving controls, personally I don't see it.  To me the driving has been better than most I have played.  The car has been easier to handle and control for me than most other games of this type.  Granted, I do not play racing games, where the entire effort of the game has gone into the driving / vehicle handling, but I do play most all of the sandbox games that involve guns and cars, and imho this one is better than most as far as vehicle control and driving is concerned.  (or again, maybe it's just because driving in THIS game is so much more fun than the others... I mean... when was the last time you were racing through a debris filled desert mashing it up with other cars and shot the driver with a harpoon and yanked him out of the other vehicle through the window?  Come on... so brutal... I LOVE it!)
There is so much to go on and on about with this title in the way of comparison with other open world sandbox rpgs, but really... at least for me... there's no need, while all of those things do mashup to equate to the overall completeness and  complexity of the game (and they do so very well so far, and I have not yet found anything lacking in the way of systems or things to do), what it really boils down to for me... is fun factor... this game is SO much fun to play!  Based on what I have seen so far, I could wander aimlessly through the desert for hours just engaging in random encounters and still feel like I was getting my moneys worth on this game.  All technical, feature, and systems talk aside, it is just plain and simple, good old fashion fun!
Def recommend this title to anyone who even remotely likes the Mad Max movies!

Open world driving meets Arkham asylum fisticuffs in this licensed title from the makers of Just Cause.  Warner Bros. these days usually isn't a mark of quality but Avalanche have made a fun little open world game with some nice mechanics.  Driving is the highlight of the title with Max making a new car to chase down the warboys of Immorten Joes forces set prior to the events of Fury Road.
Graphically it isn't stand out but it looks nice enough and the effects for things like storms and explosions look very good.  Driving is functionally good but it could be a little tighter and I would recommend playing with a controller simply because it was built around the console control scheme.  It is however perfectly playable with mouse and keyboard but if you have a controller use that instead.
Combat on foot is batman basically with counters, dodges and combo's making up your repetoire.  Enemies crunch under the weight of max's blows and some kills are quite wince inducing so it fits the dark world of Mad Max.  Car combat is fun but sometimes a little cheap when the AI can damage you a lot easier than you can damage them, and later upgrades make car combat extremely easy at times.  Still having a car you can customise is pretty cool and there are plenty of different car bodies to choose from in game.

Hands down the best campaign I have ever played. Short but poignant, Spec Ops: The Line takes a new perspective on the psychological aspect of war and what soldiers face in the field. Couple this gripping storyline with solid gameplay mechanics and you've got the recipe for one of the greatest war games ever made.

The gameplay mechanics for this are really not very good (unless you're strangely fixated on Gears of War type gameplay).  Personally, I hated everything about the cover system, but I pushed through it.  Aside from some really poorly placed checkpoints and those ham-fisted cover mechanics, the story really shined through in this title.  It takes at least an hour or so to really get going, but if you manage to look past some of it's short comings and focus on the character development, I think you will be pleasantly surprised by how good this game is.
I found myself dying a lot towards the end and I was starting to get really annoyed about it, not because I wanted to win or unlock all the achievements, but because I wanted to find out what was going to happen next.  I wanted to finish the story.  Out of say, 300 or so games that I have played over the last few years, I have probably only felt that way about 5~ games (The Binding of Issac, Gone Home, Portal, Assians Creed 1 and this game).
I feel like this is very much the modern day Medal Gear Solid due to one or two scenes in particular, so if you enjoy some really meta gameplay moments, I think you will enjoy this.  I highly recommend you check this game out if you can spare the cash.

Spec Ops: The Line is a much needed breath of fresh air for the "modern shooter" genre. The game play is 3rd person, coverage based shooting. Its good, not great....just good. The atmosphere is great in the sense that ammo is scarce and you have to constantly switch between your weapon and the weapons your enemies drop. This creates a fun conflict within the gamer, "do I hold onto this gun I really like, with very little ammo? Or take the downgrade with more ammo?"
Where this game truly excels though is in the arena of story telling. Story telling and character development being two things that seem to escape the vast majority of today's writers of games, TV and movies. The game is a roller coaster of conflict, internal and external. It follows 3 Delta Squad operators as they make decisions (most of which have potentially horrific backlash) most people would be too afraid to make.
One of the game's central themes is a subject that we in America seem to shy away from. Shell-Shock, or as the modern "news" media has ordered you to call it "post traumatic stress disorder," and the terrifying physical and psychological effects it can have on these young men that our "leaders" send half way around the world. You watch as the humanity of these young men is completely burned away as they become hardened killers, despite the desire to just leave and go home.
One character for example, goes from a happy go lucky jokester,  to having a near breakdown from the consequences of his, and more importantly YOUR, actions. This may sound difficult for a game to pull off in a believable manner, and that's because it is. Most writers would have dropped the ball on this subject so hard the ball would have fallen right though the crust and mantle of the Earth. But Spec Ops handles this very smoothly and paces his evolution (or devolutions, depends on how you view it) in a way that it feels very organic and genuine.
I would absolutely recommend this game to anyone looking for a well told story about the horrors of war.
This game has one of the best stories you will ever come across in gaming. Do not pass this up.

As an Early Access Review, this will be subjected to change and editing as newer updates are released.
Prison Architect is a 2D top down prison building and management simulation game made by Introversion Software being financed by crowd-funding, pre-orders and Steam Early Access. Since it's initial release on 2012, the game has undergone several major updates (an average of 4 weeks per update) and has raised nearly $10 Million in revenue.
The player takes on the role of a Prison owner, architect and governor who's objective is to create a prison from an expandable open world map. The player may choose the purpose of their prison either focused on reforming criminals, severe draconian punishment, or a mix of the two. Build the prison from scratch, hire guards and officers, staff and maintenance crew to keep it functioning, dog patrols to keep watch and many more. There is no end to the game, the player just needs to keep building and keep expanding until they decide to sell their prison and build a new one, or, have it burned to the ground because of a riot and find yourself in prison (seriously, your character can go to jail if you're grossly negligent in its management, ironically, in the same prison you built).
+ Great 2D Art Style
+ Good Tutorial: Comprehensive and easy to understand
+ Vast variety of Characters (Staff, Officers, Prisoners, Guards etc)
+ Expanding World Map: (Buy the adjacent lot to expand)
+ Detailed Micromanagement System (Prisoner Regime, Guard/Dog Patrols, lock downs etc.)
+ Detailed Construction System (Buildings, water systems, electrical wiring, computer controls etc.)
+ Easy to install and uninstall MODS (Steam Workshop)
+
+ Old Computer friendly
+ High Replayability
- Severe Performance Drop when the prison becomes very large (in size, prisoner and staff)
- Lacking in Soundtracks
- Occasional path-finding problems
- No main menu (minor annoyance and not a deal breaker)
- No Steam Cloud Support
- Prisoners are released Naked sometimes
GREAT EARLY ACCESS GAME. Prison Architect is what all Early Access games should try to be; it has constant updates, great art style, solid core gameplay, stable & playable and most importantly, easy on the pocket even at full price.
MUST TRY, whether the game is at full price or sale, it's worth every penny and I fully RECOMMEND it specially if your a City Building / Simulation fan. To be honest, the game is technically finished in my opinion (just need a bit more bug fixing and performance improvements) and has more features than some of the other fully released games I've seen.

+++ Classes and traits that actually do stuff. Are you tired of upgrades and skills that just add % modifiers and generic bonuses? The trait system in this game actually affects gameplay in a meaningful way, whether its vertigo flipping the screen upside-down, or runes that let you fly. They also threw in generic bonuses. But ya' know.
++ Satisfying kills. When you hit or kill an enemy, it'll just feel plain good.
++ Remix bosses. Its like playing dark souls, if the bosses in dark souls were optional, on a 2d platformer, and had weaker forms (The actual bosses). If you're not looking for a hardcore, half-impossible experience, you can just ignore them altogether and its still an awesome game.
++ Procedurally generated. Randomness is the spice of life.
+ Nice music. Always good to have.
+ No penalty for death. If you're like me and have biophobia (the fear of life), then you'll be golden.
Cons
--- The controls. Default controls for keyboard are simply terrible. There's just no way to sugarcoat it. I spent the better part of my first hour playing constantly readjusting them. BUT. But there is an option of using a controller, and many people (I haven't used one) say that it is a lot better. Don't worry too much if you don't have a controller, a keyboard worked well for me.
I'm not going to tell you that
should buy this game. If you don't like roguelikes or if you have a burning hatred of platformers, then this game isn't for you. It can be played casually or not, so it covers most people on that front. Its a hack 'n slash at heart, featuring dungeon crawling and lucrative chests. It has "fairy chests" which require you to complete a specific goal before they can be opened, and they contain a rune which can be applied to give your character special powers and buffs.
I just realized I didn't even talk about one of the core mechanics, children. When you die, your current hero will be gone forever, but thankfully 3 of his children will be nominated to take his place. You can pick any one of them to wander off into the castle and risk their lives for treasure (Sorry, but it turns out momma did pick favorites!). These 3 children are of a random class, granted you've unlocked that class, and have 0-2 random traits. Each class differs in stats, and each has a unique "special" ability that can avoid damage, clear a room, etc. Traits will affect gameplay in various ways. Some are very helpful, others can be harmful, and some can be good in some situations, while terrible in others.
I would keep rambling about how great this game is, but if you've made it this far in the review, then you're obviously interested in the game and should just buy it already. You know you want to.

A game that places you in unforgiveable situations, and forces you to make decisions - extreme decisions about who lives and who dies - as though you were in the character's shoes. These decisions are not easy by any means, and what makes them much more intense is the fact that they have to be made rather quickly, before the opportunity is missed.
This game is not just about domination and achieving personal satisfaction by becoming a 'hero', but instead it involves the dramatic and difficult side to war - the emotional and intense side.
This game is unique, not because of its game-play, but highly due to its incredible storyline. Game-play is amazing, but for me, the storyline is the decisive factor that entertains me greatly. After just recently completing the game, all that's left in me is the continuous debate between the decisions I've made compared to the decisions I could have made.
Overall, I highly recommend this game. It's unique - literally.

This game is truly one you will never forget.
There are a couple of aspects about this game, some are generic and familiar (like the gameplay, if you think Gears of War you've pretty much got the picture drawn for you), while others are not generic, like the storyline.
We begin with the gameplay, which is actually very simple. A third-person, over-the-shoulder view. In the game you take cover, you shoot blindly or get up from your cover to shoot , and then move to a different cover. If one just goes all-out, you will be dead pretty quick, this game takes a little thinking and a wee bit of patience. Also, since the game is set in a post-cataclysmic Dubai, there is sand everywhere, including on top of buildings that have huge windows. Shoot these windows and watch the tons an tons of sand crush your enemies (even though you don't get the chance to do it that many times).
The storyline is the driving force of this game, without it, it's not pleasant to get through some levels (in my opinion). This is one of the few games that will make you feel as if your brain was deep-fried, frozen, then smashed into little shards with a hammer. Seriously, this game is not for those who get shocked easily. It is gruesome, disturbing, and appalling. But at the same time, it has a feeling of serenity, ever so faint.
It is an amazing game. Definitely worth the money, go buy it.

Rogue Legacy is a very addictive very fun game made in the tradition of Metroidvania 2-D style games. It offers a wide variety of monsters to fight each with their own creative way of trying to kill you. And you will die... a lot. With each death you get to select a new "heir" from three options each with different abilities which can either help you or give you a lot of extra challange or just change the way the map looks.
As you progress you'll earn gold to upgrade your stats (which are not lost on death) and even unlock new character types from the standard mage to the less standard ninja.
What I really enjoy is that the creators didn't take themselves overly seriously. They were serious enough to make a game that is fun, but with gleefully silly nature that makes me smile when I play it.
I'm put in mind of Broforce a lot because you can get through a run in either game pretty quickly which is great if you have 15 minutes you want to kill and not commit to a game that demands hours. Though in both games I have spent hours playing it...
Bottom line, it's a fun game to play at your leisure. If it comes up on sale, pick it up and enjoy.

As an Early Access Review, this will be subjected to change and editing as newer updates are released.
Prison Architect is a 2D top down prison building and management simulation game made by Introversion Software being financed by crowd-funding, pre-orders and Steam Early Access. Since it's initial release on 2012, the game has undergone several major updates (an average of 4 weeks per update) and has raised nearly $10 Million in revenue.
The player takes on the role of a Prison owner, architect and governor who's objective is to create a prison from an expandable open world map. The player may choose the purpose of their prison either focused on reforming criminals, severe draconian punishment, or a mix of the two. Build the prison from scratch, hire guards and officers, staff and maintenance crew to keep it functioning, dog patrols to keep watch and many more. There is no end to the game, the player just needs to keep building and keep expanding until they decide to sell their prison and build a new one, or, have it burned to the ground because of a riot and find yourself in prison (seriously, your character can go to jail if you're grossly negligent in its management, ironically, in the same prison you built).
+ Great 2D Art Style
+ Good Tutorial: Comprehensive and easy to understand
+ Vast variety of Characters (Staff, Officers, Prisoners, Guards etc)
+ Expanding World Map: (Buy the adjacent lot to expand)
+ Detailed Micromanagement System (Prisoner Regime, Guard/Dog Patrols, lock downs etc.)
+ Detailed Construction System (Buildings, water systems, electrical wiring, computer controls etc.)
+ Easy to install and uninstall MODS (Steam Workshop)
+
+ Old Computer friendly
+ High Replayability
- Severe Performance Drop when the prison becomes very large (in size, prisoner and staff)
- Lacking in Soundtracks
- Occasional path-finding problems
- No main menu (minor annoyance and not a deal breaker)
- No Steam Cloud Support
- Prisoners are released Naked sometimes
GREAT EARLY ACCESS GAME. Prison Architect is what all Early Access games should try to be; it has constant updates, great art style, solid core gameplay, stable & playable and most importantly, easy on the pocket even at full price.
MUST TRY, whether the game is at full price or sale, it's worth every penny and I fully RECOMMEND it specially if your a City Building / Simulation fan. To be honest, the game is technically finished in my opinion (just need a bit more bug fixing and performance improvements) and has more features than some of the other fully released games I've seen.

Mad Max is an sandbox game set in the wasteland of endless expanse of desert, crazy war boys who think they can tangle with Max himself, and cars, lots and lots of cars.
he meat of the game comes in two different forms, Car combat and Ground combat. The latter of the two is not very interesting as such since it is a Batman clone that utilizes an attack/parry system with a few other gimmicks to attempt to keep it fresh.The car combat is seemingly better and has a easy to learn but difficult to master style that mainly utilizes collision and ranged weaponry.
The story is servicable if not predictable but entirely suits the Mad Max character as well as his environment.
The biggest problem with Mad Max, in my opinion, is the amount of stuff to do. There is simply too much and they usually seem all too similar to become invested in what you're doing when all you simply want is an upgrade to your car yet despite feeling like a challenge it feels more like a chore especially later in the game.
I do recommend Mad Max if you're a fan of Mad Max since it captures the movies so authentically or if you just like the idea of driving your vehicle through a sandy wasteland. It is a good game and I rarely ran into any bugs. It is imperative, however, to understand that the game is not without it's faults.

This game is half truck building empire and half jam session, as there are many great radio streams to choose from in multiple languages. I can highly recommend this game as it's very engrossing and can take up hours of your time as you slowly but surely build up your business into a money making machine. Here are two short lists of things I enjoyed and some of the annoying aspects of the game:
PROS
- Open world that is beautifully designed and has realistic day/night cycles
- Excellent radio music variety
- Many different truck companies to buy from (Man, DAF, Scania, Majestic, etc.) with a vast array of truck models
- A huge pool of potential truck driving applicants with unique profiles to expand your company's labor force
- A great array of companies to accept jobs from and a good variety of different cargo to carry
- Challenging and engaging, not only in the business aspect of growing your company, but also in requiring driving skill to deliver cargo from point A to B without damaging your cargo
- Dozens of cities in multiple countries to discover and expand into
- Plenty of aesthetic and mechanical improvements to upgrade your truck(s)
- Devs are very invested with offering players new expansions and constantly improving the gaming experience
CONS
- Speeding cameras EVERYWHERE...and 550.00 fine every time you run through them
- Commuters on the road who drive terribly and will likely run into you or just brake unexpectedly (somehow always your fault). 450.00 fine each time.
- Every city looks, more or less, exactly the same. There is not much differentiation and landmarks aren't all that prevalent.
- This game requires a lot of patience and can get tiresome taking long trips across Europe staring at mile after mile of road.
All things considered though, the game is an excellent addition to the Game Library and I will expect it will continue to grow and develop as time goes on.

Rogue Legacy is a 2D action game with platforming elements and a fantasy setting. I personally dislike platformers, but to dub this title as a simple platformer would be grossly incorrect. Anyone who has played the classic "Castlevania: Symphony of the Night" will instantly be drawn into Rogue Legacy.
I advise you check out the trailer to see if this game is for you. If you're still uncertain, here are some of it's finer points:
The idea of perma-death might scare some people off. Typical "rogue-like" games result in the game ending once the player dies. True to the name, however, Rogue Legacy allows you to effectively continue using the next family member in line with the same gear and attritbutes. Each family member is different (and randomized) which means you could have a warrior with irritable bowel syndrome or a wizard with color blindness. Some of these traits go from purely cosmetic to entirely game changing.
The game seems to go on sale frequently, so add it to your wishlist!

Most underrated game of 2015? possibly
Many a gaming site gave poor old Mad Max a bit of a tanning when it came out, calling it repetitive, boring and derivative.  As such, I wasn’t really excited for it, and only picked it up on sale because I have been a huge fan of the films for many years and couldn’t get over how awesome Fury Road was.  However, I was really glad to find out that the critics got this one wrong.
First off, if this is boring, repetitive and derivative, its no more so than Shadows of More Door or any of the Arkham or recent Asscreed games.  Also, unlike Arkham Knight, this actually runs at more than 5fps.
Mad Max the game is a bit of a contrast to Mad Max the movies.  Game Max is a sort of wastleand Captain America who goes around helping people, giving water to thirsty drifters and brawling like a part-time UFC fighter, nothing like the tormented and twisted survivor of the films.  You also spend alot of time DESTROYING oil pumps, the most valuable thing in the wastleland.  But put that aside, and you'll find a brilliant, open worldy game that is most fun when you make you're own fun.
Story missions are just glorified excuses to obtain upgrades for your car.  Mad Max is at its best and most immersive when you go off rails and just explore.  Avalanche have given us one of the most beautiful game worlds (perfectly optimized for pc) i can think of in their stunning rendition of the wastleland, from the burnt-out buildings and sweeping dunes to the ramshackle monstrosities of the settlements.  You spend most of the game in your customizeable car, and its a real joy to both drive around and see whats cookin' or to engage in the exhilirating car combat, which does actually nail the feel of the movies dead on and gives you a lot of fun toys to play with.  Taking on convoys is the highlight of the game for me, without doubt.  There's also some interesting underground sections too, which are a nice change of pace.
When not in the car, you raid settlements, sabotage oil pumps, and generally have a jolly time biffing people in the face.  While many said the combat was awful, I loved ever minute I was ramming fists into mouths.  Mad Max's fisticuffs is heavily based on the very familiar Arkham system, but it work by giving you so much more control over what you are doing, with light and heavy attacks, combo finishers, weapons (THUNDERSTICKS!!!) and ability to get Max's shotgun into the mix.  Even sometimes Max loses his rag and starts drop kicking and suplexing mofos.  Seriously, once you've unlocked enough moves combat is just as good as the Batman games and definitely better than Asscreed.  Like I mentioned before, the fighting doesn't fit in well with the Max of the movies, but when you're ramming a thunderstick (grenade on a spear) into someones gut amd kicking him into a mob of bald gimps just before he explodes, do you really care that much?
What I enjopy most about Mad Max is just how immersive it is.  The world is so graphically captivating that it was just a real pleasure to exist there.  Sometimes I'm on the hunt for convoys, sometimes I'm lookin for a spot of fisticuffs, sometimes i'm doing insane jumps off ramps, sometimes i'm taking part in death races,  sometimes I'm just driving around to see what there is.  And with some many things to do and most of the gameworld unlocked after the tutorials section. you're free to explore at you're leisure and jus do whatever the hell you want.  If only this had multiplayer...
It’s not a perfect game by any means. The controls mess you up occasionally, you can only climb objects painted yellow, and there's a fair bit of grinding to do to upgrade your car.  The thing that really got my goat was when the game sends random enemies/storms at you at the worst moments.  Maybe I'm waiting to ambush a convoy and a lightning storm comes along and zaps me to cinders, or maybe I've just wrecked that convoy, no armour left, and a random bunch of war boys appear right behind me and smah me into oblivion.  Or how about the fact that all the bosses look and fight EXACTLY the same?
But all its faults are negligible in my opinion, as the experience of Mad Max as a whole was very enjoyable and immersing. Don’t like these big AAA console games?  Max ain’t gonna change your mind, sweetheart, but if you do like the Arkham/Mordor/Asscreed thing and fancy a wee bit of insane car combat in the mix, Mad Max is worth a try.

Rogue Legacy is a 2D action game with platforming elements and a fantasy setting. I personally dislike platformers, but to dub this title as a simple platformer would be grossly incorrect. Anyone who has played the classic "Castlevania: Symphony of the Night" will instantly be drawn into Rogue Legacy.
I advise you check out the trailer to see if this game is for you. If you're still uncertain, here are some of it's finer points:
The idea of perma-death might scare some people off. Typical "rogue-like" games result in the game ending once the player dies. True to the name, however, Rogue Legacy allows you to effectively continue using the next family member in line with the same gear and attritbutes. Each family member is different (and randomized) which means you could have a warrior with irritable bowel syndrome or a wizard with color blindness. Some of these traits go from purely cosmetic to entirely game changing.
The game seems to go on sale frequently, so add it to your wishlist!

I've held off from writing a review for this game until most of the bugs have been fixed, there are still a few bugs but none are gamebreaking in my opinion.
The game is really beautiful, the areas are rendered wonderfully well. It also runs great, even on minimum spec systems, with plenty of options to be tweaked in the graphic settings.
If you own a decent spec system (my system is a haswell i5 @ 3.8ghz and a gtx 1080) you can maximise the graphics and even run in enhanced resolution (dsr). I run this game at 1600p and it's stunning and maintains between 45 and 55 fps :)
The hunting is fun and rewarding. You start off with a basic .243 rifle and basic ammo. As you harvest animals you get a monetary reward, xp and a score towards your weapon class.
As you level your weapon class this enables new ammunition and weapon types to be unlocked, which are paid for by your in game cash.
Xp goes towards levelling your character. For each level, up to about level 36, you get either a skill point, or perk point to spend.
Skill points are spent towards things like tracking and spotting, using scents etc.
Perk points are spent in your weapon trees, to improve things like breath control.
All these "upgrades" to your character make perfect sense, after all the more you use a rifle the better you'll get with the weapon.
There are four trees for your perk points, a tree for each weapon type.
Rifles, Bows, Handguns and Shotguns.
This enables you to customise your spec to whatever you get the most enjoyment from using. For me it's bows!
The actual hunting is great fun, the tracking system works really well and is better (imho) than in classic hunter.
There are two areas to hunt in this game and they are huge with more areas promised as dlc.
This game is well worth buying and is gradually getting better, as bugs are ironed out.
UPDATE.
I'm updating my review to include recently released dlc.
Two dlc's have been released, dlc 1 is tents and ground blinds dlc.
This DLC cost £3.99 and for that you get 5 tents and 5 Ground blinds, plus further tents and blinds can be bought for in game cash after purchase of the dlc.
My opinion of this is it offers terrific value for money and opens up new areas of the map that were previously rarely hunted, especially when combined with DLC 2.
DLC 2 is ATV's and the cost is £1.87
The atv is great fun to drive and makes accessing far flung areas a breeze.
You can drive then drop a tent enabling you to spawn in at that area for future hunts.
Both of these DLC's are not vital to enjoy the game, but they add a trememndous amount to it and are a no brainer for me!
A poll is currently in process to find out what the users of the game would like in future updates, with extra animals, weapons and new reserves on the list.
As more and more bugs are ironed out and with the devs commitment to this title, this game is going from strength to strength :)

This is the most beautiful game I have played in some time. I would say that the game is quite modestly priced for what it provides, but it is clearly a hunting experience more than a hunting game - so it's not going to be a game for everyone.
Most of the negative reviews I see claim "bugs" for what is actually how ballistics work in the real world. Example: lower calibre headshots will often not kill an animal. Many of the animals use their heads for fighting for goodness sake! I have (in real life) shot goats in the head and have the animal up and leave. The skull on many animals is very thick and therefore you're aiming for the heart/lungs.
- The Skill/Perk/XP/Points system is insane. Obviously, this is a leftover from the game having P2W/F2P mechanics which I am glad they dropped. But it's left us with a pretty terrible and confusing system that is incredibly convoluted. It doesn't rise to the point of a negative reivew, but it's close for me.
- Multiplayer is a little buggy at times. Not overly so, and it's been acknowledged by the devs and they're clearlying targeting patches to this. It's still very playable and enjoyable.
- The range of weapons available is pretty low.
- The amount of equipment available to upgrade you weapons was much lower than I was expecting. While some of this would be quite "game-y", I was expecting being able to customize your weapons and equipment more according to how you wanted to play.
+ The game is the most beautiful game I have played a in a long time, hands down. They're using dynamic color grading, volumetric lights, dynamic shadows... I mean just everything and the results are superb!
+ The map(s) are staggering in their scale and attention to detail. They're hand made and they are huge. Much bigger than ArmA.
+ The performance of the game on a high-end PC is excellent. Don't expect to run at ULTRA on current gen hardware, and don't be mad about that! The game is made in such a way that it's going to grow with hardware and that's great.
+ The pacing of the game is really superb. It strikes an excellent balance between requiring patience and keeping something happening to the player.
+ Post kill review screen. You see the pose, entry, and damage modelling for what you killed. Absolutely amazing and makes your kill "story" fantastic.
+ Tracking is exciting and the classic "easy to do hard to master". This is a well designed mechanic that leads to excellent pacing.
If you are looking for an arcade game, this is not for you. But if you are looking for a hunting game this is a fantastic find. Even better with friends! It's modest price is worth is alone for how beautiful the terrain is to explore.

The game is fairly well descirbed by the trailers and "about" text above so I'll skip what's there already.  Rogue legacy is an absolutely fantastic and addictive game.
The controls are tight and responsive as they need to be for a game of this nature.  They can be just a bit twitchy at times and fine control can take some practice.  The gameplay is difficult and occasionally frustrating, but in a fun way.
The music is superb.  It adds just the right atmosphere without being so imposing that it gets old.  I've heard the intro to the main castle music probably 500 times and it still brings a smaile to my face.
The character traits offer a lot of diversity and the random dungeon layouts allow the player to experience the unfamiliar exploration phase of the game every life (unless they buy an upgrade that will let them keep the immediately prior layout for a large fraction of the next run-through's gold).  I don't normally like the game mechanic of grinding for randomized loot, but the way it's integrated into Rogue Legacy makes it a charming and goofy quirk of the game's premise rather than just a rule that forces you to grind for grinding's sake as it is usually emplyed in games.  That is a feat.
Bottom Line:  Rogue Legacy is just plain fun.  It's on par with the best of the sidescrollers of the 8- and 16-bit eras while being fresh and quirky in its own way.

However, after playing this game, I think it's clear that Cellar Door Games has absolutely no understanding of level design whatsoever. Levels are specifically made to cause harm to the player in ways that are near impossible to avoid, whether it be putting an enemy or trap at the immediate start of the room so you run into it and take damage, or over-the-top platforming over obstacles to get to your objectives. Unfortunately, this makes the game very luck-based and difficult to play.
Game design is very poor. Enemy's have flawed movement, occasionally just running through walls, or suddenly jumping or moving back when they shouldn't. Projectiles sometimes clip through walls when they shouldn't. Spell physics don't make sense, which also makes spells almost completely useless.
All in all, these things seem to make the game a very poor experience. While the game may be fun to a few people, I just wouldn't recommend it to anyone to play unless they are extremely dedicated and can ignore all the things that pull this game down. If you're going to buy this anyway, I highly recommend you wait for a sale before buying.

I want to like this game, but almost everything about it is boring.
If you think I'm going to nag at this game just to raise attention, please know that I played all the way through the original, and loved it. It had a kind of novelty, mystery, and foreboding doom that made me totally interested. Max's time travel mechanics brought some interesting puzzle mechanics to the whole experience, along with the intense stuff that would happen. The game made me cry, and has definitely left an impact on me.
Life is Strange: Before the Storm seems to lack the sense of mystery and foreboding doom that I mentioned. This is a prequel, which means that, unless some crazy new story element is introduced, you know what's going to happen. A game like this depends on excellent writing and characters. I thought it sounded neat before I actually got to play it, but treading through the same places I was at in the original game without any real supernatural thing happening makes me feel like nothing. It's plot with a real narrative.
By the end of episode 2, I was already an emotional wreck over what had happened to that character, how powerless I felt even with the supernatural ability I was given. This made me want to continue on until the end. This feeling of being powerless, but hoping that you can somehow find a way to makes things right. The ending of the original could have been a lot better, but this idea of hope and helplessness made Life is Strange unique.
In LiS: BtS, after episode 2, I don't feel anything similar to what I felt after ep 2 of the original. It just feels like a regular high school drama. I don't feel quite as invested in saving Rachel, because I know she's going to die. Unless they pull a time paradox or something of the like, I can't see this prequel being saved. The twist, if you can even call it that, at the end of ep 2 doesn't stack up to the emotional roller coaster of the original.
The Chloe in the prequel doesn't even equate to me to Chloe in the original. She sounds fine, but she feels oddly different. Maybe it's because she's younger, but something about it just doesn't feel like Chloe. Maybe I'm nitpicking, but it's certainly something to akcnowledge.
What you do gameplay-wise isn't even very interesting. I don't remember the original being like this. I don't remember it being like you just looking around, maybe solving some fairly simple puzzles, and then going to the indicator of plot progression. Instead of filling the game with filler that isn't even fun, even cringy sometimes, have almost everything be focused on narrative progression. I don't feel like there's a narrative here. It's just Chloe and Rachel's friendship or relationship depending on which you choose. This game feels like fanservice.
If you're into fanservice, have at it. If you want to see Chloe and Rachel kissing, it's in here. tbh that isn't much of a spoiler, since this game is fanservice. And yeah, the kissing is really nice. Their friendship is really nice, but it just gets boring, at least to me, after a while. I appreciate and want diversity in games, but just because you have all of the LGBTQ+ folk, and people of color, that doesn't mean that your game deserves universal praise. If your game centers on plot and narrative, get good writers who know how to create interesting conflict and resolution, along with great characters.

This game is a very, very good game. I bought it for $5 during a Steam Winter Sale. I didn't expect anything major. Boy was I wrong. I'd argue that this is one of my favorite RPGs ever. I did a Neutral Run where no one died first, and then went back and completed the True Pacifist route, and I will NEVER do a Genocide Run. I can't bring myself to kill anybody in this game. Anyway, I'll give what I liked and didn't like:
Pros:
* Likeable unique characters. Almost every major character is likeable and unique in their own way. From motherly, loving Toriel, to goofball slacker Sans, to equally goofy cool guy Papyrus, to aggressive(ly nice) Undyne, to nerdy goofball Alphys, to flamboyant self-important Mettaton, to kindly king Asgore. Heck, Flowey is kinda like able, even though he's pretty twisted.
* Wonderful story. Every ounce of the story makes me emotional, whether it's funny, sad, cute, or kinda scary. I don't want to spoil any thing, but it's great.
*The monster design of even the generic monsters is great. You can feel detail and heart went into making each enemy feel different.
* The graphical design is pretty nice. I would say it almost perfectly replicates the 16-bit stylization of Earthbound, but also manages to have its own unique feel. Every room of the game feels different than the last.
*Turning some of the main RPG tropes on their heads is impressive. I'm suprised there hasn't been a Triple-A game to do some of the things this game does.
Cons:
*The combat is very hard if you aren't used to 'bullet hell' games. I haven't played any in that genre, and I'm not the fastest-coordinated person, so most of the bosses were somewhat difficult, especially Undyne, Mettaton EX, and Asgore. Then again, it's part of what makes Undertale unique.
*HP is really low the whole game if you run pacifist. Because HP only increases by increasing LV. LV only increases by gaining EXP. EXP is gained by... killing monsters. Not sparing them. There are healing items in the shops, but shops can be very hard to find. Not only that, but you need to have more gold. And the player receives more gold when they... kill a monster, than if they spare them. Yeah...
All and all, I'd say about 9/10, a really great game. I would definitely recommend buying it, but if you're not into bullet hell games, you might just YouTube it. Definitely worth experiencing though.
