Borderlands 2:
+ Interesting and unique visuals for the game. It's very artistic and cartoonish in appearance, which is refreshing. I can appreciate this style of graphics, even though I believe the more conventional approach is still more aesthetically pleasing.
+ Each character in Borderlands 2 is intriguing and memorable, which is important in this sort of game.
+ Borderlands 2 challenges you with semi-difficult boss fights and general combat. You'll die several times, but you're always able to overcome the challenge, which is great.
+ There's many side quests and main missions to complete in this game, so there's quite a lot of content to enjoy.
+ Open world exploration.
+ Co-op game mode to play with friends.
~ The humour in this game can be quite childish. So if you're a mature person it won't appeal to you. That being said, the other half of the humour is clever, witty and funny. In that respect, it's good.
~ Combat can be fun at times, but not always. Sometimes it's just frustrating. Enemies can have insane amounts of health or respawn CONSTANTLY and it feels more like a spam clicking FPS game than anything balanced or realistic. As a result it can get repetitive and dull, but at other moments it really stands out and is enjoyable.
-The RPG element of this game isn't well cultivated. To be honest, there isn't a good reason to call it an RPG. When you level up you get to pick a new skill to invest points in, but that's it. None of the skills available are very creative, in fact they are more like buffs to your character instead of skills. Playing as a gunzerker class, there's the choice to "increase gun accuracy", "increase critical damage" or "increase reload time", among other options, pretty standard and uninventive. I don't feel as if levelling up provides a really good advantage like it should. Most RPG games are much more in-depth with levelling and give your character practical benefits.
- Character dialogue often overlaps with combat at inconvenient times. This means you miss out on part of quest storylines, because you're too busy desperately defending yourself from being killed. This was poorly thought-out.
- Excessive DLC which should have been featured in the main game. There's a lot of additional content to buy and expand your gameplay, but too much in my opinion. Adding this to the main game would have made it epic and there's no doubt it would score higher.
Overall Score: 7.5/10

is a combat racing and beat'em up adventure game. Having lost the Black-on-Black Interceptor to Immortan Joe's son Scrotus, the Road Warrior known as Max teams up with a blackfinger called Chumbucket, who sees Max as the Holy Driver that will help him build the greatest car the Great White has ever seen: the Magnum Opus.
: The story is bitter, as a Mad Max story should be: you aren't a hero, you a survivor that cares for no one, grudgingly making uneasy alliances strictly if it benefits you. The game seeks to be a love-letter to the post-apocalyptic franchise all other games, from
to
, were inspired from. The landscape is much more varied than you'd expect from a desert, including volcanic sulfur pits, pearl-white sea beds, rocky canyons, black sludge marshes, even storms go from windy sandstorms to thunderstorm hurricanes, making sure each regions has an atmosphere of its own. The car combat mechanics are excellent, while the hand-to-hand combat is a brutal but instantly recognizable game of block, hit, parry and combo. Car customization is pretty sweet, some upgrades go without saying while others require you to balance speed and strength to fit your play style.
: The game lacks interactions, you may only speak to characters (which are pretty few) when there's a main or sidequest available, with the exception of the occasional encounter with scavengers. Many world objectives are repetitive, and camp bosses are simple reskins of each other, the level design being the only difference you'll find from one camp or convoy to another. There is no personal customization except for beard, the rest being straightforward upgrades. If you don't bother with lowering threat levels, completing Death Races or collecting cars, you will find the game to be extremely short.

A much more interesting take on prison environment than Prison Tycoon, Prison Architect takes all of the aspects one would expect to be involved in both building and maintaining a prison, and mashes them all together in a neat top-down strategy game for all to enjoy. For a game still locked in its Alpha stages, it has shown to me immense potential simply as that, an Alpha. It is an amazing game already, and for them to say "we aren't finished, there is more to come!" is astounding.
Beyond that, the team behind the game introduces a very strong sense of community, offering a number of rewards based on how much you contribute to the game, up to and including being able to design some of the main characters for the future full release, and even including your own, personalized character in-game.
I would definitely recommend this game even to people who are not exactly complete fans of strategy games, as it has a hint of roleplaying in it as well!

This is not a review of the gameplay or mechanics. This review is my personal story and experience with DayZ.
Back in 2011, I saw one video about a mod called ''DayZ". I, like so many others, was instantly hooked and inspired by the concept. The idea that literally anything could end up happening to you, and that every single interaction with another player would be completely unique sold me on the spot.
I became completely obsessed with the game. I watched endless videos of it, I became a very active member of the official forums, I bought a gaming rig (I had planned on it anyway) and Arma II just for the purpose of playing the DayZ mod. I remember being so excited for every possible update or snippet of news about the mod, and played it religiously.
Then the word hit that the mod was going to get a full release.
Holy ♥♥♥♥. I couldn't wait. I have over a thousand posts on the official forums, 90% of which are discussing and hyping for the full game. There were delays after delays, but we didn't mind. We had faith in Rocket and the team. I almost felt like I knew them from how active they were on the forums.
When the game finally dropped, in its alpha glory, I bought it, £20 on the spot. One of the only times I've paid full price for a game on Steam. I booted it up and it was a complete buggy mess. It barely launched on my rig. I didn't mind, I had faith in Rocket and the team that updates would be regular and I was happy to wait, playing the game and helping perfect it as much as I could.
This was as high as my hopes ever got.
Within 6 months, there had been minimal changes and updates. The game still barely ran. I didn't mind. I was still patiently waiting for the game to get perfected. Rocket wouldn't let us down, right?
Rocket left the team around that time, if I remember right. This was when the penny started to drop for me. Rocket leaving truly shocked me. He was spearheading the project from the beginning and I had placed all my faith in him to make what I had considered to be my perfect game.
Then the news of a PS4 release came. The fact that they were using our money to fund a project that the absolutely dedicated fanbase had paid for in entirety and would benefit nothing from frustrated me.
After that, I stopped following the game. I don't visit the forums, but I expect they're barren now.
At this point, I rarely play the Alpha. I boot it up from time to time, hoping that something has been done.
And now, 4 years after launch, the game is still a total buggy broken mess. My disappointment is now replaced with feelings of frustration. The only conclusion that I can make from this entire debacle is that DayZ is either a scam designed to hoodwink hopeful gamers into buying it on concept alone, or a project that was completely doomed from the start with a deluded team working behind it.
What hurts most is the potential this game had. It could have been completely groundbreaking. And worse yet, it gave way to a slew of unfinished zombie survival games that will never come close to achieving what this concept could be. That's the real tragedy. That DayZ got in first, and a competent, dedicated development team didn't.
Either way, don't buy it. It will never be finished and is a total waste of your time.

The voice acting in particular has an unusual twist to it, as the various things you and your squad mates call out in combat become more and more desperate as the game progresses and the squad finds itself more and more over its head.
If you don't mind gameplay that's nothing new, and a story that's so dark that it ultimately leads to a game that's compelling without actually being any

What starts off an incredibly generic war game, with some less than tight controls, transforms into a look at the horrors of war.  This is not Call of Duty, this is not Battlefield, this is not a medal of honor.  This is not a "war is hell, but not this one!" type of game.  This is a game that tries to show the dark, depressing side of war.  It throws you in, and does not cover your eyes.  Spec Ops:  The line demands a mature audience to play it, for it deals with things that should not be approached by someone not mature enough to understand the messages it is trying to convey.
What makes Spec Ops: The line special is that it's not dark, just to be dark.  You get the feeling that the deveopers knew from the first day of development where they wanted the story to go, and they commited to telling a story of the evils of war, and the stresses it puts on the human body.  I literaly had to stop playing after one level, because I had committed an atrocity that I could not have forseen.  The aftermath was handled well, not heave handed or obvious.  It showed me what my decision had cost me, but did not outright tell me.  This game is wel worth any sale price, just for the experience.

This is yet another take on the Rogue-like genre. The twist here is that while death is permanent, the gold you collect is used to upgrade your castle, giving subsequent lives stat boosts and new jobs.
The gameplay is a Castlevania-esque action platformer. You have a basic melee attack, a few movement skills limited by the last time you touched the ground, and special attacks that deplete an MP bar.
Like many Rogue-likes, this is not a game that expects to be beaten. Which bosses you have killed do save in between trips to the castle, but every upgrade you buy increases the costs of subsequent upgrades across the entire tech tree. Everything in the game is incredibly deadly, with lots of projectile attacks and collision damage to watch out for. You need good reflexes and dodging skills if you want to survive without copious grinding.
If you like Rogue-likes (i.e. don't mind failing a lot) and enjoy Castlevania-style gamplay, this is an easy recommendation. The upgrade system is a nice twist on the Rogue-like formula, but it doesn't make the game any more forgiving overall. Be sure to use a controller.

Picture this; you find a game that makes you cry, it rocks your world, and it has more meaning and power than you could have ever possibly imagined a game having. It's one of those games that you recommend to all your friends, so you can see them get just as emotional as you did, or judge them if they make the "wrong choices."
That's what Life is Strange was to me, and I can say it was that way for a large number of my pals as well. A conversation about that game that lasts more than 10 minutes among my friends... well, the phrase "ugly crying" might fit well here. So when I heard a prequel was being developed, and by somebody other than DONTNOD, I couldn't say I was keen on the idea.
I wasn't sure another game was on the table as a good thing in the first place, Life is Strange created a world so vivid and in-depth, I was wary there was even a possibility that could be recreated, let alone by a different group of people. I feared that a story told from Chloe's perspective might lose the gentle spark Max's personality gave the narrative. But loving the game as I did, I bought into the excitement as any fan would, and hoped dearly for Deck Nine to deliever a good game.
I'm pleased to say that my expectations have been far surpassed. They have done, a spectacular job creating their own game. Before the Storm is it's own brand new narrative, molding lifelike characters and storyline without stepping all over the previously lined up story that DONTNOD created.
While staying true to the original, Deck has enhanced some previously known character's personas, and brought out traits in our dear Arcadia Bay crew that were once glazed over and subtle. They've explored potential in characters that Life is Strange didn't have the time for, and turned it into a artistically faithful addition to the franchise.
The visuals they've chosen to use to convey emotions are evocative, astounding, and genuinely breathtaking, if I thought Life is Strange made me cry.. well... in just the first episode alone, I have cried more than all of said precursor's episodes combined. You've written a beautiful story Deck, I can't wait to play through more.
---------------------------------------
Additional thoughts
The system for inspecting has been changed from dragging the mouse to just pressing W, A, S, D. While this was weird at first, I had far less trouble, I think that was a great control change there.
Chloe's character has been perfectly portrayed in the time period the story is based, I cannot stress how well that has been done, and how much I appreciate the way it's been handled.
Daughter was a phenomenal music choice, and so far the music is stellar in general. I'm thankful that the music has stayed important to emotional aspects of the game the way it has.

What can I say? This game is everything I'd hoped it would be.
You are (surprise surprise) a Prison Architect, you have to design and manage your own prison constantly monitoring your funds and the happiness, safeguarding, and wellbeing of your prisoners.
You can create a fairly vast variety of rooms and buildings and all your builders (that you can hire/fire as you need) will build it from the blueprint bit by bit.
You can choose whether you want to accept low/mid/high risk prisoners to alter the challenge (and reward) for their successsful imprisonment while having to ensure you have enough staff on hand (from security guards to janitors to accountants).
By hiring certain staff members you can unlock various areas of the 'tech tree' where you can research new technologies to better maintain your prison, this is fairly basic in design but unlocks many more customisation options for your prison.
The game even goes in depth enough to customise a prisoner's daily timetable which you can modify to best suit your prison layout, get various grants where you can get initial and end cash rewards for certain tasks, and set patrol routes and security levels around the prison.
What I like about this game is that you feel like you're in control, it's very open ended and there isn't necessarily just one strategy that works (the thing that puts me off with these sort of games is when you can do whatever you want, but only one thing actually works), you can run a prison just as successful being a strict 'no-yard-time' tyrant as you could a leniant 'take as much time you need in the showers' sort of manager. The game is very in depth yet you don't need a highly detailed pre-existing strategy to succeed (although it would help).
I'd give this game:
Creativity - 7/10
Looks - 7/10
Difficulty - 8/10 (Not too hard, little bit of an adaptability curve)
Replayability - 9/10 (One of those games I can see myself returning to when I don't expect it)
Total - 7.75/10

is a combat racing and beat'em up adventure game. Having lost the Black-on-Black Interceptor to Immortan Joe's son Scrotus, the Road Warrior known as Max teams up with a blackfinger called Chumbucket, who sees Max as the Holy Driver that will help him build the greatest car the Great White has ever seen: the Magnum Opus.
: The story is bitter, as a Mad Max story should be: you aren't a hero, you a survivor that cares for no one, grudgingly making uneasy alliances strictly if it benefits you. The game seeks to be a love-letter to the post-apocalyptic franchise all other games, from
to
, were inspired from. The landscape is much more varied than you'd expect from a desert, including volcanic sulfur pits, pearl-white sea beds, rocky canyons, black sludge marshes, even storms go from windy sandstorms to thunderstorm hurricanes, making sure each regions has an atmosphere of its own. The car combat mechanics are excellent, while the hand-to-hand combat is a brutal but instantly recognizable game of block, hit, parry and combo. Car customization is pretty sweet, some upgrades go without saying while others require you to balance speed and strength to fit your play style.
: The game lacks interactions, you may only speak to characters (which are pretty few) when there's a main or sidequest available, with the exception of the occasional encounter with scavengers. Many world objectives are repetitive, and camp bosses are simple reskins of each other, the level design being the only difference you'll find from one camp or convoy to another. There is no personal customization except for beard, the rest being straightforward upgrades. If you don't bother with lowering threat levels, completing Death Races or collecting cars, you will find the game to be extremely short.
: ★★★★☆ - Next on your list!

I have 66 hours or so now and still coming back for more. There has been an update to the game but it didn't really fix any of the bugs/issues I'm having.
- I really like hunting at night. The headlamp doesn't illuminate too much but it's the only way you'll see any tracks. The night sights aren't working very well but will be really fun at night when they do.
- I've been in the middle of a few stampedes which are crazy to experience. I've had them with elk and moose. The elk herd was 30 or so deep and they wouldn't stop coming back until I dropped about 15-20 of them (wish I recorded it). The only thing that kept me alive was by jumping up on a rock so they wouldn't trample me to death. For some reason they took off after killing so many. Not sure exactly why they decided to move on. The stampede sounds like rolling thunder. I originally thought it was a motorcycle outside and took my headphones off a few times to make sure it was the game.

This is not a review of the gameplay or mechanics. This review is my personal story and experience with DayZ.
Back in 2011, I saw one video about a mod called ''DayZ". I, like so many others, was instantly hooked and inspired by the concept. The idea that literally anything could end up happening to you, and that every single interaction with another player would be completely unique sold me on the spot.
I became completely obsessed with the game. I watched endless videos of it, I became a very active member of the official forums, I bought a gaming rig (I had planned on it anyway) and Arma II just for the purpose of playing the DayZ mod. I remember being so excited for every possible update or snippet of news about the mod, and played it religiously.
Then the word hit that the mod was going to get a full release.
Holy ♥♥♥♥. I couldn't wait. I have over a thousand posts on the official forums, 90% of which are discussing and hyping for the full game. There were delays after delays, but we didn't mind. We had faith in Rocket and the team. I almost felt like I knew them from how active they were on the forums.
When the game finally dropped, in its alpha glory, I bought it, £20 on the spot. One of the only times I've paid full price for a game on Steam. I booted it up and it was a complete buggy mess. It barely launched on my rig. I didn't mind, I had faith in Rocket and the team that updates would be regular and I was happy to wait, playing the game and helping perfect it as much as I could.
This was as high as my hopes ever got.
Within 6 months, there had been minimal changes and updates. The game still barely ran. I didn't mind. I was still patiently waiting for the game to get perfected. Rocket wouldn't let us down, right?
Rocket left the team around that time, if I remember right. This was when the penny started to drop for me. Rocket leaving truly shocked me. He was spearheading the project from the beginning and I had placed all my faith in him to make what I had considered to be my perfect game.
Then the news of a PS4 release came. The fact that they were using our money to fund a project that the absolutely dedicated fanbase had paid for in entirety and would benefit nothing from frustrated me.
After that, I stopped following the game. I don't visit the forums, but I expect they're barren now.
At this point, I rarely play the Alpha. I boot it up from time to time, hoping that something has been done.
And now, 4 years after launch, the game is still a total buggy broken mess. My disappointment is now replaced with feelings of frustration. The only conclusion that I can make from this entire debacle is that DayZ is either a scam designed to hoodwink hopeful gamers into buying it on concept alone, or a project that was completely doomed from the start with a deluded team working behind it.
What hurts most is the potential this game had. It could have been completely groundbreaking. And worse yet, it gave way to a slew of unfinished zombie survival games that will never come close to achieving what this concept could be. That's the real tragedy. That DayZ got in first, and a competent, dedicated development team didn't.
Either way, don't buy it. It will never be finished and is a total waste of your time.

Playing this game is rather like watching the proverbial train wreck: you'll be horrified, but you can't look away. This is in no way a bad thing. Spec Ops wants to tell a story about soldiers in war. But unlike games such as Call of Duty, it doesn't want you to feel like an awesome, unstoppable killing machine that's fighting terrorism FOR 'MERICA!!! or whatever; it wants you to see that war is not glamorous, awesome, fun, or desirable. It wants you to see the terrible toll that combat can exact on those who experience it. And above all, it wants you to see that in real conflict, there are no "good guys" and "bad guys," and the world is full of gray areas. War is hell, and anyone who goes in will either join the fortunate dead...or have to live with what they've done to survive.
Spec Ops is a third-person cover-based shooter that alternates between desert environments and crumbling urban ruin. You have two squadmates who can be directed to attack specific targets or heal a fallen comrade; they're pretty good at following orders in a timely fashion and, unlike some other AI partners, they're not highly prone to getting themselves shot constantly or hung up on the level geometry. Enemies are decently clever, more than willing to flank you, toss grenades to get you out of cover, or trick you into walking right into a Heavy Trooper's line of fire.
The game also offers the clever idea of having drifts of sand piled up on fragile surfaces like windows, which you can shoot out to bury your enemies. It doesn't show up that often, but it's kind of neat when it's there.
There's the usual shooter stable of weapons: pistols, heavy pistols, shotguns, sniper rifles, etc. They sound good and feel decently punchy, and aiming is never a problem. Most weapons also have an alternate fire mode, which does add a little depth to the combat.
I didn't play the multiplayer, so I can't honestly review it. I will say the developers originally didn't even want multiplayer, and the campaign is designed well enough to stand on its own, so make of that what you will.
I highly recommend this game. It is a breath of fresh air in an over-crowded genre that's becoming increasingly generic. This game is also visually stunning, with exceptional voice acting, and sound. It is definitely worth the money and the effort to play the game from the beginning to the end.

Like many who've posted reviews I bought this game out of curiosity.  I don't play a lot of shooters and having served in the Marines I don't care for reminders of my military experience.
Spec Ops is a head-***k.  We're used to games with a simplistic dichotomy.  In this game I actually felt guilt for trying to survive.  Part of what makes this dynamic so effective is the excellent voice acting, especially during firefights.  You'll hear the usual jargon of American soldiers shouting to one another in battle but in this case they're shouting in response to your team attacking them.  It screws with your head.  But it also makes you appreciate how we're so accustommed to playing games where enemy soldiers are sensationalized in a way that makes them less human.  With the scary-foreigner dynamic removed you find yourself killing, men.  Guys like you.  Just, on the wrong side.  Or, is it you who's on the wrong side?
This game is definitely worth the ticket.  It can feel a bit slow and tiresome but as others have said, play for the story.  No shame in playing through on Easy just to get through the first half.  And be ready to find a support group to share your feelings with after you complete it.

While I would reccomend this game for the hunting enthusiast, I would caution casual or fast-paced gamers from playing. This game requires A LOT of time and effort to get anything done. Movement is slow, the game is quite demanding on moderate systems, and kills are very few and far between. Just today, I have spent almost four full hours of playing the game and have only managed to kill one deer. Yes, the game looks amazing and is very realistic, but it is certianly not something that the "average gamer" would enjoy. Where other games have long hours of grinding, where you're at least doing SOMETHING, this game has you walking (at an extremely slow pace to keep the animals from getting scared off) for hours on end with little-to-no signs of life for most of that time.
While I commend the developers for making a challenging and realistic game, I would advise them to put options into the game to increase the spawn rate of animals in single player worlds and on multiplayer servers. To spend so much time in the game and get little out of it is not something that people enjoy. The game isn't difficult, it just discourages people playing it because of how little actually happens in the game.

This game is something that I picked up as somewhat of an impulse buy, and for myself it is absolutely worth the money. Absolutely gorgeous visuals, provided you have the hardware to run it, and very nice audio work. I have had a lot of fun playing both on my own and multiplayer with friends. However, the game absolutely does have its issues, which honestly it shouldn't have been released with.
Pros:
-It is one of the more accurate hunting simulators out right now
-Absolutely stunning scenery, water, animal animations, and lighting effects
-The weapons are very satisfying, from the handling (which changes with different scopes, so a larger scope makes the weapon seem heavier) down to the meaty "thunk" of an arrow hitting its mark. All in all it does a much better job with the weapons than most FPSes do.
-Very satisfying payoffs to effort put in. Making a difficult shot, finding a big bull elk after a long stalk, it's all fantastic.
-Quick load times, for both single and multiplayer. The longest load times are generally when switching between reserves.
-Very large maps with nice differences in terrain.
Cons:
-It is a slow paced game. Running generates a lot of noise and that scares the animals right off.
-Depending on the map and location, you may go a long time without seeing an animal at all. Hirschfelden, in particular, seems almost desolate compared to the dense population of animals on Layton Lakes.
-Unrealistic ballistics. If I shoot a deer in the shoulder within 20 meters, I don't care if it hit the shoulder blade first, I guarentee it would go through to the lung. Having a bullet stop short and ending up with a "Flesh Wound, bleed rate Very Low" is infuriating, especially when it seemed like an alright shot.
-Bugs, so many bugs. So many, in fact, that I am going to detail them later, to avoid cluttering the cons list.
-Not a whole lot of content, really. There are six trophy species on each reserve, and that's it. A LOT of content in theHunter Classic is not present in CotW.
-Not well optimized. Even on more powerful rigs, if you're trying to play with settings maxed you're likely going to suffer some frame losses. Trying to play on a lower-end rig is not recommended.
Some more detail on bugs that are present as of this review, as well as some older ones that seem to be fixed as I personally no longer experience them.
-Frequent, inconsistent crashing. I sometimes go hours at a time without any issue, but the very next time I load up the game it crashes every five minutes. Very frustrating.
-Animals in general are quite buggy on occasion, getting stuck on scenery, running in circles, standing completely still even when you approach, not being able to harvest an animal that is right in front of you, and likely some more issues I can't remember right now.
-Walking uphill is incredibly frustrating, as it seems like your character is unable to pick up their feet more than six inches. It is also absurdly easy to slide down a slope on accident.
-When fast-travelling to a location in multiplayer, if another player was standing in that location it would cause both players to die from, what seems to be, fall damage.
-If an animal is harvested while photo mode is active, the cursor will not be visible and it is very hard to 'confirm' the kill to get back to hunting.
-Sometimes tracks disappear into the abyss, which is incredibly frustrating when you've been on a trail for a long time.
-Animals can spawn where they are not accessible. I made the mistake of shooting a few nice bull elk out on an island, where I could not walk out to as the water was too deep.
-In multiplayer if another player uses a call, even if they are across the map, oftentimes the audio from the call can be heard as if you used the call yourself. Very startling to be stalking a deer and suddenly hear a distressed rabbit in your ear!
Things in theHunter Classic that are not in CotW (that would be excellent additions)
-Small game and bird hunting
-Portable spawn points, like tents
-Customizable blind and stand positions
-Feeders
-Trophy shot mode (Please, EW, put this in. I am so tired with not being able to get a nice trophy shot of a large buck because he died in a bush)
-More variety. It would be very nice to have more species available, if not on these reserves than with added reserves.
All in all, this game is a lot of fun, for me. I am alright with the sometimes-slow pace of it because of how stunning the visuals are, and it's a nice break from hectic life to play some hiking simulator. I love long-distance shooting in this game, and the weapons are incredibly satisfying. If your rig is lower end, I must warn you that somehow movement speed is connected to FPS and this will make it go from leisurely to an absolute drag. I have played other hunting games, and this is, despite its flaws, my favorite. I highly recommend watching videos on YouTube before purchasing to see if it's something that you'd be willing to put up with the flaws of. If it seems like a game you'd enjoy but the bug list is too long, I'd slap it on your wishlist and buy when it's on sale or just later in general, as it DOES seem like there are bug fixes going out decently often.

Spec Ops: The Line is a new original title from 2K Games that features provocative and gripping Third-Person modern military Shooter gameplay designed to challenge players' morality by putting them in the middle of unspeakable situations where unimaginable choices affecting human life must be made. Features include, a gripping, storyline reminiscent of Apocalypse Now and Heart of Darkness but set in a ruined Dubai, tactical squad-based Delta Force gameplay throughout a horizontally and vertically oriented world, devastating sandstorms which can be used in combat, a variety of multiplayer modes and maps, and deep support featuring two factions.
It’s been 6 months since Dubai was wiped off the map by a cataclysmic sandstorm. Thousands of lives were lost, including those of American soldiers sent to evacuate the city. Today, the city lies buried under sand, the world’s most opulent ruin. Now, a mysterious radio signal is picked-up from Dubai, and a Delta Recon Team is sent to infiltrate the city. Their mission is simple: Locate survivors and radio for Evac. What they find is a city in the grip of war. To save Dubai, they’ll have to find the man at the heart of its madness—Col. John Konrad.

Seemingly average on the surface, Spec Ops is a hidden gem for its beautiful dystopian setting and darkly-engaging story.
If you enjoy third-person cover shooting like that found in Mass Effect 3 or Gears of War then you will find that Spec Ops: The Line provides a similar experience from a gameplay perspective. It's not particularly challenging but there are a decent number of weapons to suit different engagement styles. The enemies are all very similar to one another but as the campaign is only a few hours long you will most likely have finished it before the combat becomes too tedious.
What this game may lack in innovative mechanics it counters with an original setting and story. Your isolated special forces squad makes its way through a demolished Dubai which is suffering from a unique malady - being buried by a giant sandstorm. A series of dynamic firefights leads you on a descent into the belly of this dying leviathan city, but you will also undertake a subtle journey into the tortured mind of your protagonist. Though the scenarios you encounter will at first seem like typical action game fare, they begin to present you with increasingly difficult choices which will likely leave you feeling uneasy no matter what you decide to do. Without any overt moralizing, a few hours into Spec Ops, you may find yourself thinking differently about war and its portrayal in gaming - and that's what makes this title truly special.

Rogue Legacy is a 2D platforming action game by Cellar Door Games, an independent Canadian studio.  It’s categorized as a roguelike, which for the uninitiated, is a sub-genre that typically includes procedurally generated levels and permanent death (meaning once you die, you start over from the beginning).  Rogue Legacy has both of those, but it adds in some RPG mechanics which make the imposing threat of death easier to swallow, while not altogether curbing the difficulty that fans of the genre have come to expect.
At the beginning of Rogue Legacy, you are a generic sword-wielding hero who is tasked to fight through a dungeon.  There’s some reason for doing so, and there are diaries strewn about the world to help piece together exactly what’s going on, but for the most part the narrative is in the back seat throughout Rogue Legacy and that’s totally fine.
It’s hard to overstate just how much fun the minute to minute gameplay is in Rogue Legacy. Controls feel tight and the mechanics are all-around solid and enjoyable.  Any fan of 2D platformers such as Spelunky will find themselves at home here.  The dungeon is split into four separate areas, and while they are distinct in aesthetic and difficulty, they do tend to blend together after ten or twenty hours in the game.
The main distinguishing factor of Rogue Legacy is the way in which death, and subsequent life after death, occurs.   Upon dying (which
happen -- a lot), you get to choose a new “heir” among three choices to attempt another run through the game.  Each heir can have all sorts of randomly assigned genetic traits which affect how the game plays.  Discovering the novelty of some of these traits is fun in and of itself, so I won’t ruin them here, but I will say the traits are pretty well balanced, creative, and occasionally good for a laugh.
The other unique aspect of death is that your character continually gets stronger in whatever way you choose.  As you traipse throughout the dungeon, your character collects gold from chests and enemies.  You can invest gold after dying in a huge amount of ways; you can boost stats such as strength and armor, unlock new classes, or buy new equipment.  It’s almost impossible to beat the game during the early hours because of the upgrade system, and how weak your initial character is.  Having to rely on more than sheer skill may be a problem for some, but the feeling of progression through boosting your inherent power is pretty satisfying (as in most RPGs) and makes the whole experience very addicting.
Toward the end of Legacy, when your character is strong enough to make it most of the way through the dungeon before dying, each run can take about 30 minutes or more, and I found it becomes a bit of a grind.  Luckily the grind doesn’t last too long (at least it didn’t for me) before you become powerful enough to beat the final boss and finish the dungeon.  There is a nicely done New Game+ option, and it’s a telling sign that I immediately dove back in upon completion my first time around.
Overall, I really enjoyed my time with Rogue Legacy.  The RPG mechanics do an excellent (or evil, depending on how you look at it) job of cranking up the “Just one more run” factor that roguelikes are infamous for.  Blending rewarding and difficult gameplay with a really smart way to make death a little less punishing goes a long way to make Rogue Legacy one of the best games in the genre.
It's like dwarf fortress but easier to get into.  Highly recommended.

Wow... I think I'm in love with the Borderlands universe.
There's just something really special about this game: the way the characters grow on you, the explosive atmosphere, the compelling story, the weird but incredible way they weave heavy moments and introspection in a game filled to the brim with humor, gore and internet memes. I feel like this game is the best it can get, or at least until Gearbox or some other developer comes up with something even better. With such a diverse cast of characters, I find it hard to imagine NOT being able to relate to at least one of them despite how extreme their personalities can be. It's not all haphazard extremeness either and each is endearing in their own way. The game is very inclusive of queer characters and neurodivergent characters. They follow stereotypes, they break stereotypes, and their differences are natural and introduced as such. Handsome Jack is on par with Pagan Min as my favorite antagonist. Every character feels alive and has defining dialogue and the areas you can explore are often beautiful. Pandora is a harsh yet vibrant world that you will blast through over and over until you finally come out on top. The FPS genre generally isn't very memorable but here's a game that smashes the rules and brings out its own style.
Gunplay is the heart of Borderlands and there is a huge number of quests you can complete to gain better guns, loot and experience. I found levelling and looting enjoyable and the skill trees are decent but slightly underwhelming as a lot of them become useless if you grind to endgame difficulty modes. It goes without saying... there's a lot of grinding in this game and a couple "fetch" sidequests. Especially early on when you're stuck with some really low level equipment. But once you get past that initial slow start, the game really picks up and you'll find yourself shooting electricity out of shotguns and facing more challenging opponents with better rewards. I think the only gripe I might have with the gameplay is that some bosses felt poorly designed-- sort of same-y with almost all of them having unavoidable area-of-effect attacks. Until recently the drop rates for legendaries was notoriously difficult but has been fixed. Minor bugs exist but with the rest of the game being completely incredible I found them more funny than annoying.
There are four playable characters (plus two more in GOTY edition) that each have their own perks and quotes. No matter who you choose you'll have a good time while they rattle off at enemies or make it to second wind just in time. There's Axton, Pandora's most handsome (next to Jack!) but smart-mouthed bisexual man, who makes a great tank and support. Maya, an ace siren, is my personal favorite with her phaselock ability and makes for a nicely balanced offense and support unit as well. Her background ties her in somewhat with the going-ons of the game and playing her can involve you more in the story. Zer0, my other favorite, is your key "outsider" nameless, mysterious type. He recites haiku and displays emotes on his face.... which is honestly more adorable than it should be. You just can't quite put your finger on him but that's probably part of his charm. It should be noted that although he's an assassin class, there's no stealth (this is not a subtle game!) but over time he can become a very specialized, powerful character. Sal is the only one I haven't tried out yet but from what I've heard his skill tree makes him one of the most OP tanks in the game. Sadly there isn't a lot of backstory on the protagonists but there's plenty on all the other NPCs you'll be dealing with.
UPDATE: I've finished playing all the characters to OP8 and Sal is the pure definition of this game. EXPLOSIOOOONS! Gaige and Krieg, the other two characters included in GOTY/season pass as dlc, are fun, fast-paced power tanks. Highly recommended.
This is an attractive game full of creativity and it's clear upon playing that the people who made this game really put in a lot of effort and attention (and also memes) into it. Aside from the characters, small details like occasional ECHO logs and the differences in gun part brands add depth. The landscapes and cartoony art are great and perfectly suit the game's action-savvy theme which creates a unique combination of lightheartedness and gore. I loved the day-night transitions and many areas make for some beautiful, detailed scenery that are nice to look at while you're in or out of a fight. The world is literally blowing up with fun! And despite some really tough mobs you'll crawl through, you might find yourself coming back for more because there's nothing quite like it. For a game that makes a million jokes, I copped lots of feels and it somehow really touched me.
If you have the time and energy to spare, I strongly recommend the GOTY edition. Tiny Tina and Captain Scarlett's DLC that are included with it are some of the biggest, best DLC I've seen to date. There are many ways to play the game and trying out new characters or difficulty modes lends itself to some high replayability. On days you just want to sit back, kick some butt and feel like a badass, this is the perfect solution for everyone and anyone. Now excuse me while I write a love letter to gearbox.

Euro Truck Simulator 2 is that rare thing, a strong sim tethered to a strong game. Where other vehicle-obsessed devs seem to take player motivation for granted, Czech studio SCS understand that a pleasingly modelled steed needs a pleasingly modelled environment to shine.
On this occasion that environment is a swathe of Europe stretching from Plymouth in the west to Wroclaw in the east, from Aberdeen in the north to Milan in the South. The tangle of motorways and major roads is stylised and condensed, but feels massive.
There's satisfaction in exploring new routes, seeing new golden been-there-done-that squiggles appearing on the in-game map, but it tends to be the promise of cold, hard cash that gets you out of bed in the morning. Like Farming Simulator, ETS2 has a simple yet resonant economic sandbox at its centre.
You start as a low-skilled, truckless lorry jockey, forced to take work from established haulage companies. Slowly (or rapidly if you go to a bank) you amass the funds to buy your first rig and rent your first yard. Then the fun really begins. Contract perusing, truck pimping, skill upgrading, driver hiring... this is Eddie Stobart: The Game in all but name.
Spending 90 minutes ferrying a tank of propane from Sheffield to Prague could (should?) be tedious. The fact that it isn't is largely down to good-if-not-quite-OMSI-standard physics, and varied road layouts and scenery. Periods of smooth, almost soporific motorway motoring nestle between passages of edgier wheelwork. One minute you're cruising along contemplating the sunset over the central reservation, the next you're on a rain-lashed country road at night, waiting for the right moment to pass a painfully slow pantechnicon. Tiredness can't kill in ETS2, but it can leave you jack-knifed in a ditch, feeling awful with a substantial repair bill to pay.
The only time when the game itself loses concentration is when attempting to evoke certain regions and sounds. The further you get from central Europe the less convincing the landscapes become. No one seems to have told SCS's countryside crafters that rural Britain features long green things called hedges. Cities are often depicted with the shortest of visual shorthand – a few warehouses, the odd landmark if you're lucky. Don't expect to see a favourite local roundabout, slip-road, or speed camera in this highly-recommended HGV-driver RPG.

My name is Max. My world is fire and blood....ops. The game adaptation of Mad Max cinematographic universe lives up for the legacy of the movies. The game focus on two things that are well shown in the movies: car combat and survival. The story is not based in any of the movies, but is based on them, creating an unique one, with a great narrative, some amazing twists at the end (but a dissapointing ending) and an amazing lore and stories behing the world told by "historical relics" and beautiful scenarios like wrecked ships, airports...Overall, it's a pretty good narrative and a good story, with some character development i liked a lot, with secondary missions that connects with the story. The graphics? Amazing and photorrealistic. The atmosphere captured by it with the soundtrack makes up a superb Wasteland. The explosions and effects, including lighting and particles are very very cool to see. The bad point is the character modelling, compared to he scenarios it's pretty poor, but yet accetable. The soundtrack as i said is pretty atmospheric, with great sound effects in explosions, car chasing and in an underground parts it shows the thrill of the place. Technical things apart, the game does great, now about gameplay. The game combat, vehicular or on foot, is where the game shine. The foot combat is a Batman-like, but more visceral, with usable weapons from enemies, and you also have your own shotgun (but ammo is scarce), you can also use blast-like spears like in the movie, fuel cans to explode things and more. The bad about foot gameplay is the movements. It's very tank-like, you don't even jump, just do a little parkour on pre-defined places, but at least you can run. and roll. The car vehicle is where it shine. It can be complex, fun and hard at the same time. There is a lot of ways to destroy cars, you can use your arpoon on enemies inside or in some places of the car, you can use also your thunder-arpoon to explode them, the shotgun on their fuel, and do damage using spikes and a lot of other things, with amazing explosions and a lot of car-hell. It's outstanding. This takes us to the other aspect of Mad Max: it's magnitude and grandiosity. The game is big. Very big in a lot os aspects. You can personalize Max with clothes, faces, combat technics, equipments like lantern and crowbar. And there is a lotof things in all the options, with effects in-game. The same goes to car personalization. You can change and build every aspect in your Magnum Opus (the car). From weapons, to armor, to V8, EVERYTHING with a LOT of options. Ok, the personalization of a lot of stuff is high, what more? The map. Is big. Very big. Possible Witcher 3-size or even more. And, it's not just desert. There are a lot of things to do. Hundreds and hundreds of activities, including encounters with wastelanders, freeing regions from the villain control, helping forts to grow building projects in them that helps in-game, giant scarescrow to destroy, snipers to kill, a good variety of race modes to compete and the coolest, the Camps, with approaching startegy using your binoculars, destroy it's defenses and completing the objective (there is a variey of objectives for the camps). You will also encounter a lot of cars and enemies in the world, and convoys that you have to steal the car and take to a fort, gaining a decoration for yours. You can also make your collection of cars in the gaming world stealing them from the enemies (which you can use also to go unseen). The survival aspect is about your life bar, as it doesn't regenerate, only on forts if you have the project of a kind of Farm installed. Then you need to use food you find in the world and water from your canteen (that you need to fill in ceratin spots) to regain your life-bar. You also need fuel for your vehicle, which you find in fuel cans. Works good and put some challenge on the game, on the right way. Building some parts for your vehicle will also make possible to crete unique ones, the Archangel, each for a certain kind of gameplay. The variety and size of the game is too big. Even the enemies and car-type, there are possible a hundred of them. Boss battles in camps and on the story are good too.Thre is a kind of level up system using tokens to upgrade, and a lot of challeges to complete.The problems is after some time it becomes too repetitive. There is also some bugs. There is also a full night and day cycle with beautiful sunsets. Dynamic weather too, as you can face sandstorms, but in this game the storms are special, you face great danger and you can die, but also can gain scarps in flying junk (scraps is the money of the game you use for everything). Mad Max may have it's flaws but it's a big-sized action adventure game that is very fun to play, and a good 100+ hours if you want to complete everything.

I just completed all the achievements for this game,  so I thought I'd drop some thoughts.  Mad Max is a solid and immersive experience, though it does have some significant flaws that prevent it from being amazing. The story is fitting for a Mad Max tale, though like the films, it's the action that makes the game fun. There is some interesting mysticism sprinkled here and there as well.  Max himself fits the reluctant hero archetype very well. His sidekick, Chumbucket, acts great as Max's foil and comic relief to the harshness of the wasteland, which itself is beautifully rendered. There are other characters scattered here and there, though not enough for the player to care for them. Ground combat follows the Batman formula; various finisher unlocks help keep it fresh. Vehicle combat is where the game shines as you can upgrade your car to have some killer weapons and defensive items.
PROS:
-Performance (Best PC port in a long time, looks beautiful, runs smooth)
-Vehicle Combat (You can harpoon stuff!)
-Environments (Lots of detail for an open world; the wasteland is filled with all kinds of scenes that tell a story of the apocalypse without having to spell it out for you. Lots of cool and disturbing imagery all around. I found myself in the game's great photo mode grabbing amazing screenshots that now serve as awesome wallpapers)
-Immersion (You are Max, and you are a cold, yet broken badass. Very easy to get lost in this wasteland, much more interesting to me than the other post apocalyptic game right now)
CONS:
-Side quests too repetitive / too much grinding
-Lack of End Game content (This is what keeps this game from being amazing; you spent a long time upgrading Max and your car, only for the game to be virtually empty by the time you are ready to be a true Road Warrior. The best vehicular combat scenarios, the convoys, for instance, never respawn. The game is desperately in need of a way to reset enemy camps and convoys, or a New Game+ mode.. not sure this will happen as Avalanche is busy with Just Cause 3)
-Difficulty (It's pretty easy, and you can make Max pretty overpowered pretty fast - could use a Survival mode of some sort)
OTHER THOUGHTS:
I'm not a completionist usually, but for this game I didn't want it to end so I did a lot of grinding that I don't like doing.  Note: If you want to 100%, look at the challenges first and plan your attack; if you get rid of all Threat Level in the game too early, it will be very difficult/annoying to complete some of the challenges required. See End Game comments above.
Where are the War Rigs? Would be awesome if the convoys had big trucks that you had to board. Imagine fighting War Boys on a moving behemoth, before finally taking out the driver and hijacking the truck. Generally this game needs more convoys and maybe even convoy escort missions.

The customization is a bit lacking, there could be more classes/items and more extra stuff to unlock/find. Some classes i feel were way better than others, but maybe that's compared to how i played through the game.There is also inifite replayability, as the game never really ends. You can continue on a new game+ everytime you beat the game,with the difficulty ramping up every playthrough.  Some of the Bosses can be annoying at times, especially after many playthroughs, but in general they never feel "cheap".
To sum it up, if you like games like Metroid or Castlevania, i highly recomend this game to you.I'd give this an 8/10, overall a pretty solid game for its price. Hoping for a sequel :D

Let's be real, if you played Life is Strange you're probably starved for any way to revisit our favorite heroines and would buy this game even if it were rated "Overwhelmingly Negative". The good news is that you don't really have to worry about that. This is a good game, though it lacks the ambitious exposition of the original. While Life is Strange violently plunged you into a world of secrets and conflict armed with a rewind button, Before the Storm focuses on smaller, and maybe more mundane happenings of Aradia Bay like teen angst, familial strife, betrayal, and the fast formed bond between two very different girls. Without the superpowers of her best friend Max, Chloe's tale in Before the Storm shapes up to be a much more intimate, personal, and human tale than the original.

Life is Strange: Before the Storm is the game that I have been wanting since playing the original. I wanted to meet Rachel Amber since I learned how much she meant to Chloe. I wanted to experience what Chloe experienced to make her love Rachel so much, to make her push herself as hard as she did. Before the Storm is exactly what I asked for.
Yes, the time travel aspect from the original is absent in this one, but to me, it makes the choices you make much more permanent. You won't be able to redo all of your choices to find the best one, you'll have to live with each decision you make.
I have also seen some people say that this game is pointless because we know how it will end and the choices can't change that. While that may or may not be true, I see it as getting to live the events leading up to the story we already know, living the story of Chloe and Rachel that we were previously only given clues about.
At the end of the day, I loved the first episode, and I'm certain I'll love the next two. I'm just going to have to figure out how to wait for them in the meantime.

So, this is Prison Architect. It is what its name promisses and more. You build and manage a prison, which grows and grows. I would say, it's not a really good game, but above being average. Why? Because for every fun moment the game gives you, it smackes you the next. I will just give you 2 lists of things I like and dislike in this game:
What I like:
- it is easy to controll. Selfexplaining categories for items etc make it really easy to go into the game itself
- the graphics, I simply like the style
- the self acting AI. If you hire a guard, he will furfill his tasks by him, even though you can assign guards for special tasks later. I think that helps very much, because micromanagemant would be too hard, when a prison grows bigger and bigger
What I don't like:
- the game left too often just sitting there and asking myself: "Why did the game didn't explain that mechanic?" In 8 hours of gaming, I had to restart way too often, because I messed something up because I simply did not know how to do it right. Because the game didn't explain a single bit of the first steps, such as how to assign prisoners to work etc. It shows you how to build, ok, but building is only one aspect of the game.
- the AI. Yes, I said, I liked it. And that's true. But sometimes I just wanted to slap the delevopers in the face. Workers crowding in front of a door they can't open, totally ignoring their entrance with a staff door, I build only for them. Prisoners, who prefer to use the small shower in the first building, instead of using the large one in their own cell block... Or my guards, who prefer to crowd in the yard (which is for the prisoners) or the cafetaria instead of doing the work they're payed for. That just pisses me of.
- the prisoners. Yeah, I really don't get the way they work. People, who have to stay maybe 5 years in prison start riots, because their needs were furfilled. They just started to riot. Why? I can't say, the game gives me no hints. That's just what prisoners do.
Finally I would give this game a 6.5/10. It's nice to play and I will do it more often in the future. But sometimes I just feel left behind, because I shall do things nobody explained me. That is a bit frustrating. One could argue, that the solutions are found on the internet, but I say that a game needs to be selfexplaining. A tutorial for the first steps of building a prison would've been better, that the tutorial given, even though that tutorial is well executed. If you like that type of sandbox games and can forgive some minor flaws, this game is great.

I came into this game expecting a easy and classic platformer. Boy, was I wrong! Instead, Rogue Legacy gave me the funnest and hardest experience I ever had. This genre of rogue-like games is a blessing to other game genres out there. Instead of a linear story and a one way approach, Rogue Legacy pitted me against the unknown.
This unknown was the part of the charm of the game. I never knew what to expect in the next room because every version of the castle differed from the rest. However, there is a way for the heroes to keep the same version of the castle and it is by reducing the amount of gold earned. Speaking of this feature, the other features that Rogue Legacy presented broaden the aspects of the game.
Rogue Legacy offered the ability to upgrade the castle so that the heroes would have better skills and more job advancements. In addition, every hero is unique due to the randomization that the game does. Some heroes may be of a certain class or possess a certain trait that would be vital to complete certain areas of the game.
To recap, I ventured into this game with a completely different mindset. After completing the game, I realized the potential Rogue Legacy has and how satisfying the gameplay was. Even though the game provided me a few hours of enjoyment, it's a good game to purchase when it goes on sale.

Mad Max is one of those games that succeeds in many ways but still somewhat lacks substance. Not to say this game is terrible (I mean just look at my playtime), it's really really good, just not great.
The visuals are fantastic, never before has a virtual wasteland been so perfectly created (it feels more post-apocalyptic than Fallout's settings). However, there are MANY bugs. I'm not one one to complain about these, but in this case it has to be said. Some of the cutscenes freeze for half a second while the audio is still running in the background. Result? The cutscene returns to its normal runtime and the audio becomes totally desynced. Since this issue has happened to me on several occasions, I couldn't help but feel a little annoyed. There are also quite a few frame stutters during gameplay and some Wasteland Missions wouldn't start at all unless I restarted the game.
The real cons revolve around the storyline and some of the characters.
...
Max is by far the most boring character in this game. His lines feel very monotonous and repetitive. I was honestly hoping for a deeper or more grounded version of Max. Borderlands 2:
+ Interesting and unique visuals for the game. It's very artistic and cartoonish in appearance, which is refreshing. I can appreciate this style of graphics, even though I believe the more conventional approach is still more aesthetically pleasing.
+ Each character in Borderlands 2 is intriguing and memorable, which is important in this sort of game.
+ Borderlands 2 challenges you with semi-difficult boss fights and general combat. You'll die several times, but you're always able to overcome the challenge, which is great.
+ There's many side quests and main missions to complete in this game, so there's quite a lot of content to enjoy.
+ Open world exploration.
+ Co-op game mode to play with friends.
~ The humour in this game can be quite childish. So if you're a mature person it won't appeal to you. That being said, the other half of the humour is clever, witty and funny. In that respect, it's good.
~ Combat can be fun at times, but not always. Sometimes it's just frustrating. Enemies can have insane amounts of health or respawn CONSTANTLY and it feels more like a spam clicking FPS game than anything balanced or realistic. As a result it can get repetitive and dull, but at other moments it really stands out and is enjoyable.
-The RPG element of this game isn't well cultivated. To be honest, there isn't a good reason to call it an RPG. When you level up you get to pick a new skill to invest points in, but that's it. None of the skills available are very creative, in fact they are more like buffs to your character instead of skills. Playing as a gunzerker class, there's the choice to "increase gun accuracy", "increase critical damage" or "increase reload time", among other options, pretty standard and uninventive. I don't feel as if levelling up provides a really good advantage like it should. Most RPG games are much more in-depth with levelling and give your character practical benefits.
- Character dialogue often overlaps with combat at inconvenient times. This means you miss out on part of quest storylines, because you're too busy desperately defending yourself from being killed. This was poorly thought-out.
- Excessive DLC which should have been featured in the main game. There's a lot of additional content to buy and expand your gameplay, but too much in my opinion. Adding this to the main game would have made it epic and there's no doubt it would score higher.
Overall Score: 7.5/10

There isn't much here for single player (yet), but with a few controllers and friends hilarious battles ensue. There are a few bugs but it doesn't effect (or affect?) the game much.
One mode sees you and up to 3 friends battling it out on a variety of maps. From knocking your friends off of moving trucks, to shoving them into a furnace or even grinder. What's great is the controlls which allow you to controll your arms separately. So I can hold LB (on an Xbox controller) to grab my opponent with the characters left hand, and then repeatedly press RB to start smashing him with the right. If I grab with both hands by holding both RB & LB I can drag opponents around of even press Y and lift them up. X and B allow for head butts and kicks which when mixxed with the jump can make for some hilarious moves. If you can get in a good hit, you can knock your opponent unconcious for a second, which gives you time to throw him off an edge/into a crushing device. Continue getting more good hits and he will be unconcious for longer - but usually matches are ended by lucky hits or good timing pushing someone into a fan/onto the subway track.
Another mode sees you and up to 3 friends CO OP together to take on waves on bot enemies on top a building.
Looking forward to future updates like online multiplayer and more maps!
PROS:
- Great fun with friends (playing locally)
- The controlls make for a new way to play fighting games
- Good mix of some fun and hilarious maps
CONS
- No online multiplayer
- Some minor bugs

You will look in the mirror and understand the fear mankind has of itself for perhaps the first time. And remember- the developer has stated that one of the endings- a legitimate ending to the game- is at any point seeing the path forward, and simply refusing to play- refusing to do what is needed to progress. This is a game that is aware of its audience, of its genre, and manages to dissect both without coming across as hamhanded or overbearing in its message.

An under-appreciated game that deserves to be played. The excellent storyline carries the solid (albeit generic) third-person shooter gameplay, along with fantastic visuals. Gruesome, impactful scenes eschew the usual 'team America' FPS tropes.

Spec Ops: The Line is a good third person shooter that aims to make you question your actions in this and other shooters. As you progress your motives are questioned, the heroic nature of your actions are questioned, and your character becomes less likable and more violent. Other reviewers have commented on most of the quality elements of the game, but I would add that this game is filled with lots of little details that add a lot to the story. Things like how your character becomes dirtier and more wounded helps support the story. The way your character performs execution moves becomes more brutal as your progress also helps support the story. It's a great game with a great story and numerous immersive touches that really show attention to detail.

What Spec Ops lacks in tight gameplay, it more than makes up for in its rich, thought provoking story. Not to say that the gameplay is bad though, it just doesn't quite stand up to games like Battlefield 2 or Call of Duty 4 in terms of mechanics. Personally, I think anyone who likes military games should play Spec Ops; it is well worth your time.
May not be the most fun gameplay wise, but the story is worth it. So worth it, in fact, that I could play the game three more times without getting bored.

Prison Architect can be a challenging game at times, but still is amazingly fun. I greatly recommend you buy it.  +_=

Drive the truck you've ever dreamed of. Purchase,customize,upgrade,paint - be the badass truck driver,PIMP YOUR RIDE!
Okay,enough jokes. ETS2 is a strategy real time(not the casual RTS game)truck driving simulator. The point of the strategy is that you have to manage the time,profit,covered distance,truck maintenance and tons of other stuff to make as much fortune in the shortest period of time as possible. The plot of the game isn't just truck driving. Your main goal is to purchase your own truck,make some profit,found your own organisation and create the hegemony in the whole European continent.
Atmosphere of the game is marvelous,the sound of the rain,cows in the farm,highway traffic and the most overwhelming sound of all - the powerfull(750hp) engine of your own truck,it's so relaxing,frankly speaking,I even used to fall asleep sometimes at the highway,but then I made up a trick for myself. I've found a really nice Welsh radio station which plays the top charts and keeps me awake,also entertained(It's called Nation Radio if you're interested,check it out).
The most amazing thing imo is the nature - biome - the way it changes along the road. In Germany it's so green and grassy,especially the evergreen trees like firs are so nice and atmospheric; Lowlands and sea in Netherlands,Belgium and Denmark, Wine valleys of France,the mountains of Austro-Switzerland and many other things which I can't tell you now. Let's consider it as a spoiler,you gotta check it out,believe me.
The base game is quite entertaining,but if you add some expansions it will grant you the 10 times more experience and will add about 40-50 hours of additional gametime. DLCs are pretty cheap on sales like approximately below $10(including VAT) and I asure you,they're worth it if you've already enjoyed the based game. The biggest DLCs/Expansions are "Going East" which adds several countries and cities as Poland,Slovakia,Hungary and Czech Republic and "Scandinavia" which adds,as the title says,the whole Scandinavian countries with their unique biomes.
Don't you wanna pay for expansions? OK. It's no big deal,because there're several good web-sites where you can find free mods and even the expansions as addition to your base game. I've been using tens of such mods as for myself. Or if after some time you're bored of Single-player,you can play unofficial Multiplayer ETS2 with thousands of truck drivers on the server. Almost no AI drivers,mostly real people creating traffic jams,it's so fun,omg. Check it out,dude!

This is a first impression view.
I've put in over 30 hours and I must say being a fan of the NBA 2k series this game blows it out of the water. I mostly loved the NBA games for the "my player" mode and have always been a fan of the online team-up and black top mode, but due to people using glitches, micro-transactions, and horrible internet connectivity it ruined the online experience. This game however has usually perfect ping, though as it does have the problems that newly released games suffer from.
*Character Customization* You first choose which position you wish to play (PG,SG,SF,PF,and C) Though the options may seem limited at the start you essentially unlock different hair and clothes from the shop offering a large array of customization.
*Lobby System* This game runs on a "hop in-hop out" lobby system where you can create or join a lobby a friends and compete online
*Gameplay* The game consists of a 3on3 5 min. Matches where the goal is to out score the opposing team. (obviously). an indivdual mode where you choose a team of 2 other NPC and go against another single player with their team of NPC's and duke it out, and a free mode where you can inv your friends for 1on1's or practice against bots.
All in all this is a very enjoyable game, though the micotransaction will give you an obvious boost it is NOT impossible to beat people who have spent 100's of $ on items (I have plenty of experience with this). The game also gives you a chance with the ever going event which once you achieve level 24 they will reword you 1000 gcash (10$ value) which will allow you to buy some things to make you more competitive.
I may renew my review but all in all if you are an NBA STREET fan or a fan of the NBA 2K series you should at least give it a try, as it is FREE to play. I don't believe the game is fully PAY 2 WIN but as it is a free to play game there needs to be insentive for people to spend money and as I love the game so far I won't feel bad about spending up to $60(the price for a standard new game) on this game is it provides an amazing online basketball experience.

Amazing sequel for Life Is Strange! Cannot wait for release of episode 2!

Let's be real, if you played Life is Strange you're probably starved for any way to revisit our favorite heroines and would buy this game even if it were rated "Overwhelmingly Negative". The good news is that you don't really have to worry about that. This is a good game, though it lacks the ambitious exposition of the original. While Life is Strange violently plunged you into a world of secrets and conflict armed with a rewind button, Before the Storm focuses on smaller, and maybe more mundane happenings of Aradia Bay like teen angst, familial strife, betrayal, and the fast formed bond between two very different girls. Without the superpowers of her best friend Max, Chloe's tale in Before the Storm shapes up to be a much more intimate, personal, and human tale than the original.

Life is Strange: Before the Storm is the game that I have been wanting since playing the original. I wanted to meet Rachel Amber since I learned how much she meant to Chloe. I wanted to experience what Chloe experienced to make her love Rachel so much, to make her push herself as hard as she did. Before the Storm is exactly what I asked for.
Yes, the time travel aspect from the original is absent in this one, but to me, it makes the choices you make much more permanent. You won't be able to redo all of your choices to find the best one, you'll have to live with each decision you make.
I have also seen some people say that this game is pointless because we know how it will end and the choices can't change that. While that may or may not be true, I see it as getting to live the events leading up to the story we already know, living the story of Chloe and Rachel that we were previously only given clues about.
At the end of the day, I loved the first episode, and I'm certain I'll love the next two. I'm just going to have to figure out how to wait for them in the meantime.

Having played this game for 32 Hours now, I can safely say I am quite addicted to this game.

Pros:
Easy to learn how to play,
Simple yet pleasing graphics,
Nice take on the prison system,
Comical in a lot of ways.
Cons:
The tutorial didn't work for me very well.
Hard to keep the prisoners happy.
Construction issues (Building Blocked / Too Dangerous)
Speeding up time does not seem to actually speed time up.
I am certain that the cons will be amended shortly by the Game Devs, but for now it is causing a bit of bother.
Still, it's a highly enjoyable game and I would certainly tell others to buy and play it for themselves!

I found my first ever review to be a travesty to an epic game, so here is my redux :)
A combination of first person shooter and role playing game, Borderlands 2 is an addictive mix of genres that will suck away thousands of hours of your time. The cell shading art style is different - but beautiful - and can be removed with a minor tweak in the config files if you want to take it off for a small increase in performance. Removing the cell shading does not detract from the beauty of the game, just changing it slightly.
The storyline, voice work, and pace of the game are all fantastic. And I loved the humour and subtle (and some not so subtle) jokes throughout. Not much else can be said about it without giving too much away.
I would highly recommend purchasing the Game Of The Year edition and playing through the game as each of the characters to explore the differing fight mechanics that come with them. Go in guns blazing as a Gunzerker, or sneak in as an Assassin; the choice is yours. There are a few more characters and others ways to deal with enemies, and those methods will keep you busy for a long time in this game as you explore the world anew each time.
Although many of the side quests are not mandatory, they are recommended to be completed to gain experience to be able to progress through the story missions without having to empty hundreds of rounds of ammo into enemies. If you try to run through the story as fast as possible, you will find yourself coming across enemies many levels above your own, and you will die, a lot.
If you like first person shooters, you'll like this game. If you like 4 player co-op with friends, you'll like this game. And if you want a game that provides a lot of content that is good value for money, you'll like this game (GOTY Edition, anyway).
Don't waste your time.

This game is...different, on the surface it looks like any other 3rd person shooter trying to be what call of duty is (An america ♥♥♥♥ yeah shoot everything simulator). However once you start playing it you quickly realize that that's not the case at all, this game is dark, depressing and at times it truely makes you feel uncomfortable and guilty of the actions you as the player do (however for the sake of spoilers your just going to have to find out why on your own). The visuals are actually quite good at times and the ruined city dubai is a perfect setpiece for this game, some textures couldve been better but it honestly wont take anything away from the experience which is whats important in the grand scheme of things.
It does have its problems though, the controls in my opinion is a bit unintuitive and even unresponsive at times (sometimes my character wouldnt take cover when I told him to, resulting in my unfortunate death) however this only happened a couple of times so its not by any means a huge issue but still something to mention. I would also say that the gunplay is a bit combative towards the player (The targeting reticule feels a bit too heavy in my opinion) but I got used to it after a while, a bit annoying but by no means gamebreaking.
Overall theres really not a lot I can say to do this game justice, its definatly a game made for the story aspect so if your going into this looking for a mechanically amazing shooter you'll probably be disappointed. However if your willing to sit back and experience what this game has to offer I really think that you'll be surprised by how different this game feels. Personally this is one of the best shooters ive played in a long time due to that and certainly worth your time.
