Every once in awhile, what I call a crime is committed in this industry, a game will be released and end up being one of the greatest games I've ever played. However for one reason or another, it ends up doing horribly. Spec Ops: The Line may be the biggest crime I've ever witnessed...
Spec Ops puts you in the shoes of Captain Walker, you and two squad mates are sent into a sandstorm destroyed Dubai to find survivors. At first glance the game may appear to be another Call Of Duty type of modern shooter. Disaster occurs and America comes in to save the day, but that is definitely not the case.
The first thing I noticed about this game is how beautiful it is, some may disagree, but Spec Ops on PC with max settings truly looks next gen to me, and this game was released a good while before next gen was a thing. The animation complements this point, for example since Dubai is a city destroyed by uncontrollable sandstorms, you will be traveling through a lot of buildings that are now buried deep below the sand. The moment when I first shot out a giant window I gleefully watched as the sand poured in and buried alive an entire squad of soldiers.
Everything that should be good in a 3rd person shooter gameplay wise is present in this game, but I do not want to waste any time so I'll just tell you about the one thing in Spec Ops that will make you love it, the story. This is hands down the greatest story I have ever had the pleasure of playing in a "Modern War" shooter. Within the first couple levels, Spec Ops shows you that unlike what other games will tell you, war nowadays isn't as clear as "America=good guys, Foreigners=bad guys". Without spoiling too much you quickly see other American soldiers killing innocent families. What choice do you have? Will you just stand by and let mothers and children get burned alive? No of course not, you are going to take action and start killing your fellow soldiers. While going through the campaign I couldn't believe the light Yager was casting on the American military...and I loved it. Just because you wear a uniform doesn't mean you are a good, or sane, person. Your squad has to witness the entire breakdown of a city, piles of bodies litter the streets, peoples are dying of everything you could imagine, soldiers killing the innocent for sport, but Walker keeps pressing on, because he believes he is doing the right thing.
The voice acting is also great and it isn't just because Nolan North plays the main character, it is because not only do you see, but you also hear the changes these characters are going through due to what they are forced to live through. Once again I do not want to spoil anything, but Walker starts off as a by the book, top tier soldier, and North does an incredible job showing just how much war can change a man.
Spec Ops: The Line is an incredible game that will blow you away. The graphics are beautiful though the images you will see are gut-wrenching. The voice acting is fantastic though what these characters go through is horrible. The story is perfect, you will feel like you have walked through hell with these soldiers. If you are not interested in the "Modern War" genre because of it's glorification and unrealistic approach on war, play this game. If you do like the "Modern War" genre because it is fun, action packed, and brutally violent, play this game. If you haven't figured it out yet what I'm trying to say is Spec Ops is a game you should play, easily an unforgettable experience. Play this game and lets give Yager the praise and recognition they deserve.

I would describe the core gameplay as a competent shooter. Nothing too unique. I have become tired by repetitious shooters over the last few years when I just have so many other options in regard to games I can play. What makes this game recommendable is everything else about it. Most obviously the story - its great, and it actually feels pretty important. Its similar to Apocalypse Now but in modern Dubai rather than 70's Vietnam. The story, once it gets rolling, asks you to question how you as a player of a shooter video game can convince yourself that it can ever be right to take the life of another human being - and the lengths we go to make rationalizations for killing. The game is an exercise in cognitive dissonance; you're forced to question the act of killing and come to terms with the consequences of taking another person's life, but at the same time you're supposed to kill hundreds of people. People who thrash about near-death on the ground, coughing up blood, frantically asking for help with what little breath they have left. The story is thoughtful, the voice acting is great, the sound design and implementation of soundtrack are both great, and the game looks great. The core gameplay itself, though, is still pretty average for third-person cover shooters.

If your looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if your looking for an outstanding pie recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

Having played through the first episode (And more recently, the second), I now feel a more thorough review is in order.
(Note, this review is for Episode 1 of a 3 part game. When you purchase the game, keep in mind it is episodic in nature and they are not all available at launch. You can see the expected release dates on Wikipedia if you do a search for the game, though at the time of this writing episode 3 have not been announced)
This game is basically a love letter to the Life is Strange universe; it is clear that it was written by fans of the series. If you have not played the original Life is Strange game, do yourself a favor and pick that one up first. While BtS is totally coherent even if you have not played the original, you will be missing crucial context that is very important in a game focused on story and characters.
All that being said, this is an excellent start and I'm very much looking forward to the remaining episodes. Chloe and Rachel's relationship feels very organic, if a tad fast-paced at times (one could make an argument that when you consider how desperate each of them is for meaningful companionship, the fast pace makes complete sense. This is sometimes hard to understand if you have never been in similar situations as our two main characters, but I'd be willing to bet that anyone who has been in high school has seen these sorts of relationships played out on a regular basis).
As with the previous Life is Strange game, there are dozens of little tidbits in each scene that make the world a joy to explore. The inhabits of Arcadia Bay are interesting to interact with, especially when Chloe's sass is on full display (the "Backtalk" gameplay feature focused on picking the best responses for Chloe to argue with anyone and everyone is a fun feature, and what it lacks in the gravitas of Max's time-bending power, it more than makes up for in fun interactions.)
In short, if you are a fan of the original Life is Strange, you will find plenty to be happy about here. If you are not a fan, you might still be pleasantly surprised, but you will get a lot more out of it if you play the original game first.
Regarding the Deluxe version's particular features:: The extra outfit choices are great, as is the mixtape mode. However, if you plan on purchasing this version for the bonus episode (featuring both Chloe and Max, the main character of the original game) keep in mind that the bonus episode has also not been released as of the time of this writing. So don't expect too much right now, but based on the writing for this episode I believe it will be worth having for the future.

Pros:
+ Fantastic Sandbox Gameplay with loads of freedom
+ Beautiful if bleak world to travel around
+ Great atmosphere - really captures the feel of Mad Max
+ Loads of great customization with meaningful choices
+ Top notch combat both in car and on foot (uses a modified version of the Arkham melee combat)
+ Loads of value for money - will take dozens of hours to complete everything
+ Travelling is fun thanks to rewarding car combat
Cons:
- Mad Max style dialoge gets old fast
- Strange story that never quite finds its footing
- Slow to get going - too much hand-holding in the first couple of hours
Overall I really love this game. It shares many of the great features of Shadow of Mordor, but also brings enough of its own ideas to be a worthwile addition. It took me a little while (perhaps a few hours) to find my momentum, largely due to the strange hand-holding the game foisters on you to start with. However, once I was free to head off into the Great White and start having my own adventures I soon fell in love with it.
If you enjoy sandbox style adventure games then this is a great purchase and will give you hours of fun. It's not a story game in the way that GTA or Assassin's Creed is, so do be aware of that. But take it on its own merits and it's a wonderful game that is unique enough to warrant a place in almost anyone's library.

Just a couple thoughts on this game. First, this is probably one of the best hunting games out right now, it feels like there's been a dry spell for these over the past few years. Understandable since it's a small fan base I'm sure. Nonetheless, this game is quite fun and enjoyable to play solo. A couple thoughts after putting in 12-15ish hours:
- The game is quite slow paced, I saw a joke of "walking simulator 2017" and it's not far off. I'd love to see an ATV or the ability to fast travel to blinds/stands/lookouts.
- This one time, I shot a doe in the head and it ran away. When I eventually tracked it down the shot tracker basically showed the bullet going right into the center of the skull and said "flesh, skull, jaw" So yeah...that happens
- Personally, I think putting guns behind a level-up wall is BS. At least give me some other options.
- Also, I have yet in my life to see a single-shot 7mm Magnum that someone actually takes hunting.
- More guns plz. Seriously, there's like 9 rifles.
- The stealth system could use a little more balance. For example: I want two speeds of crouch walking (toggle crouch, hold shift to move a little faster). Then walking should not producer the same amount of sound as running. You can walk quite softly through the woods IRL
- The UX is strange. It took me 10 minutes to figure out that items in the store scroll left to right
- Speaking of store, the text on the guns and stuff moves really fast, be nice if the space for the text was a little bigger so it didn't have to scroll.
Please don't take my critisism to mean it's a bad game. It's not at all. In fact I've quite enjoyed the few hours I've put in. I hope it gets some updates and changes in the future. Definetly recommend if you're into the whole hunting genre.

8.2/10
+ Interesting Story
+ Amazing writing/script
+ Great Characters and Nice Character Development
+ Engaging story that makes you feel emotionally involved
+ You make decisions that affect outcomes
+ Great Twist at the end
+ Nice use of environments in play
+ Different locations throughout Dubai that all are interesting
- Some "choices" seem like you actually have no control
- Nothing new with gameplay (Generic Third Person Shooter Gameplay)
- Some controls were frustrating (ex. X [Gamepad] was used to get to cover AND to run)
Overall Spec Ops: The Line was an interesting and engaging interactive cinematic experience. Spec Ops had the story of a big budget hollywood action movie, but also had the familiar third person shooter in it. The story kept me on the edge of my seat and wanting to know what happens next. At some parts Specs Ops was just another grindfest, but then again what sooter today isn't? Spec Ops did not have a huge selection of guns, which did not hurt the game at all. Instead of looking for the coolest weapon, you were looking for weapons to help you clear the level so you could find out what happens next.
In conclusion Spec Ops: The Line is a great game that should not be missed out on due to the new emotional and mental take on war. The game will rank up there with my favorite games that would make me want to play again, to play the many different ending.
P.S. The graphics for this game was pretty okay, nothing fancy, but nothing terrible. I put this at the end of my review as to not get this confused with pluses and minuses. I would NEVER include graphics as a means of judging a game.

It's sad to think of how little this game has made an impact on the shooter market, because the story and the message are far deeper and more interesting than any other cover-based shooter I've played in years.  It presents war in much worse a way than you've seen in *any* video game.  Remember the huge twist midway through Modern Warfare, where you play as a soldier caught in a nuclear blast, slowly crawling towards his inevitable doom?  This game will tug at you so very much harder, you can't possibly imagine.  And the fact that every choice you make actually does change how the ending plays out really does help emphasize the player-video game connection, enhancing immersion and reflection.  Even the times where you die (and you will die a lot if you play on the harder difficulties without making use of assets such as patience and tactics), messages at the bottom of the loading screen help provide short snippets of internal monologues the character is feeling.
In terms of gameplay, the game does a lot with the cover-based-shooter genre that may not be totally new, but performs it in a way that doesn't keep the player bored at any time.  I often found myself choosing weapons not because I preferred them, but because they had ammunition, and I was almost constantly going through an ammo shortage.  It helps emphasize the feeling of desperation in everthing the player does.  Grenades were a godsend when you threw them, and an absolute curse when they were thrown at you.  Perhaps it was because I was on the harder difficulty, but grenades seemed to be a bit unfair at times.  Combine that with situations where ammo would sometimes disappear after a battle or after a reload - or even once when no enemy would drop ammo until I died - and there's clearly a few things that could have been done better.  Other than that, I ran into no graphical glitches, no weird situations with the physics engine, no issues of any kind.  The textures are incredibly detailed (2k?), and it doesn't hurt that some of the most detailed textures are in the player's model, which progressively gets more beat-up over the course of the game.
tl;dr: Put this game on your wishlist, because this is one experience that will actually change how you view the real world and how you make decisions.  It's always on sale for like 3 dollars, and quite honestly, *everyone* should own a copy of this.  Fair warning, though - this game does not make a hero out of you.  You have to be willing to make some very tough choices at times.

Hello :) I bought this game in the year 2013.
Over the years, SCS Software, spent time and efforts in:
---> Game development
1. Renewed graphics (driving looks more realistic than it was with first versions of the game)
2. Better AI Traffic management
3. Better weather simulation
4. Rebuilt menu interface
5. Introduction to World of Trucks
---> Trucks
1. Obtained licenses for all the trucks in game (Scania, Volvo, Iveco, DAF, Mercedes-Benz...)
2. Fixed truck handling and added more realistic engine sounds for most trucks
3. Added more trucks for free (in November 2017 they added the New Scania Euro6 series)
4. Added more trailer options
As I said in my 2015 review, this game is constantly updated and on the SCS Software Blog you always find a list of the "most interesting things added" in every update they release for the game.
This is not something you can find with every game.
Talking about the game itself... well... it's not a game, it's a SIMULATOR, it's made for people who actually like driving a truck (or giving a chance) across Europe. You start the game with no trucks and no garages. You have to start working for other people delivering trailers with THEIR trucks, until you spare a little bit of money you can use to get your first truck, your first garage, and then.... another truck, your first employee... until you let your business grow up :)
Of course, if you want to immediately get money to buy your first truck, you can deal with the Bank that will offer you loans up to 400.000€, but be careful and check out the interests % ;)
This is an endless game. You play it, you enjoy it, you get bored of it, you leave it... but then after weeks, months... you want to play it again :)

So, what do I think of Mad Max? Even with its weak storyline, it’s such a pleasure to play. The combat system is absolutely fantastic both in-car and on-foot, and the sheer amount of violence and explosions is enough to make anyone happy. If you’re a fan of games that let you play your own way, Mad Max is definitely a game for you. There are multiple ways to tackle almost every area of Mad Max, and customisation is a huge theme throughout the game – it’s very much your personal game. Even though scrap collection can be tedious, it’s all worth it when you buy the upgrade you’ve been waiting for and you feel the improvement it makes to your cars handling and performance.
In fact, I was really surprised about just how good Mad Max is when compared to the amount of attention its getting. I think its down to timing - it was released on the same day as Metal Gear Solid V, a game that people have been waiting for, for years. In all the MGSV excitement, it seems Mad Max has been pushed to one side and even though it's a fantastic game, I don't think it'll get the recognition it deserves.

I used to be a big fan of management games such as Theme Park/Hospital, Startopia, Capitalism, Transport Tycoon, RollercoasterTycoon and so on. Back to those days i really wanted 2 types of those: a school management and a prison management game. Introversion Software realized some kind of childhood dream here, just thank you for daring to cover this harsh topic!
Prison Architect is a 2D prisoner management game. You'll be asked to give each wave of prisoners a place to sleep, to eat, to wash and eventually to learn as well as ensuring the atmosphere is safe enough for them to go out of there in 1 piece. There is always something to do in Prison Architect due to the pressure of the constant wave of prisoners coming. This brings good dynamics to the game.
Each prisoner has its own personnality, a good warden will quickly split those petty thieves and those murderers into different level of security within your prison. Treat any of them bad, and they'll soon riot. Give them a place to receive education and visits from their families, soon your prison will be famous for putting criminals back on the right track.
Most of the time in Prison Architect, you're buidling. New rooms, electricity, water, fences, the content is big concerning the building part. The gameplay diversifies when it comes to drug enforcement, establish a security strategy, tunnel digging counter measures... I really like the way  it densifies the game. You also need to research to get new features and get extra cash from grants when you achieve certain goals.
It's deep and well done. Graphics are unique, check the video above and you'll immediately understand. No technical problems are restraining you from playing the game except for the biggest prisons, but it's no big deal..
At the moment of this review (10/2014) the game is still early access. The team is working hard and keeps communicating with the community. I didnt want to play the early access not to waste the experience but at the moment the content is so important that you can really have fun with the game.
I strongly recommend you to play Prison Architect!

Just a couple thoughts on this game. First, this is probably one of the best hunting games out right now, it feels like there's been a dry spell for these over the past few years. Understandable since it's a small fan base I'm sure. Nonetheless, this game is quite fun and enjoyable to play solo. A couple thoughts after putting in 12-15ish hours:
- The game is quite slow paced, I saw a joke of "walking simulator 2017" and it's not far off. I'd love to see an ATV or the ability to fast travel to blinds/stands/lookouts.
- This one time, I shot a doe in the head and it ran away. When I eventually tracked it down the shot tracker basically showed the bullet going right into the center of the skull and said "flesh, skull, jaw" So yeah...that happens
- Personally, I think putting guns behind a level-up wall is BS. At least give me some other options.
- Also, I have yet in my life to see a single-shot 7mm Magnum that someone actually takes hunting.

- The stealth system could use a little more balance. For example: I want two speeds of crouch walking (toggle crouch, hold shift to move a little faster). Then walking should not producer the same amount of sound as running. You can walk quite softly through the woods IRL

- Speaking of store, the text on the guns and stuff moves really fast, be nice if the space for the text was a little bigger so it didn't have to scroll.
Please don't take my critisism to mean it's a bad game. It's not at all. In fact I've quite enjoyed the few hours I've put in. I hope it gets some updates and changes in the future. Definetly recommend if you're into the whole hunting genre.

So before I begin I would like to say that I really love this studio. I am a big fan of theHunter and have put a long time into playing that game. That being said, this game is currently unplayable for me. There are so many bugs and crashes that I simply cannot look past them and enjoy myself. But before I list those I would like to list what I do like so far.
PROS:
- beautiful world, graphics are simply stunning
- audio ambiance and SFX are amazing
- skill and perk trees are a cool addition
- no microtransactions (which i did not mind in theHunter)
- your in-game money is actually worth something in the store
- cool story based missions and side missions
- unknown points on the map to encourage you to explore the area
- buildable blinds at some points of interest
- wounded animal animations, this is something I thought was missing from the last theHunter
CONS:
- not a large variety of equipment
- outfits says they have no effect on whether or not animals can detect you? - whats the point on spending 12k on an outfit then?
- using callers seems to be pretty ineffective
- although they are large, there are only 2 maps
- there is much less to hunt it seems than theHunter
- no dynamic bullet wound textures on the animal
- very poor bullet penetration
- with all its bugs and limited equipment it feels more like an early access or BETA rather than a full game
- the original theHunter set the bar so high that this game pales in comparison, I would still much rather play the original even if this game had 0 bugs
BUG LIST: (after a pretty short time playing)
- MULTIPLE HARD CRASHES!!!
- when starting game, background blur does not go away until openeing a menu
- earned experience/perks/skillpoints are displayed at the top at incorect times
- tracker sometimes displays nothing
- animal tracks sometimes do not show up after resting or fast traveling
- nav points show in multiple directions
- animals run in circles
- animals do not interact with other animals - spooking one type does not seem to spook other animals near them
- after opening a menu, it takes multiple presses of ESC or BACKSPACE to exit the menu
- storage/backpack menu are very glitched
- the same item is displayed multiple times in the store
- animals get stuck on rocks and trees very easily
- player can get stuck in water very easily
- many tracks below the surface of the ground
In summary, I really want to like this game and continue playing but as I said before, the bugs make it too frustrating. The amount of time you must dedicate to a hunt only to be foiled by tracking bugs or hard crashes is absolutely infuriating. While I will not play this for awhile, I do hope the devs fix these problems so that I can come back to a fully functioning and beautiful game to play in the future. I hope this is helpful to some who are on the fence about this game. Buy and play the original theHunter, and wait for them to complete this one.

I’m not going to talk too much about how the game actually plays or what it is because the narrative is what deserves the most praise. However I must get the standard blah blah blah out of the way so, Genre. This game is your standard Cover based 3rd person shooter. You run around place to place, in cover hopefully each time because you die too fast outside of cover, and kill the baddies. Who are the baddies you ask? Well we’ll get to that soon enough. You are allowed to carry 2 guns at a time plus 3 different grenades.
There are some pretty unique mechanics in this game that Yager Studios created more emphasis on in their E3 presentations than the actual story.  Because the player is in Dubai there is lots of sand, Lots of it! During a lot of areas while fighting the enemy you’ll notice some areas that are structurally weak and have lots of sand behind it. Well lo and behold, you can shoot those objects out and sand comes pouring in killing all those around it. Another feature is that of extreme ammo conservation. There are very few bullets lying around so you’ll have to swap weapons often and make every shot count.

Now I feel like gameplay is very generic other than that but I’d like to think unintentionally this adds to the story greatly.  Six Months before the game even starts Dubai gets hit by some of the worst dust storms in history. While some of the powerful elite evacuated, they didn’t tell the other citizens how bad it really got. After a little while the storms got much worse and these people were all stuck there. Colonel Konrad and his 33rd Battalion were ordered to assist in evacuations. After the storms got even worse the 33rd were ordered to abandon the citizens and evacuate themselves, they disobeyed. Because of the Storm wall the dust storms created, it limited any communications and hampered any air travel. Thus anyone in the city was essentially stuck there.
You play as Captain Walker who, after receiving a transmission 2 weeks earlier from Konrad about the failure of the evacuation, is sent in to investigate what happened and rescue any survivors. However what you find there is disturbing for delta squad, Walker’s 3 man unit. At the very beginning of the game you start out with a helicopter battle which ends up being a foreshadowing part of the game.


After that the game starts with Walker and Delta Squad walking into Dubai. They pass what can only be assumed was the convoy that was trying to get out of the city. When they come across a soldier that was shot up, they figure out something went very wrong with the evacuations. You come across insurgents that have held a member of the 33rd hostage. However the insurgents aren’t led by who you would think is leading them. Before starting this game or hearing anything about it I just assumed it was another lets fight terrorists in the desert game. I couldn’t have been any more wrong. Without spoiling too much the enemies you end up facing are that of your own, American Soldiers.

This whole game’s story follows a more modern version of Apocalypse Now and how war can affect the soldier. Many times throughout the game you realize that Walker is succumbing to PTSD and it helps the narrative immensely.  This is where the bad gameplay comes into play. You don’t feel like a super soldier throughout the game, unlike many other games like COD or Battlefield, because they want you to feel how much war sucks. There is a small part in this game that makes Walker snap and I want to talk about it but I’m going to force a little scrolling order to. If you want to skip this spoiler search for #GRAPHICSANDSOUND otherwise keep scrolling.
Now there are going to be several pictures here as I can’t illustrate with words how well done this part was.  White phosphorus is one of the painful weapons the US has ever used and when deployed can cause lots of burns and death. When used with mortars it can rain hellfire down on whoever is below and the deaths are painful. There is a part where a CIA agent tells you to go to “the gate,” however when you come to this point you see it riddled with soldiers. The only way to get to the gate is to use a white phosphorus mortar to kill the soldiers. After much debating on if it was right to use it or not Captain Walker decides to go do it. After this you end up walking through that which you destroyed.


Eventually you come to the end of the area and discovered that the reason the CIA agent wanted you to attack the gate was not to get to some area where all of the soldiers were but to rescue the civilians in the area. Well you just mortared that entire area and with it were the civilians. My personal belief was this was the turning point for Walker where his PTSD took over and he started going crazy. The thought of him kill all of those innocent men, women and children was just too much for his mind to handle. You could also see it in the eyes of his squad mates as they were slowly getting worse as well.  This mission was no longer about rescuing people, this was about revenge.


#GRAPHICSANDSOUND
Now that that depressing bit is over how about the graphics and sound. Now I mentioned that this game’s story takes after Apocalypse Now so does the sound in a way. All of the music is based around the Vietnam era which the same can be said about that movie as well. On top of that the dialog and voice acting is top notch. This game is very pretty and seeing Dubai covered in sand from above in one of its many skyscrapers is really cool. Another nice feature is as the game moves along you can start to see it on Delta squad. They start to lose parts of their cloths and their bodies are beaten up and bloody.
Let’s just say this game is very good and if I could give more marks on my score to story I would. The gameplay, though very generic, can add to the story if you look at it as you aren’t a super soldier. The graphics and sound are also very nice and can really add to the environment of the game. I would like to add that once you finish the game you should definitely check out the tvtropes article about it. It is really long and has several items in it that I didn’t even think about the first time playing the game. Be warned though, you will probably lose at least a day reading that website.

This is my favorite game, and will be for a long time, if not forever. Don't be put off by the graphics. Although it takes a relatively short amount of time to play through the game once, don't be fooled: there's plenty of content you missed. I didn't even know about the True Pacifist route until I had played through the game twice. Even if you choose to play the game the same way every time, you won't be disappointed. At the start of every new playthrough, a "Fun value" (I'm not joking about the name of it) is chosen randomly. Certain numbers will give you some of the more... interesting content that Undertale has to offer.
I haven't even mentioned the characters yet. Each character is very unique, and hard not to love. Even the most villanous of people in this game have a reason to be forgiven. It's obvious Toby Fox put a lot of love into his characters. Speaking of characters, the fun value I spoke of earlier has specific numbers that will hint to the existence of a character you will never meet- W.D. Gaster. Looking into the backstory of Gaster, you can find some pretty dark stuff, if you're into that. Playing the True Pacifist route to see the true lab is probably the easiest way you can do that.
Last but not least, the soundtrack for this game is amazing. Listen to it, and you won't be able to get it out of your head.
I would recommend this game to anyone who likes story focused RPGs. Play it, and you won't regret it (unless you take the Genocide route). This is a game that will change you as a person, and it's most definitely worth $10. Shame on you if you don't buy it.

At first, I only bought this game because i liked the art style, but now, after beating the main story, I absolutely love this game.
To start, the whole concept of "no two castles are the same" is done very well, with defferent rooms challenging different classes, plus there being secrets for characters with specific traits. The enimies are varied and intersting, esepcially the mini-bosses, even though at the beginning, you won't last very long. If you continue playing though, your skills will increase, as well as your armour, runes and stats. The 4 main bosses of each area are fun and are diffuclt, being extremley hard to beat them on your first time ( except the 4th boss, he is too weak to be the 4th area boss.) The controls are very good, with all the key assingments feeling natural. The finally thing is that the music in Rogue Legacy is some of the finest indie music I've heard. Overall, If you are a fan of Metroid, or the Metroid-Vanias, or are looking for a great indie game, this is the game for you. Also, on a side note, my longest living character was a midget, bald, assaisan.

The aesthetic, while simple, is well-executed and unique, while the music is absolutely fantastic and worth purchasing as a soundtrack. Also, don't pick vertigo. NEVER. PICK. VERTIGO.

This game is as enjoyable as it is good looking; exploring dense forest, wavey plains and steep rock faces all in search of that perfect deer. You've got a decent selection of gear to choose from, such as bows and shotguns, bolt action rifles and lever action repeaters, scents and callers and ammuntion focusing on either penetrating thicker hides or causing more damage to the vitals. You'll be using these against several breeds of deer, fox, bears, herds of bison, moose and wild boar, all of which spread over two large open maps. One map takes place in Northern America and the other in rural Germany.
This game still has a few flaws, however. The animal AI can sometimes get caught on the terrian or get stuck in pathing loop. Whenever you go prone, the camera can clip through the ground, revealing the vast nothingness below. The sound glitches and crackles when there is a lot going on.
It you can look passed a few rough edges, you'll have a great hunting game on your hands. I've paid full price and I do not regret waiting for a sale. It you enjoy hunting games or exploring vast open worlds, then I highly recommend this game.

The premise is cool and I was really looking forward to this but... no. It's not like I hate it, nor did I have a terrible experience playing it. Sadly it just doesn't really add up to an enjoyable game.
Let's break this down quickly:
PROS-
- Cool Idea.  3v3 Online Basketball? Check.
- Graphics are decent (Aside from horribly clunky animation)
CONS-
- No controller support.... in a sports game? In 2015?
- No way of remapping keys. (Hope you like arrow key movement.)
- OMG the music gets repetitive, and it never.stops.playing.
- Doesn't feel like a basketball game, just a twitchy "be in the right place and press the right button at the right time" sim.
- Pay to Win
- No full court options.
- Twichy Clitchy Clunky Character animations when playing. (Just look at the gameplay videos)
- User Interface is confusing at best
- No character creation, just customizing existing characters.
I wanted to like this game, I really did. I love basketball, and the thought of a F2P online basketball MMO where you play as a single player sounded awesome.
Sadly after playing the game for about an hour and just closed it and uninstalled. This is NOT the game for you if you have a sports game itch wanting to be scratched. The gameplay basically consists of keeping your character as close the the opponents as possible and then pressing the appropriate button of steal or block at the right time. That's defense. Offense is basically just the opposite, but your steal and block buttons change to pass and shoot. Simple enough, the controls seem streamlined, although awkward. Only one problem... you can't change them. At all. No remapping, no controller support... wtf.
In game your character feels very sluggish when moving... even when you hit your dash key he moves forward about a head's width. Really. The half court isn't bad, but I'd love to see at least an OPTION for full court play. (though with the slow, clunky characters it'd take forever to traverse.) After playing 2 games I wanted to punch the person who made the music. It becomes obnoxious very quickly. There's about 3 songs, that just loop...
All in all I can't say I enjoyed playing this. It doesn't feel like a basketball game, and it's shortcomings, especially the controls, really kill it. (Some people may argue you can use third party programs to make a controller work with the game, but that does NOT excuse the game for not having any controller or remapping capability itself.)
TLDR:
If you want to play a fun basketball game, go play something else.

Where do I start with this game?
It is... wonderful. Rogue Legacy is the sort of modern retro classic that dreams are made of.
Entering the looming castle, unaware what awakes you inside, it quickly becomes apparent that this is not the simple 16-bit platformer it first appears. It cleverly blends genres, from roguelikes to RPGs to traditional platformers and bullet hell shooters, into a consistent and dangerously addictive blend of beautiful originality that feels fresh yet instantly familiar. It's also constantly and abundantly rewarding, making sure your many, many deaths feel worthwhile instead of frustrating as you continually rush back into the castle hoping this run will bring greater victories.
The concept is deceptively simple. You are the descendant of a dying king, embarking on a quest to find what lays inside this castle that will allegedly cure the king. But within moments you are struck down long before you can make it anywhere near the deepest layers of the castle. Thankfully you were rather, ahem, "friendly" in your life and know it's up to your incredibly large number of offspring to take up the sword in your place.
This then leads into RL's broad progression system, which incorporates a level of randomness while also allowing you to level your hero to better confront the monsters within the castle. No two children are ever the same, with each being a random combination of a huge amount of classes, traits, and special items they can use. For instance you could be a giant colorblind mage, or an ectomorphic shinobi that gets sent flying with every hit. It's a tad disappointing that some of the traits are merely for laughs (for instance one that causes you to pass gas with every jump), but there are enough that drastically alter the gameplay for it to be considered a success that plays largely into how you intend to approach a given run.
These runs are what I love most about RL, because they take the most compelling elements of roguelikes (such as randomized level designs), and combines them with a more approachable leveling system and patterns that can be learned and mastered. Although you lose all your gold each time you enter the castle (at least at first), what you manage to attain can then be used to buy better gear, equip skill runes, or level your skills and unlock more classes. This leverages the difficulty away from impossibly hardcore, into something far less daunting. I constantly like like I was making progress even when I died, and it's this constant drive that makes finally overcoming a particularly challenging boss or section so satisfying. Overcoming RL's obstacles was easily some of the most rewarding moments I've ever had while playing a game, and finally beating it felt like the epic accomplishment it ought to have.
Don't take this to mean RL is an easy game, because rest assure you will get pounded into the dirt more times than you can count. But it's not an insurmountable challenge, and it's in this that I feel it most succeeds at turning hardcore design philosophies into something everyone can enjoy. It makes the difficulty something you can realistically see yourself beating if you just try one more time; upgrade one more stat; find one more blueprint. It's the best sort of "hard" game that knows when to reward you and when to hold you up, only long enough to keep the hunger for victory ever present and relief just out of reach.
Even though I've conquered the castle, beaten the bosses, and discovered what lays within I don't see myself putting Rogue Legacy down anytime soon, and that more than anything is what sets it apart as a brilliant experience that I want to play over and over again. Every element of its design is polished to a glorious sheen, glued together by it's fantastic artwork and mind blowing soundtrack, and it's relentless attempts to empower you while always leaving you something more to accomplish. Everything about it is just freaking rad, and hopefully you realized that already and are now  metaphorically running to pick it up.

Prison Architect - Strategy-Management.
If no one elses reviews, or any gameplay videos (Which we are by far not lacking them with this being the second most lets played videogame, first being minecraft) If they dont describe the game enough for you or your completely bewildered by it. In short your going to build a prison from the ground up.
Including all guard routeens, all kitchen duties and which sort of prisoners you want. With you being the maker of it all.
Positives - great gameplay, it might be in alpha, but i am loving the gameplay, there really is not much i can say thats wrong on this front. If you have ever played dungeon keeper, or theme hospital (from bullfrog) this is based off them.
Negatives - many will go "upgrade your system" or go, you shouldnt play it because of the specs, i run on a laptop (6 years old) it has over-heating issues (thanks to my mom smoking) which the laptops welded itself shut so i cannot open it. the specs of the system are 2.0 (processor speed) 2 gig of RAM and hard-drive of 120 gig. the game runs choppy, Which it should considering the "minimum" or recommended specs are 2.4-3.0 (processor speed) and 4 gig of ram.
What i would say is, if you have double what my specs are, you can run it flawlessly. Half of it if you ask me is RAM, the other half is processor speed (Which i have tried a second computer, it runs worse on that as it has 1 gig of RAM, and 2.4 processor speed)
Music - there really is not any until theres a riot, So feel free to put on your own music in the background (Which i recommend)
the last negative i have is the price of it. £20, which is cheap by most games today, but it is actually the "name in game" "bonus" you can get which costs £15 quid, £15 quid for a prisoner named after you (you actually get to pick the name) who will appear in the final game. Granted that is quite a big thing, but you seriously have to be commited to the game to get that upgrade due to the price.
Bottom line - If you want a strategy-esk management game, this is a worthwhile purchase. The price is quite high (For name in game at £15) But you literally get a prisoner within the game. Named whatever you want, have whatever bio you want (within reason) and that is quite awesome. The game plays well, but first time players will struggle to get started. I remember the first prison i tried to make, i spent around 3 in-game hours before i had even placed foundation because i was not sure where to put anything.
My recommendations - Get the game if you have watched any footage and your fine with it being in alpha and you think it looks decent and worth your money (when it comes out you will get a full version for free) i would stick with the first version, UNLESS theres a deal where you get the "name in game" for a bit cheaper or unless you are commited to the game. Only try running the game if the specs of your system are 2.0 processor speed, and 2-3 gig of RAM Minimum.
Anything above that the game will run smoother and will be more enjoyable, Given it is alpha that may change and they can optimise it to run better on lower spec computers. (Which i can hope they do) Its worth the money, and the name in games only worth it if you really enjoy the game and want to give a little more to the developers for the title.

So, guess it's time for me to leave a negative review on this game, too.
I loved the mod. I really did, but it felt like it was build on an old, outdated and unfitting engine. The movement felt odd and not quite 'fluent', zombies were glichy like hell, 90% of the houses in the mod were unaccessable, you needed to reload your hatched. There were a lot of things that needed improvement, so I really was happy when they announced the standalone of DayZ. I hoped all these minor issues would be addressed to make this game even more fun ... oh how wrong I was.
I tried to play the standalone a couple of times in a period of roughly 2 years and this game seems to just get worse everytime i try to play it again.
After all this time in the standalone
- Zombies will still glitch through terrain and are nearly impossible to hit due to their buggy movement. But don't worry, you might never see one, because the game is so terribly optimized it can't handle more than 3 zombies on the map at once.
- Loot is rare. Food is scarce. In this point DayZ is truely a survival game, because I spent most of my time just trying to stay alive. There might be a single can of Canneloni in a supermarked at best, which won't even feed you enough to compensate the time you spent trying to find the right tool in your inventory to open it. Drinks have been that rare in my previous games, that i tried to drink screenwash to stay alive, because it is literally the only liquid I found after scavanging houses for hours.
- The game will constantly tell you how awful your health is. "I feel hungry", "I feel thristy", "I am bleeding", but then you suddenly drop dead after a singe "I am freezing" on a beautiful sunny day with a padded jacked, padded boots and a nice wool hat.
- The net code is sh*ttty. You can shoot a whole magazine at an afk dude without hitting him a single time, while other players can shoot you sometimes before even moving around the corner. People often run on the spot or just teleport around, because the server is lagging.
- The game is awfully optimized leaving me with low fps and freezes with a 1080Ti, a SSD, 32 GB RAM and a 3,6GHz Processor.
- Neither the features promised on launch nor the features from the mod at the time of lauch have been implemtented yet. Dunno about vehicles, but I still didn't find a single tent, nor have i ever heared of any of these giant underground bases you should be able to dig.
- The movement still feels odd. Play something like battlefield and then dayZ and just prone, crouch and jump a few times. You'll soon realize how fluent this feels in bf compared to the robotic movement of DayZ. Moving over a fence in bf happens for me without even thinking about it, while the process in DayZ is like: "Ok there is a fence, slow down now" <move finger away from run key> ... Character slows down "Okay now stand up" <Press C> Character does a stand up animaton. "Okay, now go over the fence" <Press V> Character begins his 20 second 'climb' animation, but is gliched back, because you didn't move him close enough to the fence. "Oh great, let's do it again" <Move character closer to the fence" Cracking noice "Ah darn. Why are my feet broken now?"
- Other players are not a fun and challanging encounter, but just reset you back to 0 once you found this one fresh tomato to sature you for another half an hour. But hey, at least your game isn't in such a depressing gray anymore.
Once in a while I come back to DayZ to see weakly update logs, which really makes me feel like there is still progress in developement, but it feel like the game is constantly getting worse, so seriously, what are these devs doing?

I hoped all these minor issues would be addressed to make this game even more fun ... oh how wrong I was.
I tried to play the standalone a couple of times in a period of roughly 2 years and this game seems to just get worse everytime i try to play it again.
After all this time in the standalone
- Zombies will still glitch through terrain and are nearly impossible to hit due to their buggy movement. But don't worry, you might never see one, because the game is so terribly optimized it can't handle more than 3 zombies on the map at once.
- Loot is rare. Food is scarce. In this point DayZ is truely a survival game, because I spent most of my time just trying to stay alive. There might be a single can of Canneloni in a supermarked at best, which won't even feed you enough to compensate the time you spent trying to find the right tool in your inventory to open it. Drinks have been that rare in my previous games, that i tried to drink screenwash to stay alive, because it is literally the only liquid I found after scavanging houses for hours.
- The game will constantly tell you how awful your health is. "I feel hungry", "I feel thristy", "I am bleeding", but then you suddenly drop dead after a singe "I am freezing" on a beautiful sunny day with a padded jacked, padded boots and a nice wool hat.
- The net code is sh*ttty. You can shoot a whole magazine at an afk dude without hitting him a single time, while other players can shoot you sometimes before even moving around the corner. People often run on the spot or just teleport around, because the server is lagging.
- The game is awfully optimized leaving me with low fps and freezes with a 1080Ti, a SSD, 32 GB RAM and a 3,6GHz Processor.
- Neither the features promised on launch nor the features from the mod at the time of lauch have been implemtented yet. Dunno about vehicles, but I still didn't find a single tent, nor have i ever heared of any of these giant underground bases you should be able to dig.
- The movement still feels odd. Play something like battlefield and then dayZ and just prone, crouch and jump a few times. You'll soon realize how fluent this feels in bf compared to the robotic movement of DayZ. Moving over a fence in bf happens for me without even thinking about it, while the process in DayZ is like: "Ok there is a fence, slow down now" <move finger away from run key> ... Character slows down "Okay now stand up" <Press C> Character does a stand up animaton. "Okay, now go over the fence" <Press V> Character begins his 20 second 'climb' animation, but is gliched back, because you didn't move him close enough to the fence. "Oh great, let's do it again" <Move character closer to the fence" Cracking noice "Ah darn. Why are my feet broken now?"
- Other players are not a fun and challanging encounter, but just reset you back to 0 once you found this one fresh tomato to sature you for another half an hour. But hey, at least your game isn't in such a depressing gray anymore.
Once in a while I come back to DayZ to see weakly update logs, which really makes me feel like there is still progress in developement, but it feel like the game is constantly getting worse, so seriously, what are these devs doing?

“Only the living and the dead now. No egos.”
Mad Max is an imaginative action-packed open-world experience. It feeds on the mythology left behind by George Miller, and it successfully brings the Wasteland to gaming, both visually and spatially. Racing and race-battling has never been so dynamic and thrilling, and melee combat is as polished as a combo-oriented gameplay could deliver. The core of the quest design revolves around upgrading a "mystical" car named Magnum Opus, and delving into revenge against Scabrous Scrotus, the archenemy who initially assaults Max and his Interceptor, leaving the drifter for dead in the hot white desert. Thematically, pride and an apparent sense of dignity are still present in the narrative. Max refuses to eat “long pig” (basically, cooked human flesh), and instead feeds on maggots from human carcasses. Thirsty wanderers can be given precious water from the protagonist’s canteen, and a feeling of gratitude is promptly served. Stronghold upgrade projects raise the morale of the inhabitants, and their impression of Max. The Wasteland is represented as a place suited for brutality and survival, but also hope – albeit often romantically portrayed.
As regards story and plotline, there is not much to be said. Well, if you are interested in everything Mad Max, you probably know that a complex and foregrounded chain of narratives is not the franchise’s emphasis (especially if considering the latest film). The game follows that premise. What it does offer is a myriad of apocalyptic motifs, from the re-domestication of nature, to the emptiness of Earth’s post-nuclear shell, to the nostalgic grief over a long-dead world. Such motifs could inspire much more immersion were it not for Max’s always-melodramatic lines when collectable pictures from before the fall pop up. Additionally, the figure of Scabrous Scrotus is forgettable at best, and just a sootier and bossier version of Rictus Erectus.
Characters are often tragicomic representations of eschatological personalities: they are usually on the edge of their beliefs. A fume-induced sadist, a pyromaniacal prophet, a bloodthirsty tyrant, a delusional road rider. Hope and Glory show little promise from start, and never actually manage to entice any significance or emotional attachment from the player, even towards the end. Chumbucket’s permanent company may intimidate the player at first, but with some time, they will find that his persona is an inseparable part of the game, an inseparable part of Max’s quest. There were moments when I was driving along in an enemy car and caught myself missing his very personal remarks about the landscape, the Magnum Opus, the dangers around, about everything worth remarking about in the Wasteland. The rest of the characters are interesting and colourful individuals that show precisely how they have survived the wretched world for so long under those sorry conditions, exhibiting perfect doses of leadership, insanity, and sarcasm.
There were some other wee things that I could not avoid feeling annoyed by: no matter how you approach the open world configuration of the game, you will never complete a task only once. Be ready to scavenge repeatedly, fight repeatedly, rescue and explode repeatedly. Repetition is not necessarily a compulsory aspect in the exploration of the map, and it may not be a problem for completionists, but it is there to fatten playthrough time. Also, ignore what the first shots of the game tell you about the scarcity of Max’s basic resources: there will be plenty of them, more than enough to get you by until the end. You will most probably never run out of water or fuel if you look decently enough. Scrap can be an annoyance, but only if spent away carelessly or if the urge to scavenge seldom arises during your gaming sessions. The structure of quest design is much standardised, oftentimes a list of identical objectives to be ticked off one by one across the available map, until the quest is finally over. Although this works in perfect unison with the background story of these quests, it does not help much to have that layout, considering the game’s already repetitive nature of open-world tasks.
All these aforementioned things – good or bad – are not even close to expressing precisely how much fun I had playing Mad Max. Only when you hop in the Magnum Opus, build it up little by little, and scavenge the entirety of the massive game world, will you feel that the hours you spent were worth it. However, I have to warn those who are not fond of open-world "collectathons" to think twice and watch some vids before getting hold of this game.

Loved every minute of it! And the scenery is gorgeous if you can handle the graphics. The gameplay is sort of a Far Cry style where the territories are controlled by the tyrant, and you can free territories by capturing camps. Also gave me a Wind Waker-ish feel traveling across the sea of sand from place to place. You gain scrap and parts along the way to upgrade your car, the Magnum Opus; and yourself, Max. You can also use any other car you find in the game, but sadly no bikes or war rigs. This is only singleplayer, however you can compare race times with friends. On-foot gameplay is in third-person, but there is the (suicidal) option to use first-person while driving. Vehicle combat feels great! Fast-paced and intense like in a movie. and the on-foot combat looks and feels just as brutal and intense! There are a few bugs like occasionally having the cursor stick around after being in the menu which can be easily fixed by quickly opening and closing the menu; another is very rarely (twice in 92 hours for me) being stuck in the menu, where I would have to turn off the game. This wasn't a big problem though since the game frequently autosaves. I've heard complaints about the game feeling repetitive, which I guess just depends on the person because I never got tired of exploding cars, chases, shooting, looting, surviving storms, and just exploring. This has got to be one of the best, most annoying games I've played in recent years. The hunting experience is fantastic and the gameplay is a joy, however the constant 'quality of life' issues just make it a hassle to play.
The maps are huge and detailed however movement speed is glacial and there are no vehicles. Fast travel is limited to a handful of spaced out locations that must be unlocked by spending hours walking to them.
Huge amounts of grinding are required to unlocked better equipment, for some bizarre reason the developer has felt the need to restrict players as to their style of play, perhaps to add longevity, but I would have appreciated the option to just unlock everything, after all, I am the player and it is my game.
There are some bizarre design choices, like the 'consecutive harvest' feature. In short, if you want to get high scores for your harvests you need to rack up multiple harvests beforehand for no apparent reason.
The UI is awkward and unclear especially re movement speeds and noise as well as visibility (apparently using a controller is the best way to play, unacceptable for a PC game).
Bugs are frequent, although the developers are working hard to iron them out, however as plenty of other reviewers have stated, the game should not have been released in the state that it is (or at least, for the price that it is).
There is no steam workshop/mod support that I can see. This would be by far the easiest way to start fixing bugs and letting players customise their experience, and is the lifeblood of PC gaming imho that adds years to the longevity of any game.

A very good 3rd person shooter, with an interesting story to tell. While on the surface it may seem like just another cover based shooter, with a modern combat focus, the story quickly shows it to be much more than that. It's hard to say too much without giving away the plot line, but along the way you will be faced with moral choices, ones that may stay with you as you play through the game and reach the (I think) excellent conclusion.
Visually the game is very nice, good character models, very nice atmospheric & particle effects ensure that firefights get very intense. The levels are very detailed, although as typical in these games, it is not an open field, you are basically guided through a fixed path. That said, in some arena based areas you do have a choice of which way to tackle a situation.
Lots of weapons to choose from, meaning you can always look around for your favourites and alter your play style based on what you are using. Your team mates have reasonable AI, which doesn't hinder you as you play. I did not try playing MP, so my opinion is purely based on the SP campaign.
So all in all, a very good game, and worthy of your time. Please don't disregard this game based purely on the fact that it seems like "another military cover based shooter". The story draws you in, and gets progressively stranger as time goes on, and is definitely not just a "by the numbers, kill the bad guy" scenario. Again, without giving away any part of the story, the game also has replay value, I will be going back to this one.

The environment, Dubai covered in sand, is interesting and the game has a dark feel to it. Findings and other details point to people being caught up in a terrible event, and the shouts of your opponents as you fight is excellent and give them a human touch. At its best Spec Ops should not be treated as a mindless run and gun, but you should take in the sights, the events occuring around you, and the people involved. What is happening, what has happened, and what is your part in all of it.
As a PC-player the controls takes some getting used (especially the cover system) to as they are built for console, and the core gameplay itself comes across as a bit bland. That said, the gunplay itself is satisfying. The PvP multiplayer is dead as of today, and the coop part is limited to 4 maps, each with its own objective.
Don't let the shoot-by-wire put you off, this is a gem hidden in the rough. Few games swim up from the generic pool and leave you wondering...

I neglected this title for a long time, because it looked like Yet Another 2D Indie Pixelated Platformer, but with some permadeath and the sticker "roguelike" (as if that isn't stamped on everything these days).
But I regret that i waited so long. The game sucked me in and held me for an entire weekend. It took about 12 hours to finish, and I expect there'll be 10-12 more in the "+" campaign.
It's fun and fast, without throwing cheapshots around. Enemies are predictable, but finding ways to weave around groups of them in order to kill them is not predictable.
The death adds to the game. Sure you die, but it's not frustrating to die. Only after death can you use the gold, runes, and blueprints you got last round. It's bitter to die, but at least you get to have a bit of fun afterwards, by immediately spending your cash. It takes the edge off of death, and creates a cycle of adventuring -> dying -> upgrading -> saying "just one more" and repeating the process.
It's also a varied experience, forcing you to take different classes, dealing with random traits, a different castle each run, and fresh enemy placement. It may not hold up after 50 hours of play, but it's sure satisfying to step foot inside the castle and think "how am i going to do it *this* time?"
And of course, the story ties it together. Death of a character is just one generation, his descendents carry on his legacy. The end boss is a prince who was on the same quest as you were, and the castle is an extension of the madness of the final boss. It's a thin story that could have been slapped on in an hour, but the fact that it explains why the game has this death system (and what it's achieving by having it) makes me feel good about it. If you like when a story glues the game together, you'll enjoy this one.

Hello :) I bought this game in the year 2013.
Over the years, SCS Software, spent time and efforts in:
---> Game development
1. Renewed graphics (driving looks more realistic than it was with first versions of the game)
2. Better AI Traffic management
3. Better weather simulation
4. Rebuilt menu interface
5. Introduction to World of Trucks
---> Trucks
1. Obtained licenses for all the trucks in game (Scania, Volvo, Iveco, DAF, Mercedes-Benz...)
2. Fixed truck handling and added more realistic engine sounds for most trucks
3. Added more trucks for free (in November 2017 they added the New Scania Euro6 series)
4. Added more trailer options
As I said in my 2015 review, this game is constantly updated and on the SCS Software Blog you always find a list of the "most interesting things added" in every update they release for the game.
This is not something you can find with every game.
Talking about the game itself... well... it's not a game, it's a SIMULATOR, it's made for people who actually like driving a truck (or giving a chance) across Europe. You start the game with no trucks and no garages. You have to start working for other people delivering trailers with THEIR trucks, until you spare a little bit of money you can use to get your first truck, your first garage, and then.... another truck, your first employee... until you let your business grow up :)
Of course, if you want to immediately get money to buy your first truck, you can deal with the Bank that will offer you loans up to 400.000€, but be careful and check out the interests % ;)
This is an endless game. You play it, you enjoy it, you get bored of it, you leave it... but then after weeks, months... you want to play it again :)

However, you will notice that none of these reviews will tell you how the gameplay actually feels. There's a good reason for that. It's because it's downright atrocious. Response time is terrible. Pressing either the accelerator or going in reverse will either not move you at all or send you sailing. The camera angles are abysmal and unhelpful in the least. The control may be a little bit better if you use a controller, but not everyone has a PC controller or is willing to get one for just one game. As it stands, I only tried this game with the keyboard and mouse/keyboard combination. Neither were the least bit competent.

“Only the living and the dead now. No egos.”
Mad Max is an imaginative action-packed open-world experience. It feeds on the mythology left behind by George Miller, and it successfully brings the Wasteland to gaming, both visually and spatially. Racing and race-battling has never been so dynamic and thrilling, and melee combat is as polished as a combo-oriented gameplay could deliver. The core of the quest design revolves around upgrading a "mystical" car named Magnum Opus, and delving into revenge against Scabrous Scrotus, the archenemy who initially assaults Max and his Interceptor, leaving the drifter for dead in the hot white desert. Thematically, pride and an apparent sense of dignity are still present in the narrative. Max refuses to eat “long pig” (basically, cooked human flesh), and instead feeds on maggots from human carcasses. Thirsty wanderers can be given precious water from the protagonist’s canteen, and a feeling of gratitude is promptly served. Stronghold upgrade projects raise the morale of the inhabitants, and their impression of Max. The Wasteland is represented as a place suited for brutality and survival, but also hope – albeit often romantically portrayed.
As regards story and plotline, there is not much to be said. Well, if you are interested in everything Mad Max, you probably know that a complex and foregrounded chain of narratives is not the franchise’s emphasis (especially if considering the latest film). The game follows that premise. What it does offer is a myriad of apocalyptic motifs, from the re-domestication of nature, to the emptiness of Earth’s post-nuclear shell, to the nostalgic grief over a long-dead world. Such motifs could inspire much more immersion were it not for Max’s always-melodramatic lines when collectable pictures from before the fall pop up. Additionally, the figure of Scabrous Scrotus is forgettable at best, and just a sootier and bossier version of Rictus Erectus.
Characters are often tragicomic representations of eschatological personalities: they are usually on the edge of their beliefs. A fume-induced sadist, a pyromaniacal prophet, a bloodthirsty tyrant, a delusional road rider. Hope and Glory show little promise from start, and never actually manage to entice any significance or emotional attachment from the player, even towards the end. Chumbucket’s permanent company may intimidate the player at first, but with some time, they will find that his persona is an inseparable part of the game, an inseparable part of Max’s quest. There were moments when I was driving along in an enemy car and caught myself missing his very personal remarks about the landscape, the Magnum Opus, the dangers around, about everything worth remarking about in the Wasteland. The rest of the characters are interesting and colourful individuals that show precisely how they have survived the wretched world for so long under those sorry conditions, exhibiting perfect doses of leadership, insanity, and sarcasm.
There were some other wee things that I could not avoid feeling annoyed by: no matter how you approach the open world configuration of the game, you will never complete a task only once. Be ready to scavenge repeatedly, fight repeatedly, rescue and explode repeatedly. Repetition is not necessarily a compulsory aspect in the exploration of the map, and it may not be a problem for completionists, but it is there to fatten playthrough time. Also, ignore what the first shots of the game tell you about the scarcity of Max’s basic resources: there will be plenty of them, more than enough to get you by until the end. You will most probably never run out of water or fuel if you look decently enough. Scrap can be an annoyance, but only if spent away carelessly or if the urge to scavenge seldom arises during your gaming sessions. The structure of quest design is much standardised, oftentimes a list of identical objectives to be ticked off one by one across the available map, until the quest is finally over. Although this works in perfect unison with the background story of these quests, it does not help much to have that layout, considering the game’s already repetitive nature of open-world tasks.
All these aforementioned things – good or bad – are not even close to expressing precisely how much fun I had playing Mad Max. Only when you hop in the Magnum Opus, build it up little by little, and scavenge the entirety of the massive game world, will you feel that the hours you spent were worth it. However, I have to warn those who are not fond of open-world "collectathons" to think twice and watch some vids before getting hold of this game.

Dont know what to write, so I will write a recipie for pancakes.
ingredients
100g plain flour
2 eggs
300ml semi-skimmed milk
1 tbsp sunflower oil or vegetable, plus extra for frying
pinch salt
Method
Blending in the flour: Put the flour and a pinch of salt into a large mixing bowl and make a well in the centre. Crack the eggs into the middle, then pour in about 50ml milk and 1 tbsp oil. Start whisking from the centre, gradually drawing the flour into the eggs, milk and oil. Once all the flour is incorporated, beat until you have a smooth, thick paste. Add a little more milk if it is too stiff to beat.
Finishing the batter: Add a good splash of milk and whisk to loosen the thick batter. While still whisking, pour in a steady stream of the remaining milk. Continue pouring and whisking until you have a batter that is the consistency of slightly thick single cream. Traditionally, people would say to now leave the batter for 30 mins, to allow the starch in the flour to swell, but there’s no need.
Getting the right thickness: Heat the pan over a moderate heat, then wipe it with oiled kitchen paper. Ladle some batter into the pan, tilting the pan to move the mixture around for a thin and even layer. Quickly pour any excess batter into a jug, return the pan to the heat, then leave to cook, undisturbed, for about 30 secs. Pour the excess batter from the jug back into the mixing bowl. If the pan is the right temperature, the pancake should turn golden underneath after about 30 secs and will be ready to turn.
Flipping pancakes: Hold the pan handle, ease a fish slice under the pancake, then quickly lift and flip it over. Make sure the pancake is lying flat against base of the pan with no folds, then cook for another 30 secs before turning out onto a warm plate. Continue with the rest of the batter, serving them as you cook or stack onto a plate. You can freeze the pancakes for 1 month, wrapped in cling film or make them up to a day ahead.
