This is both a great game, and kind of meh at the same time.
My first impressions of the game is its beautiful - followed by - "♥♥♥♥ me, this games setting has me hunting in europe? i've only ever hunted in the backwoods of the USA.... wonder what this will be like?" followed quickly by a murdering rampage though the hills, :D.  in the span of 100 minutes I killed 5 Roe deer, 2 foxes, and 1 fallow deer.  But thats where the game starts to break down.
The Good - This game is great for casual hunting, and by that i mean its a great pick up and shoot stuff hunter - not  much required in the way of getting started. You are given a decent set up right from the get go, you arn't required to buy hunting licenses or anything like that, and since the game is set up as a Arcade shooter - you can kill as manythings as you want - no bag limits :D.
The Bad - For anyone looking for a more realistic hunting game this isn't going to be your bread and butter. This game is very beautiful however, it is not a deer hunter replacement. I never had to sight my gun, prep for my trip, buy hunting licenses, there was nothing in this game that made it feel like anything more than a casual arcade mode hunting game. Deer and wildlife are extreamly easy to track from the very begining since tracks light up and glow for you to track the game.
The Ugly -  Its a bit buggy in a few areas - I got attacked by a rock and lost half my health walking down a steep hill :P. Another kind of disapointing feature is the scorecard system - For example, I shot a deer and missed its lung (the hold your breath is extramly short starting out) and shot the deer in the stomach - it didnt go down right away as to be expected and ran off and died around 200 meters away. Upon collecting the "Trophy" A score card is presented and then I was given a rather high score for botching this kill. Most anyone who hunts knows this was not a clean kill - the animal,  if this were in real life,  suffered immensly before dying of bloodloss and exhuastion.  I further tested this out and shot a deer resting in the face - Bang "trick shot" achievement - thats when it set in for me that this game was not going to come close to being a deer hunter replacment.
All in all though - its a great game that seems to have a team deadicated to fixing the game and improving it - its just not going to scratch the itch of being a real hunting simulator to get you through waiting for the next hunting season.

What can I even say about this game? It's amazing, really.
Rogue Legacy takes the best elements from games such as The Binding of Isaac (the random layouts and permadeath) and mashes them up with a Metroidvania sense of exploration and platforming as well.
At points, it can feel challenging, but you never feel like you can't get through a section no matter what you do. You can always level up your various abilities and stats to help you out. Another potential option is to change up your armor and rune sets, which can be necessary against certain bosses. If none of those work, however, you just need to git gud.
I'm joking, of course - skill, however, is quite an important factor in this game as well. Which is always a good thing.
Overall, Rogue Legacy is an interesting game in how it combines various elements of (seemingly unrelated) games and genres, ultimately running away with a solid concept that never feels like it was wasted or unpolished.

This wasn't a game I was watching very closely at all, but once I saw a sale on it I grabbed it and haven't looked back.
In a summation, you're basically looking at a GTA game with a Red Faction: Guerilla setting and Batman Arkham Asylum style fighting. That is to say, an open world game with missions in a post apocolyptic desert... with Batman fighting.
If you like cars, upgrading them to become death machines and then putting said death machines to use, then this is the game for you! I really got into cruising around and harpooning towers to bring them down and crashing into convoys. I was a little less thrilled with the on foot combat in the game (think Batman: Arkham Asylum) and not because it's bad but just that it gets a little old after 30 hours of gameplay. However, the car stuff was always fun and I can see myself returning to it just to take out buzzards and raiders!
There is some glitchy stuff going on in the game as well. Things like enemy cars disappearing and UI statusing disappearing (Like when the game tells you that you 100% looted an area, those messages went away). However, this was very few and far between.
The game also feels kind of janky at times. It's odd design decisions too, stuff that can be remedied. Like only being given the option to refuel your car or the air balloon on certain sides of it? Some times damage to your car and other cars doesn't register at all. Also, the controls are a bit wonky to get used to at first. But again, these are things that didn't bother me anymore after I played the game more and got absorbed into it.
So there are a few things to get used to in Mad Max but I feel the positives far outweigh the negatives. I Definitely recommended this for the open world/car game fans out there. I think you'll find a lot to like here!

This is both a great game, and kind of meh at the same time.
My first impressions of the game is its beautiful - followed by - "♥♥♥♥ me, this games setting has me hunting in europe? i've only ever hunted in the backwoods of the USA.... wonder what this will be like?" followed quickly by a murdering rampage though the hills, :D.  in the span of 100 minutes I killed 5 Roe deer, 2 foxes, and 1 fallow deer.  But thats where the game starts to break down.
The Good - This game is great for casual hunting, and by that i mean its a great pick up and shoot stuff hunter - not  much required in the way of getting started. You are given a decent set up right from the get go, you arn't required to buy hunting licenses or anything like that, and since the game is set up as a Arcade shooter - you can kill as manythings as you want - no bag limits :D.
The Bad - For anyone looking for a more realistic hunting game this isn't going to be your bread and butter. This game is very beautiful however, it is not a deer hunter replacement. I never had to sight my gun, prep for my trip, buy hunting licenses, there was nothing in this game that made it feel like anything more than a casual arcade mode hunting game. Deer and wildlife are extreamly easy to track from the very begining since tracks light up and glow for you to track the game.
The Ugly -  Its a bit buggy in a few areas - I got attacked by a rock and lost half my health walking down a steep hill :P. Another kind of disapointing feature is the scorecard system - For example, I shot a deer and missed its lung (the hold your breath is extramly short starting out) and shot the deer in the stomach - it didnt go down right away as to be expected and ran off and died around 200 meters away. Upon collecting the "Trophy" A score card is presented and then I was given a rather high score for botching this kill. Most anyone who hunts knows this was not a clean kill - the animal,  if this were in real life,  suffered immensly before dying of bloodloss and exhuastion.  I further tested this out and shot a deer resting in the face - Bang "trick shot" achievement - thats when it set in for me that this game was not going to come close to being a deer hunter replacment.
All in all though - its a great game that seems to have a team deadicated to fixing the game and improving it - its just not going to scratch the itch of being a real hunting simulator to get you through waiting for the next hunting season.

I have a hard time believing that this game is still in Alpha. It plays better than many Strategy-Sims that have a full release. Not to mention that most of the updates, which occur once a month, change the gameplay in very significant ways. The draw of this game for this game varies for many people as well. The Alpha 25 build of the game has greatly impacted the way the game is played by making prisoners much more dynamic and adding "New ways to fail".
My only gripe with the game is that the method in which you report bugs is dysfunctional at best. You can't do it from the Devs website, and have to go to a different website. After spending a half-hour posting a bug report, including recording footage of the bug and attaching it, I was very frustrated when the website timed out on me... 5 times.

In its current state, I think Prison Architect is quite expensive for what you get. But it is indeed a good game. As of Alpha 25, maintaining a functioning prison where anything can go wrong is pretty fun. The chaos that could break out in a matter of seconds requires quick player response to the issue, and can lead to some amusing situations which the player can learn from to improve their facility. The want to expand is always present, and it is likely some players will create prisons that are too big for their own good. The attention to details (education programs, the needs system, contraband, etc) continues to surprise me. The fact you are able to tell where contraband comes from, how it got in, where it went, and where it was found is just one of many of the detailed features that can affect the build of your prison. All this said, it is pretty buggy (it is an alpha after all), but I reccomend picking it up when it is discounted if you are at all interested.

This review is a bit biased as I'm a huge Mad Max fan.
That said, this game is still amazing. Maybe you've read other reviews that say it's the most open world open world action adventure action adventure trope game. Yes, it's open world, yes, it's an action adventure game, but let me ask those reviewers one thing? How else would you have preferred a Mad Max game? The primary focus in Mad Max is vehicular combat across the vast open terrain of the wasteland. Yes, Max has free flow combat similar to other WB published games in the past few years, but he isn't Batman or the guy from Shadow of Mordor. Max is, to an extent, a regular ol' dude with some emotional issues pertaining to his past and the fact that he is a shell of his former self. Point is, Avalanche made the Mad Max game that Mad Max fans had always wanted; so f * * k the reviewers that say the game is repetitive or lacking. Have they even seen a Mad Max film? The stories aren't exactly as complex as Metal Gear Solid, which I think is another reason why Mad Max is being overlooked, the fact that MGSV came out the same day. The Mad Max stories are rather simple with an even simpler context, global economic crisises and nuclear warfare.
Now that I got my little rant out of the way, I can actually talk about the game. Max is driving his beloved Interceptor through the Wasteland, trying to reach the Plains of Silence in hopes of finding a more civilized society. Unfortunately, Scaborous Scrotus, son of Immortan Joe, succeeds in vehicular combat with his mighty Land Mower and Max is forced to jump out, ending up fighting Scrotus himself. After apparently killing Scrotus, Max finds himself somewhere unknown and befriends Scrotus' dog. Together, they find Chumbucket, a hunchback mechanic. This is where the story really takes off as Chum and Max plot to build a Magnum Opus, a car better, stronger, and superior in each way to the Interceptor. Chum and Max travel throughout the Wasteland, assisting faction leaders and progressing throughout the story to upgrade car parts and Max's own gear. The story is actually more interesting than just that, but I don't wanna spoil it.
Gameplay, as noted in my rant earlier, is similar to recent action adventure games. Besides comparing it to recent WB games, I could also compare it to Assassin's Creed: Brotherhood, as you invade camps (Forts) and complete a primary objective in order to take control of it where your allies will then be there. Also the strongholds where you meet various "community" leaders. You do favors for these leaders (i.e. side missions that actually have plot) and are then able to upgrade these strongholds by collecting project parts at various scavenging locations or camps scattered throughout the wasteland. These locations could be massive forts or hidden caves, or underground passages below a hatch. There is so much to do in this game, it can actually be overwhelming. Anyway, I wanna focus on the vehicular combat gameplay, I shouldn't have to explain what action adventure is. Vehicular combat is pretty rare in modern games, so having vehicle combat in Mad Max was astounding. You can use side burners, t-bone or rail cars head on, use a harpoon to rip off doors and tires and bumpers, or the thunderpoon to blow stuff up. And then the beloved shotgun, which can be used for a variety of things while driving. Not to mention that much of this will be occurring at high speeds. Basically, Avalanche did a splendid job with the vehicular combat.
Graphics; jeez. I could tell you about how great and stunning the graphics are, because they are. But I won't bore you with that, instead, I just want to mention that this game is clearly set sometime after Thunderdome as there is sand practically everywhere. In the first two films, we got to see a side of Australia comparable to Arizona where there was a lot of small cacti life and dry ground. But man, Thunderdome really struck home field with the sand. And so does this game. The sand is awesome. Your tires leave imprints, as do your feet, whether driving or running along, on top of it. The vibrant skies are perfect. Graphics.
Let me also just add that there are side quests in this game that are not just fetch quests. They might seem menial and menial side quests have become a modern thing to complain about since I guess The Witcher 3 perfected the side quest formula. But here, in Mad Max, the side quests actually lead to upgrades and are integral to the character's leveling system. You'll get more griffa points which can be used to upgrade Max's stats. Plus several of the side quests actually have stories to them, as you'll learn with Hope and Glory who later become a main point to the main story.
Ending on that, Mad Max turned out to be a great great game that will be overlooked at the end of the year due to being shadowed by the release of MGSV and not being Mad Max: Furty Road The Game. It's just Mad Max, a game. It's its own thing, and works well as its own thing (although it does lead well into Fury Road except for a few minor details).

Mad Max Surprised me in many different ways. I came into this expecting a mediocre port of a mediocre open world game but I was wrong. Mad Max doesn't take may risks and excels on most aspects. There are two forms of combat: Driving and Fighting. Driving is where this game thrives. The mechanics are solid and easy to get used to. You can kill other divers and destroy enemy cars many ways. You can ram into them dealing more damage depending on the car parts you have, you can use a harpoon and tear off a piece of a car or pull the driver out of the car. You can use the slingshot to instantly kill enemy's and take out fuel tanks/tires but it has very little ammo so it's not recommended. There is a sniper for taking out opponents from a distance, and the thunderpoon which is a explosive harpoon. Well driving you have the help from a hunchback named Chumbuket which easily is the best character in the game. He fires the harpoon and fixes the "magnum opus" which is your car. He loves that car more than anything and you can't help but share the enthusiasum as you dive across the open desert. Fighting is pretty dull. I consists of a lot of button mashing but when you deal enough damage to fill up max's rage meter, Max does a lot more damage. You need to be on foot to take out Scrotus camps and other outposts. The camps have you fighting a bunch of enemy and either destroying feul tanks or destroying something else. In some special camps there is a forgetable boss fight that is always the same. The story is very hit and miss. Compared to the movie it's not as good but it isn't bad either. What makes the story not as good as it should be is Max. I have never seen a charecter in a game that was this stuborn. He very selfish and does all of this just to get his car back!!! His back story is very vague and I found myself caring about Chumbuket more than Max. The other characters are forgettable as well. Scrotus, the main antagonist, appears in the intro cutscence and you don't see him again till near the end. Most characters have no development or personality what so ever. It's not so bad considering the location of the game but it wouldn't of hurt. You have the ability to customize your car to your preference, you cant have a fast weak car, a strong slow car, or a little of both. There was a ton of options to choose from and really added to the gameplay. You can also upgrade your fighting abilitys but those didn't really add much. The problem is fiding the scrap metal to upgrade. Very few things reward enough metal and it can become repetitive searching for scrap all across the giant map. The port is great!!! I was worried after the port failure of Batman: Arkham Knight but this is one of the best PC ports of all time. Tons of customization settings and a FPS that never went below 60 and sometimes went in the 100's sets the far beyond any other PC port of this year. Overall it's a enjoyable experience. Is it great, no, but I still thing this game is worth a look for those interested. It represents the Mad Max universe well and fans of the arkham series should fine this game enjoyable as well. Mad Max gets a 7.6/10

The Good:
*Fun, action oriented gameplay
*An absolutely incredible weapon selection. Seriously, it's enormous.
*Great game to play with friends
*Creative art style + pretty decent music
*Long playtime, you really get your money's worth. Definitely buy this if it's on sale and you like western RPGs
*Large maps, with distinct geography
*Competent  voice acting
*No fall damage. You can jump off a mountain and live.
The Meh:
* The tech tree doesn't drastically alter the gameplay too much and the bonus stats don't make a noticeable difference either. Still, not a downside.
* Vehicles and fast travel are not present in the early areas, meaning that if you go back to do side quests, you'll sometimes find yourself walking large, tedious distances on foot. It also means you'll have to back track some. However this is limited to a few levels.
*It's a little bit lacking in the stealth department. I played as Assassin and was a tad disappointed that my special skills amounted to just a holographic distraction. There's no real sneaking in it, aside from staying out of your enemies' range of vision and sniping unsuspecting targets.
The Bad:
*For the most part, the writing in this game irritated me a lot. Almost every single line in the game is a joke--aside from key plot points--and sadly, most of them are not funny. Now, I feel that it won't bother most people, but it really started to get kind of grating after awhile. I'll admit there's a few good lines that I chuckled at, but it was more misses than hits. This hasn't ruined the game for me, but I honestly wish the developers had hired a better writer. The humor in this game is on par with something a highschooler could come up with. As for the story itself, it's completely acceptable. It feels a little drawn out in the middle, but for this kind of game, it's fine. The characters didn't really jump out to me, since almost every character is "zany" and "whacky". Thankfully several members of the main cast are grounded enough that the whole plot (and your involvement with it) isn't lost to the humor.
*While fun, the gameplay is really not that varied. You shoot everything you see, basically. It's good shooting, don't get me wrong, but that's all the game has to offer. As I started to play more and more quests, I began to assume any objective I got, no matter how mundane it sounded, was going to end with me shooting something. And aside from the driving oriented missions, that was exactly the case. In a nutshell the game is a huge, bullet-riddled fetch quest, and if that's something that bothers you, be aware of that.
Overall:
It's a straight up fun game that is only slightly marred by its annoying sense of humor and lack of variety. If you're a fan of FPS/RPGs, this is for you. You can think of it as a bit like the newer Fallout games, just more action oriented, without VATS, and significantly less serious (well, compared to 3 that is). If you like playing co-op games with your friends, this is a must-buy.

Rogue Legacy is an extremely fun and addictive game that requires some patience.  I'll go through some bullet points on what this game is:
- A metroidvania style game.  Explore a castle and its sections to accquire currency, equipment blue prints, and ability runes.
- Difficulty starts high but slowly decreases as you upgrade your stats and abilities, and become more familiar with the enemies.
- You will die many times playing this game.  Each death allows you to choose a new character which may be a different class and will have a new set of traits which may help, hinder, or have funny non-gameplay altering effects.
- When you die, the castle changes layout so it's a new opportunity for more treasures.  You're also given the opportunity to upgrade your stats, abilities, and equipment.
- The goal is to defeat the four bosses and the final boss.
The controls are very good as the character doesn't feel sluggish, slippery, or unresponsive.  The only gripe I have regarding controls is that there is a slight delay between hitting the attack button and when sword strikes in front of you.  This contributes to the difficulty and requires you to time your strikes correctly.
The game may be brutal but the way the castle layout changes, and the fact that you get stronger with each iteration motivates you to keep playing until you are strong and skilled enough to conquer each room and beat the bosses.  Highly recommended.

You have to work to get the gold and beat the bosses, and when you buy something, anything, THAT alone feels like a reward, and that's what I feel this game does so well on.

It starts out as a generic-feeling 3rd-person, cover-based, action game, but Spec Ops: The Line is set apart by its story or, rather, how it tells it.
While the plot itself is a fairly standard gung-ho tale of militarism, the game unashamedly points out its own ethical flaws. Other reviews I've read said that it often feels like Spec Ops hates the player, and I'd have to agree; nevertheless, it's a fascinating journey to take at least once.
There are a handful of different endings, but you can see them all in one playthrough just by reloading a previous save - how you played the game up until the end makes no difference. As a result, replayability is limited unless you want to go for all the collectibles/achievements. In particular, the achievement for completing the game on 'FUBAR' difficulty seems almost impossible. Playing through on Hard is punishing enough!
If you like 3rd person action games, you'll probably enjoy Spec Ops: The Line. If, like me, you have a healthy cynicism about modern military shooters, you may also appreciate the direction taken by this game despite the repetitive gameplay.
Gameplay can be pretty generic but it's the story/journey and the choices you make along the way that make the game a blast to play.

DayZ is a game that has been in development for a while....a fair while...so what...
I was one of those people who saw gameplays/videos on YouTube about DayZ, and loved the idea of it, eventually i got it, and encounted a lot of the issues people seem to be talking about here in the reviews, i've seen some angry comments about running for...20, 30, 40 or so minutes to reach other locations, in every game, people want bigger maps, more locations, more options, this game offers it, and people still complain, they would complain again about it being too small if the map consisted of just 2 towns, and 1 city.
Others seem to base their negative reviews on not being able to find food or drink, you can drink from streams/ponds as long as you've not got a wound or are injured in any way, otherwise you will get an infection, you can get food from apple trees/bushes, takes a while to get a good amount (without doing the apple glitch) but it's do'able, there is food out there, you just have to look for it, it is a survival game...there's not going to be a gift basket in every building with several cans of Tactical Bacon and Pipsi's....
The main focus, for me, is to make choices based on the encounters you have, players will try to kill you, in some cases, you may have something they want/need, or they just want to kill you, there are so many options, which is the entire point of DayZ, kill or be killed, or take a chance, and try to help one another out, that's it, you will go through different frames of mind, you will swear by all that is holy if you ever see another player you will have full on revenge for all the times you've been killed without question/warning, or you will decide screw this i want to team up or find a friend to travel with, eventually you will die to another player, and return to killing on sight, it's a circle, but that's what DayZ is, it's about making your own choices, so disregard the reviews, watch YouTube, make a choice for yourself on DayZ, but here are some mechanics of the game;
There are realism mechanics, such as hypothermia/hyperthermia, results of being too hot, or being too cold, these are EASILY managable.
Hypothermia - wear more clothes, stay out of the rain, make an occasional camp fire in the woods in a lul in the ground so no'one can directly see the fire itself, (careful cooking meat, it attracts wolves, or kill them too, and cook their meat also which refers back to the "not being able to find food" issues people complained about)
Hyperthermia - take a break, stop running, wear less clothes, get away from the fire, go sit in a pond or swim in the lake, get drenched, or actually go stand in the rain for a bit.
These mechanics add another layer of attempted realism to the game, it isn't a straight foward, get a weapon, go hunt players kinda game, you can do that if you want, but it's not that simple, you do have other things to take note of and combat in order to survive for longer, DayZ to me...seems to be more about surviving and making choices, travel by road, encounter potential players/bandits/thieves, travel by woods...encounter wolves, try and out run them and make it to a town/city to hide, or stand your ground and try and kill the Alpha Wolf, ( a pack of white wolves will have one grey wolf *the Alpha* and a pack of grey will have a white wolf as their alpha, kill that alpha, and the rest will cut and run.
All in all, yes it's still in alpha, they rebuilt their engine, they made a game from scratch, after the successfull DayZ Mod, that takes time, any half decent game will usually be years in development, yes, fine, they're usually out by now, but DayZ is this HUGE open world Survival game, with a lot of different mechanics, they've been turning a Mod, into a fully fledged game, they can take another two years or three, we can still play it...and enjoy, so please, if you're interested in the game, make use of YouTube, make a decision for yourself, everyone's entitled to their own opinion, but most of the comments here, seem to be from people making a trend of hating on DayZ, just because....
4 Years of standing still while everyone else rushes past with fresh ideas.

I have a hard time believing that this game is still in Alpha. It plays better than many Strategy-Sims that have a full release. Not to mention that most of the updates, which occur once a month, change the gameplay in very significant ways. The draw of this game for this game varies for many people as well. Some buy it to construct cool looking prisons, or efficient prisons, while others, including myself, play the game for the prisoner interactions. The Alpha 25 build of the game has greatly impacted the way the game is played by making prisoners much more dynamic and adding "New ways to fail".
My only gripe with the game is that the method in which you report bugs is dysfunctional at best. You can't do it from the Devs website, and have to go to a different website. After spending a half-hour posting a bug report, including recording footage of the bug and attaching it, I was very frustrated when the website timed out on me... 5 times.

In its current state, I think Prison Architect is quite expensive for what you get. But it is indeed a good game. As of Alpha 25, maintaining a functioning prison where anything can go wrong is pretty fun. The chaos that could break out in a matter of seconds requires quick player response to the issue, and can lead to some amusing situations which the player can learn from to improve their facility. The want to expand is always present, and it is likely some players will create prisons that are too big for their own good. The attention to details (education programs, the needs system, contraband, etc) continues to surprise me. The fact you are able to tell where contraband comes from, how it got in, where it went, and where it was found is just one of many of the detailed features that can affect the build of your prison. All this said, it is pretty buggy (it is an alpha after all), but I reccomend picking it up when it is discounted if you are at all interested.

This is my spoiler free review of Life Is Strange: Before the Storm, the prequel of the original Life Is Strange. My expectations were huge after the Life Is Strange. The story was so emotional and the artstyle is just on point. I preordered Before The Storm (usually i don't preorder games since a few years at all). But I had confidence in the developers. Was I disappointed? No, by any means. Not at all. Actually Before the Storm was a great surprise for me and takes some new and fresh ideas into the gameplay without loosing this ... "Life Is Strange feeling". It's still the same - but new. And most importantly: With a new, important story before the first game starts - Before the storm as the title says. You can even get a bonus chapter with Max when all 3 episodes are released. The good thing about it? You'll now pay for all episodes at once. You just have to wait ... or play it later with all chapters.
The artstyle is still fantastic. Shure, Life Is Strange is not known for it's photorealistic graphics. Graphics totaly matter - but not how realistic they are. Rather how well the style has been implemented and how good the world is brought to life. And the developers did it very good. It begins with the user interface and ends with little details. The world of Life is Strange is just beautiful and i love how both games play.
Should you buy it? Yes. But you definitely have to get Life is Strange & Life is Strange: Before the Storm together! You would miss something otherwise in my opinion. So i just played the first episode from Before the Storm and it hits me again. Thats what i wanted. And i can't wait till the other two episodes are here for us. Even if I am a man, i just cried at the end of the first game. And the end of the first episode from BtS is also very deep.
Just get it ... and enjoy.

At the time of writing, only the first of three parts of the story has been released. I like it so far. It's definitely different from the original but the story is engaging and the artwork is solid. If you haven't played the original Life is Strange, I highly recommend you do.

Graphics were awesome and really captured the essence of the Mad Max universe.  The game itself is really well optimized so you won't need a high end card to get the best out of this game.  Gameplay shifted from slightly above average fighting mechanics to great driving mechanics and car battles. Jumping and climbing is a little odd in the game and the yellow indicators, although welcome, felt a little lazy design wise.  Sound overall is amazing in this game and the engine sounds are a thing of beauty.  I've heard criticims of Max's accent, but as an Aussie I thought the voice actor did a great job.  The story is average, but marginally better than Fury Road the movie.  Main characters are reasonably well developed and Chumbucket is a likeable companion, quite funny in parts and never gets annoying.
I spent about 60 hours on the game, taking extra time to finish areas needed to fully upgrade the Vehicle but not worrying about 100%'ing.  Once cleanup crews are implemented the scrap collection became much less of a grind.
I was disappointed that the map broke when I was 90% of the way through the game and I had to wait 3 weeks for a patch to fix it, however in the grand scheme of things 3 weeks is pretty good although it did break immersion and my overall enjoyment.  Areas I see that could use improvement would be adding some complexity and difficulty to the hand-to-hand combat mechanics (definitely making bosses more difficult) and perhaps adding a few more types of missions/tasks as the current stock were a little repetitive for a 60 hour game.
Overall I really enjoyed my time in Mad Max and would definitely recommend this game to fans of the movie, or genre. I enjoyed Mad Max more than previous Batman games and found it about on par with Shadow of Mordor.  I would give the game a solid 8/10 and wait in hope for a sequel some time down the track.

There is something about driving down the road at 80-90 kmh hauling a heavy load driving a big truck tractor.  I have played many driving sim games, ladies and gentlemen SCS Software has nailed it.  The concept of this game sounds extremely boring, but there is something that I cannot put my finger on that makes everything about this game fun as hell and very addictive. My first play was 14.0 hrs straight, very rarely that happens to me or anyone, all signs of a great game.
Considering the overall physical size of the game "less than 2gb" the in-game world and content is huge.  It never feels like a rushed overwhelming feeling of the game forcing you to do anything, everything is at your own pace.  There are several and I mean several different types of loads ranging from literally everything.  Not to mention the heavy DLC that just came out giving the player oversized/super heavy loads and at a cheap price.  SCS isn't one of those companies that will nickel and dime you to death with dlc, the game itself without DLC is huge, it never feels like anything is missing or that they finsihed the game using DLC. I hope that made sense. :)
You can hire drivers, provide them with a truck tractor and choose what area you want them to train in and they take off working and are self contained while making you money.  You can check thier log books to see what they have been doing and upgrade thier trucks for them so they can haul better more high value loads.  Eventually you can have a fleet of trucks, garages, and drivers.
There are lots of customizable options for your truck, paint, graphics, metallics, chrome, lights, tires, engines, transmissions, rear axles, interiors, tons of exterior kits and packages. I really can't name them all here, there is a lot of customizable features for the trucks.
The traffic ai is easily one of the best I have seen around, you get the occasional jerk that mashes his brakes in front of you out of the blue or someone cuts you off but overall they seem pretty good. Most accidents are my fault. :p  Example: Driving down the freeway, turn on your signal and the approaching vehicles will notice and back off so you can get over instead of disregarding it because it doesn't know any better.  Glad to see they put detail in the traffic system..what I mean by detail is "brains" not just a path for them to follow blind.
The fact you can program live stream radio stations in the game is a nice touch, took me a bit to figure that out but really not too difficult, the hardest part is finding a site where the live stream works in game. People ask, why not just turn music on in the background?  Cause it's not the same! lol..jk   Its nice to just boot the game up and hit a hot key and your music starts playing rather than loading up a entire site to stream music.
Overall easily the best 22.99 I have ever spent on a game.  Worth it..finally.

Euro Truck Simulator 2 is a very relaxing game. Relaxing because, well, it just is. Euro Truck Simulator 2 lands you in Europe. You first of all pick what city you want your Virtual trucking company HQ at. Then you start off with a small amount of cash. However, you don't start off with your own truck. So, until you can rack up the money to be able to afford one of trucks, Such as, MAN, Scania, Iveco, DAF, Volvo ETC. You need to do some jobs working for a company. You do this by going to the Job Market and picking a job. A truck is provided for you to complete the job. There is also the freight market which is where you can take jobs with your own truck. (Assuming you have one)
Euro Truck Simulator 2 has a multiplayer mod. Allowing you to play alongside people online in 2100 capacity servers.  It's a fun and addicting game in which relaxes you and allows you to explore countries such as the United Kingdom, France, Germany, Poland, Austria, Czech Republic, Slovakia, Switzerland, Netherlands, Belgium, Luxembourg, Hungary and parts of Italy.
Euro Truck Simulator 2 is also very realistic. It has speed limiters for certain roads. It tells you in which speed you should be driving on your GPS. You can be jackknifed if you take turns to fast. The game also has a sleeping simulation. After a certain amount of time you will become tired and will have to stop, refuel, and park at a parking bay and rest.
I'd defo reccomend this game as it is very relaxing. If I had another name for this game it would be 'Speed Camera Simulator' as you can easily be caught off guard by various speed cameras placed across the map, which often fine you for going over the speed limit.
On a final note, if you are playing the multiplayer mod. Beware of the Russian drivers. They are crazy. I was once in Hungary driving to Debrecen and I was cruising along the motorway and this Russian on the other side of the motorway decided to come through the gap down the wrong side of the road. He nearly well hit me. But I just narrowly missed him. I was lucky.
10/10 would get mauled by Russian drivers again.

In what is perhaps one of the greatest narratives in a video game is also an amazing deconstruction of the military shooter genre. The game sends you on an intense journey only for you to learn that war is gruesome and brutal and you will not only hate the enemy, but you will hate yourself.
You are a soldier sent to Dubai to look for survivors and help them out of the city of Dubai that has been ridden with sand storms. It seems like an easy mission, but everything turns upside down when you get there and realize that the survivors are your enemy.
As a 3rd person shooter, this game has all the controls you'd expect, cover systems, OTS aiming, running etc, but that's not the main point of the game.
You come across files, tapes and other objects that tell the tale of what is similar the story of 'Hearts of Darkness' which was adapted to 'Apocalypse Now'. Your character believes that a leading US military official is alive in Dubai based on conversations and recordings of his voice heard through loud speakers. It all unvravels in the end.
Plus the art style of Dubai is gorgeous and massive.

DayZ is a game that has been in development for a while....a fair while...so what...
I was one of those people who saw gameplays/videos on YouTube about DayZ, and loved the idea of it, eventually i got it, and encounted a lot of the issues people seem to be talking about here in the reviews, i've seen some angry comments about running for...20, 30, 40 or so minutes to reach other locations, in every game, people want bigger maps, more locations, more options, this game offers it, and people still complain, they would complain again about it being too small if the map consisted of just 2 towns, and 1 city.
Others seem to base their negative reviews on not being able to find food or drink, you can drink from streams/ponds as long as you've not got a wound or are injured in any way, otherwise you will get an infection, you can get food from apple trees/bushes, takes a while to get a good amount (without doing the apple glitch) but it's do'able, there is food out there, you just have to look for it, it is a survival game...there's not going to be a gift basket in every building with several cans of Tactical Bacon and Pipsi's....
The main focus, for me, is to make choices based on the encounters you have, players will try to kill you, in some cases, you may have something they want/need, or they just want to kill you, there are so many options, which is the entire point of DayZ, kill or be killed, or take a chance, and try to help one another out, that's it, you will go through different frames of mind, you will swear by all that is holy if you ever see another player you will have full on revenge for all the times you've been killed without question/warning, or you will decide screw this i want to team up or find a friend to travel with, eventually you will die to another player, and return to killing on sight, it's a circle, but that's what DayZ is, it's about making your own choices, so disregard the reviews, watch YouTube, make a choice for yourself on DayZ, but here are some mechanics of the game;
There are realism mechanics, such as hypothermia/hyperthermia, results of being too hot, or being too cold, these are EASILY managable.
Hypothermia - wear more clothes, stay out of the rain, make an occasional camp fire in the woods in a lul in the ground so no'one can directly see the fire itself, (careful cooking meat, it attracts wolves, or kill them too, and cook their meat also which refers back to the "not being able to find food" issues people complained about)
Hyperthermia - take a break, stop running, wear less clothes, get away from the fire, go sit in a pond or swim in the lake, get drenched, or actually go stand in the rain for a bit.
These mechanics add another layer of attempted realism to the game, it isn't a straight foward, get a weapon, go hunt players kinda game, you can do that if you want, but it's not that simple, you do have other things to take note of and combat in order to survive for longer, DayZ to me...seems to be more about surviving and making choices, travel by road, encounter potential players/bandits/thieves, travel by woods...encounter wolves, try and out run them and make it to a town/city to hide, or stand your ground and try and kill the Alpha Wolf, ( a pack of white wolves will have one grey wolf *the Alpha* and a pack of grey will have a white wolf as their alpha, kill that alpha, and the rest will cut and run.
All in all, yes it's still in alpha, they rebuilt their engine, they made a game from scratch, after the successfull DayZ Mod, that takes time, any half decent game will usually be years in development, yes, fine, they're usually out by now, but DayZ is this HUGE open world Survival game, with a lot of different mechanics, they've been turning a Mod, into a fully fledged game, they can take another two years or three, we can still play it...and enjoy, so please, if you're interested in the game, make use of YouTube, make a decision for yourself, everyone's entitled to their own opinion, but most of the comments here, seem to be from people making a trend of hating on DayZ, just because....
4 Years of standing still while everyone else rushes past with fresh ideas.

Graphics were awesome and really captured the essence of the Mad Max universe.  The game itself is really well optimized so you won't need a high end card to get the best out of this game.  Gameplay shifted from slightly above average fighting mechanics to great driving mechanics and car battles. Jumping and climbing is a little odd in the game and the yellow indicators, although welcome, felt a little lazy design wise.  Sound overall is amazing in this game and the engine sounds are a thing of beauty.  I've heard criticims of Max's accent, but as an Aussie I thought the voice actor did a great job.  The story is average, but marginally better than Fury Road the movie.  Main characters are reasonably well developed and Chumbucket is a likeable companion, quite funny in parts and never gets annoying.
I spent about 60 hours on the game, taking extra time to finish areas needed to fully upgrade the Vehicle but not worrying about 100%'ing.  Once cleanup crews are implemented the scrap collection became much less of a grind.
I was disappointed that the map broke when I was 90% of the way through the game and I had to wait 3 weeks for a patch to fix it, however in the grand scheme of things 3 weeks is pretty good although it did break immersion and my overall enjoyment.  Areas I see that could use improvement would be adding some complexity and difficulty to the hand-to-hand combat mechanics (definitely making bosses more difficult) and perhaps adding a few more types of missions/tasks as the current stock were a little repetitive for a 60 hour game.
Overall I really enjoyed my time in Mad Max and would definitely recommend this game to fans of the movie, or genre. I enjoyed Mad Max more than previous Batman games and found it about on par with Shadow of Mordor.  I would give the game a solid 8/10 and wait in hope for a sequel some time down the track.

Game is okay, shooting mechanics-wise.
The humor is ehhhhh most of the time. Don't really get why people like it so much.
Most cutscenes are unskippable. When you've done several playthroughs and still have to run through the same animation over and over again, you get sick of it.
They buffed the drop rates to a respectable rate, getting proper level-appropriate loot is no longer the massive pain and grindfest it was. Game is actually fun to play now without having to grind the same boss over and over for hours to get a single legendary.
TVHM and UVHM (NG+ and NG++) have issues with difficulty scaling. While I can understand enemies dealing more damage, making them have so much health is kinda lazy. Slag solves the problem with it dealing granting 3x damage from other sources, but turns the game into a mode where slag is mandatory. You. Must. Slag. Everything. Else you're going to take 3x the bullets to kill an enemy. Having to slag everything is not an issue with me, but unslaggable enemies such as badass constructors are the most bullet spongy enemies I have ever seen.
Damage scaling at higher levels (UVHM) also start getting pretty ridiculous. At a point late into the game, some enemies deal so much damage that no amount of legendary gear is going to pump your health+shields stat above their single shot damage (hyperion hawks with their RPGs come to mind), and instead you'll have to rely upon health gating (cannot be one shotted if current health is above 50%), and immediately healing up after going below health gate level. This leads to some interesting situations and frustrating ones.
The Inventory UI is still clunky ala skyrim inventory menu. The bug where your actual hover area being different from where the cursor is, is still present and occurs occasionally. Have fun trying to not sell something you want to keep.
Co-op's where the game's at. Playing alone is...well, lonely. While enemies scale according to the number of players, having just another partner alone makes the game noticably easier. Besides, co-op is fun.
While the game does indeed have many different variation of guns, bandit and dahl guns are mostly inferior. One has crap everything (accuracy, ROF, damage per shot, reload speed) but high magazine size, which doesn't really matter unless it's a rocket launcher, and the other has terrible accuracy unless you ADS, which forces burst fire. Unfortunately, dahl guns have meh dps when burst firing. The only thing burst fire is good for is controlling weapon spead and accuracy, which isn't an issue when you're ADSing. Tediore weapons are gimmicky and require a specific build to fit their use. Jakobs isn't really viable in endgame due its lack of elemental damage.
None of the above really matter if you don't care about minmaxing though. But if you do, it does cut down on the amount of weapon variations available. If you want to be able to use everything, you're going to be sacrificing dps and survivability.

Let me start this off by saying I'm not a huge fan of 2D games with elements similar to this (Castlevania, etc..) but Rogue Legacy is a very refreshing take on the genre. The goal of the game is to fight your way through several areas including a castle, a forest, a tower, and a dungeon; all of which feel connected yet set apart from each other.
There is one twist on the game however. Every time you die you will lose your character forever. FOREVER. While that may seem a bit dramatic and perma-deathy fear not! You will retain everything you previously earned with your character and pass it on to an heir who will inherit your treasures and continue your quest! With the gold you have earned you will be able to buy new armor, buy runes to enchant your armor, and upgrade the very extensive skill tree represented by your own castle! As you upgrade the skills tree it will branch off into different sections allowing you to unlock more classes to play as and more passive bonuses to your character.
Now onto the characters.. you can play as several character classes off the bat and have the ability to unlock many more by upgrading your skill tree. Every character you play as will be different from the last, not only set apart by their different class abilities and stats, but also by randomized traits and magic abilities! Have you ever wanted your protagonist to be a gay, color blind barbarian? Well that is one of hundreds (possibly thousands) of different character combinations you can have! These traits can have either positive, negative, or neutral effects on your gameplay. You could gain the ability to knock enemies back further, or you could take more damage from enemies, or you might have irritable bowels and flatulate while jumping!
Now finally in conclusion I feel like a pros and cons list would suit this game well, here you go!
Pros:
+ Randomized dungeons make dungeons fresh every time you play!
+ The boss fights in this game are brilliantly designed and a blast to play, including the buffed up, more difficult versions of the fights.
+ The extensive skill tree will satisfy that need to upgrade.
+ Death doesn't feel as devestating as other games.
+ Different character classes and traits keep the game interesting.
+ Excellent comedy factors
Cons:
- While your first playthrough may take a long while because you need to learn how to play, the game is very small.
- For casual players the game could get boring very quickly.
- Classes don't feel too much different from each other
- Not much depth in combat (Could be a pro or con)

This is literally the digital definition of a Rogue-Like video game.
Rogue Legacy is a platform based rogue-like dungeon crawler, in the same vein of Castlevania and Metroid, with the common elements of a standard rogue-like game. Rogue-like games are made to be extremely difficult games that encourage trial and error playstyle; constant mistakes, multiple deaths and some form of carry-over (either in items, experience, or personal knowledge) to get past the trials that stand before the player in question.
Several games (Baroque for the PS2 and the Nintendo Wii being a prime example) are based on this method, where the failure of a player is considered another step towards victory rather than an active punishment. Rogue Legacy prides itself on this idea; each time you start the game, you play as a stereotypical knight with some form of genetic deformity which can either act as a hindrance or an advantage. Each knight also has their own class with special abilities and statistics, and each is better at certain parts of the game than others. The ultimate goal is to defeat the four main bosses to unlock the door at the start of the game leading towards something important.
Each time the player character dies, their progeny takes over, becomming the new player character, and repeating this process until the player achieves victory in a single playthrough. Certain actions (killing a boss, for example) remain permanent beyond player death, and act as rough checkpoints.
With an ever shifting castle system, some rather challenging rooms and bosses, and a story that can be called "existing", Rogue Legacy is worth enough time to catch a person's attention and repetition for play. I personally enjoyed it at least.

It has been a couple years since Life is Strange first came out and tons of people of people experienced the story. It may be a long time since we played as Max Caulfield and we thought that it was the end of all the other characters that showed up along the way. Until the announcement that we will revisit Arcadia Bay not as Max, but as Chloe.
We come in three years before the main events of the main game, more specifically after Max packed up and left Arcadia Bay and Chloe is hurting. It does not help that Max left after Chloe's dad died and contact has halted. With Chloe being the local outcast at Blackwell, who can she go to when her soon-to-be stepdad, David, becomes unbearable as he starts hanging around the house more? Of course she has a journal she can have letters addressed to Max that will never be sent, but even that brings bitterness. The reality that she must of done something wrong if even Max does not bother contacting her. It comes in no surprise that Chloe might act out and jump into an opportunity of hanging out with the famous Rachel Amber.
Before the Storm brings in a different mechanic called Backtalk. Here you have to listen to what your opponent said to you and make it backfire on them. If they call you childish, bring up something childish about them and Chloe will say it with her aggressive and smartass attitude. And if it was the wrong choice, Chloe gives off a really weak insult that the opponent will shut down. With each successful backtalk you will gain a point and if you fail, or time runs out, your opponent will. Depending on who you go against, the amount of slip ups vary. Though honestly, it really has nothing substantial to the story. Either way what was meant to happen will happen anyway.
Let's get into the choices you make. While we only have one episode, and a month or a month and a half till the next episode is out, a lot of the small choices have not made an effect on the story just yet. But the choices based on the main plot will lead to the plot area no matter if you did the choice that would of gotten you out of it. There are also some choices, that do not show statistics at the end of the episode, that you have to do. Some backtalks are necessary, though by the time you do the first one it feels more like Chloe (and who can pass it up) rather than opting out of it, and some choices will prove unhelpful. There is one that you notice, during a DnD game which is one of the best moments, that is mentioned if you make a certain choice but if you do not, they will ignore it and continue on what happened if you did it.
Instead of having Max's collectable being photos, Chloe's collectable is graffiti. Once you find a spot, you will be able to choose between two options before Chloe takes out her marker and writes or draws what you picked. Showcasing her streak of rebellion, especially when the targets go from school walls to saws being used for decoration (and honestly making it look better).
Undoubtedly the game does pick up once Rachel appears. Before, it gets overbearing with how much cringe moments you get. You get the whole she likes fire and wants everything to burn, she loves drugs, and that she hates David so much she thinks about killing him. You really get the impression that Chloe is not worth being in her head. We all remember our years that we look back at how cringey we were, and I do think it is realistic in that way as I do see Chloe looking back at what she did after a couple years. And since most of us playing already went past this phase, it is obvious. Before the Storm is strong when it goes with Chloe’s and Rachel’s developing relationship. We get to know about her more vulnerable side that we heard about when we were playing Max. Chloe couldn’t tell Max in person about her problems, and I do understand that it escalated to her teen angst self, but it is understandable that she jumped into being friends and loving Rachel so quickly.
Though at the same time, the part that made Rachel’s character interesting is that we had to learn about her by second hand experience. Which does culminate into why she was killed in the way we heard about in Life is Strange. In Before the Storm, we already know what is going to happen with Rachel and how this relationship will pan out. There will be no surprises as it was definitely an easy move to make a prequel based on a character we know about that died before the first game started. Rachel still holds secrets, but her life has a timer that we already know about.
Let’s address the elephant in the room, Chloe’s changing in voice actors. Honestly, it is not noticeable if it has been a while since you played Life is Strange. Though it does get evident when it gets more emotional as the voice breaks away from the gruff sound in the middle of a sentence. Otherwise she does a good job filling in. The other voice acting has retained the same amount of quality from the first game. As well as the soundtrack still being as good as Life is Strange's soundtrack.
Before the Storm relies heavily on the player experiencing Life is Strange beforehand. Mostly showing on how you will view Chloe. Without prior knowledge on how the events coming up changed her, Chloe just seems like an angsty teen that takes drugs, steals, badmouths which somehow gets her out of trouble, and does graffiti on walls. This first episode certainly does not paint her in a good light for the players. You will also have a stronger connection to Arcadia Bay and the various objects and events that you will remember.
+ Realistic characters
+ Stays true to Chloe's character
+ Backtalk mechanic, but still can be worked on
+ Letters addressed to Max
+ Soundtrack
+/- Cringe embracing dialogue
- Foreshadowing obvious
- Lots of reliance on the player recognizing a lot of areas, items, and people from the first game
Life is Strange: Before the Storm brings us to the past in the shoes of Chloe Price. Three years before the main events took place, we focus on what made Rachel Amber special to Chloe. While also giving us that Rachel may have cemented herself to be the perfect angel in the minds of most people but she has flaws. And when it comes to looking back at someone that was important to you, only the good moments will come to mind. Before the Storm has flaws, but those flaws does not take away that it is fun to play. With the time period we were placed in and knowing this will end around six months before the first game, as we will not see Rachel's fate, it will be interesting to see how they handle time skips, if they do, incorporating choice consequences, and how Rachel began skirting around Chloe. I do recommend that if you hated Chloe, or just hated Life is Strange, I do not recommend this. If you have not played Life is Strange yet, I recommend playing that first before moving to Before the Storm.

First off, I highly recommend this game. Provided you also get he following DLC, High Power Cargo Pack and Going East Expansion. The first adds new cargo and trailers that are both more rewarding and heavier than the original cargo variety. The second adds a large new section of map to drive, and many more cities and countries. Both are well worth the added cost. The other DLC's available consists of custom paint jobs. They add nothing to the gameplay, but you can buy those if you like them.
About the game;
You are a truck driver in Europe. You select what city you want to base your future company in, and start out working for companies delivering cargo with their trucks. You gain experience with each load that is safely delivered without doing too much damage. You can choose to buy your own truck as soon as you save enough money, or by getting a loan from the bank. If you own your own truck, you can upgrade or customize it however you choose (once you obtain the experience levels to unlock the upgrades wanted). You earn more money if you own your truck vs. driving a company's truck. As you get more money and discover various cities, you can buy additional garages and hire drivers to work for you... increasing your income. You will have to buy a truck for each new driver, and upgrade your garages to gain space for more drivers.  Garages come in 2 sizes. Small has space for 3 drivers and costs $180,000  A small garage can be upgraded to a large garage for an additional $100,000. A large garage also has a fuel pump for your benefit.
While the game is a good game, it is not without certain shortcomings.
First, There are many features that SCS had the code for from prior releases in the series that could have been included but were not. In Hard Trucks wipers had 2 speeds, now they only have 1. In Extreme Trucking, you had a variety of weather and road conditions, from ice and snow, to dirt roads and steep terrain. Here, the weather is very simple... it is either not raining, or its raining. Roads are all paved and quite uneventful. Hills are gradual, and the roads are formed from a set pattern of road sections that have been copied and repeated over and over.
Another omission is that much of the available upgrades do absolutely nothing.  Most trucks offer 3 different truck cabs. A standard cab w/ no sleeper, a standard cab w/ sleeper, and a larger cab with a bigger sleeper. None of the cabs affect the trucks fuel economy, handling, or performance. The addition of a sleeper does not enable you to rest anywhere that a non-sleeper truck can. It's all purely cosmetic. Same for the transmissions. Al trucks come with a 12 speed transmission regardless of engine. Upgrading to the other 12 speed transmission does nothing for the performance or fuel economy. Tires are another thing, no matter what tires you choose, the handling, performance, fuel economy and wear are the same. All pure cosmetics. Adding a front bumper or guard does nothing to increase the durability of the truck. the AI traffic pays no attention to the existance of the roof mounted safety strobe lamps, nor is there and aerodynamic penalty for the wind drag from a roof mounted light bar full of lights and horns. Horns are ignored by traffic as well. Both horns and roof safety strobe lamps are purely there for cosmetics.
The AI traffic has it's own issues. They will change lanes suddenly, stop suddenly, crash into you, and cause traffic jams lasting over an hour. They also are prone to hauling♥♥♥♥♥.. I've been running 102 mph and been passed and couldn't keep up with traffic cars before in 50 mph zones.
A big issue relates to the drivers you hire and the trucks they drive. It does not make one bit of difference if you buy the cheapest truck you can get (a $97,000 Man for example), or buy the most tricked out, most powerful, most expensive truck (A fully decked out Scania or Volvo costing $275,000+)... you earn the same. Upgrading their trucks does not speed them up, enable them to haul heavier loads, or make them happy... It doesn't do anything. Save your money and give each driver hte cheapest basic truck you can buy. You also cannot see the other trucks on the road, nor in the garages, ever. They only exist as a small thumbnail picture in the manager section.
Things I'd like to see in future updates:
More weather types... Snow and Ice, hail, fog, etc...
More variety in roads, Steep hills and switchbacks, narrow roads with high dropoffs and no guardrails. Dirt, gravel and pothole filled bumpy roads. Roads with deep ruts.
Functional tires that have varying grip depending on terrain and weather. Make better tires last longer or have better traction than cheap tires.
Adjust the engine outputs and trailer load weights so that pulling a 55,000lb trailer with the entry level engine is nearly impossible... making having a more powerful engine something you both need and desire. Adjust fuel economy so that the more powerful the engine, the worse your mileage (currently, there is no difference)
Make upgrading trucks for your driver have a benefit.
Make traffic AI react to safety hazard strobes (stay back a safe distance, give way when turning, etc...) as well as move over when possible if you blow the horn at them.
Make truck cab differences matter. If no sleeper, you stay only in a Hotel or at your upgraded garage. If a small sleeper, you can rest at gas stations and rest areas, but you have to rest longer to get a full 11 hrs driving time. If you have the large sleeper, you rest better, so you don't have to rest as long to get fully rested.
Add additional transmissions to different trucks. Some trucks have 10 speeds, some have 18 speeds..
Just one more delivery, then I'll go do something constructive...

There ought to be a rule of common sense that a developer should have played Rogue or Nethack at least once before claiming their game is "roguelike", let alone aluding to the classic in their title.
There is no strategy  in this platform-jumping action game. It's Mario with a generic fantasy skin and a couple of ideas that would have been interesting in a real roguelike.
Sure, quite a few of the checkboxes in a clueless marketer's list of what makes a "roguelike" are ticked off here, but with the exception of procedural generation every one of those is equally true of a Mario game. And of things that would distinguish the two types of game, every point falls on the Mario side - frenetic button pushing combat, platform puzzles, and on and on through a catalog of things that are why I never play Mario games and like real roguelikes. Heck, the thing even defaults to assuming you have a game controller connected.
If you are looking for game that's really roguelike, there are quite a few interesting ones available on Steam. I'd particularly point out Tales of Maj'Eyal and FTL for two nice and fresh takes on this genre.

DayZ is by far my most favorite game. Together with various iteratiosn of the mod, I must've spent close to 3000+ hrs playing the game. In terms of immersion and amount of details, this game is unrivaled. Though most players rate it negatively due to lenghty development progress, I still recommend to play it for the following reasons:
- The firefights actually mean something, i.e. the feeling that you get when in a firefights is one of immense tension with realistic sounds and gun physics.
- The Chernarus map is most probably the best multiplayer map of its kind. The layout of the map, different areas, sights to see etc are mindblowing and, if your setup permits, playing on high graphics, it is actually a very enjoyable game. Unlike, for example, PUBG whose map is functional and purpose driven but lacks a certain kind of love for details, the DayZ map never fails to impress. Trees are not put randomly on the map, houses and towns make actual sense beyond providing the player with loot.
- The implementation of hunting and diseases is good and realistic giving you an actual experience of fighting for survival. Unlike othr games, where you just push a button to heal 60% of your HP, in DayZ things are more complicated and, for me, enjoyable because it involves some amount of thinking while managing your health.
- The development progress, though a bit slow, has made tremendous changes to the game. If you bought this game at the start of early access and play it now, you will notice what a vastly different game it is. The amount of new items, towns on the map, firearms, mechanics is quite honestly mindblowing.
Finally, as a survival game, there is nothing better in the store - hands down. Though PUBG is a very good game getting some amount of hype right now, DayZ is an entirely new game altogether and with the addition of modding in DayZ, I think that PBG and its Unreal engine will not be able to compete in terms of competitiveness.

**This Review has been Updated**
**Update: Since the update, I have noticed that the small animals(ie, rabbits and squirrels) are no longer wearing rain jackets, and thus no longer sound like they are running through empty bags of Doritos. However, when tracking a moose that I shot, I completely lost the blood trail randomly. I don't know if this is a new feature or what, but the moose circled around in the area of an old trail, and while I found plenty of tracks, I found no more blood trail which is key to finding a wounded animal and keeping on the right track. That could have been an issue on my end, I suppose, and I'll have to look into this a bit more in order to determine if this is some sort of bug. Also, it is obvious that the crouch-walking works better now in this new update, and you get spotted less frequently when you are crouched and moving. On the downside though, you walk painfully slower when traveling this way. But I suppose that's supposed to be realistic, so that's fair.**
Is it worth buying at this point? That's for you to decide. There are both positives and negatives about the current state of this game, keep reading.
Starting with the Positives about the game: The settings are great. From the visuals in the scenery, to the audio with raindrops and the wind blowing through the leaves, the background really is pretty stunning. You don't have a wide variety of animals to shoot at this point, but those that you can they look very well done. The animals also sound really good, and often behave like wild animals. If you don't get good shot placement, you can very much rely on having to track a wounded animal for some time until you can either finally put it down, or it eventually succumbs to it's injuries. The little stories in singleplayer and missions are also pretty neat.
And on to the Negatives: Why do the squirrels and rabbits sound like they are wearing little little rainjackets when they run around? While the game animals sound fairly normal as they walk through the grass and brush, the smaller critters sound like they are wearing plastic as they romp about the trees and meadows. Nothing breaks the immersion as you're sighting in on a large buck as you suddenly hear a pair of squirrels wearing windsuits dashing about the boulder you've perched on to take your shot. And as you suddenly look around to see what is going on around you, your buck notices the movement and shoots off like a rocket into the safety of the forest as you silently curse the creators of these squirrels.
Also, at random times, the game suddenly decides that it's done playing nice. And your leisurely stroll through the meadow as you search for a black bear takes a sudden turn as you notice that you are now walking in slow motion. So you switch for your tracker to a rifle so you can walk a bit faster for a bit, but soon you're still forced to a virtual crawl as your walk becomes visibly slower. And so you have to restart the game.
Sometimes, you come across an animal that is stuck in some way. Sometimes it is stuck between a tree and a rock, for example. At other times, it's stuck in a loop, walking or running in a sort of circle. And so you fire a shot at the stuck animal. Sometimes you'll kill it. Sometimes you'll just scare it, and it will run faster even though it's still stuck. Now and again, it'll take one hit, but it won't kill it, even though it just runs faster and faster and as you shoot at it over and over again-at times you'll see the shot take effect and it stumbles to the ground-it'll get back up and refuse to die. And you'll have to restart the game because you're never going to kill it. Sometimes you'll shoot a stuck animal, and no matter how point-blank you shoot it, the bullets magically fail to hit their intended target. Other times you'll clearly and visibly hit the animal, and it'll eventually run off. But when you come up to find the blood trail, you'll see that there is no blood. Even though the animal clearly fell the ground and got back up to run away, there's no blood. You may have hit it three or four times, and there's no blood trail. And when you eventually give up, you suddenly notice that you don't see animal tracks anymore, and if you fire a shot at something, it magically misses(although it does expend ammo). Sometimes this can be fixed by fast traveling to an outpost.
You might think that the negatives outweigh the positives. Or vice versa. And that's up to you decide. For me, even though the game is currently frustrating at it's present state, I still enjoy it. The visuals are well-done, the animal movements are excellent, etc. But it's also frustrating and a little buggy. The immersion breaks at points(especially when you or a small animal moves through the brush and grass), the game crawls at times, and you sometimes can't hit what your aiming at even if you could literally touch the animal you're shooting at. Would I recommend this game? Yes, with the caveats that this game is currently buggy, but I do believe that the developers will get it fixed. The makers of this game have done well with other games in the theHunter line, and there's no reason to think they won't get these problems fixed. For that reason, I do recommend this game.

Very few games have made me feel like Spec Ops: The Line has. To me, it seems like an abundant number of shooters are growing increasingly generic. Producing gore for gore’s sake, and scarcely ever using mature or violent content to actually make you feel for a character. Spec Ops: The Line is the embodiment of evidence that not all games adhere to this philosophy. Sadly, the game is also highly overlooked. Many people have, despite its obvious superiority to popular shooters, never been aware of its existence.
The story is well written and quite riveting. Spec Ops: The Line places you in inconceivable situations, and imposes morbidity regardless of choices you make. For example, if you were given an option to save either a close friend or a hundred innocent people, you will feel equally awful no matter what you choose. While this might refrain from appearing unprecedented, Spec Ops: The Line does so in a believable setting with well-built characters, conveying emotional and vivid events.
I thoroughly enjoyed the graphics. The yellow sands contrast well with the blue and purple hues used throughout. Many scenes are beautiful, the conjunction of ruined city and serene sand paints a stunning landscape. Spec Ops: The Line’s port (the game originally debuted on the Xbox 360) is adequate, most elements perform perfectly, however there are a few things that were not implemented well. Apart from minor issues, the game looks and plays fine on the PC.
Unfortunately, Spec Ops: The Line does not innovate further. The gameplay mechanics are similar to an average third-person shooter. Acoustics are acceptable, but far from memorable. I felt that even slight enhancements on these elements would significantly improve upon the overall experience. Nevertheless, it is still enjoyable to play.
Overall, I highly recommend this game to anyone who is seeking a shooter with a fantastic story. To me, a good story is always imperative - this one supersedes many others of the genre. Spec Ops: The Line is usually on sale during special events. That being said, I think it is completely worth it at full price, especially considering the quality that rivals many full-priced games.

Life is Strange: Before the Storm is a decision-based episodic dramatic story-driven adventure game where it serves as a prequel of the original season of Life is Strange in which it takes part two years ago.  With three planned main episodes for this season, the other main character, that is, the 16-year-old Chloe Price, is being introduced in further details in which we get to see her perspective toward her surrounding environment and feel the emotions and hardships she goes through to better understand how she reacts and deals with different issues in her life, that being family, friends, high school, and lifestyle.  With many changes that occurred in her life, Chloe is faced with new realities each time.  The sorrowful passing of her father, the mysterious disappearance of her best friend Max, who is the main character in the original season, the struggle of both emotional and financial stabilities, and the new unusual scary love of Chloe with Rachel Amber are all aspects of story-rich adventure which covey the dramatic elements of Chloe's life.  Yet, she stands determined to follow her motto, that is, "dream life over real life" where she unconditionally pursue her happiness with little regard to the negative consequences this may result.  Living real and not faking it is what really derives Chloe to perform her best in life.  The balance between the power of courage and the beacon of innocence in her heart is vital for her success.  Throughout the story, Chloe is seen to face the challenges of this required balance of forces which leads her to the many possibilities in her life both sad and happy ones.  It is crucial now, however, that this season’s perspective of Chloe and Rachel two years prior to the return of Max is considered important to understand the outcomes of this season and how they affected the beginning of the original season.  The emotional concept of relationships and true happiness is a dynamic process in which all the above characters find unsettling while living it.  It is as of a living heart which has its own learnings from the many impacts and alternations of realities due to sever conditions that are out of control. The involvements of other characters, no matter how small, find their way into the story line where views from others could be shifted to reflect new changes upon many issues.  Ultimately, good deeds truly pay off.  Good heart and good human are what make us unique and beautiful.  The lesson of dream, happiness, and achievement is what one will learn from such a lovely story of emotional survival.
