First off, if you're a completionist like me, this game gets tiresome.  I did 100% of the side stuff in the first two areas (three if you count the starter zone,) and that's when the dullness set in.
To me, it feels like they had a good 8-10 hours of story planned out, then added in a ton of exploration.   Grabbing upgrade materials is nice, and scavenging for artifacts of the past can be fun, but it all felt the same after a while.
Now, I would still say the game is worth a playthrough.  If you work toward getting all the things, you can pretty much fully upgrade Max before the second half of the game.  Upgrading the car takes a bit more due to other ingame requirements, but the main car does feel nice, and feels better with each upgrade.  I found the other vehicles in the game a bit of a chore to drive after getting used to the Magnum Opus.
I ended up finishing it quickly and skipping most of the exploration in the second half of the game because I wanted to finish it before Fallout 4 comes out, and I was happy with how the story unfolded when I actually played the missions one after another instead of one mission every 5 hours or so like the first half of the game was played.  The very final battle was a bit lackluster, but the leadup was entertaining, and most of the characters are well portrayed.
No pro/con for me.  It's a fun, beautiful, fairly interesting game if you play it for the story.  If you play it to get 100%, you'll find yourself getting tired of doing the same stuff over and over.

First off, I highly recommend this game. Provided you also get he following DLC, High Power Cargo Pack and Going East Expansion. The first adds new cargo and trailers that are both more rewarding and heavier than the original cargo variety. The second adds a large new section of map to drive, and many more cities and countries. Both are well worth the added cost. The other DLC's available consists of custom paint jobs. They add nothing to the gameplay, but you can buy those if you like them.
About the game;
You are a truck driver in Europe. You select what city you want to base your future company in, and start out working for companies delivering cargo with their trucks. You gain experience with each load that is safely delivered without doing too much damage. You can choose to buy your own truck as soon as you save enough money, or by getting a loan from the bank. If you own your own truck, you can upgrade or customize it however you choose (once you obtain the experience levels to unlock the upgrades wanted). You earn more money if you own your truck vs. driving a company's truck. As you get more money and discover various cities, you can buy additional garages and hire drivers to work for you... increasing your income. You will have to buy a truck for each new driver, and upgrade your garages to gain space for more drivers.  Garages come in 2 sizes. Small has space for 3 drivers and costs $180,000  A small garage can be upgraded to a large garage for an additional $100,000. A large garage also has a fuel pump for your benefit.
While the game is a good game, it is not without certain shortcomings.
First, There are many features that SCS had the code for from prior releases in the series that could have been included but were not. In Hard Trucks wipers had 2 speeds, now they only have 1. In Extreme Trucking, you had a variety of weather and road conditions, from ice and snow, to dirt roads and steep terrain. Here, the weather is very simple... it is either not raining, or its raining. Roads are all paved and quite uneventful. Hills are gradual, and the roads are formed from a set pattern of road sections that have been copied and repeated over and over.
Another omission is that much of the available upgrades do absolutely nothing.  Most trucks offer 3 different truck cabs. A standard cab w/ no sleeper, a standard cab w/ sleeper, and a larger cab with a bigger sleeper. None of the cabs affect the trucks fuel economy, handling, or performance. The addition of a sleeper does not enable you to rest anywhere that a non-sleeper truck can. It's all purely cosmetic. Same for the transmissions. Al trucks come with a 12 speed transmission regardless of engine. Upgrading to the other 12 speed transmission does nothing for the performance or fuel economy. Tires are another thing, no matter what tires you choose, the handling, performance, fuel economy and wear are the same. All pure cosmetics. Adding a front bumper or guard does nothing to increase the durability of the truck. the AI traffic pays no attention to the existance of the roof mounted safety strobe lamps, nor is there and aerodynamic penalty for the wind drag from a roof mounted light bar full of lights and horns. Horns are ignored by traffic as well. Both horns and roof safety strobe lamps are purely there for cosmetics.
The AI traffic has it's own issues. They will change lanes suddenly, stop suddenly, crash into you, and cause traffic jams lasting over an hour. They also are prone to hauling♥♥♥♥♥.. I've been running 102 mph and been passed and couldn't keep up with traffic cars before in 50 mph zones.
A big issue relates to the drivers you hire and the trucks they drive. It does not make one bit of difference if you buy the cheapest truck you can get (a $97,000 Man for example), or buy the most tricked out, most powerful, most expensive truck (A fully decked out Scania or Volvo costing $275,000+)... you earn the same. Upgrading their trucks does not speed them up, enable them to haul heavier loads, or make them happy... It doesn't do anything. Save your money and give each driver hte cheapest basic truck you can buy. You also cannot see the other trucks on the road, nor in the garages, ever. They only exist as a small thumbnail picture in the manager section.
Things I'd like to see in future updates:
More weather types... Snow and Ice, hail, fog, etc...
More variety in roads, Steep hills and switchbacks, narrow roads with high dropoffs and no guardrails. Dirt, gravel and pothole filled bumpy roads. Roads with deep ruts.
Functional tires that have varying grip depending on terrain and weather. Make better tires last longer or have better traction than cheap tires.
Adjust the engine outputs and trailer load weights so that pulling a 55,000lb trailer with the entry level engine is nearly impossible... making having a more powerful engine something you both need and desire. Adjust fuel economy so that the more powerful the engine, the worse your mileage (currently, there is no difference)
Make upgrading trucks for your driver have a benefit.
Make traffic AI react to safety hazard strobes (stay back a safe distance, give way when turning, etc...) as well as move over when possible if you blow the horn at them.
Make truck cab differences matter. If no sleeper, you stay only in a Hotel or at your upgraded garage. If a small sleeper, you can rest at gas stations and rest areas, but you have to rest longer to get a full 11 hrs driving time. If you have the large sleeper, you rest better, so you don't have to rest as long to get fully rested.
Add additional transmissions to different trucks. Some trucks have 10 speeds, some have 18 speeds..
Just one more delivery, then I'll go do something constructive...

The controls are really wonky on a keyboard but because of the way the mechanics work, there's not really a better way to assign keys than the defaults already present. The actions in game are a little weird, the timings are very odd, and there are times that I think I'm going one direction but in fact I am not because you can't change the direction your character faces when it is swinging a weapon, which is all the time because many levels have you surrounded my enemies who ignore walls and launch homing attacks, requiring you to swing and run as fast as you can. There is no time to examine situations a lot of the time, you just run and attack and die. Other people have said it gets easier after many hours of gameplay because you will have eventually acquired enough upgrades to your legacy (HP upgrades and equipment, etc., all stay permanent to all new characters, despite the game telling you that their corpses were not recoverable from the dungeon), but I've invested maybe two hours into dying repeatedly without getting enough gold to get anywhere. Each time you start over you lose all of the money you acquired during the previous life, so by the time you have bought out all of the cheaper upgrades, you are just running repeatedly into a meat grinder hoping that you get really lucky to walk into a room with a huge pile of money in the very beginning of the dungeon. Of course that never happens, and the cheaper upgrades don't matter.
If you are a stubborn person who wants to die constantly and eventually after tens of hours be able to say you can speedrun a dungeon in five minutes because you spent all that time getting character upgrades, maybe this is for you, but if you are like the rest of us who don't find frustration amusing then this is unfortunately not as fun as, say, Symphony of the Night.

Very few games have made me feel like Spec Ops: The Line has. To me, it seems like an abundant number of shooters are growing increasingly generic. Producing gore for gore’s sake, and scarcely ever using mature or violent content to actually make you feel for a character. Spec Ops: The Line is the embodiment of evidence that not all games adhere to this philosophy. Sadly, the game is also highly overlooked. Many people have, despite its obvious superiority to popular shooters, never been aware of its existence.
The story is well written and quite riveting. Spec Ops: The Line places you in inconceivable situations, and imposes morbidity regardless of choices you make. For example, if you were given an option to save either a close friend or a hundred innocent people, you will feel equally awful no matter what you choose. While this might refrain from appearing unprecedented, Spec Ops: The Line does so in a believable setting with well-built characters, conveying emotional and vivid events.
I thoroughly enjoyed the graphics. The yellow sands contrast well with the blue and purple hues used throughout. Many scenes are beautiful, the conjunction of ruined city and serene sand paints a stunning landscape. Spec Ops: The Line’s port (the game originally debuted on the Xbox 360) is adequate, most elements perform perfectly, however there are a few things that were not implemented well. Apart from minor issues, the game looks and plays fine on the PC.
Unfortunately, Spec Ops: The Line does not innovate further. The gameplay mechanics are similar to an average third-person shooter. Acoustics are acceptable, but far from memorable. I felt that even slight enhancements on these elements would significantly improve upon the overall experience. Nevertheless, it is still enjoyable to play.
Overall, I highly recommend this game to anyone who is seeking a shooter with a fantastic story. To me, a good story is always imperative - this one supersedes many others of the genre. Spec Ops: The Line is usually on sale during special events. That being said, I think it is completely worth it at full price, especially considering the quality that rivals many full-priced games.

Life is Strange: Before the Storm is a decision-based episodic dramatic story-driven adventure game where it serves as a prequel of the original season of Life is Strange in which it takes part two years ago.  With three planned main episodes for this season, the other main character, that is, the 16-year-old Chloe Price, is being introduced in further details in which we get to see her perspective toward her surrounding environment and feel the emotions and hardships she goes through to better understand how she reacts and deals with different issues in her life, that being family, friends, high school, and lifestyle.  With many changes that occurred in her life, Chloe is faced with new realities each time.  The sorrowful passing of her father, the mysterious disappearance of her best friend Max, who is the main character in the original season, the struggle of both emotional and financial stabilities, and the new unusual scary love of Chloe with Rachel Amber are all aspects of story-rich adventure which covey the dramatic elements of Chloe's life.  Yet, she stands determined to follow her motto, that is, "dream life over real life" where she unconditionally pursue her happiness with little regard to the negative consequences this may result.  Living real and not faking it is what really derives Chloe to perform her best in life.  The balance between the power of courage and the beacon of innocence in her heart is vital for her success.  Throughout the story, Chloe is seen to face the challenges of this required balance of forces which leads her to the many possibilities in her life both sad and happy ones.  It is crucial now, however, that this season’s perspective of Chloe and Rachel two years prior to the return of Max is considered important to understand the outcomes of this season and how they affected the beginning of the original season.  The emotional concept of relationships and true happiness is a dynamic process in which all the above characters find unsettling while living it.  It is as of a living heart which has its own learnings from the many impacts and alternations of realities due to sever conditions that are out of control. The involvements of other characters, no matter how small, find their way into the story line where views from others could be shifted to reflect new changes upon many issues.  Ultimately, good deeds truly pay off.  Good heart and good human are what make us unique and beautiful.  The lesson of dream, happiness, and achievement is what one will learn from such a lovely story of emotional survival.

Now, I would still say the game is worth a playthrough.  If you work toward getting all the things, you can pretty much fully upgrade Max before the second half of the game.  Upgrading the car takes a bit more due to other ingame requirements, but the main car does feel nice, and feels better with each upgrade.  I found the other vehicles in the game a bit of a chore to drive after getting used to the Magnum Opus.
I ended up finishing it quickly and skipping most of the exploration in the second half of the game because I wanted to finish it before Fallout 4 comes out, and I was happy with how the story unfolded when I actually played the missions one after another instead of one mission every 5 hours or so like the first half of the game was played.  The very final battle was a bit lackluster, but the leadup was entertaining, and most of the characters are well portrayed.
No pro/con for me.  It's a fun, beautiful, fairly interesting game if you play it for the story.  If you play it to get 100%, you'll find yourself getting tired of doing the same stuff over and over.

This game is worth the $30 and it is a great improvement over the last game.
Pros:
-No microtransaction (everything can be unlocked relatively easily, to those saying it takes ages you just have to stop scaring away everything you are about to shoot, I've unlocked 2 new rifles in 10 hours of gameplay)
-Beautiful graphics (the optimisation however isn't the best for example having too many points marked on the GPS can cause lag when the GPS is open)
-Easily the most realistic hunting sim (weapon ballistics, correct hitboxes for each animal)
-Multiplayer is very easy to setup and is p2p (just invite your friend to your game and they'll be able to join)
-Very nice sounds
-Very large map and nicely decorated
Cons:
-Animals sometimes stand in place (haven't encountered this since patch though)
-Average optimisation
-Some animals for example rabbits and birds can be killed but you cannot harvest their bodies
-You make way more noise than you should (having a walk button that makes you slower and quiter could solve this)
-Sometimes the tracks are pointing in the wrong direction
-Bears attacking you is a bit glitchy
-Some form of campaign/storyline which is nice however they're basically just quests to go do things
Things you should know before buying:
-Only 14 different weapons without around 2-3 ammo types for each
-This is a very slow paced game so you'll probably find yourself getting frustrated if you're sprinting around looking for animals to shoot
-Map is very large and there isn't any vehicles however when you claim an outpost you can fast travel between them
-Your shots can ricochet off animals and you'll probably get mad and think it is a bug like I did the first time it happened
-It helps to know how to hunt in real life
-Knowing where to aim is key
-Ballistic system
-RPG like leveling up and skill system however they don't make much of a difference
-High end system is probably needed
-This game has controller support
So yes I recommend this game at it's current price of $30 with no microtransactions

It's a decent shoot and loot, not as enjoyable as the first game in terms of gameplay, however, Borderlands 2 has a much better story and more interesting characters.  Personally, I think the level design is much more monotonous so while the replayability is fairly high, it's not enjoyable seeing the same landscape/environment more than once.
I've noticed that the loot system isn't as interesting or randomised anymore either, there's only a set amount of legendary gear you can obtain whereas in the first Borderlands, every single legendary had random stats and a randomised name.
The DLC in Borderlands 2 is quite fun, each DLC is more developed and has a more interesting quest/storyline which interesting new characters in each one. my personal favourite was Tiny Tina's Assault on Dragon Keep because it incorporated so many RPG and Dungeon Crawling stereotypes and elements which made it funny and also interesting to play.
In my opinion, if you loved the first game for what it was and have high expectations, Borderlands 2 (preferably GOTY edition) is only worth purchasing on sale.

Summary: A wonderfully created and well thought out game. There is obvious love in this series with the sky being the limit with the type/amount of content this developer could add. I highly recommend anybody interested in creating their own prison, or even thinking about "hey I need a new building game," to give this little gem a shot.
Post 8 hour summary: Prison architect is an easy to learn, but harder to master, game that involves delicate manipulation of prisoner populations in order to run a successful and profitable prison. The indie nature of the game is apparent but adds to the charm of this title with the easily animated "circles" of characters happily whistle and glide throughout the lengths of your prison in comical fashion. Donot, however, feel like this game will be a walk in the park for even experienced sim users. If you do not quickly address your prisoners needs you will soon learn that beneath the "friendly" nature of the game lies a darker system of violence, blood shed, and even death. I mean, who wants to see their favourite K9 get killed in a mass riot?
(review to continue)
Positive:
+ Wonderfully complex prisoner mood/attitude system
+ Moderate learning curve with steep learning curve to mastery

Negative

- Worker AI still manages to trap themselves in rooms
- Tutorial could be expanded to cover more topics

Nobody is going to read all of what I wrote so I'm going to put a required TL:DR right here:
Undertale is a game that I enjoyed, the plot was basic for me but for people that only play shooters ( younger gamers ) it's probably one of the best thing's they'll ever witness, the soundtrack was amazing and the characters are enjoyable. I would personally give it a 6.5/10 but for most gamers I would give it a 8/10 because most gamers these days haven't played something that has this much time, and care put into it. I would say it's a required buy if you are a young gamer or if you want a game you can play to just relax and not take too seriously. You'll definetly enjoy it. ( don't look anything up though it ruins the game, also the community is one of the worst things i've ever seen in my entire life )
I bought this game the year it was released and I only heard about it because it was in a "best game of all time" vote in 2015 and it was crushing all of it's opponents. So I bought it after doing some light reading on it about how it has this 'mercy' mechanic and how it made some people really chose how they played the game and made them think etc and etc.
I thought 'cool whatever' as a fan of indie games I'm always interested in different mechanics that put into these games compared most bigger production games. Before I continue I will state that I do NOT think that this puts triple A games to shame, nor did I have a review on my entire life after playing this game through with all three of it's story arcs. I beat the game the first time in around 3 hours but most of that time was spent messing around and checking things out.
I definetly enjoyed the characters, some more then others, although they were too transparent about everything and started to feel a bit stale the other times I went through this game. I never felt this 'emotional' connect towards any of these chraracters. And I definetly did not feel any personal development towards them during my playthroughs, it was more like: 'oh this character is kinda funny, this one is kinda annoying. This one is a total ♥♥♥♥♥ wtf seriously'.
The plot was so one dementional I did a double take when reading some of the reviews of this game saying that the story is one of the best things about this game. The story is one of the most overrated things about this game in my opinion luckily it's overshadowed by the amazing soundtrack which in my opinion is the saving grace of this game.
The mercy consept was pretty neat in theory but the overall effect that it has on the game is minimal besides ( as mentioned before ) some dialogue and story arc. Sparing one boss but killing another won't actually change anything in the story. I didn't find that sparing bosses or monsters was 'the right choice' or something I felt like I wanted to do it was just something I did to get a different ending so that I could say that I did that.
The next section contains kinda spoilers, it's basically my description of my playthroughs of this game and thats about it. I would personally skip it if you have never played undertale before as going in blind is 50x better then going in with prior information.
The first two playthroughs I killed who I wanted but not everyone and I breezed through the game with extreme ease as everything was actually a joke, the final boss was a letdown after the entire game was spent building him up as someone that would kill me on the spot, the ending of this playthrough was actually a surprise and I enjoyed this playthrough the most of them all. The second playthrough I wanted to see what would happen if I spared everything that I came across and again, I get a different ending, this one was less enjoyable and extremely undersatisfactory especially as this is the 'best ending' you can get. The third time I desided that these miserable sprites didn't deserve to live anymore so I killed everything in my path, most people that I found online thought that this was the hardest one to do especially after building a 'connection' with the characters which I personally thought was crazy. The final boss in this run was moderatly difficult and after you get past the first half of the fight it's actually pretty easy ( in my opinion ). The ending to this run in my opinion felt pretty rushed although I would much rather it over the first ending that I did.

I would make some remarks about the community but that would quadruple the length of this ( decently long ) review so I'll spare you. Undertale is a pretty enjoyable game, while I did kinda drag myself through the third playthrough of the game I wouldn't say that I disliked the game. My review would probably leave you scratching your head ( is that something people still say? ) about what I just wrote but i'll explain. I didn't dislike undertale, I do not think that it was the best game of 2015, I do not think that the story was one of the best things i've ever expirienced in the world. I would never say that the characters in this game were the most connected i've ever felt with video game chracters. I would never say any of that and I wouldn't say a lot of other things about undertale that a lot would. But I will say that it's something that every young gamer has to play because the majority of games that they will play won't ever have the amount of thought, creativity or depth as this game has. I've played better but that doesn't mean that everyone has and that's where I would say the praise that undertale gets is from, it's a NEW game that NEW/YOUNGER people need to play rather then the next call of duty or battlefield or whatever.
Most young gamers have never played a game with this much time put into it or with an actual story ( insert basically any game released in the past 3 months here ). They're just used to seeing a person with a gun and shooting the person. And that's the appeal to undertale, it's a game with time, effort and care put into it that just so happens to have possibly one of the most annoying communities out there.
So if you are a younger gamer out there I would definetly reccomend this game to you, you need this game to realize just how much there is out there to expirience in the world of games, there's a lot of good stuff besides CSGO or league or the next 70 COD's. Take a chance, I'm sure you'll enjoy it. You actually don't have to be young, I would reccomend this game ( besides all of it's massive flaws ) to basically anyone that plays the same 1 genre of game ( FPS ) because they need a break from mindless killing to just relax, play a game that doesn't take itself seriously and just enjoy it. Although if you are buying this game do NOT ( i'm going to say it again ) DO NOT. Play this game with ANY prior knowledge about any of the characters, endings, or story if you wish to enjoy the game to it's fullest, if you learn anything, just wait a bit til it goes on sale then buy it because it'll be so much better if you do.
I give this game a solid 6.5/10 ( my score ) and a 8/10 for anyone else, the story is basic but better then anything released in the past couple months, the mercy mechanic has minimal effect on anything unless your doing a full mercy run or a full kill run. Characters are enjoyable ( some more then others ) and soundtrack is one of the best i've heard in a long time.

How can you release a game this broken after having made the same game (in essence) twice already? It looks great, has great atmosphere but it has so many bugs in it I should be talking in Starship Troopers quotes.
Let's update the review to the current (1.62 version).
1) EW releasing an alpha version game as a full game release (see
) they have not improved the game in any significant way so far. About 50% of all the forum threads at the point of writing are bug report threads (1500 out of 3000). This EW comment sums it up:
Any player that tries to claim 'I have seen no bugs so far' I just want to punch in the face. If you logged thousands of hours ingame like I have in hundreds of games, you recognise bugs when you see them. Don't even try to tell me there aren't bugs ingame. I have contributed several pages worth of bug reports so far and the response from EW so far has been underwhelming. Communicaiton is key in any company, but aparently not for EW.
2) Any information gathered so far about ingame mechanics has been community wise (see breakdown of integrity/hunting score. The ingame 'codex' system is severely lacking and questions in the forum get answered by fellow gamers. Maybe a 100 sensible posts were made by EW staff. All other posts are 'Dev team is looking into this...' or 'we have removed your posts, read up on the guidelines'. Right now people are trying to make a wiki because hey... where else can we get info?
3) Too much arcade things going on still... if you have seen a few deer, you will have seen pretty much all of them. Antlers all look the same in the same category, you cannot zero your gun to distances other than what they implemented in a skill(!) No choosing grainload, "Consecutive Harvest" (sort of fixed now), ... it's like a better Cabela game at this point... but that is really it. They talk about 'hunting tactics' while all you really do is sprint untill you hear a 'warning call' or you just spam callers untill animals show up. Animal/pathing AI has a lot to be desired.
4) DLC so far has been weird at best. We got a 'free' reskin of an already ingame bow. And some free textures. Any normal devteam would have just patched that in. But this is EW we are talking about. The company that has so far excelled at milking loyal customers up to the point of alienating their playerbase. I have nothing against DLC, but it has to be substantial or it should not give DLC owners an advantage over other players. (not if you want online competition - if they ever get the multiplayer working correctly). What happened was the folowing: Outposts are bugged in multiplayer -> you need to BUY DLC to mediate the problem. Core mechanics such as fasttraveling should not be added in DLC. Reskins of tents and whatnot could be sold as cosmetic DLC, but not things that should have been in the game from the start. And to top it off; DLC AFTER TWO MONTHS?!? WHAT?
5) And don't even get me started on the UI, it's a mess beyond comprehension.
Don't get me wrong, it's a great walking simulator. Just not a hunting sim. A hunting game, yes, but it lacks core features to make it a great hunting game.
How I see it so far is this: The game world was bought (Apex engine) and that works fine. All the rest is EW coded and it is sloppy at best. Unfortunately EW has continued to disappoint so far where they could have had a great game on their hands. If any of their employees does decide to read this review, then I really recommend to polish up your marketing strategy and enhance the communication towards the playerbase, which is starting to lose faith.
Discussions on the forum are heavily moderated in a way where EW is not 'doing anything wrong'. Anyone claiming otherwise will see his/her posts removed and getting banned. So much for feedback. Some of the new mods have a (toxic) attitude and behave in an utter hypocitical manner.
When looking at EW's track record (THC microtransactions milking players beyond what is considered normal and THP where they straight up abandoned the product) customers have all the right to be distrustful of this company.

Modern Military Shooters (MMS) are some of the biggest budget games that are released every year, with "extreme" realism and crappy storyline that look copied from a children's book and tries to get under our skin, but epic fails and falls flat.
WELL, Spec Ops: The Line skullf*cks the formula by giving one of the most epic single player experiences, making it one of the best games of 2012 for me and one of the best stories of all time in a game, despite the barebones competitive multiplayer and Co-Op missions...
Graphics are really good, detail is nice, voice acting is stellar and so is face animation. Some of the controls, however seem to be directly ported from console as the key to vault over cover is the same as melee, and sprinting is the same as getting into cover
, however, after a bit of playing it, you will get used to it, but you may get some cheap-shot deaths from those awkward controls in the start...
As for story, the game nails it. It happens in a corrupt war-damaged Dubai, where a squad of 3 soldiers battle to get civilians out of the mess that happened, however, you face many decisions, that fight your moral principals and can make you feel bad for the sh*t you've done throughout the game. Your choices, like an RPG, affect the ending and most of them are really tricky as you don't know which one to take, since all of them have heavy consequences. Spec Ops: The Line makes you use your morality and ethical code to the extreme. Something rare nowadays in the gaming industry...
Multiplayer is just...there, it can provide fun moments but not many, since it feels tacked on, you can clearly see that all the effort was put in the SP Campaign. Co-Op can be fun with a friend but not much else as you only have 4 missions, but they are really hard to pull off so an extra hand can be a life-savior, too bad the Co-Op isn't for 4 players or 3 (like a squad, like from the campaign), it's only for 2 players, but i'm ok with it actually unlike, MW3 survival mode for example, as 4 players would make much more sense.
Also, gameplay is well done, the gunplay is smooth but some guns come punch a bit harder...
The cover system works well (one of the best and most fluid I've ever seen!), and other mechanics (execution for example) work nicely too, despite the confusing controls, but although the gameplay mechanics work, it isn't groundbreaking in any stretch of the imagination so the game may get repetitive after your first playthrough so the final difficulty unlocked after beating the game may never be experienced due to the repetitive nature of the gameplay.
Spec Ops is one of those "don't miss it" games, and, despite it's *minimal* flaws, it deserves an 9.5/10
While the game doesn't really surprise in the beggining, the situation gets better in the middle and end, so youtube gameplay may not be helpful to make up your mind. Also, only when you *are playing the game yourself* does the game appeal, not in gameplay videos, in my opinion. It's like 20 euros now on steam, much lower on sales (like 4,99 €) so, you can't miss it!

Can a video game use clunky controls and cheap deaths to get its message across? Can a video game make you feel guilty about things it told you to do?
War is hell, and you experience it as Captain Martin Walker of Delta Force who is sent to a apocalyptic Dubai along with his friends to look for survivors. What starts of as an average 3rd Person military shooter, turns into something that most video games shy away from. You witness public executions, walk through a mass grave, and see soldiers burst into flames, each one effecting Walker and his friends mental state until they are a shell of their former self. You are not meant to enjoy Spec Ops The Line, as the game will always put the odds against you and any "heroic action" will get you killed. The choices you make will affect everyone around you, and doing what needs to be done isn't always right thing to do, and sometimes, you don't have a choice. Spec Ops: The Line is a dark and grim game that I highly recommend.
Take your time with this one. And when it's a 75% sale, buy the GOTY edition. You're better off with it.

Summary: A wonderfully created and well thought out game. There is obvious love in this series with the sky being the limit with the type/amount of content this developer could add. I highly recommend anybody interested in creating their own prison, or even thinking about "hey I need a new building game," to give this little gem a shot.
Post 8 hour summary: Prison architect is an easy to learn, but harder to master, game that involves delicate manipulation of prisoner populations in order to run a successful and profitable prison. The indie nature of the game is apparent but adds to the charm of this title with the easily animated "circles" of characters happily whistle and glide throughout the lengths of your prison in comical fashion. Donot, however, feel like this game will be a walk in the park for even experienced sim users. If you do not quickly address your prisoners needs you will soon learn that beneath the "friendly" nature of the game lies a darker system of violence, blood shed, and even death. I mean, who wants to see their favourite K9 get killed in a mass riot?

Negative

This game is frustrating because it could so easily be better if the devs put more work into it; and because with a few patches, it could become something great.
While you can lift things, there doesn't seem the be a button to throw what you've picked up. Neither are there any loose objects that you can pick up to use as weapons, which seems like a missed oppurtunity. Punching seems to occasionally be able to knock people out (though is usually completely ineffective), but they only stay KO'd for a second or two.
All of these thing I discovered through experimentation while trying the game with a few friends, as neither the controls nor the mechanics are explained in the slightest. In the end, we were only able to extract about 45 minutes of fun from it, at which point I promptly requested a refund. The game badly needs a tutorial and possibly a Smash Bros style HUD.

Since last year, me and my room mates have enjoyed drinking and playing this game together. The last update however, made the game significantly less fun. It was so bad, that we actually put the game down after only fifteen minutes. This is the shortest that we have ever played the game. All in all, the latest update is a very large step backward.
The first of my three biggest complains, is that that knockouts are totally broken. You can't knock people out anymore. If you hear the *crack* sound when you knock someone out, they're back up within a second. This takes all the fun out of watching helplessly as someone clumsily tries to throw you over a railing. It's almost impossible to even throw someone out now in the wrestling ring arena now. The only way we were able to get someone out, was when the game glitched, and the person trying to pick up someone knocked out flew into the air.
The second, is that the climbing mechanics are practically nonexistant. A large portion of the game's appeal to me and my room mates, was trying to grab onto someone climbing a wall, and pulling them off. The new climbing is awful. We used to be able to scale the wall in the train arena to avoid being hit by the train, but you can't even get that high anymore. Even worse, if you try to continue to climb after running out of "climbing stamina", you slide back down the wall. On a similar note, it appears that the grip strength has been reduced as well. This has also been very frustrating.
The third issue, is that the lives no longer appear on screen anymore. It turns out that if you hit the back button, you can see them, but that's extremely inconvenient.
As much as it pains me, I can't recommend this game until the developers have either fixed these issues, or rolled back to the previous version. This really is a great game, and the developers have been on top of updating it and adding new levels. I would still reccomend this game, but I hope that this negative vote is enough to get the attention of the developers.

In it's current state, playing a 4-Player Local co-op has lost its appeal.  The number of lives remaining is no longer shown on screen, and each round takes much too long due to the 'knock out' changes.
I will change my vote to 'recommended' again if the mechanics are fixed or adjusted for the better.

A very fun game that explores the brutal post apocalyptic part of the world that was Australia.  The game has two major gameplay elements with one being the car and the other being on foot or ground combat.  Driving your car through the world and mixing it up with the random gangs in the wasteland is the best part of the game.  As you gather more scrap you are able to upgrade your car with fun "toys" that truly does some damage to anyone that crosses your path.
On the other hand, being on foot can be very boring compared to the car.  Ground combat is a very simple affair with one button counters that pretty much win every battle as long as you can time them up correctly.  Most of the time I try to limit my time on foot as much as possible so I can stay where the fun is at.....in the car.
The story isn't that great, but it does enough to get the job done.  The game allows you to do your own thing more or less and you can pick up and drop the story as you see fit to run around the world exploring or blowing stuff up.  I did feel at times that the game was almost too much sandbox and there needed to be more of a direction given to the players.
Overall, if you are looking for a post apocalyptic game with excellent car combat then Mad Max will satisfy that itch.

Can a video game use clunky controls and cheap deaths to get its message across? Can a video game make you feel guilty about things it told you to do?
War is hell, and you experience it as Captain Martin Walker of Delta Force who is sent to a apocalyptic Dubai along with his friends to look for survivors. What starts of as an average 3rd Person military shooter, turns into something that most video games shy away from. You witness public executions, walk through a mass grave, and see soldiers burst into flames, each one effecting Walker and his friends mental state until they are a shell of their former self. You are not meant to enjoy Spec Ops The Line, as the game will always put the odds against you and any "heroic action" will get you killed. The choices you make will affect everyone around you, and doing what needs to be done isn't always right thing to do, and sometimes, you don't have a choice. Spec Ops: The Line is a dark and grim game that I highly recommend.

Ein großartiges Spiel welches meiner Meinung nach sowohl grafisch als auch storytechnisch sehr gelungen ist. Durch einige Entscheidungen, die getroffen werden müssen und die 4 Enden erhöht sich der Wiederspielwert der Kampagne. Spec Ops: The Line zeigt sowohl die Grauen des Krieges als auch den Wahnsinn, dem die Soldaten verfallen können, auf recht brutale Weise. Durch unterschiedliche Sekundärfunktionen (wie zB. Schalldämpfer oder Granatwerfer) der verschiedenen Waffen wird versucht, diese einzigartig zu gestalten. Weiterhin positiv hervorzuheben ist die wunderbare Grafik sowohl die passende, wenn auch teilweise zynische musikalische Untermalung während der Kämpfe. Den beiden Teamkameraden kann man leider nur konzentriertes Feuern auf ein festgelegtes Ziel befehlen, das teilweise sinnlose Im-Weg-stehen der beiden nervt etwas und trägt dazu bei ihnen ab und zu versehentlich eine Kugel zu verpassen. Es gibt zwar einige taktische Ansätze, jedoch werden diese nicht weitergeführt. Weitere Kritikpunkte sind sowohl die etwas gewöhnungsbedürftige Steuerung (zB. die Mehrfachbelegung der Leertaste) als auch die stellenweise zu schweren Kämpfe. Jedoch macht der Multiplayer durch die unterschiedlichen, etwas anderen Modi einen recht guten Eindruck.
Alles in allem ist dieser Antikriegsshooter, bei dem es nicht wirklich einen Helden sowie ein Happyend gibt und hinterfragt was gut und böse im Krieg ist, eine gute Alternative zu anderen Shootern und sehr zu empfehlen.

This is pretty much an experience that isn't fun, and I mean that in the best way possible. You see, it's what the designers wanted, and this game succeeds in what it tries to do. It's meant to explore PTSD and the psychology of war while offering a parody and criticique of modern military shooters, which it does with the engaging narrative, the mechanics that act as metaphors for the themes and the unifying artistic vision. Reviewers that lambast the game for poor gameplay and an overall lack of fun perhaps do not understand the design decisions behind these elements. The developers used the gameplay to make the player feel exactly like the protagonists: weak, worn out and not having fun at all. This isnt a glorfied portrayal of war and killing that ries its damnest to make the player feel like a murderous badass and hence the clunky gunplay and repetitive cover shooting. This isnt a squad-based shooter starring an ammoral, efficient squad of killers and hence the mostly useless and utterly limited squad commands. What this is, is a narrative driven experience that engages the jaded virtual killer that is me and makes me feel shameful for my actions before mocking me about my guilt and disgust at the genre as a whole. When one of the game's characters say "You're here because you wanted to feel like something you're not: a hero," you will never feel the same playing a modern military shooter ever again. This game is a experience that hints at the themes and emotions gaming as a medium can evoke.

While the gunplay is serviceable in this third person, cover-based shooter, most players would stay for the story that tells the ugly side of war instead of its glorification in most modern shooters.
As a narrative-heavy story, you should try to go in spoiler-free. Just know that Nolan North's swears a lot by the end and is praised as one of the release year's best vocal performance.

I think I’ve given this game a fair shake at this point and so far it’s been strongly negative. Maybe it’s just because it’s so over hyped but overall I have two primary complaints:
First and foremost, how in the hell are these guys getting off with charging $30 for a barely functioning alpha that plays like a senior year Comp Sci project? This game should be a pay-as-much-a- you-wish or a Kick Starter or something. There are so many bugs and so little content, how are people so pumped about this game? I’m glad I only paid $10 on sale.
Secondly, regardless of whether you tick the option to disable a continuous stream of prisoners, every day a random amount of prisoners – usually between 8 and 15 – arrive at your prison.  Simply put, this breaks the game. It takes near 24 hours game time, and more money than you make in a day, just to build the housing for your next batch of prisoners. What this means is, the entire game ends up being a tedious race to build yet another cell block, followed by inevitably building another cell block, and repeat to infinity. You have no actual time to enjoy the game. It’s monotonous and vapid.
What I expected was a fun, goofy, Sims-esque game where instead of directly controlling your little avatars, you had to facilitate or abuse them however you saw fit all whilst trying to run a successful prison. What I got was a super buggy repetitive building micro-management game where 95% of content is clicking where to put another cell.

Nobody is going to read all of what I wrote so I'm going to put a required TL:DR right here:
Undertale is a game that I enjoyed, the plot was basic for me but for people that only play shooters ( younger gamers ) it's probably one of the best thing's they'll ever witness, the soundtrack was amazing and the characters are enjoyable. I would personally give it a 6.5/10 but for most gamers I would give it a 8/10 because most gamers these days haven't played something that has this much time, and care put into it. I would say it's a required buy if you are a young gamer or if you want a game you can play to just relax and not take too seriously. You'll definetly enjoy it. ( don't look anything up though it ruins the game, also the community is one of the worst things i've ever seen in my entire life )
I bought this game the year it was released and I only heard about it because it was in a "best game of all time" vote in 2015 and it was crushing all of it's opponents. So I bought it after doing some light reading on it about how it has this 'mercy' mechanic and how it made some people really chose how they played the game and made them think etc and etc.
I thought 'cool whatever' as a fan of indie games I'm always interested in different mechanics that put into these games compared most bigger production games. Before I continue I will state that I do NOT think that this puts triple A games to shame, nor did I have a review on my entire life after playing this game through with all three of it's story arcs. I beat the game the first time in around 3 hours but most of that time was spent messing around and checking things out.
I definetly enjoyed the characters, some more then others, although they were too transparent about everything and started to feel a bit stale the other times I went through this game. I never felt this 'emotional' connect towards any of these chraracters. And I definetly did not feel any personal development towards them during my playthroughs, it was more like: 'oh this character is kinda funny, this one is kinda annoying. This one is a total ♥♥♥♥♥ wtf seriously'.
The plot was so one dementional I did a double take when reading some of the reviews of this game saying that the story is one of the best things about this game. The story is one of the most overrated things about this game in my opinion luckily it's overshadowed by the amazing soundtrack which in my opinion is the saving grace of this game.
The mercy consept was pretty neat in theory but the overall effect that it has on the game is minimal besides ( as mentioned before ) some dialogue and story arc. Sparing one boss but killing another won't actually change anything in the story. I didn't find that sparing bosses or monsters was 'the right choice' or something I felt like I wanted to do it was just something I did to get a different ending so that I could say that I did that.
The next section contains kinda spoilers, it's basically my description of my playthroughs of this game and thats about it. I would personally skip it if you have never played undertale before as going in blind is 50x better then going in with prior information.
The first two playthroughs I killed who I wanted but not everyone and I breezed through the game with extreme ease as everything was actually a joke, the final boss was a letdown after the entire game was spent building him up as someone that would kill me on the spot, the ending of this playthrough was actually a surprise and I enjoyed this playthrough the most of them all. The second playthrough I wanted to see what would happen if I spared everything that I came across and again, I get a different ending, this one was less enjoyable and extremely undersatisfactory especially as this is the 'best ending' you can get. The third time I desided that these miserable sprites didn't deserve to live anymore so I killed everything in my path, most people that I found online thought that this was the hardest one to do especially after building a 'connection' with the characters which I personally thought was crazy. The final boss in this run was moderatly difficult and after you get past the first half of the fight it's actually pretty easy ( in my opinion ). The ending to this run in my opinion felt pretty rushed although I would much rather it over the first ending that I did.

I would make some remarks about the community but that would quadruple the length of this ( decently long ) review so I'll spare you. Undertale is a pretty enjoyable game, while I did kinda drag myself through the third playthrough of the game I wouldn't say that I disliked the game. My review would probably leave you scratching your head ( is that something people still say? ) about what I just wrote but i'll explain. I didn't dislike undertale, I do not think that it was the best game of 2015, I do not think that the story was one of the best things i've ever expirienced in the world. I would never say that the characters in this game were the most connected i've ever felt with video game chracters. I would never say any of that and I wouldn't say a lot of other things about undertale that a lot would. But I will say that it's something that every young gamer has to play because the majority of games that they will play won't ever have the amount of thought, creativity or depth as this game has. I've played better but that doesn't mean that everyone has and that's where I would say the praise that undertale gets is from, it's a NEW game that NEW/YOUNGER people need to play rather then the next call of duty or battlefield or whatever.
Most young gamers have never played a game with this much time put into it or with an actual story ( insert basically any game released in the past 3 months here ). They're just used to seeing a person with a gun and shooting the person. And that's the appeal to undertale, it's a game with time, effort and care put into it that just so happens to have possibly one of the most annoying communities out there.
So if you are a younger gamer out there I would definetly reccomend this game to you, you need this game to realize just how much there is out there to expirience in the world of games, there's a lot of good stuff besides CSGO or league or the next 70 COD's. Take a chance, I'm sure you'll enjoy it. You actually don't have to be young, I would reccomend this game ( besides all of it's massive flaws ) to basically anyone that plays the same 1 genre of game ( FPS ) because they need a break from mindless killing to just relax, play a game that doesn't take itself seriously and just enjoy it. Although if you are buying this game do NOT ( i'm going to say it again ) DO NOT. Play this game with ANY prior knowledge about any of the characters, endings, or story if you wish to enjoy the game to it's fullest, if you learn anything, just wait a bit til it goes on sale then buy it because it'll be so much better if you do.
I give this game a solid 6.5/10 ( my score ) and a 8/10 for anyone else, the story is basic but better then anything released in the past couple months, the mercy mechanic has minimal effect on anything unless your doing a full mercy run or a full kill run. Characters are enjoyable ( some more then others ) and soundtrack is one of the best i've heard in a long time.

I enjoyed this game!
Pros
+ Excellent vehicle based combat. Especially convoy missions where you have to chase down and destroy a vehicle that's protected by other vehicles.
+ Well-optimized. I'm playing on a laptop (i7, GT750M, 8GB RAM) and FPS is 45-60.
+ Arkham-style hand-to-hand combat. If you've played the Arkham Batman games, you'll feel right at home.
+ Interesting locations in the big world.
Cons
- Average story, but the main story mission builds to an exciting ending.
- No real stealth gameplay. You will take out most enemies using combat, or by sniping from far.
- Almost all the bosses you encounter are reskinned versions of the same model, and use the same moves.

This game had me hooked right from the start, I grew up with the Mad Max movies having pride of place in the video cabinet. I had the bugs every one else had but it didn't matter enough to stop me playing.
The ground combat appears easy enough, for the most part it is pretty straight forward and a bit slow but it keeps up with you pretty well.
As I got used to the timing it changed, almost tetris style, it keeps going up another gear and is a lot quicker than I expected it to be and it flows flawlessly.
The vehicle combat is hard to describe, it's like opening the first 'need for speed' and just driving around, slack jawed repeating "Holy Sh-t" over and over. It doesn't take long to get the hang of it driving kbd/mse and is mostly consistent and predictable enough.
This game is awesome and in my case the 'bugs' are sorted now, my only gripe is that it's too short, mainly because I want to play more.
I am not sure it's a pro or a con but this game is resource hungry and it will take whatever you throw at it, what you get back is truly beautiful if not a bit desolate.
**** Update:
It's a month later and a whole lot more hours.
Patch #4 has been released and  the remaining bugs are gone in most cases.
I had visions of Arkhem Knight but fortunately we've missed the low standard set by that fiasco.
The word is that there will be NO DLC, so this game has to stand on it's own making it too short and lacking a bit of variety in gameplay which is a shame.
As it stands game time can run from from about 25 to 70+hrs depending on your wish to complete 100% or not.
It's still a fun game and I'm still playing but the game could be so much better with a few more maps and side missions.

This is my second edit of this review, this time I'm going to be bit more in-depth.
The game is well worth the $30 price tag. The game is gorgeous and contains 2 massive, interesting, and varied hunting reserves. I have yet to even explore more than 25% of each reserve.
In my opinion the game has enough weapons for now, I've yet to use anything other than the starter rifle. The ammunition prices could be a bit more modest but I suppose it does encourage you to conserve ammo and take safe shots.
The game still has a few AI bugs and UI problems here and there but after today's (3/3/2017) patch, I haven't experienced any crashes and have had more success in-game as a result of the sneaking fix.
This game is relaxing, even if you don't enjoy hunting in real life (I don't) this game is still very enjoyable. Take a break from hunting and go out and explore for some artifacts, lookout points, and lore points.
A few things I would like to see in the game:
-Portable Campsites - Pack a tent for a mobile outpost (does not have to contain shop)
-Tree Stands
-Jonboats or canoes for navigating the rivers, lakes, and ponds of the world.
-Fishing
-Able to complete missions and unlock outposts/lookout points in multiplayer.
See you on the trails!

NOTE: This is the only review i've written on steam since i've found no game really in need of it.
I started playing the old hunter game as an escape with one of my friends and it was all right but this one is one of the best games i've played. It's so relaxing so stroll around without any competition tracking down your prey and then taking a well prepared shot. The two maps that are available are huge and has by far the most beautiful scenery and environment that i've ever seen. Walking around the huge maps really takes your mind of everything in life, add some calm music and i'm in total bliss. The sounds made for this game are amazing and it's so much so that you might for a second actually believe that you're in whatever forest or field that you're currently tracking prey in.
The game is so calm, the only thing that disturbs the peace is your bullet leaving the muzzle.
I found this game awesome to play with a friends and ganging up on some resting bear that just happens to get shot 5-10 times it's just friggin' hilarious and also brings time to talk about other stuff that might not even be related to the game.
Now on to the bad parts, the game in single player for me is running flawlessly on my setup and i have no issues at all really except for some minor bugs that won't really affect the experience.
On the other hand, multi player is riddled with small bugs that actually stack up, one of my friends game crashes all the time whilst mine doesn't and i have almost the same setup as him. The mission system doesn't work in multi player, menu's will click without any warning and i have accidentally kicked friends from the multi player game by accident because of this. If you're the host you can still locate landmarks/cabins and get the experience and lore from interacting with them, BUT your friends that are clients on the server can't which hinders the experience on their part since they can't progress in the game world when they play on your servers. But this isn't really a problem if you switch between host/client from time to time. You're usually not even concerned by this since you always get sidetracked by prey.
I can wholeheartedly recommend this game for those with patience with some minor bugs. I would agree that this game should still be in a Beta stage. But it is so immersive that i'm glad that i can take part in it right now.
If you're constantly annoyed by bugs and can't let go. Then this game might not be for you right now.

Don't let the title and genre mislead you - this is not your typical war-themed shooter. Spec Ops: The Line explores the horrors of war through its harrowing, psychologically jarring narrative while blending in elements of science-fiction with its dystopian vision of a sandstorm-ravaged Dubai (the setting itself being the real star of the game). The cover-based third-person shooter mechanics, while essentially lifted from Gears Of War, are tightly crafted and well executed enough for the action to fluidly draw you in over an engrossing 10+ hour campaign. A mature game with the brains to match its brawn - a solid
(9.5/10) and Game of the Year material.

This game is the answer to the attitude of modern military shooters and their position towards war. It does not tolerate the actions done in said games and will leave you with a sour taste in your mouth if act like those games told you, but that's what makes it stand out from all the other third person shooters out there. Spec Ops: The Line's storytelling and its moral ambiguity makes it one of the greatest things in gaming history.
Everyone should play this game sometime in their life.
The game starts off like just another run-of-the-mill 3rd person shooter, but after an hour or so the story becomes gripping. Give it a chance and see the darkness that lies in Dubia.

That said, the less you know about the game going in, the better the experience will be, so I recommend against reading dozens of reviews in favor of simply playing it.

So you're reading a review about Rogue Legacy? Odds are you either are coming to see if the hype around this game is warranted, or you've seen it was on sale and need that one last push to convince you that your purchase won't be in vain. While a bit lengthy, this review holds everything you could ever want to know before buying.
WELL LET ME TELL YOU!!! This game is by far one of the most fun games I've purchased in a long while. I'll start with a synopsis of the game's plot, followed by the pros and cons of the game, and end it with an official rating and some inside info on gameplay.
You are the heir to a throne occupied by a king who has fallen ill. To what, you don't entirely know. The king has set out on a quest to remedy himself by venturing in to a castle that has been rumored to be haunted for years on the outskirts of his land. Within this castle is the key to curing all sickness. If a hero proves himself worthy to battle through the arduous citadel, they will find themselves with the ultimate power to cure themselves of any ailment.
Your father has disappeared. It was rumored he found himself the treasure within and decided to stay with his new found riches. Others believe he fell to the beasts that inhabit the dangerous depths. Regardless of his fate, this prompts your brother, the antagonist of the story, to begin his own journey into the castle and claim the fortune for himself.
You play as a generation of heroes, all dedicated to saving the king, and rescuing your brother who also has appeared to be lost. Throughout your exploration of the castle, you stumble across various journal entries, chronicling your brothers advancements. I won't reveal the ending, but I will hint that the castle's riches are far more evil than any monster ever could be.
As you begin your journey you find that the castle is most certainly under some type of spell... Every time a traveler enters the cold, unwelcoming halls, the rooms are randomized entirely. No floor plan is ever the same, causing confusion and plenty of surprises for any weary guest. Being a fortress for countless foes inhabiting the keep, your only reference is a map you create as you navigate each room. Moving from area to area, you find that the castle leads out to a haunted forest, a miasma of ghouls, and a crypt of darkness. Of course there is a mighty enemy that dominates each territory. These boss-like creatures are found out eventually to be previous explorers who have fallen victim to the castle's ultimate secret.
The further your travels take you, the more accomplished you feel each time. But at what cost? At the end of each life, you reawaken as new kin. A son or daughter to the previous explorer's family. Countless years pass, and you find that entire generations of warriors are dedicated to a pointless cause it would feel. Will your efforts prove fruitless? Will the castle's secrets finally be unlocked? What of the long lost king, and your traitor of a brother? Spoilers:
- Every new life leads to a highly randomized generation of soldiers, ready to fight your fight. This means that you will be able to constantly explore new play styles, receive new perks, and have a great time laughing at some of the unfortunate traits you receive.
- The replay value of this game is through the roof. It's never the same, meaning each playthrough yields a new experience.
- New Game + mode is exceptional. Like most games, there are new items, harder enemies, and even the storyline changes in minor ways.
- The traits each character inherits that causes them to be unique, on top of their abilities their class grants them, leads to a fantastic character selection that makes each run memorable.
- Many have reviewed this game to say that it is too difficult. I will not disagree with the thought that it is difficult, however, I will counter the argument with this: Once you get the momentum rolling, and build your character up a bit, the difficulty is something you enjoy and crave. Building your characters up is far more enjoyable with a real challenge before you. The difficulty that crushes so many is only temporary, as most will not play past the first hour due to frustration.
- One major drawback of the game is that the skill tree is too limited and feels pointless at times. Once you've unlocked everything, you spend the rest of the time building small things like health and defense. You no longer have any real goal to aim for, you're simply buffing up your character. This occurs approximately 14-15 hours in, usually just before you defeat the penultimate boss, or clear the third area. A shame as new game + offers so much, yet leaves the skill tree lacking.

The game's controls are a bit difficult. As simple as they are, you'll find yourself going out of your way to execute a much more difficult approach to combat, rather than the intended one. An example of this is the "downstrike" ability. You should have the ability to jump over an enemy, and attack below you. However, the attack is too fast, and you end up hurting yourself, by being susceptible to enemies. Instead, now you'll learn that it's best to jump around all over place, narrowly avoiding attacks, and attacking from the side, to avoid damage. Movement does feel very fluid despite its speed, and you are able to manipulate your character well. The additional perks of certain traits lends itself greatly to gameplay, as some characters have the ability to go where others cannot, some are not knocked back by hits, and some are able to send enemies flying.
Cellar Door Games outdid themselves with the items and skills in this game. The various weapons you can find, equipment you can earn, runes that will allow for special techniques or perks, and items that can assist you (or one in particular that horribly ruins you), are all brilliantly put together in this game. As said before, the only area where they fall short, is the stat system. Once you've unlocked everything in the skill tree, you are left to adding to stats while you yearn for more unlockables. The character system that has you choosing between being "The One" and going on a Tron-esque journey into the grid, or having insatiable bowels that cannot stop playing you the song of its people, helps really flesh out this game and give you a feel of infinite scenarios/builds.
On a scale of 0-10 (keeping it simple), I'll give this game a fantastic 9/10.
I highly recommend this game to anyone who has even gotten this far in the review. Trust me, it is extremely deserving of your time. Cellar Door Games has created a fantastic way to expend your time. A few honorable mentions are that this game does a great job of helping you truly appreciate the story... The tutorial portion of the game ends up being the last path you take before the end of the game. The dialogue is fantastic and makes you laugh from to time, and of the last statements by the last boss... "Truly I have lived a rogue's legacy"... it definitely struck me. This game is fantastic. I will find myself playing it again and again, restarting a character or continuing off of an accomplished one. Please enjoy this, and see what all the hype is about. Would I invest my time in writing so much if I didn't think this game was freaking amazing?!

What a game!  Rogue Legacy's accomplishments are many - from a captivating setting, a soundtrack that complements the look and feel of the game, a decidedly tongue-in-cheek melodramatic narrative, to inhibitive character flaws that actually augment the flow of the game.  However, there is one thing this game contains that many others like it fail to capture - this game has soul. I bought this game the year it was released and I only heard about it because it was in a "best game of all time" vote in 2015 and it was crushing all of it's opponents. So I bought it after doing some light reading on it about how it has this 'mercy' mechanic and how it made some people really chose how they played the game and made them think etc and etc.
I thought 'cool whatever' as a fan of indie games I'm always interested in different mechanics that put into these games compared most bigger production games. Before I continue I will state that I do NOT think that this puts triple A games to shame, nor did I have a review on my entire life after playing this game through with all three of it's story arcs. I beat the game the first time in around 3 hours but most of that time was spent messing around and checking things out.
I definetly enjoyed the characters, some more then others, although they were too transparent about everything and started to feel a bit stale the other times I went through this game. I never felt this 'emotional' connect towards any of these chraracters. And I definetly did not feel any personal development towards them during my playthroughs, it was more like: 'oh this character is kinda funny, this one is kinda annoying. This one is a total ♥♥♥♥♥ wtf seriously'.
The plot was so one dementional I did a double take when reading some of the reviews of this game saying that the story is one of the best things about this game. The story is one of the most overrated things about this game in my opinion luckily it's overshadowed by the amazing soundtrack which in my opinion is the saving grace of this game.
The mercy consept was pretty neat in theory but the overall effect that it has on the game is minimal besides ( as mentioned before ) some dialogue and story arc. Sparing one boss but killing another won't actually change anything in the story. I didn't find that sparing bosses or monsters was 'the right choice' or something I felt like I wanted to do it was just something I did to get a different ending so that I could say that I did that.
The next section contains kinda spoilers, it's basically my description of my playthroughs of this game and thats about it. I would personally skip it if you have never played undertale before as going in blind is 50x better then going in with prior information.
The first two playthroughs I killed who I wanted but not everyone and I breezed through the game with extreme ease as everything was actually a joke, the final boss was a letdown after the entire game was spent building him up as someone that would kill me on the spot, the ending of this playthrough was actually a surprise and I enjoyed this playthrough the most of them all. The second playthrough I wanted to see what would happen if I spared everything that I came across and again, I get a different ending, this one was less enjoyable and extremely undersatisfactory especially as this is the 'best ending' you can get. The third time I desided that these miserable sprites didn't deserve to live anymore so I killed everything in my path, most people that I found online thought that this was the hardest one to do especially after building a 'connection' with the characters which I personally thought was crazy. The final boss in this run was moderatly difficult and after you get past the first half of the fight it's actually pretty easy ( in my opinion ). The ending to this run in my opinion felt pretty rushed although I would much rather it over the first ending that I did.

I would make some remarks about the community but that would quadruple the length of this ( decently long ) review so I'll spare you. Undertale is a pretty enjoyable game, while I did kinda drag myself through the third playthrough of the game I wouldn't say that I disliked the game. My review would probably leave you scratching your head ( is that something people still say? ) about what I just wrote but i'll explain. I didn't dislike undertale, I do not think that it was the best game of 2015, I do not think that the story was one of the best things i've ever expirienced in the world. I would never say that the characters in this game were the most connected i've ever felt with video game chracters. I would never say any of that and I wouldn't say a lot of other things about undertale that a lot would. But I will say that it's something that every young gamer has to play because the majority of games that they will play won't ever have the amount of thought, creativity or depth as this game has. I've played better but that doesn't mean that everyone has and that's where I would say the praise that undertale gets is from, it's a NEW game that NEW/YOUNGER people need to play rather then the next call of duty or battlefield or whatever.
Most young gamers have never played a game with this much time put into it or with an actual story ( insert basically any game released in the past 3 months here ). They're just used to seeing a person with a gun and shooting the person. And that's the appeal to undertale, it's a game with time, effort and care put into it that just so happens to have possibly one of the most annoying communities out there.
So if you are a younger gamer out there I would definetly reccomend this game to you, you need this game to realize just how much there is out there to expirience in the world of games, there's a lot of good stuff besides CSGO or league or the next 70 COD's. Take a chance, I'm sure you'll enjoy it. You actually don't have to be young, I would reccomend this game ( besides all of it's massive flaws ) to basically anyone that plays the same 1 genre of game ( FPS ) because they need a break from mindless killing to just relax, play a game that doesn't take itself seriously and just enjoy it. Although if you are buying this game do NOT ( i'm going to say it again ) DO NOT. Play this game with ANY prior knowledge about any of the characters, endings, or story if you wish to enjoy the game to it's fullest, if you learn anything, just wait a bit til it goes on sale then buy it because it'll be so much better if you do.
I give this game a solid 6.5/10 ( my score ) and a 8/10 for anyone else, the story is basic but better then anything released in the past couple months, the mercy mechanic has minimal effect on anything unless your doing a full mercy run or a full kill run. Characters are enjoyable ( some more then others ) and soundtrack is one of the best i've heard in a long time.
