I want to preface my review with a bit of information, just incase anyone reading this feels/felt the same way I did.
I was not hyped for this game. Not at all. As a freaking
fan of Life is Strange, I felt a prequel was a stupid idea. I then heard Ashley Burch would not be returning to voice a younger Chloe, despite doing her 14 year old voice in Episode 3. I understand the reasoning, but it really rubbed me the wrong way. Then I realised that pretty much no one came back to reprise their roles. This game fell way
off my radar.
Good Steam reviews changed my mind enough to at least give it a shot. I am very glad I did.
The acting, for the most part, is very good. The worst offender (not for acting) in my opinion is Chloe, with Principal Wells and Victoria coming in after, only because they aren't very important. At least not yet.
However. Chloe's new voice is not bad. The voice match is on point a lot of the time. There are a few lines I could have sworn were Burch. Despite this, she has a different accent than Burch, so a lot of the delivery is just... wrong for Chloe. She doesn't just sound younger, she sounds like a different person, almost solely because of the accent.
Again, I want to make this clear. Chloe's new voice actress is not a bad actress. Her voice even fits Chloe. Her acting is pretty great. It's just the accent that makes it hard to swallow, as I am too used to Burch.
The lack of rewind hurts. The Talkback "minigame" or whatever they call it is... okay at best. It just feels like expanded dialogue options with a different HUD element. It doesn't really feel special. Maybe I just didn't encounter anything that triggered something unique in my first playthrough. Aside from that, it feels exactly the same as LiS. Which is a very good thing to me.
This is what I was most worried about. The reason I didn't think I'd be interested before I even heard about the voice cast. LiS is already concrete. They can't change anything. Choice would matter even less than the ending of LiS, as you'd have to end up where LiS started. And this is still a concern. But maybe they can cleverly do some paradox correcting BS at the end of BTS Episode 3.
On the other hand, most everything in this game is very interesting. It
like Life is Strange, and that's what's most important. It has a lot of tie in with the first game, and it isn't afraid to establish huge crap. It's not shying away from expanding on important backstory, theories, and random crap established by either LiS or the fan community. And I'm all about that. The Deck Nine writers aren't scared to do interesting stuff, and that makes me happy.
Overall, it looks almost identical to LiS. Character models seem maybe a bit smoother? Kind of hard to tell. Some of the environment textures seem maybe even lower res than LiS? But I could just be misremembering. There
a switch from Unreal 3 to Unity, but that doesn't seem like it's changed much. The amazingly utilised Depth of Field from LiS returns, and it doesn't seem misused or worse enough to warrant saying anything about. I don't know. What's important, is the game runs fine, and is bug free, which, from my experience, it does.

I imagine I'm somewhat over spec for the game, but not by a LOT. The game runs fine on HDD, loading is speedy, but you'd expect that if you've played LiS.

Euro Truck Simulator 2 is a game where you manage a trucking company, building it up from nothing to become a corporate empire. You also drive trucks.
The game is very relaxing and provides that comfy feeling when the rain patters against your windshield. While you will be driving trucks the entire game, the on-the-side company stuff is what will keep you playing as it ultimately allows you purchase new trucks and gives you reasons explore. The map is fairly large as you can drive around all most all of mainland Europe as well as the UK. The game even comes with internet radio stations in different languages for you to listen to.
As much as I enjoy the game there are some issues with it. The AI is terrible as they will drive into the oncoming line at 75mph [you can change the units of measurement] just to pass you. The GPS also isn't very good due to the problem where if you go off the set route, the GPS will not update, which means you are going to have to pull an AI and drive backwards.
Aside from those complaints Euro Truck Simulator 2 is a great game with great devs and great mod support. If you are interested in the game you should also check out the free multiplayer mod being created by fans.

So I'm just about 10 Hours into the game, so first impressions I think are in order. A little background, for the longest time I wanted to get "the Hunter: Classic", but I wasn't interested in shelling out the cash that the reviews mentioned. So then this came along and I jumped on it. I had finally gotten the "the Hunter" experience I was hoping for; unfortunately, it also came with those things I've learned to expect from this industry. Those things you hate, you know, those dirty little bugs.  Anyways, while I applaud the devs for abandoning their previous pay-to-win business model and not succumbing to the "early access" model (that plagues the industry); they certainly shouldn't have released the game without some sort of heads up that it was in fact very much in early access stages. So with all that said I'm going to try and point out what I've noticed the devs did right and what they did wrong(In hopes they'll read this and patch this beautiful ♥♥♥♥♥♥ game).
Pros:
- The game is ♥♥♥♥ing gorgeous.
- The sound is pretty damn impressive, mainly the ambient noises(wind, leaves, rain, etc) and atmosphere they create.
- Love the weapon handling. It can be a ♥♥♥♥♥, but it seems fairly accurate to RL gun handling.
- Pretty fair price for content. The maps are massive, and you'll find yourself constantly being distracted while exploring them.
- Good :/ AI. It's nice to see a studio that can manage at least getting the AI in a sandbox environment like this without it completely bugging out **cough** DayZ **cough**. When you are stalking animals you just can't go gallivanting through the woods and expect to ever find anything. I think last I checked around 6 hours in, I had scared some 600 animals away from noise alone cause I was just out running around trying to find the nearest cabins. You have to be all predator like and pop up being like BOOOOOOM
. No you should shoot them in the heart... it's more "humane" < better trophy.
Cons:
- Let me start with the most outrageous one of all. NO 'Back to Menu' button, that's right! HOW in the hell did you guys miss that one in said "Beta", the♥♥♥♥ how did you guys not catch that in Alpha. You mean to tell me, when I get into: a buggy game, a slow server/ host connection game, get stuck in the water, or want to switch from multiplayer to single player.... I have to exit and restart the entire game?!?!? Save us someone! We are going 1 step forward 10 steps back here.
- Multiplayer in general seems to be a buggy mess. Bad D-Sync, characters stuck in walk, spawning in with no ammo, spawning in and immediately dying, awful hit registration, you name it they got it there it would appear. I have had a very minimal amount of bugs in single player.
- In single player I've had interaction bugs, where I literally can't click on anything. I'll give you an example of how unbelivably frustraiting this one is. So I walked ALL the way to one of the northern most cabins to only find out once I had gotten there that I couldn't click on anything. I had to restart my game( ^ since I couldn't close to menu and spawn back in), and when I spawned back I was all the way at the southern most cabin. I would have to walk all the way back to that cabin to gain fast travel access since I couldn't claim the spot before the bug appeared.
- Hit registration in single player seems to be an issue as well. I had shots that I just know I didn't miss, shots that were point blank, and I would hit nothing but air. No blood, not even a flesh wound.
This game could use a quad, but otherwise is a amazing game

It's as step up from theHunter: Classic in some areas and a step back in others, however it's a good platform to build on like they did with Classic.
Pros:
- Updated graphics, some of the best scenery you will see in any game.
- Hunting pressure, new mechanic to make it difficult to hunt in areas you've already hunted.
- Improved animal behaviors. Animals will give warning calls, mating calls, and can be found in large heards.  There was also the addition of "need zones" that you can discover such as sleeping zones, drinking and feeding zones where you can find specific species at certain hours of the day.
- Night hunting, with the help of a headlamp.
- CoTW replaces a membership pay model of Classic with a RPG system that makes you gradually unlock new weapons and equipment through XP, also has a pretty neat skills/perks system that really adds some flavor to hunting.
Cons:
- Lacks the diversity of theHunter: Classic. Only 2 hunting reserves at the time of launch, a handful of weapons and a pretty small roster of game to hunt.
- Scoring system seems wonky, not a huge fan of the "consecutive harvests" idea. The game awards senseless killing and not being patient and selective like it should be.
- Small features like trophy shots and trophy galleries not available at this time. Guessing in the future? Not sure why something like this would be cut from the game.
- Performance issues, some people complaining about crashes/bugs. Latest patch addressed some issues though.
-  No mobile tree stands, or tents. You have to discover outposts around the map and use them to fast travel.

Picked this game in the Humble Bundle, and for me it's been like a bag of my favorite potato chips... hard to put down once I've started, and still looking forward to more.
I enjoy all types of games, and this one has apparently struck a chord with me.  The graphics are simple but well-suited for the game.  I haven't experienced any bugs that I've noticed, just a few difficulties with placing the wrong door and trying to dismantle it.  The game as it stands is pretty complete as far as a simultaion goes... you can build, manage finances, build more, realize you've made mistakes and start over, fine tune, expand, and so on.  You can play this with your full attention, or with a movie going on while monitoring the prison (when waiting for prisoners to arrive, or cash to accrue, etc).  I don't see a pure sandbox mode... i.e. full access to all features, God-like control and oodles of cash to play with... but I have to believe that's in the cards.
I haven't looked at much in the way of dev news... check that for more info and future plans.  After I got the game installed, I started playing and din't have much time to bother with future features and all that.
Basically, for this to be complete, there needs to be an end game.  Otherwise, what's missing are the scenarios, campaigns, and end game goals that you traditionally find in games like this.  Ideally, we could play through random scenarios, campaigns, user-created content, or the sandbox.  Where they go with music, further sound effects, gameplay modifications is kind of a moot point... the game is great fun as is.  With the support of the Steam Workshop, PA has the potential for endless gameplay and hours upon hours of unforced "labor".

Ok so, here I am. One of those guys who's going to give the game a positive review.
I've read many of the negative reviews and most of them are actually fact based and have legitimate complaints (instead of people who just hate hunting games saying they hated it.  If you're listening, don't play warcraft if you hate elves and dwarves, and stop playing grand theft auto if you hate cars.)

So, yes, the game has many issues which need to be fixed ASAP and many others which we would all like to see dealt with over time.
Having said that,  this game was a great way for me and a close friend to spend some time walking through the woods, when we are too far away to do it in real life. (not to mention, regulations on hunting here are a bit more strict than in game where you can bag 6-7 deer in one evening haha)
The scenery is great, its well done, has a ton of variation, and lots of space. Its also pretty simplistic in its design, not a ton of gimmicky stuff that isn't needed... Have you been way out in the woods before? Its a lot like this game shows.
The feel of the firearms is good, the sounds (when they work) are good, the animal behavior is above exceptable, the game offers challenge as well, since you don't start playing, and an hour later have every piece of gear available. I like the "grindy" aspect of it. Maybe others don't but I call this a bonus.
The game is quite relaxing and slow paced, perfect for when you need a break from the typical ADHD shooters of our current time or bucket-of-ice-cold-water to the face pvp most online games throw at you.  I like to put this one on the big screen in the living room with a fire going and an ice cold lager, and take my time looking down those fields and wandering the woods. Definitely a relaxing, low stress title here.
So, what needs fixing? well...Plenty.   I'll write more about it in suggestions, and hopefully some Devs can take a look at what I have to say!
TL;DR    Yes its not perfect, but with some work it easily could be one of, or even THE greatest hunting game title (depending on what you're after)  Is it worth the cost?  I'm going to say yes, but only with the stipulation that they continue to work on it, and provide the community with more content and bug fixes without asking for more money.

Ok, so I've only played about 10 hours so far, but I thought I should write this while the thoughts are fresh in my mind.  I'll start by saying that I gave this a positive review in steam, and suggested people take a closer look at it.  I spent quite a few hours last night having a lot of fun playing multiplayer with a close friend of mine.  We talked a lot on discord and discussed a few of the issues people are complaining about, as well as some of the bugs and issues we encountered ourselves.
I think this game is really good already and potentially will be amazing.  Having said that, here are a few things I would like to draw some attention to (in no particular order);
1. Option of "exit to main menu/home screen"  I really think this should have been here already, and many agree.  Exiting to desktop is a bit annoying, especially for people on my friends list who see "mike is playing, mike stopped playing, mike is playing" lol.  Lets add a "quit to main menu"?
2. In Multiplayer, only the person hosting is able to interact with the (?) on the map. As far as we could tell last night, only the host is able to fast travel as well. This is a huge disadvantage and also makes no sense. It would be nice to say "hey, lets all meet at the lodge/outpost for a moment and restock and regroup" or something. It can take a while if you get separated to walk all the way to your friend!  Not to mention, wandering up to a landmark or lookout and not being able to do anything, or being unable to build a blind, etc.  Lets make it so anyone can use these things!
3. Money.  So, I have no huge issue with this but I wanted to add a few personal points here. I think the money system should be scaled a bit.  I'm going to use $, so please euro players, etc, bear with me (i'm canadian but I'll use USD).  A box of ammunition doesn't cost 300$ in real life.  and the normal hunting rifles a regular person buys (i'm talking AVERAGE here) are maybe 2000$ or even less.  (I bought a browning for 800 once, and it even came with a scope).  I think charging 30,000$ is a bit high. Perhaps have the money earned cut down a bit, and then scale the cost of things for a bit more realism.  I'd suggest 20 rounds of ammunition for lets say 45-50$
4.Sound issues.  Some people don't have this, but a few I've spoken to do. I don't know about you but for me, there is nothing worse than waiting an hour for that perfect tag to show up (deer, etc) and lining up your perfect shot and then "silence" when you pull the trigger.  It's quite anticlimactic when that happens. Not to mention the calls sometimes being silent, or rain sounding a bit buggy, etc.  I hope these sound bugs are eliminated soon. Not a deal breaker for me, but should be addressed.
5.Here's one I haven't seen anyone mention. Why do female characters run like the flash? Friend of mine literally leaves me in the dust when we're moving together (and yes I triple checked, i'm running, not walking)  She ran about 85% faster than my male character. Is this a bug or intentional? Do male characters get some other bonus like carrying more weight or something? (not being sexist, just asking)  Is there a point in playing as a male when you can essentially speedwalk as a female?
6. Wildlife changes.  Bird hunting should be added (and forgive me if it is but I haven't unlocked it)  if you're going to have shotguns in the game, there should be geese, duck, turkey, pheasant...whatever.  As far as I can tell this isn't really a thing. Can anyone confirm? I've not read anything definite so far, but some have told me there is no such gamebirds added. More wildlife would be nice too, but mostly just the bird hunting (a favorite of mine in real life) is something I'd love to see.
7.Group activity.  It would be fun in multiplayer to have some quest/challenge that is co-operative. Maybe a party system or something where if 2 people collaborate on a kill, they share the rewards, regardless of who pulled the trigger.
9.I've heard this mentioned before but,  seasons.  Would be kind of interesting if you could make some selections when starting a multiplayer like winter, rain on or off, night only, day only, fall, spring...etc.  Some other maps/terrain variations in general would be nice (sort of goes along with that)  Just vague ideas I'm throwing out here.
10. Firing range, practice. Something like that might be useful for those who have never hunted or shot in real life, or are new to these types of games.
Well, that's all for now, I welcome any comments and bumps.

-----Full Review-----
I am pretty frustrated because this game has so much potential. This is a gorgeous game and the concept is simply amazing. The devs really should be hiding their faces in embarassment at the moment. It truly feels like a very long time was put into the creation of the game and then they ran out of money and released it as an unfinished product. I encountered my first bug within seconds of playing the game, where the screen was unbareably blurry for the first 7 or 8 minutes of gameplay.
A primary issue - The pathing of Wildlife
The pathing is completely ridiculous. Often times when you fire at a game species they freeze in place after you hit them. I am not referring to a shocked hault, I am referring to a glitchy sudden abrupt freeze of the animation. They stay there for 3-5 seconds until you shoot them again and might take a step or two. I also noticed that after you shoot an animal, they run in a 10 x 20 area in the woods in circles, and you can walk straight up to them and keep shooting at the ground and they will just keep running in circles. This is very frustrating.
A second issue - The death of the Wildlife
Why do animals die standing up? They are frozen in place and sometimes hovering off the ground. There is absolutely no transition between a stationary deer and death at times, this is especially frustrating.
A third issue - The hit registry
I was able to walk up on a 12 point buck and get legitimately right next to it (due to the glitches and terrible pathing of the current state of the game) and I scoped in on my rifle and took a headshot at the buck (because there is an achievement to kill a certain amount of wildlife with headshots). This was an extremely easy shot because the animal was stationary. I put two headshots at point blank range in the deer and then he randomly galloped off and I had to go on an 8 minute chase where he proceeded to take two more body shots and finally collapsed (in a terribly awkward and buggy position).
----- Final Thoughts -----
Why was this game that has so much potential to be amazing released with so many bugs that simply make this game unplayable. I can not even complete some of the missions such as taking a photo (with the in game camera) of the Fallow Deer, because of bugs. This game is no where near ready to be played by the public. It should be labeled as early access or an open beta and the price tag should be dropped to around 10-12 USD for the current state of the game. I would love to recommend this game to my friends but I simply can not with the current state of the game.
Developers ----- Fix these game breaking issues and save your game before it is too late. You should already be ashamed that you released such an unfinished product.

It needs to be out of the way first, theHunter: Call of the Wild is about hunting wildlife. If you are okay with that, then the game is going to be pretty much what you expected. I played the original Hunter quite a while back and I was not able to get into it for some reason. theHunter: Call of the Wild seems much more streamlined than the previous game which was pretty inviting for me as well as new player to the series.

theHunter: Call of the Wild puts you in the boots of a Hunter in a huge open world with the prospect of hunting virtual wildlife. That is pretty much all the story that is present in the game, because even after the narrator telling you a few lines and giving you some quests, it is pretty vague. Do not go in expecting a brilliant narrative adventure out of this game. Now, how does the actual hunting holds up.
For the most part, the hunting in theHunter: Call of the Wild is pretty solid. You get all kinds of tools at your disposal to hunt down the surprising less diverse wildlife. From noise maker to sprays to attract your prey towards a location and then putting a bullet through their lungs, that is the game. theHunter: Call of the Wild does falter in the skill tree it uses to unlock all these fancy tools and you really need to grind your way by murdering quite a lot of fauna.
This requires a lot of patience and time and might frustrate some players. You can unlock Far Cry 3 like towers which show you points of interests on that particular part of the map. The gun recoils are nice and feel quite good to use.
Don’t expect to go in all bullet blazing though like a Call of Duty game. theHunter: Call of the Wild requires you to be patient and wait for the creature to be at a perfect position when you take the shot. The animal can even run away wounded and you will have to follow its blood trail to track and hunt it down. theHunter: Call of the Wild is at its best in these moments, I remember trailing a rare bear for some time following a blood trail it left and finally catching it a water body it came near to drink. It keeps you immersed in these moments and truly feels like something special. The wildlife is also very quick to react and they make the world a living breathing one.
But in theHunter: Call of the Wild you’re basically like a god. It is nigh impossible for a creature to kill you unless you stand right in front of a bear. Even the fall damage from a high outpost isn’t enough to actually kill you. I felt bad for these poor creatures who were just waiting to be preyed upon.
There is no food requirement, nothing that can force you to tense up. You can go hunting in the night and there will be literally no other danger. While there is plenty of wildlife to hunt, the diversity is pretty low. More often than not you will run into yet another bear or deer and it gets very repetitive after a while. You also have to walk a lot which is expected but it won’t please most of the audience.
It is not helped by the fact that theHunter: Call of the Wild is extremely buggy. I can’t recall how many times a creature clipped through the trees, my bullets just whizzed past the animal’s lungs without hurting it and the constant crashes are enough the annoy anyone out of their wits. While the multiplayer works fine when playing with friends, it seems that this game is not really made for it. Too many hunters spoil a game and it is very much true here.
Visually theHunter: Call of the Wild looks stunning. From the god rays of the sun to the gentle breeze flowing through the forest, it is one of the prettiest games I’ve played. The animal models are also really stunning and the game just takes your breath away quite some times with the beautiful vistas it presents.
There is a fair amount of visual pop in and there are some really hilarious visual glitches which might break your immersion sometimes but overall it is pretty beautiful. What is a letdown though are the human models in multiplayer. They look like someone put a bunch of dolls in a jungle and that does help the game.
Excellent. From the animals sounds to just the rain pattering on the leaves, everything is done beautifully. The only trouble is when you walk through a water body which is when your shoes make more sounds than a bear who is ready to mate. But overall it has an excellent sound package.
I can’t help but like theHunter: Call of the Wild. It has its problems and it does certainly feel like an early access game but if you want a proper hunting game, theHunter: Call of the Wild should be your choice.
It needs some polish and more content but as it stands, it is a solid hunting game which sports outstanding visuals and excellent sound design. It is not for everyone though and you should keep that in mind if you are purchasing this game.

Rogue Legacy is one of the most fun games I've personally played in a while. You play as one of several classes entering into a castle in order to kick♥♥♥♥♥and get gold. You die easily, expecially at first. You'll be lucky to survive a couple minutes your first few rounds of the game. After you die you choose a new heir to replace you between three randomized choices, and the one you choose determines not only your class for the round (Warrior/Barbarian/Mage/Shinobi/Lich/Miner/Etc.) but also varying traits that can make the round either much harder, or much easier. (Colorblindness, near/farsightedness, short, tall, weak limbs, etc. to name a few) It's pretty cool because you can see the family tree of every heir you've chosen up to that point. On top of that the castle is also randomized so you never know if it'll be a walk through the clouds or the literal incarnation of hell itself.
Upgrades you buy are permanant throughout all your characters though so any max health, strength, critical stats, etc. you buy along with any weapons and armor you buy will transfer over as you die. As more and more people sacrifice themselves for teh epic lootz the easier it will be to make it farther and farther into the depths of the castle. There are other locations aside from the castle that you can make it too, as well as minibosses and bigger world bosses to fight but as of now (Almost 5 hours in) I'm still unable to survive anywhere outside of the castle.
You will unlock upgrades that slowly build your castle from the ground up and range from stat increases to blacksmiths, enchantresses, new classes, gold increases, and many more. Eventually you can even upgrade the games difficulty in order to keep yourself challenged at higher levels for bigger rewards. Aside from upgrades you can also find random items in the castle that you can interact with such as diary entries, paintings of other games made by the developers, carnivals with mini games, and even a jukebox that lets you choose a track to play for the current round. The music is reminisent of titles from the Sega Genesis and so the music brings back a sense of nostalgia to me. It's nice, it doesn't ever feel repetitive, and it sets the mood rather well.
All in all I would recommend this game to anyone who likes rogue-like games, or just general addicting timewaster games. It's cheap and it's really worth the money.

Rogue Legacy surprised me. At its core, it's an addicting game. You are tasked with trekking through a trecherous castle, and you will die. A lot. However, with each death, you are given the option to make your next character (child) stronger using money you find in your previous run. What you get is a continuous quest to make your "family" of characters stronger, with the ultimate goal of beating all of the castle's bosses. In addition, the castle changes each time, making each run unique (although you later gain the power to "fix" the castle in place as you see fit).
What adds to this addictiveness are the mechanics. The game feels great, with your character moving fluidly and having several different spells and techniques to choose from, from throwing axes Castlevania style to double jumping. Music and visuals are on point as well. The game treks the line between intense and fun quite soundly. Difficult enemies and clever level design require players to focus to their utmost while exploring, while fun extras such as unique traits (aspects of each child such as being gay, colorblind, etc) put a humorous twist to each run.
That being said, the game lacks a certian finesse. Monster designs are repetitive and unoriginal. Bosses are simply regular enemies but larger. Although there are different classes, such as mages and assassins, that you can choose for each run, each class looks and fights the same, just with different stats.
Overall, however, I would reccomend Rogue Legacy. Ultimately, it was a blast to play, which was most important to me, and it is a very satisfying game to beat. 15$ is a bit pricy for its quality imo, but it's a great pick when a sale rolls around.

A fun, procedural rogue-lite, rouge-like, whatever you what to call it.  The randomization of rooms and enemies is well-done, despite the different zones sharing a ton of similarities with the big difference being a coat of paint.  Rogue Legacy also controls really tight, even when you're triple-jumping or flying around the screen with about a dozen enemies crowding around you.  Since you're going to spend most of the game jumping and dodging, good controls are extremely important.
The big push of the game, playing as your offspring with different traits, actually is a bit of a letdown.  All characters have the same basic controls and models and share most of the same skills.  Playing as a mage character will involve a lot of the same running, jumping, and sword-swinging as a knight, just with a few minor differences.  The character traits are mostly a mixed bag, with a decent bit of them being one-off things you try once (like vertigo) and never bother with it again.  Some are useful, but more often than not you're going to end up picking the heir with the least negative traits rather than any with a particularly cool effect.
Enemies are heavily re-skinned in Rogue Legacy, you'll be fighting same 8-12 enemies most of the game.  This doesn't really bother me since the gampelay is smooth and controls so well and combat is more of a mortal affair where enemies and the player character can both die rather quickly.  Then there's the bosses, easily the worst part of the game for me.  They're not even original enemies, just the same ones you fight over and over but much bigger.  That's the not bad part though.  The actual boss fights are mostly bullet hell sequences when you have to avoid twenty other things going on, dodging the huge boss, and trying to fight all the while.  It's quite annoying to fall onto one of a half-dozen floating spike balls or twenty lingering flames and die while jumping frantically to avoid a boss.  All five bosses in the game have this type of gimmick and they're more frustrating than entertaining.
Rogue Legacy is also a bit on the bland side visually.  The character art and backgrounds are perfunctory and that's it.  Music is catchy but not particularly memorable.
While it seems I spent most of the review nit-picking about the game, I greatly enjoyed most of my playthough.  The most important aspect of this sort the game, the gameplay, is really good.  The progression system is pretty rewarding and just exploring the castle is fun.  I'd definitely recommend it to anyone that enjoys 2-D platformers or fans of the traditional Castlevanias.

This game has to be one of the top five greatest steam games for me!!!
I have been watching the game for quite some time and was recently informed that multiplayer was in beta and also had a going away party for my Marine brother coming up (now passed) so I decided to pick it up. So, I'll give you my insight and expereinces on both the multiplayer and singleplayer (party)  gameplay.
Starting with the Multiplayer (remember it's in beta)
So my best friend and I finally decided to pick up the game since you can play online. We find a game, pick our beast's color and costume, and pop into a game. The match starts and instantly, I realize for an early access game, the multiplayer experience (even in beta) is pretty solid. 5-6 hours after straight beating the sh!t out of 6 other people, I realize what an addicting great game this is and what it will hopefully become, but I notice a couple things.
1) The multiplayer crashes occasionally.
2) there is no time limit.
Number two is bad because you will get teamed people who are complete D-bags and will sit around for 5-10 minutes straight and run around taunting players to aggrivate them because there is no time limit and they can do what they want. If they wanted they could sit, just the two of them, and run around for hours and ruin a server. I'm sure this will get fixed soon and hope it does, although it's not often, it sucks when it happens.
Also I will add that the multiplayer only has four playable maps as of now.
Now for the Singleplayer (at home) gameplay.
Okay just so this is clear, by singleplayer, I mean multiple people in the same room playing off of one laptop. Okay so this game in the "singleplayer" is actually loads of fun. Like I mentioned earlier, I had my brothers going away party and decided since we had lot's of people coming over of all ages, this game would allow people to meet, blow off stress, and have fun like old times playing some good games together and boy this game did exactly that and more! The "at home" game play was an absolute blast, I hooked up multiple controllers to my laptop and connected it through HDMI to my TV and had about 20 people in the room switching off between 5 controllers and everyone was enjoying it. The gameplay is very smooth and even more crisp than the online (barely a difference), we experienced no crashing, and access to all of the maps with multiple people. There was occasional glitching but the glitching in this game is FREAKING HILARIOUS and I actually hope they do not fix it because out of nowhere you will find yourself in tears because Little Jimmy was getting ready to toss you out of an elevator but his body stretched a mile long ejecting you both outside the map XD.
Overall, I really recommend this game especially with the multiplayer under works, whether you will play it with friends or family at home or online with friends, it really is such an enjoyable time and was well worth the money.
I would also love to thank the Developers for such a great game, you guys brought a lot of family and friends together and back together in a much needed time, I really appreciate it.

Graphics: The graphics off this game are amazing! Seriously they are so good that you can only wish you can play on max to truely enjoy the game for what it really offers, thankfully I can so on this basis I would say the graphics alone are 9.5 out of 10 because they are that good!
Audio: The guns sound good, the animal noises are good, rain, thunder, wind all are good but there are problems. Would I recommend this game? If you are a big fan of hunting games and want something that is going to draw you in and keep you focused and enjoy a slow pace simulation style game then this is the game for you!

It's not so much that Rogue Legacy is a bad game as it feels like it's nowhere near as good as it really ought to be. The core mechanics are pretty solid, and there's no part of it that feels like a colossal misstep; the problem is that a lot of the game's innovation feels like it falls flat:
For the most part, equipment is pretty samey, only a small handful of upgrades do things unexpected and fewer still do things that feel like they really change the game in a meaningful way. Everything just feels like it should be more varied and unique than it actually is, for a game which sells itself on the idea that every hero and every playthrough is unique.
On the note of "every hero is unique", a large part of the problem is that most of the traits you can start out with really aren't terribly interesting--Entirely too many of them are novel the first couple of times you see them but don't actually have any meaningful gameplay consequences, so the novelty is quickly lost. A large chunk of those that are left are either strictly positive or strictly negative, and so more often than not choosing a hero feels more like you're minimizing bad traits and maximizing good ones rather than dealing with the strengths and weaknesses of a unique character.
The end result is a kind of bland Metroidvania-style platformer that just feels like it really ought be more interesting than it is.
Another game that confuses "punishing" with "difficult." Retro =/= Good.

For those out there who enjoy realistic simulations, Euro Truck Simulator 2 offers that and more. Having racked up 100+ hours on multiple profiles when writing this review, I've enjoyed every second of it and will continue to do so for many months to come! A quick break down:
PROS:
- Offers incredible accuracy when it comes to realism
- The map is designed well and jam packed with locations and features
- The features of the game are too many for me to list; air break simulation, realistic fuel consumtion, wide range of trucks, trailers, cargos, fines for speeding (naughty naughty); I could go on and on!
- The AI traffic is decent and isn't like most other games which are poorly designed and easy to break AI's. They react smartly to you and their surroundings.
But the main PRO to this game is the fact that this game is steam workshop enabled and the beautiful community over on steam workshop have designed many incredible mods to push this already incredible game over the edge. You can choose from thousands and thousands of mods that cover every catergory. Graphics, maps, vehicles packs, truck packs, truck skin packs, AI control, lighting effects; again, another section I could go on and on and list! These mods turn a realistic simulation game into an even greater realistic simulation game.
If you have a steering wheel such as the G27, this game not only supports it but gets even more immersive if you've picked yourself up one! It really makes me feel like a trucker when I'm sitting behind the wheel of my G27 with a glass of milk in one hand, a bowl of coco pops in the other and a cigar in my mouth as I'm driving down the M25!
However, there are a couple of CONS:
- As good as the map is, compared to the TSM map mod, it's not as good as the developers could of made it. The TSM map mod adds a ton of new cities, towns and places of interest as well as making the map have more places to pick up jobs and to travel to.
- The AI is good but again, a mod called AI tweak finely tunes the AI to be even better!
Overall this game is great as a standalone but then throwing mods on top of it turns it into something ungodly addicting! I haven't even mentions the multiplayer mod which means you can go trucking with your pals!
10/10

If you're like me, the reason you're a bit hesitant around Undertale is that you've seen some cringey memes and the game probably looks a bit feel-goody with awkward humour thrown in. Fear not, after my initial apprehension I found out that this is a game that has substance over style.
You probably know by now that one promise of Undertale is that you will engage in an RPG where you can be completely nonviolent. The game achieves this by granting each character that you may encounter some hidden problems, and conflicts with other characters or the world that they inhabit. When engaging such a character they will attack you, yet you may deduce their issues and calm them, soothe them or reassure them which will make it possible to dodge combat after a few rounds. My favourite example is ...erm... Tsundere Plane. The plane that wants you to get close to it, but not too close too fast (or it starts insulting you). Undertale never becomes repetitive because combat itself is an interesting spin: the game works like a JRPG but the turns are about you facing a sort of shmup waves where each enemy has some patterns.
This works for the regular enemies, but the game does far more than that. It is foremost memorable as a deconstruction of RPGs. Without wanting to spoil too much, the game will play a lot with the game mechanics, HUD and even RPG conventions. Each boss fight will become a unique sort of rhythm+puzzle about how to achieve your desired ending. Oh yeah, it has quite a few endings, one of them requiring not to take any lives (it's not as hard as it may seem at first).
Undertale is full of quirky surprises, easter eggs and other secrets. Lots of the characters are well defined, with humour and depth. Its flexible story can be surprisingly dark at times and accomodates either a heartwarming or a psychopathic playstyle if you so desire.  There are many athmospheric moments and the soundtrack is truly a treat. Even though the story is steeped in contemporary Western culture, many of the moments left me with the impression that the author grew up with Ghibli films or similar influences.
All in all, I discovered a game with far more depth and inspiration than met the eye at first. The game packs quite a punch with its twists, but in order to do that it needs to carefully set up its surprises; so don't give up on it from the first hour or so - it's a slow burner.

This game is brilliant. Sure, the graphics aren't 1080p HD or whatever, but you play this game for story and gameplay. It constantly surprises and makes you laugh. I had this game spoiled for me, and I still wanted to play it. The bullethell mechanics could reinvent RPGs as we know it, and its focus on morality and choice leads to a variety of different playthroughs. The most prominent of these playthroughs are the Pacifist and Genocide runs, where you spare or kill all monsters respectively. Both of these endings will not leave you disappointed. There are also the many, MANY neutral runs, where you both kill and spare monsters. For example, if you spare one boss and none of the others, you'd get a different ending than if you only killed one monster. I really liked how this game played out in all of these endings. In Pacifist, the characters warm up to you and become your good friends, and each unique boss is as funny as the last. In Genocide, the characters desert their homes in fear of you, and some bosses become much harder, while others become much easier to defeat, which is quite interesting; it kept me on my toes. Neutral can play out in a variety of ways, but I wouldn't recommend playing a neutral run because you see its ending in the Pacifist run. Still, the final boss of the Neutral run will surprise you. The way the game is always expanding on its battles is interesting as well. You see new varieties of the bullethell formula all the time, and new attacks are presented all the time. The game will blow you away with its ability to remember what you've done in previous playthoughs, and terms like "SAVE" and "RESET" aren't just terms the player uses, but they're acknowledged by characters in the game as well. The rich story, the admirable battles, the great characters, the many endings, and the fourth wall shattering are what you get whet you buy this game. It will not disappoint.

So around 3 months ago I decided to get this game for $7.50 during a sale. I heard it was a pretty good game and that it was severely overlooked. Looking at the title screen, it looks like any other generic Americans-kill-all-the-brown-people shooter. I began playing as soon as I got it for around an hour, then I stopped completely and never played it until last night. Bored, I decided to give it another chance. I then beat it all in one sitting. Let me tell you, this game isn't fun. It plays like a bland cover shooter, and that's exactly what it is. Although, as I delved further into the story line, a darker part of my squad and I became present. Keep in mind the 3 main characters are all the generic army man stereotypes, a black guy who blows things up, a gritty guy voiced by Nolan North, and a wisecracking whiteboy who fixes♥♥♥♥♥♥ Who knew they could seem so real. This video game made me feel like I was in as much♥♥♥♥♥♥as these soldiers were. This game makes you feel like an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, most of all. The entire experience is basically trying to make you feel like a horrible person, and boy, does it. You know a story is compelling when, even though the GAME part of the game was bland, you keep pushing through to let the story unravel. You know a story is good when after that final cutscene you sit in your chair for a few minutes, in utter shock, and proceed to call it a night. You know a game is well written when you begin to question the reason you're still playing at all, and you realise that the trauma your character is going through feels so real, you need to know and feel more. It's sad really, how much emotion and thought a video game put me through. This game had a plan from the beginning, to trick you into thinking it's another ♥♥♥♥♥♥ bang bang america simulator, and once that tone is set, it's thrown out a window and burned, and you're cast into a soldier's mind, gradually wearing away along with it's surroundings. You slowly walk a downward spiral into the dark bellows of the human mind, and let me tell you, it's ♥♥♥♥ing brilliant. I shouldn't really get this serious over a game, but man, is it an experience, I really wish I could spoil some of what happens and how it all ties together, but that would just ruin it. You need to experience it yourself, and take from that experience whatever you choose. Play this game as soon as you get the chance. Go in thinking it's just another shooting game in the desert, that's just what the devs want you to believe.

Prison Architect is prison building/simulation game, where you're able to build and manage your own prison.
Pretty awesome game for still being in early acces. I guess if you like games like RC Tycoon or maybe Zoo Tycoon, I would totally recommend it to you. You can choose between different ways how you're handling your prisoners, from a gulag-like hardcore jail to a some kind of holiday resort like prison. Also, I like how many different buildings there are. Of course you should still consider that it is NOT finished; there are for example some buildings which don't really work (e.g. the security room) and the whole foundation thing is sometimes acting weird. Also the bureaucracy/technology tree has some glitches and bugs BUT it is absolutely playable.
Something I really missed was a proper tutorial. Although there is an introduction at this point, it does only explain the absolute minimal basics (or mabye I missed something there). It took me around 4-5 hours to actually comprehend how important parts of the gameplay are working. I hope this gets fixed, but one the other hand there's already a busy community, which delievers you FAQs, wikis and even some mods.
As this is my first early acces game, I can't tell how good or bad it is for its status, but I can truly say that it is a hell lot of fun to play and I hope other Early Access games should be similar good!
I got this through an Indie HumbleBundle, but I guess it is also worth its price of 28 € considering how good his game already is (despite some flaws I blame on being an early acces game).
So, pretty good! I hope it gets even better. I may write another review when Prison Architect is out of EA and considered finished!

I've been playing Rust since it's Legacy version and have to say this is one of the best games I've had the pleasure of playing and watching grow. I've been through the different directions and experiments they've tried, and they're nailing it!! The steady growth and expansion of how you can play, what you can create, how you interact is exciting and leaves me looking forward to the next steps in the evolution of this game. I see a lot of folks giving negative reviews since the "twig" update, and it boggles my mind that a step towards more realism is considered bad. Now people can use ladders to scale walls, build basic scaffolding next to a building to check it out and to be able to attack from different directions. The bases are no longer protected by the "magic" power of a Tool Cabinet, you have to be more creative and resourceful to defend your home. I recommend this game wholeheartedly to anyone who isn't afraid of a challenge and isn't afraid of change. I'd also recommend learning it on smaller private servers, which tend to be friendlier and more helpful than the larger public servers. When you're ready for the mayhem that is a large public server, jump in and see how it goes.

The more experienced builder you are, less chance you will be raided. Servers do get wiped to keep performance at high standards. I do only have a small amount of time played on RUST but any update the DEVS release affects the community and does not put anyone at a advantage or disadvantage, each player is able to access the same things. It goes like this: You pick a guy and he goes into the castle. You collect gold and some stuff, but then you die. So, then you pick a new guy and you get to spend the gold you picked up. Now you want to try out the new guy and the new stuff you bought. So you go in the castle and get more gold and you die. You'll repeat that over and over and, eventually, you'll need to stop. BUT there's never a place to stop.
"Well, my character just died. I can stop now, but I guess I'll go ahead and pick out my next guy."
"Well, I picked out my next guy, I guess I'll spend my gold real quick."
"Well, I've got some new stuff to try out, I guess I'll go into the castle."
"Well, now I've been in the castle and gotten more gold and I'm dead."
You will be able to quit the game, but only when you realize it's 3 a.m. and you decide that you may need that 3 hours of sleep. Highly recommend.

My personal 2013 indie game of the year.
A great game that perfectly blends old school 2D action platforming with modern game design and a large dose of roguelike elements.  The drip feeds you rewards just enough to keep you from being discouraged but has enough random elements to keep you from feeling complacent or bored.
The only two cons I can really bring up are playing with a controller is a must, and even then the controls can feel a bit loose at times (in a game like this that can mean deaths that could easily be avoided if things were a little tighter).  Second, there's not a particularly large variety of enemies.  Mostly just bigger stronger versions of the same enemies you see at the very start of the game.
Still a fantastic game and well worth your time.

A great Castlevania style game, plenty of grinding but the grinding barely feels like grinding, with the ability to lockdown and unlock the constantly changing castle you can focus on exploring one, or unlock it and move on to a new one. I am awful at platforming, but I do love roguelikes. Maybe that's why I like this game as much as I do. It's designed in such a way that you're gonna die, but instead of making it a frustrating neverending cycle of screwing up the same level over and over... you get exiting new ways to die! And if you weren't too awful, you get to invest money into being less awful, win-win!
And despite dying (frequently) the game did have me coming back for more, mostly because I wanted more gold to make my hero slighly less fragile. The best part about randomized dungeons, is that even if you find a hellroom that you're too incompitent to traverse... It's okay! You die and you never have to see it again, unless you sign over 40% of your gold to the engineer! Frankly I think he's kinda a jerk, so he doesn't get my hard-earned shines.
Granted the game has some flaws, ones that are big enough that I'd feel rather cheated if I didn't nab the game while it was on sale. I'm kinda bummed out that I often can't spend the money I have. I also don't feel like when I upgrade my stats, that I've made any meaningful progress. When I upgrade my HP, I don't feel any tougher when I play. My favorite aspect of rouge-likes is how much of it is luck. You can gain a fortune and epic loot, just as quickly as you can lose it. Here it feels like a very slow climb.
Also, this game really wants you to play mages and squishies. All the classes, except one (barbadian) have less HP than the paladin/knight. While I get that magic is a important part of surving, I am resentful of the fact that a vast majority of the time I need to play with glass cannons.
The graphics are nice and I like that the game maintains a mostly comical and light-hearted tone. I'm not sure how I feel about the story though. It progresses slowly and is rather dour. I'm not here for the story, so it doesn't bother me that much.
Short Version: A pretty nice platformer/roguelike hybrid with a neat concept. Worth getting if it's on sale.

So around 3 months ago I decided to get this game for $7.50 during a sale. I heard it was a pretty good game and that it was severely overlooked. Looking at the title screen, it looks like any other generic Americans-kill-all-the-brown-people shooter. I began playing as soon as I got it for around an hour, then I stopped completely and never played it until last night. Bored, I decided to give it another chance. I then beat it all in one sitting. Let me tell you, this game isn't fun. It plays like a bland cover shooter, and that's exactly what it is. Although, as I delved further into the story line, a darker part of my squad and I became present. Keep in mind the 3 main characters are all the generic army man stereotypes, a black guy who blows things up, a gritty guy voiced by Nolan North, and a wisecracking whiteboy who fixes♥♥♥♥♥♥ Who knew they could seem so real. This video game made me feel like I was in as much♥♥♥♥♥♥as these soldiers were. This game makes you feel like an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, most of all. The entire experience is basically trying to make you feel like a horrible person, and boy, does it. You know a story is compelling when, even though the GAME part of the game was bland, you keep pushing through to let the story unravel. You know a story is good when after that final cutscene you sit in your chair for a few minutes, in utter shock, and proceed to call it a night. You know a game is well written when you begin to question the reason you're still playing at all, and you realise that the trauma your character is going through feels so real, you need to know and feel more. It's sad really, how much emotion and thought a video game put me through. This game had a plan from the beginning, to trick you into thinking it's another ♥♥♥♥♥♥ bang bang america simulator, and once that tone is set, it's thrown out a window and burned, and you're cast into a soldier's mind, gradually wearing away along with it's surroundings. You slowly walk a downward spiral into the dark bellows of the human mind, and let me tell you, it's ♥♥♥♥ing brilliant. I shouldn't really get this serious over a game, but man, is it an experience, I really wish I could spoil some of what happens and how it all ties together, but that would just ruin it. You need to experience it yourself, and take from that experience whatever you choose. Play this game as soon as you get the chance. Go in thinking it's just another shooting game in the desert, that's just what the devs want you to believe.

The best part about randomized dungeons, is that even if you find a hellroom that you're too incompitent to traverse... It's okay! I also don't feel like when I upgrade my stats, that I've made any meaningful progress. When I upgrade my HP, I don't feel any tougher when I play. My favorite aspect of rouge-likes is how much of it is luck. You can gain a fortune and epic loot, just as quickly as you can lose it. Here it feels like a very slow climb.

I had seen some of Rogue Legacy before, and I heard a review or two, so I figured when I saw it on the Summer Sale, I'd pick it up.  It has not disappointed me at all.  You start with only a few classes and basic items, but the unlock system is wonderful, giving you the chance to unlock classes, class upgrades, and global upgrades to your character such as extra HP or Mana, more money, and even the chance to defy death randomly.  Each class, while visually the same, lends itself to different styles of play.  You can go with a hack-and-slash type or heavy on magic, or even just try to run through and collect chests, money, blueprints, and runes.  The toll ensures that you use as much of your money as possible on upgrades each time, and you find yourself slowly getting more and more used to the enemies and traps that populate the castle.  Once the classes are upgraded, they all feel completely different and tend toward differing styles of play.  The traits also make each playthrough just a bit more different, and can make you choose or not choose a certain class depending upon their enhancements or liabilities.
If you like challenging Metroidvania style games, and you want hours of play, get this title.
Oh, and have fun storming the castle!!

Mad Max is loosely based on the world built up in the Mad Max: Fury Road movie. There is Scrotus (Immortan Joe's son) and his hordes. There are Buzzards and there is also the Roadkill faction. Each faction is uniquely identifiable by their garb and veichles of choice. This is one of the places the game falls flat though. Each faction whilst looking and sounding different are basically the same sorts of people you'll fight but reskins of each other. No faction has a unique fighting style.
This lazy design choice also filters into the bosses, where every Top Dog mini boss has exactly the same fighting style despite "intel" saying they each have specific weaknesses and such. This is a let down because the mini bosses having their own unique fighting styles and designs would've improved immersion in the game. The game is also very easy, you can block your way through most fights and there's hardly any times you'll find yourself in trouble.
Where the game excels though is exploring the land presented to you in the game. Despite it mostly being nothing but sand each area has its own style and helps makes the drives throughout this post apocolyptic wasteland less of a bore. Whether it's driving through sulfur pits, garbage mountains, decrepit motorways or canyons each location is fresh and encourages you to dive around.
Each location typically has the same amount to do in it. So 2 minefields to clear, a few scarerows to rip down, snipers to remove and camps to raid. This sounds dull and can get tedious at time I do admit, but I was having a blast 90% of the time. Especially when sieging the camps, most of them are pretty different from each other in terms of aesthetics so it doesn't get boring to explore and it gives you incentive to fully scout out every crevice of the camps for scrap and insignia signs to destory.
Each major non enemy leader who hands out missions will own a stronghold. Each stronghold will have projects for you to do (basically mini fetch quests). The projects at each stronghold give bonuses and change the aesthetic of the stronghold too. At first the stronghold will be run down but with each project you do, it'll not only give you a bonus such as refueling your car or rearming you with fresh ammo but it'll transform the look of the stronghold from rundown slum to a place which is relatively nice to live in. It's nice to see your actions having a profound effect on the people living there.
The sound design for this game is excellent, with thumping engines, ear shattering explosions and cool australian accents. It almost never lets you down, they've really excelled here. My only complaint is the NPCs dotted around the map you can talk to, they sound as if they got someone off the street to do a fake accent and babble some rubbish. Only part of the audio that's a let down. These NPCs are visually a letdown too because they all look very similar so the developers obviously didn't put too much effort into them.
The story isn't very compelling, but then again Mad Max isn't famous for excellent story telling. It's mediocre, except my main problem with it is that it ends too early. Just as the story missions start to get interesting the game ends abruptly. It took me 20-30 minutes to finish Act 5.
Max can have his items and car upgraded and his skills unlocked via Scrap. You can find Scrap all over the world, on dead bodies, in forts and in scavenging locations. The upgrading system is very satisfying and you can definitely see yourself and your car progress in strength and capability. You can do up your car however you want, so you can have a fast but fragile car or a slow but tooled to the nines car and all inbetween. The choice is yours!
In conclusion:
+ Lots to do
+ Lots of places to explore
+ Art / Sound design is fantastic
+ Car combat is fun
+ Upgrading your car is very satisfying
- Very easy foot combat
- Car combat can get tedious
- Story ends abruptly
- Mini bosses all have the same fighting patterns
- Factions don't have unique combat moves
In conclusion Mad Max is a fun open world game with nice enviroments to explore. It will get repetitive at times, which can be dull for a lot of people. It's easy but don't let that put you off. This is a great game to buy.

The game is set in a post-catastrophe Dubai that has been all but buried by an immense sandstorm that continues to rage 6 months on. We follow Captain Walker and his Delta Force team who are sent in to search for survivors and Colonel Konrad, the man in charge of the evacuation. What we find is a decaying city in the midst of a war.
What sets this game apart from other third-person cover-based shooters is the way the story unfolds. The story is nothing short of amazing, with the premise being inspired by Joseph Conrad's novella Heart of Darkness (similar to Apocalypse Now, which is a Vietnam War era adaption of that novel).
The intention is to show the grey, morally ambiguous side of war. The player is required to make tough moral decisions, sometimes resulting in a terrible outcome despite you best intentions. This is in stark contrast to your typical (COD) shooter which makes you feel like the hero. Here, there is no moral high-ground, and you're left dealing with the consequences of your actions. You (and your character) will feel unhinged, exhausted and empty by the end of it - which is a testament to how powerful the story is.
Great graphics, beautiful and original setting, good cover-based gameplay - but most of all, an emotionally deep story that makes you reflect on the true ramifications of war. A masterpiece, highly recommended.

The first thing to get out of the way is that this game is not fun, nor was it meant to be fun.  That said, I feel that it is an incredibly important game that everyone should play.  Like in all modern shooters, you get turned into a mass murderer, but this time it is openly acknowledged and you will feel terrible about it.  One of the best examples that comes to mind is a part where you are forced to kill 2 men right after listening to them have a talk about actual things that make you have feels.  That's right, THIS GAME WILL HIT YOU RIGHT IN THE FEELS.  Another great aspect of the game is the lack of black-and-white morality.  Pretty much the entire game is spent questioning who is in the right, and the answer pretty consistently ends up being nobody.  It seems like everybody is trying to do the right thing, but they're doing horrible things in the process.  I must say that one of my favorite things about this game was the way that they portrayed the mental deterioration of your character and your squadmates. You can see these people that used to be great friends start to fall apart and get in fights with each other over what's right.  Anyways, I suppose I should also discuss the gameplay.  It's not very good.  Everything about the game is pretty generic if not sub-par.  It's a cover-based 3rd person shooter, but the cover system sucks and the shooting is nothing special.  One of my biggest complaints is actually that sprinting and taking cover are bound to the same button, so sometimes I would sprint past cover into the open, and other times I would want to sprint and accidentally get attached to cover.  You also have 2 squad mates that you can "command" but that basically involves telling them to shoot at a specific person until the target is dead.  The game is driven very hard by the story/themes, and I'd say it safely gets away with it, especially since the game is only about 5 hours long.  Buy it.

You have to respect development teams who cater so such a niche audience. It's really hard to find a decent hunting game now. The only one's that come to mind are Cabela's and the last game I (and many others) played from them magically stopped launching after about 30 hours.
Call of the Wild is a flawed gem, though. It has some of the most beautiful scenery I've ever seen in a game. So beautiful that I often find myself surprised that it runs at all on my hardware (750ti, i5 7700k) With a huge map, day and night cycles and varying weather systems the game boasts a deeply immersive atmosphere that is only broken by the often buggy behavior of an animal you're hunting. I'm giving the game a positive review because I'm enjoying it, and I am confident the devs will fix the animal behavior/pathing.

Soooooo, this game. It looks damn amazing. The controls are solid and the aiming, shooting, etc. are competently done. But the reviews are mixed, so what gives?
The big problem this game has at the moment is issues with animals getting stuck in terrain and you getting killed if you get stick in a little ditch in the ground.
There's other issues too, for example I'm missing a decent form of transporation in the extremely vast maps. Yes there's teleport to outposts you discovered before, but getting there can sometimes take a very long time.
Where's my Bullet cam? I know it's not realistic, but I loved having good shots rewarded with a satisfying Sniper-esque slowmo bullet-following camera. Sadly this game doesn't have this at all, not even as an option.
Unlocking the various items can take a bit of time, with some of the objectives really testing your patience.
The bugs are the major negative as far as I can see. The game is gorgeous though, the two environments are well crafted and positively massive in size. The sound design is a 9/10 with some individual sounds sticking out from the mix more than they should, but overall it's a beautiful experience to roam through the forest in this game. Some of ambient bird calls aren't exactly correct for a supposedly german forest, but I'm nitpicking here. The weapon sounds are realistic and satisfying.
You only get two maps though, as well as a handful of weapons. The animal variety also isn't too great. However it's only 30 Euros at the time of writing, and the devs were smart enough to provide a skill and perk system to help with long term motivation. If you're a fan of hunting games, or enjoy realistic renditions of nature in games, this is a solid game. No microtransactions, what you see is what you get.
Could do with bugfixing though. The issues don't happen all the time, but they're there.
Overall, considering the price and the quality of the environments, and the otherwise solid shooting mechanics, I give this one a thumbs up.

It's more like Mass Effect (gameplay, deep story) meets Call of Duty: and heavy on the Effect, and heavy on the Duty. This game makes you think...constantly, trying to figure out just what the hell is going on, and makes you think about moral decisions you must make to walk the path of Darkness, or of Light. Like The Walking Dead game, you will be given choices to make and you will grit your teeth and think "Goddammit, I don't want to decide...all choices are ♥♥♥♥ed!". But you have to make a decision, and live with it, and listen to your teammates give you♥♥♥♥♥♥about it.
It makes Call of Duty look like kindergarten. The setting is amazing. The wonder city of Dubai is cast into chaos when a freak, apocalyptic sandstorm buries the city under red death. The citizens just want to survive. But something's not quite right... If you've ever seen Apocalypse Now, or read the book/watched the movie Heart of Darkness...you'll instantly start seeing similarities. And hopefully, you'll get the shivers. Because this game holds no punches, and you'll be wondering if your sanity will remain intact by the end of the game. Okay, maybe your character in the game will be wondering, but you'll be okay though.
It's not a very long game. I think I finished it in about 12 hours, exploring everything I could. But it's the story that makes you feel like you've been through epic hell and lived to tell the tale. It is hard to equate this game to words- it is clear by the number of hours I have put into this game that I like it. Liking it may be an understatement. I came to this game looking for fun, heard of it's joyous nature from many a friend, however my common distaste for FPS games at the time left me wondering if I'd even appreciate it at all.
Within hours I was corrected, it's an Action/Role-Playing/First Person Shooter with wit and humour that genuinely makes me laugh each time.
"Bacon is for sycophants and products of incest."
While the game is twice as fun with a friend or two, or three- I find it's exciting gameplay to be just as fun alone. The 'bazillion' guns they boast about the ads is partially true, at first it will seem like there are millions upon millions of guns, which there are, yet this becomes much more refined and obvious the more you play and learn about the gun types.
Be prepared to grind, the game offers an amazing story and a bounty full of additional content, but the harder difficulties (True Vault Hunter Mode and Ultimate Vault Hunter Mode) can become slightly repetitive, however they do definitely maintain the challenge for veterans.
My largest complaint however is its horrendous un-optimisation on PC. While it still looks stunning for a game made in U3 (Unreal Engine 3) from 2012, most all computers will suffer some form of frame drops during intense situations, for some it can ruin the experience, yet hopefully you find enough in the game to continue despite this glaring flaw.
Either way- buy this game, it is always on sale, I beg you, I plead you, I'll adore you if you do and you'll thank me for it every day.

Mad Max is a game I'd highly recommend. It does so much more than most games and is obviously lovingly crafted.
From a story perspective it's there and it's in perfect quantity. You can rush through the story if you want and have a nice compact experience, or you could play for 15 hours after you get done with the intro not touching the story at all and just focus on clearing camps, taking out snipers, taking down scarecrows, clearing minefields, searching for scrap, taking out a convoy, or upgrading a fortress to its completion before you decide to take on another mission. The ending while I can imagine it being divisive is my favorite since Red Dead Redemption. I won't spoil it for you but I will advise you giving it some time to sit with you and reflect on how fitting it is.
Touching a bit more on those optional objectives. I've heard complaints about the grindy aspect of it, and I will admit that if you don't enjoy a grind it may be a bit tedious for you. I am the kind of gamer though that enjoys a nice solid grind with a reward at the end. When I completely lowered the threat down in someone's territory I felt accomplished, I had a much faster and more dangerous vehicle, and my Max had gotten much better as well.
Visually the game is gorgeous. To me the beauty of the Mad Max movies (particularly The Road Warrior and Fury Road) is the contrast between the deep blue sky and the browns/oranges of the desert wasteland and this game pulls it off perfectly. The visuals are also somewhat varied with white sea beds, tan dunes, orange earthy deserts, black tarry oil pumps, and black/gray dumps. Color isn't muted either and when you see a brighter color from a flare or an enemy covered in paint it's a very pretty sight.
The sound is very top notch. The bass of the shotgun or the roar of your engine (especially when you get a V8) is very deep and a pleasure to listen to. The higher sounds like the scraping of your vehicle against another or the screech of your tires also comes off as real and fantastic.
Your gameplay is going to be split into driving and on foot brawling. The driving is a lot of fun and is quite the spectacle. Taking out a convoy is a blast as you grapple off tires, shoot explosive harpoons, or use your shotgun while driving to blow up an enemy's gas tank. Driving feels fast and fluid and is a lot of fun on its own, the combat is great and is the perfect icing on top. When you're on your feet brawling around a camp it's very gritty dirty and fun fighting that's a blast. You'll be body slamming, drop kicking, and gut punching enemies into submission, and you can even dirty it up with a shotgun to the stomach, taking an enemy melee weapon and quickly disposing of a group, or a shiv to the throat when an enemy lets their guard drop. Brawling mostly consists of parries, hits, and dodges with an indicator above enemy heads to signal what they are about to do, if you're familiar with the Arkham series or Shadow of Mordor you'll feel comfortable quickly.
Mad Max is a game that deserves a lot more recognition for the amount of fun fullfilling content it provides. It had a very unfortunate release date but if you ever get a chance it's definitely a fun game that dips its toes into a lot of genres whilst also making them fun and unique to fit its tone. If putting on some music and driving and fighting around a wasteland on a quest for a better car and better gear sounds like fun to you it's a definite must buy.

Gameplay wise I find it very pleasing, tailing and calling in prey to be shot is really satisfying, especially if the kill is a beauty. Patience is a virtue in this game thats for sure.

A few bugs I've noticed so far is sometimes the hitscan seems way off, I'll aim for the vital organs but when I claim the trophy ive shot right up the poop shaute.. Another is that the callers seem to bug and wont go off when used. I'm unsure if this is an audio thing or if it actually doesn't work in game when the item is used. Lastly I've had a really rare bug where I can't toggle to other eequipment. It isn't holdstered and the symbol in the bottom right will change but the character won't take out the respective equipment nor is it able to be used.
Overall I love this game, and I am sure to have many more hours! As mentioned I just hope DLC isn't something that takes the mick over time.. Last thing steam needs is another Train Simulator DLC mockery!

Spec Ops: The Line....what's there to say. It's a very good game and i was suprised over how it got to me with it's story. You're Captain Martin Walker and you and your squad is given the task to enter the sandcovered ruins of Dubai that has been the victim of numerous sandstorms to save civilians and to find Colonel John Konrad who is the head of the "Damned 33rd" Infantry Battalion. Although the whole mission goes to hell real fast and as the story progresses you will uncover more and more of what's really going on and it will keep you playing til the end and even after you have completed the game you're gonna want to more.
The story is deep and gripping and the gameplay is quite nice, although the cover system is a little bit sluggish and can be frustrating sometimes. Remember when i said that Dubai was covered by sand? Well heres the thing about sand. Sand is something that you can use to your advantage out on the battlefield. if you throw a grenade on a sandcovered location the explosion creates a cloud of sand thats blinds enemies for a limited time, and if you see a window or a glass roof with sand on it you can shoot it to crush your enemies with immense force of the sand dune that's pours in. You can give orders to your squad like focus on a specific enemy or to help a downed squadmate and your squadmates will have some pretty useful shouts like "Shotgunner on the field" or "Enemy in the open"
Overall this is a underestimated game and it deserves all the credit it gets and moore. This game has easily become one of my most beloved games of all time due to is story and characters. I give this a 9/10 and i advise you to pick this game up and play it through.
