The First Life is Strange was my absolute favourite game. But it had one problem: many dialogues and characters seemed to be a bit shallow. Especially what Max thought about them.
In Before The Storm this problem is completely solved. You fall in love with the characters so quickly. And Chloe actually looks behind the facades of the different people.

I haven't been a long term fan of the Life is Strange franchise myself, I only got the first game when it was on the steam sale this summer. But with the little time I've had with the whole universe I have enjoyed it. Before the Storm was a really hyped up game for me because of the fact that you play as Chloe during her time of distress, her Dad's dead and Max has run off. Though I do have a couple of questions that stir in my mind when playing, though nothing major.
One that really annoyed me however, was that in episode 1 of the first game. Chloe says that she met Rachel when she was 14. "Well you never made much effort to find out. I was 14, we were best friends" But in the game Chloe is 16 and you meet Rachel at the Firewalk concert. Along with this, in episode 3 and 4 of the origional
you see in the photos that fly around that Chloe has a blue strip in her hair on her 16th birthday and that David has already moved in. This is another mess up because in the game as 16 year old Chloe she hasn't dyed her fringe blueas it shows in the photo and in the garage scene you see that David is starting to move in and that he wasn't already there.
For the writters of this game, I just want to ask how they came up with such awkward dialouge. I get the awkward dialouge being in Chloe's head
but you don't need the awkward dialouge anywhere else, it kind of put me off because I know that Chloe wouldn't say half of them. Some of it actually seems like you felt the quote was empty so you added in pointless sentences to give it more depth, which ruined the quality of the quote. One of them which really got annoyed was
Rachel uses the word exactly back-to-back, granted you've added in the scene where she doesn't and I think that moment suits it better because Rachel doesn't have to say exactly again, it doesn't feel like it's what Rachel would say, judging from the personality I've detected from episode 1. I don't know why it annoys me but in a future update I'd say to get rid of the second exactly... that's all I want because that's all you can really do, since its already in the game, just plays 1/2 the time when I want it to be cut out every time.
Enough criticisms now, because I've run out of them, onto the pros of the game.
The story itself is a good choice because we get to experience what Chloe was going through when Max has gone, the death of her dad still fresh in her mind and meeting Rachel, who those who have played the origional, know that she was special to Chloe. Just from the first episode I can safely say that I'm genuinely dying for episode 2 and 3 and what they entail. My current theory is that the game will revolve around either Frank and his "friend" Damon Merrick or it'll look into who the woman that made out with Rachel's dad was... those are my guesses mainly because they were shown in the end cutscene of the first episode, I didn't quite bother working out what will happen with Principal Wells because in the origional we see him arguing with Mr Jefferson at the end cutscene of the second episode though nothing really happens between the two of them.
My favorite scene so far would be
this is because we see exactly what she believes in David, Max, Rachel and even her dad William. I'll be honest the first time I played this scene I cried at the end when she sees the car that William died in half because of Rihanna's performance in showing a girl who's seen a sort of physical concious of her dad and half just for personal reasons. But needless to say it was my first ever game cut scene where I genuinley cried.
The music for Before the Storm as well is just perfection in my opinion, yes I know that Deck Nine partnered up with Daugher to make the Score for the game but that's how perfectly fitted music comes from, the origional Life is Strange did well to use existing songs into their game but they always seemed slightly off and maybe the developers felt like that too... but with the music being made specifically for this game it fleshes out the story more like a film, adding this extra layer of what the gamer is supposted to feel at the moment and with the developers working with the artists they can protray exactly what they want instead of finding a compramise with a song that brings probably 70% of what the gamer should feel.
I personally enjoy this game, hell I completed episode one 3 times with all of the grafitti on each save for my playstation and nerly 3 times on my PC, I think mainly the game stands out as interesting because there's hardly any other game like it, there are Telltale games but they go off of stories that have a premade lore, with Life is Strange they have the freedom to make the story how they feel like, plus I think if Square Enix and Dontnod push for it, they could make a successful TV series, but people don't like it when games change platform like that because it takes away the emersiveness so it was smart of them not to, but I think Life is Strange could be a good TV series, if they do it right! If memory seves me right it was Jean-Luc Cano that came up with the idea of Life is Strange and I have to tell Jean-Luc that this game and the idea of it is absolutley amazing, I know you won't read this since it'll get lost in the reviews of this game and lost in translation but I sincerely thank you and probably all of us thank you for coming up with the story of Life is Strange.
Anyway, I'd rate this game a 9.8/10 because nothing is perfect and can always see improvement but it's a good job

I usually don't make long reviews, unless it's a game that got overlooked and worth giving a chance.
Mad Max Is an Action RPG Open-World game developed by the same studio that brought you Just Cause games.
At first you would say "Another game based on a movie? Nah, it will be crap"
But this isn't the case. This is really probably the best movie tie-in Video Game in long, long time.
This Game feels like a 3rd person version of RAGE (remember RAGE? another post-apocalyptic game).
You get a car, you upgrade it and your arsenal, gets to several areas/strongholds/camps, meets new people, gets missions and so on.
The Story, however isn't really that outstanding.
Mad Max gets picked on by War Boys, stole his car and he want to get it back to continue his journey, instead he found a guy that offered him a "Car with potential". But Max found out that car can't withstand the harsh environment, so he need to work hard to upgrade it so he can get out of the place to somewhere else.
Mad Max is a 3rd Person Action RPG. That means you navigate through the world. Loot scraps, fight random enemies and loot them, destroy threats, help strangers, take down strongholds and upgrade your companions' ones for services.
The combat is a kin to that of Batman Arkham Games, you use you arms to strike down enemies and break their bones and necks and you can carry weapons to crush skulls (the game is so violent btw) while countering incoming attacks.
In addition of that, you have a shotgun for quick kills but ammo is so scarce and hard to find.
In Vehicles. Your Magnum Opus equipped with a Harpoon to pull enemies and objects with and a Rocket-Launcher-like weapon to destroy other cars and metallic gates and a Sniper Rifle to take down long range enemies. With further upgrading, you could make your car a moving flame thrower.
During your navigation in the world, enemies will ambush you, chase you and annoy the♥♥♥♥♥♥out of you.
You can shoot down their cars' tires, blow up their engines and take their loot for bigger scraps.
The World is that big, so many activities to do.
As for collectibles. There are historic relics that give you some other people's thoughts and concerns from the world before the Nuclear weapons fell. They are really interesting to read.
The game is surprisingly very detailed. The environment, the locations and in-doors places are very well-designed.
like the sand hills which looks beautiful and realistic in the desert areas, and the mountainous and valleys areas looks damn gorgeous giving the perfect post-apocalyptic sight.
The Character models and animations are detailed, high quality stuff.
The worst thing about this game is probably the Boss Fights. There are several Bosses (named TopDogs here)
in each Stronghold and at the end of several missions. But the problem is.... They Are ALL the SAME.
They are all the same design, same pattern, same animations, and the same way you have to do to take them down.
It feels like it's just 1 boss that spawn in different locations. No variety at all. Good thing they don't appear all the time so it's just a matter of choice to encounter them all.
Another unique, but annoying feature of the game.
The upgrade system doesn't rely on the player experience points gained from battles or missions.
Instead, it rely on Challenges made throughout your actions. Like defeating enemies with specific ways or take them down within a specific time.
In addition to character upgrade point which you can spend on Health Points, Loot/Ammo/Water/Food bonus,etc...
That's for Max's character abilities.
For Car's upgrades, they get unlocked for more reduction of threats you made in the world.
Other upgrades are only unlocked for completing specific missions.
Don't really know if i can recommend it for a full price or on sale. I got it $20 and enjoyed it.
So, it's depends in your budget.
The Good:
+ Too many things to do
+ Combat System is well-made
+ Taking over Strongholds and Camps is fun
+ Collecting relics is a fun read
+ Upgrading Max and the Magnum Opus is super rewarding
+ Beautiful and detailed world environment
+ Missions and side missions are varied
The Bad:
| Upgrading things you want can takes too long time to unlock
| Lowering threats for car upgrades can be repetitive and annoying
The Ugly:
- Absolutely no variety for Bosses. It's just 1 Boss with different skins.
- Max has an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ character.

Is it as good as the original? No. But that would have been a lot to expect from anyone. Is it good on its own? Most definitely. The soundtrack is great, the graphics give the same "ugly but charming" feeling as the first one, and the voice acting is perfect through most of the episode. Some have said it's a pity we actually get to meet Rachel, as she was acting as a ghost figure in Life is Strange, but here the devs have very cleverly replaced her with Max, whose not seen but mentioned lots of times. Narratively speaking, it really works and also gives new insights about Chloe, which is the whole point of the prequel. The backtalk thing isn't as good as time traveling, obviously, but it's still fun; the whole "paperish" aesthetics and the diary/phone interfaces have been kept, which I think is great, and other than that, it's a perfectly enjoyable storyline for anyone who's into the genre. Okay. So. Let me start this review off by saying I am a die hard LIS fan. I played the first game multiple times just to explore every single possible option out there for the original. So I will be very straight forward and blunt about Before the Storm. Before the storm does not feel as, natural I guess as the original. Not at all. Also the end of the first episode did not leave me with the same anticipation or excitement as the original did after each and every episode. Before the Storm feels almost, kind of forced in a way. And the character building seemed very awkward and clunky. The way Chloe builds relationships feels  very, again forced and unnatrual. You almost feel as though you have no true say in what you do, as if all of it turns into the same outcome. Even plenty of dialogue options only have 2 options. not 3 or 4 much like the original. However. The game still does have some charm. I dont want to call this game worse than the original simply for two reasons. It isnt the same game, we all have personal preference, and this game simply just went for a different vibe due to the fact you play as the rebellious chloe price vs innocent max. And the second reason. It simply is not finished yet. We have only seen the very first episode. So no one should say the game is a total flop yet. Overall, if you played the original, you should get it. If you played other games such as TWD telltale series and enjoyed it also defineintly get it. However i would get the original first for sure. But reasons to not get it, simply if you dont like story motivated video games, dont get it.

Classic Rating: ★★★★★
ETS2 is an awesome driving simulator, it's got many different features and they fit very well together.
These are some of ETS2's strong points:
● Good playability, easy handling/steering (I'm using an XBOX 360 Controller, but Steering Wheels are also supported)
● Nice gameplay: you don't just drive; you can run your own company, hire drivers, take a loan if you need money to buy a truck or personalize it - the game offers many (unlockable) items for your trucks. You also advance in your driver's career, adding skills every time you gain enough XP; those upgrades are needed to take longer trips, carry fragile/expensive/dangerous cargos which let you earn money faster.
● You can listen to your favourite music in-game, being it a Streaming Radio or MP3 files.
● ETS2 is highly moddable and there is plenty of Mods: I can suggest "ProMods" for Single Player and "ETS2 Multiplayer Mod" which adds a living layer to the game (only human player are in there).
● You can have your favourite avatar and plate, registering at World of Trucks website (they will also give you a free key for a "Metallic Paint Jobs" DLC).
Some downsides too:
● The AI is not the best, sadly. You'll have to pay a lot of attention when driving near crossings or when switching lanes, because the AI drives faster than you and it doesn't care very much about you; a little delay in your maneuver and some car can easily hit you - and yeah, you're the one being fined - always.
● Mods: they're cool but you should chose wisely and do not draw the longbow. Some game breaking is to be expected, so always save your game before adding a new Mod. Another problem with them is that if you want to remove any, you'll have to reload a previously saved game and all of your gameplay with that Mod will be just gone; so, again, pay attention while modding.
● The game is a little "heavy" on Graphic Cards, but I guess that's to be expected.
I've got this game on sale, no DLCs, but I'm enjoying it so much - recommended.

tl;dr version in the end
-----------
I usually don't make long reviews, unless it's a game that got overlooked and worth giving a chance.
Mad Max Is an Action RPG Open-World game developed by the same studio that brought you Just Cause games.
At first you would say "Another game based on a movie? Nah, it will be crap"
But this isn't the case. This is really probably the best movie tie-in Video Game in long, long time.
This Game feels like a 3rd person version of RAGE (remember RAGE? another post-apocalyptic game).
You get a car, you upgrade it and your arsenal, gets to several areas/strongholds/camps, meets new people, gets missions and so on.
The Story, however isn't really that outstanding.
Mad Max gets picked on by War Boys, stole his car and he want to get it back to continue his journey, instead he found a guy that offered him a "Car with potential". But Max found out that car can't withstand the harsh environment, so he need to work hard to upgrade it so he can get out of the place to somewhere else.
Mad Max is a 3rd Person Action RPG. That means you navigate through the world. Loot scraps, fight random enemies and loot them, destroy threats, help strangers, take down strongholds and upgrade your companions' ones for services.
The combat is a kin to that of Batman Arkham Games, you use you arms to strike down enemies and break their bones and necks and you can carry weapons to crush skulls (the game is so violent btw) while countering incoming attacks.
In addition of that, you have a shotgun for quick kills but ammo is so scarce and hard to find.
In Vehicles. Your Magnum Opus equipped with a Harpoon to pull enemies and objects with and a Rocket-Launcher-like weapon to destroy other cars and metallic gates and a Sniper Rifle to take down long range enemies. With further upgrading, you could make your car a moving flame thrower.
During your navigation in the world, enemies will ambush you, chase you and annoy the♥♥♥♥♥♥out of you.
You can shoot down their cars' tires, blow up their engines and take their loot for bigger scraps.
The World is that big, so many activities to do.
As for collectibles. There are historic relics that give you some other people's thoughts and concerns from the world before the Nuclear weapons fell. They are really interesting to read.
The game is surprisingly very detailed. The environment, the locations and in-doors places are very well-designed.
like the sand hills which looks beautiful and realistic in the desert areas, and the mountainous and valleys areas looks damn gorgeous giving the perfect post-apocalyptic sight.
The Character models and animations are detailed, high quality stuff.
The worst thing about this game is probably the Boss Fights. There are several Bosses (named TopDogs here)
in each Stronghold and at the end of several missions. But the problem is.... They Are ALL the SAME.
They are all the same design, same pattern, same animations, and the same way you have to do to take them down.
It feels like it's just 1 boss that spawn in different locations. No variety at all. Good thing they don't appear all the time so it's just a matter of choice to encounter them all.
Another unique, but annoying feature of the game.
The upgrade system doesn't rely on the player experience points gained from battles or missions.
Instead, it rely on Challenges made throughout your actions. Like defeating enemies with specific ways or take them down within a specific time.
In addition to character upgrade point which you can spend on Health Points, Loot/Ammo/Water/Food bonus,etc...
That's for Max's character abilities.
For Car's upgrades, they get unlocked for more reduction of threats you made in the world.
Other upgrades are only unlocked for completing specific missions.
Don't really know if i can recommend it for a full price or on sale. I got it $20 and enjoyed it.
So, it's depends in your budget.
The Good:
+ Too many things to do
+ Combat System is well-made
+ Taking over Strongholds and Camps is fun
+ Collecting relics is a fun read
+ Upgrading Max and the Magnum Opus is super rewarding
+ Beautiful and detailed world environment
+ Missions and side missions are varied
The Bad:
| Upgrading things you want can takes too long time to unlock
| Lowering threats for car upgrades can be repetitive and annoying
The Ugly:
- Absolutely no variety for Bosses. It's just 1 Boss with different skins.
- Max has an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ character.

You know how some people think that animals have souls? Well...they don't. But I'm pretty sure this video game does.
Before I gush about how much I love this game, let me preface my rave review with a warning. It's my opinion that if you are about to play Undertale for the first time, the less you know about it, the better. If you have any interest at all in the game, stop reading about it--listen to your heart and play it.
Now I'll resume my review which, consequently, contains some minor SPOILERS.
If you allow yourself to be fully immersed in its complex & weirdly meaningful world, Undertale will challenge everything you've come to understand about RPGs. Undertale is the only game I've ever played that has inspired me to question my every action and the motivating thoughts behind them.
Set in a beautifully nostalgic world with minimalist-yet-intricate pixel art, a whole slew of head-turning experiences await the player. The sizeable cast of characters range from the mildly misunderstood to the downright demented with a few goofballs thrown in to keep things kind of kooky. Depending on how you choose, these characters will either warm your heart as they help you along your friendly quest, or fill you with determination as you set out to accomplish your less-than-friendly mission.
The soundtrack is hauntingly captivating. Each piece of music throughout the game is masterfully crafted to fit the mood of each scene. Playing this game on "mute" would be a woeful mistake. The music & sounds of Undertale are a critical part of the soulful journey, breathing life into every dark corner of the game.
Gameplay is unique, yet familiar. The game itself is not challenging to "beat," but that's not really the point of Undertale. The challenge is deciding how you want to beat the game. This is where the experience becomes truly unique.
Overall, I was greatly pleased with the way Undertale gave me a new perspective while telling a gripping story in a unique way. I had already decided to play it again before I was even halfway done with my first playthrough. It's moving, enchanting, funny, and fun.
Bottom line: Play Undertale and follow your heart. Then follow your heart and play it again. You won't regret it...or maybe you will.

In this review I will only review the first episode of LIS BtS, since no other episode is out yet. It will contain as minor spoilers as possible.
Now after I played the first episode of LIS BtS I ended up a bit disappointed in the game and my guts tell me, not to recommend this game. The game presents itself well enough and the LIS-feeling from the first part definitely is there, so why does it feel to fall short?
The reason would be that in comparison to the first game this one just falls short.
- The graphics seem inferior to the first game. Some characters look totally fine (like Chloe), but some models are not consistant. This is especially painful, since Rachel is one of the not-consistant character models, She definitely has some camera angles, where she seems to be a different model completely.
. It still is a pretty game, but it is disappointing, if you feel, that technology has made a step backwards.
- While in the first LIS the power of rewinding created a really interesting game mechanic (which was not exploited enough throughout the game), that gave that game an unique feel to it and was able to advance the plot, that meachanic is really missing in this game. They tried to subsitute it with the "backtalk"-mechanics, but instead of helping the story I feel, it gets in the way of storrytelling. I's a hit- and miss- minigame, where winning the minigame just gets you, what you wanted to archieve, while loosing just leaves you in the same outcome you would have get, if you never tried to backtalk. The worst thing in this minigame is, it is so obvious and not a challange at all to "win" it.
Look for example at the scene in the first LIS, where you meet Frank at his trailer by the shore. That scene was beautifully set up and depending on what you do in and before this scene the outcome of the scene could have been vastly different
.
I was hoping for the second game to do more of those complex choices, but with "backtalk" being a thing I don't see it happening anytime soon.
-The plot is completely linear,
I wanted more scenes like in LIS with Kate, where my relation to her really depends, if I end up in Scene A or Scene B. So far nothing like that can be seen here.
-People are not subtile in this game. The characters reactions and emotions seem to be a bit over the top. It's a bit of a missed opportunity, if reaccuring (or preaccuring?) characters only seem to be an overstated version of the character you already know. People could change over the years, especially teenagers, but you won't see someone act a different way, because events would have happend 3 years earlier.
All in all I still would recommend this game to others. While all those points above are true, it is a little unfair for LIS BtS, since tbh I would not have compared the game with the first episode of LIS, but with the whole first game. If I try only to look at the first episode of the first game, I'd have to adimt, the first episode was no is not the real memorable part of the first game, it's storytelling really gets strong in Episode 2 and 3. The first episode was there to give a setting but not to tell the tale. And LIS BtS does this job, and it does this job well. As I have written above, it has the vibe of a LIS-Game.
*S*P*O*I*L*E*R*

So all in all LIS BtS has its problems but seems to be promising, while also is not expensive, so that even if episode 2 and 3 fail to deliver, I am sure, I won't regret having bought that game.

Ever watch TV shows like Oz, Prison Break or Orange is the New Black and want to run your own prison? Now is your chance! Prison Architect is a simple, fun, top down, real time strategy, management, building game with a lot of depth yet it is so easy to pick up and play. While it is still 'Early access,' it feels complete and polished.
Prison Architect is not like the Sims. You are just building a prison. Everything is not instantly done when you place it. You have workers that take time to go through your prison to carry out what you want. Not just that, but the trucks with the items need to arrive. It is a really nice system and the workers are fast and efficient enough to quickly carry out things. Your workers can die and if things aren't getting done quick enough, hire more workers. Every staff costs X amount to hire them, and Y amount to keep them employed every day. You have funds and a daily budget. Your daily budget cannot be in the red, that becomes the limitation and challenge of the game.
Since this is a prison, every 24 hours new inmates arrive. You need to get ready for them. So you build walls, a holding cell, dozens of private cells, a shower, a yard, a kitchen and a canteen. Then you hire staff and place objects into each room to make them functional. Objects such as beds, benches, tables, kitchen cookers, freezers, a wide sofa for your staff room, desks for your offices and of course a variety of doors. Jail doors, large jail doors, staff doors, solitary confinement doors. These are all objects. Only guards can open jail doors so if one of your worker / laborers needs to get through they need to wait for a guard to let them through.
When you start a game, you can select different things to make your game different, such as having randomly generated empty rooms and landscape. You can select whether or not to have 8 normal prisoners per day or a random number of maximum, minimum or normal security prisoners. This adds a lot of variety to each time you start a new game.
The game lets you do whatever you want, but as a guide, it gives you optional objectives. You can only do 2 objectives at once. That's the beauty of this game, you pick the objectives whenever you want at any time. You're not pigeon holed into a scenario. When you select an objective you will receive a money grant to carry out the objective. There is no time limit. There is just a money limit. Run out of money doing a project and you'll be stuck waiting until your funds build back up. For the most part you are given more than enough money and once you're done with the objective you get the other half of the money. The objectives have a list of mini objectives that benefit and grow your prison. Everything to build a cell block that can hold 15 prisoners to all the steps needed to have a functional medical ward, which involve offices, doctors, an intermarry and a psychiatrist that need to be unlocked in bureaucracy.
Once you hire a warden, he will open up bureaucracy, which is the game's version of unlocks. You can unlock a slew of new personnel such as a security chief that can unlock cameras, an armory and other things. You can even unlock an accountant that leads to land purchases for when you outgrow your plot of land. These are all nice touches that really let the game feel like your own.
Since you are an architect, you need to lay out pipes and wires. Not just that, but you need to place water pumps, generators and conduits. Every room needs to have wires to it, big items such as freezers and monitors need wires directly to them. If you use too much power for your generator and conduits, it'll result in a power outage and then chaos happens. When it comes to toilets and showers, you have small pipes and large pipes, small pipes lose pressure the further they go, so you need to have large pipes, but the catch is inmates can use large pipes to crawl in and escape. So never have large pipes near inmates. There are other ways inmates can escape, such as tunneling, walking out if they break a door lock and go over an unattended wall.
The game has emergency services so if you get uncontrollable riots, you can send in an emergency swat team and tell them where to go. If you have a fire, then call for the fire department and you'll see their hoses strung through your prison. EMTs can also be called in, but for the most part your medical ward / infirmary should handle things.
You have a lot of control over the prisoners including their schedule, how much free time they have, when the have it, when they eat and when they shower. It is helpful for big prisons that have small facilities, you can have the minimum security prisoners eat when the maximums are showering and when the normal prisoners are in the yard. You can unlock restricting certain levels of prisoners to certain areas. On top of that you can even sell and buy stock from your prison.
There is also a lot of unintentional comedy such as a K9 patrol using a broken toilet, workers getting cemented into walls, inmates killing guards with spoons, and of course the names of inmates and why they're in prison. On top of that there are mods and prison downloads, the game is really about having your fun the way you want to have it.
In all the game is probably worth $30 and I rarely say that, but its been on sale plenty of times. You can sink a lot of time into the game and enjoy every second of it.

Specs ops the Line has an interesting story, that is immersive and well paced throughout the entire single player campaign. The story and setting are the two strong points to the game, as the gameplay does not live up to those. The gameplay mechanics are good but most of them have been used in countless other shooters, making the game feel somewhat generic. There are a couple of nice gameplay mechanics such as slowing down time when a bullet is pumped into an enemy's skull and the ability to execute an enemy in brutal ways, like smacking the end of your weapon into an enemy's face repeatively, while they are injured on the floor and bleeding to death.
The campaign is short, only taking me approximately 5-6 hours to complete on normal difficulty. There are hidden items in the game such as intel, where they will tell you about events that have happended within the Specs Ops universe. There is also a run of the mill multiplayer mode, which plays out like many other military shooters and a co-op mode that is based on different missions to the single player campaign, that aren't as engaging. Overall this game is worth picking up on a steam sale, or somewhere cheap.

TL;DR - Enjoyable, feels like a beta but very pretty with an iffy interface, less of a hunting game and more an animal shooting game. Bows are OP. No microtransactions.
After putting more time into this, I feel I can write a proper and serious review. At the time of writing, this game functions like beta. That said, despite being riddled with bugs and occasional crashes (though your mileage may vary on bugginess) this game is a graphically superb and worthy sibling to theHunter Classic, and I don't regret my purchase. My only major complaint is that they somehow managed to be less realistic in this game than Classic with both the general feel of the game and with animal behaviors - I feel I can describe it best in the way that Diablo 3 is not a dungeon crawler like D2, but a very large loot run. Similarly, you are placed in the vast reserve (and I do mean vast, the maps are colossal) with free reign over a never-ending hunt. It doesn't feel like hunting to me, it feels like animal shooting. Veterans of theHunter Classic (or even other hunting games, I suppose) might understand better than someone fresh to the genre.
Animals, particularly female deer, are still dumb as walking rocks with the added bonus of sometimes running you over on accident in their zeal to be the first to stand as close to you as possible. Bright side? They don't seem to magnetize toward you anymore - they go where the call was and stick around the immediate area. You're free to sprint like a madman with (seemingly) little consequence. In fact, it seems rewarding by the warning calls provided by animals, alerting you to their rough location. Just crouch and spam your callers. Move toward them for increased efficiency. Animals also seem to be very nonchalant about gunfire, even within ranges where they would probably reasonably hear it. They also seem to not mind returning to the same area where you butchered several herd members already. That said - the hunting pressure system seems to mostly work. Animals outside the group (if there was one) you killed from are very unlikely to enter the area when attracted to calls or scents. They do, on occasion, wander through to get somewhere else, though.
So far, weapons handle reasonably well and have satisfying sounds and animations, though I personally find the kick-up of recoil to sometimes be laughably extreme as an avid hunter in real life. The .243 is not as woefully pathetic as in Classic, and will absolutely do the work you need it to (until you can get the .270. Get it.). However, I recommend polymer tip bullets when available. They are a pleasant step up from the standard soft points, but certainly not a critical upgrade. Bows, however, seem grossly overpowered at the moment. Flesh wounds will have deer bleeding out in times comparable to decent rifle shots.
The interface is a bit cumbersome and lacks information (e.g. current weapon scores outside of the shop, experience until next level, return to main menu button) that I would like to have access to, although this is more of a personal gripe than a point against the game. Most of the nitpicky issues I have with menus and interface are personal beyond being unrefined. The map also has the tendency to find itself focused on anywhere except where you are when opened.
If I sound harsh on this game, it's not because these are glaring faults that should dissuade you from buying. This is a good game for the state it's in, but realize that it does have issues. I can recommend this to veterans of Classic that want a more streamlined and immediate hunting experience without fussing through menus and launchers or simply want to support Avalanche and Expansive Worlds. It's more of theHunter, what can I say? If you're on the fence or new to this series, perhaps stick with Classic until this game is fleshed out more.

Pros: Great engine, excellent & addictive combat, beautifully crafted setting/atmosphere/world, great voice acting, surprisingly good movie related game.
Cons: Not enough story, repetative tasks, lacks variety of content, leaves you wishing there was more depth.
The review:
If you're looking for a wasteland survival simulator, this is not it. This is a Mad Max action game, and there is a LOT of action. Coming into the game I didn't know what to expect, I was impressed with the introduction and noticed it has combined elements from both the original Mad Max movies, and the recently released version. There was Mad Max's famous interceptor from the originals, and character types from the new version. You arrive in the game having your beloved car stolen from you from the villain named 'Scrotus' and you'e left for dead in the barren deserts of this very detailed and desparingly beautiful world. You meet a strange character named 'Chumbucket' who helps you to build a new car and guide you on the path to getting your revenge and interceptor back from Scrotus. This side-kick is one of the most endearing and well acted characters I have ever come across in gaming and I really liked him.
You work your way through various story missions and side-tasks to collect new parts and build up your new vehicle. I found the main story missions to be very engaging and interesting, the side-tasks however, are far too numerous and repetative and I soon got tired of doing them, even if they are an excuse to explore the wonderful wasteland, practice beating up enemies in style and uncovering treasures from a long forgotten world. I was able to get through them because of how interesting this wasteland is, but after 20 hours of playing, it was hard for me to keep doing them. Most of the game is just this, I finished the story line, but it was too short and lacking, the rest of the time I was just grinding through these tasks to get car parts necessary to proceed with the story missions. You're able to continue playing after the story, and there was a lot more exploring to do and tasks/challenges to complete but I had lost the motivation to do so. The game suddenly felt empty and felt like chores. This game needs more content & depth for it to be perfect.
Regardless, the combat wether on foot or in your crazy death machine on wheels is so much fun. On foot the combat style is similar to the Batman Arkham games where you can counter an opponent's attack and follow up with combos, chains moves, special attacks, melee weapons or the best part, entering fury mode where Max turns into a heavy hitting, blood-lusting lunatic. In the vehicle you can customize it for speed, attack, or both and have a variety of weapons or tactics for taking out other vehicles in a furious display of carnage, explosions & metal. My favourite part was using a harpoon gun to rip drivers out of their cars and have their corpses flinging out of their rides. The game may be repetative at times but you will have a damn lot of fun playing it, and I recommend you give it a go, worth the price in my opinion.

Mad Max is a franchise which has a back story but most people really dont go to the movies to listen to a long, in-depth story. They go to watch the movies for the explosions and the hardcore action theme running rampid inside the films core. Mad Max the game doesnt capatalise on the movies story, which is a shame because some of the characters in the most recent movie know more about exploding stuff then Max. They make their own story for Max, which for the most part is full of plot holes and can be summed up with not much of a paragraph: You find a friend, your car has been stolen. You team up with that friend to build your new car. And that is about it. But now onto the actual Review.
Atmosphere
Mad Max might have a lackluster story but they really aim for the Mad Max action feel, you will see parts fly off of car's as you fire heavy rounds from you shotgun at them, you will see fire take hold of an enemies car, and you will see your harpoon glitching inside of a rock because you forgot to disconnect it from the poor blokes body. The car building in this game is AWSOME, you can change everything from the paint to the flamethrowers, this game does a great job of letting you build your ride, from a small buggy with no doors, to a baddass speed tank scouting the desert.
Performance/Port
Now lets talk about the PC Port of this game, the pc port is one of the best that I have seen in a LONG time. It has plenty of features for complete customisation over your settings.It also controls very well on both keyboard/mouse and controller. I really like this part but I shouldnt be surprised as the port was made by the guys who made the Just Cause franchise and as we all know those games set the bar for system ports (until they released JC3 which had HUGE amounts of memory leakage so......maybe they have slipped from their PC port greatness since Mad Max's release). So far I have only encountered a few minor bugs, as I said before bodies glitching inside rocks and stuff of that nature. Nothing game breaking, and as an excenllent note not a single crash!
Combat/Gameplay
The combat in Mad Max can be split in two, Car Combat and On-Foot Combat. The car combat can be a bit daunting at the very start, as the game tries to list off all the different moves right off the bat, which can become quite confusing. However as you proceed to play more of the game you will learn all the moves just by doing side quests and driving around. You will pick it up even earlier if you bother to look at the key mapping. The on-foot combat is not as good because well....its a Mad Max game but is utterly satisfying to say the least, the brawling feels so powerful and controls very well. Using WB's signature system of press a button to counter then press a different button to hit the guy. It is for the most part the same system that they use in games like: Shadow of Mordor, Batman Arkham City and Batman Arkham Knight (Teh Arkham Knight) The game can also do a lot of halarious things like all of a sudden Max will pull off a suplex or a Hell's gate, you cant help yourself but to laugh in amusement as you realise that you didn't need to subscribe to the WWE Network for a great wrestling show, as you alrready owned the best wrestling simulator out there.
Negatives
For everything that I have said so far, the game suffers form one thing, and that would be that Mad Max is very repetative. You will go to camps trying to find a few pieces of scrap (the main currency of the game) and then you will hop in your car and leave to the next camp. It really is a lot of busy work but I think that I have put up with it because I love open world games, atleast 70% of my steam games are open world so perhaps im just used to games like this but if you are just meh when it comes to Open World games then you will start feeling board and thristy for new content right after the first hour or so.You will become quite board with the side quests as well as the main story, because as I said, there isn't much variation with the missions and activities to do. But if you are like me and just like to complete everything no matter what, there is a HUGE wealth of content here and a massive open world which feels like the descelet wasteland that Max romes, ecapecially since you will encounter a wide range of veichle variety when it comes to enemies.
Overall Max can be quite boring if you dont LOVE open world games and the story is just utterly pointless but if you enjoy open world games A LOT I can reccommend this game even if you havnt seen the movies, it's worth it.

Mad Max explores the typical life of an average Australian. Driving around recklessly in a custom made V8, Beating up endless waves of lymphoma patients who are bearly out of their teens, before stealing all their food and drinkable water, in your never ending quest to destory the precious few remaining fuel pumps left on the planet. Befriend a friendly hunchback, who you will treat like utter garbage, before betraying and killing him. Fall in love with the only female in the wasteland, then watch her die due to your own stupity. After playing this game you will finally understand why most people call Australians the naughty fore letter C word, as you yourself will feel bad for what you did in the end to all your friends.

It just feels so smooth and solid. Theirs also a small base development system where you can choose to donate scrap to upgrade it or collect plans and upgrades for the base which is also nice. I enjoyed seeing the base change from a pile of rubble to a nice little settlement or fortified stronghold bursting with life. The enemys are diverse and have different abilities and the whole reduce territory system is fun to do and never gets repetitive. Why? Because each base has different defenses, enemies, layers, and overall buildings. Their all unique and never the same bland base that you typically see in other games. Even the driving combat in this game is fun but a little annoying at times when a random war party randomly crashes into you while you're just chilling.
Character customization isn't that much in-depth except maybe the facial features with the face paint/goggles etc. Skills are pretty handy and decent enough to make you want to get them all. I definitely recommend this game!

In this review I will only review the first episode of LIS BtS, since no other episode is out yet. It will contain as minor spoilers as possible.
Now after I played the first episode of LIS BtS I ended up a bit disappointed in the game and my guts tell me, not to recommend this game. The game presents itself well enough and the LIS-feeling from the first part definitely is there, so why does it feel to fall short?
The reason would be that in comparison to the first game this one just falls short.
- The graphics seem inferior to the first game. Some characters look totally fine (like Chloe), but some models are not consistant. This is especially painful, since Rachel is one of the not-consistant character models, She definitely has some camera angles, where she seems to be a different model completely.
. It still is a pretty game, but it is disappointing, if you feel, that technology has made a step backwards.
- While in the first LIS the power of rewinding created a really interesting game mechanic (which was not exploited enough throughout the game), that gave that game an unique feel to it and was able to advance the plot, that meachanic is really missing in this game. They tried to subsitute it with the "backtalk"-mechanics, but instead of helping the story I feel, it gets in the way of storrytelling. I's a hit- and miss- minigame, where winning the minigame just gets you, what you wanted to archieve, while loosing just leaves you in the same outcome you would have get, if you never tried to backtalk. The worst thing in this minigame is, it is so obvious and not a challange at all to "win" it.
Look for example at the scene in the first LIS, where you meet Frank at his trailer by the shore. That scene was beautifully set up and depending on what you do in and before this scene the outcome of the scene could have been vastly different
.
I was hoping for the second game to do more of those complex choices, but with "backtalk" being a thing I don't see it happening anytime soon.
-The plot is completely linear,
I wanted more scenes like in LIS with Kate, where my relation to her really depends, if I end up in Scene A or Scene B. So far nothing like that can be seen here.
-People are not subtile in this game. The characters reactions and emotions seem to be a bit over the top. It's a bit of a missed opportunity, if reaccuring (or preaccuring?) characters only seem to be an overstated version of the character you already know. People could change over the years, especially teenagers, but you won't see someone act a different way, because events would have happend 3 years earlier.
All in all I still would recommend this game to others. While all those points above are true, it is a little unfair for LIS BtS, since tbh I would not have compared the game with the first episode of LIS, but with the whole first game. If I try only to look at the first episode of the first game, I'd have to adimt, the first episode was no is not the real memorable part of the first game, it's storytelling really gets strong in Episode 2 and 3. The first episode was there to give a setting but not to tell the tale. And LIS BtS does this job, and it does this job well. As I have written above, it has the vibe of a LIS-Game.
*S*P*O*I*L*E*R*

So all in all LIS BtS has its problems but seems to be promising, while also is not expensive, so that even if episode 2 and 3 fail to deliver, I am sure, I won't regret having bought that game.

This game is simply so amazing I can barely begin to describe it, im going to start with the fanbase, even though many people will say the entire community isnt good, they are wrong Some of the community you will definitely want to avoid, however there are legitimately amazing and crazy supportive fans who love this game with a passion and are both supportive of others in the community, Toby himself and other players, Now onto the game. As i have previously said this game is so good that it is hard to describe, but I will try my best. This game Has amazing characters that you will feel as though they are real friends you know, andmanages to create an atmosphere of care, love and positivity, however not all of undertale is lighthearted, there are many choices you must make to make the story move in a direction, however on small choice could forever change your first run of this game, I almost cried many times while playing this game (its very hard to make me cry) and I have heard of many other players crying many times throughout this game. There are many secrets to find and will keep you thinking and theorizing for a while, I will say now though, that this game is best expirienced when you know little to none about this game, I myself watched a playthrough of this game before I was able to play and so I thought "why not i'l never be able to play it anyways". I then realized after a while that I could in fact play Undertale (around the time I got a computer). And I Hated myself for spoiling it for myself. And so I waited longer So I would forget much about what happens in undertale, but not long enough to completely forget about playing it, I played and I still absoluetely loved this game (I still do). Undertale is by far my favourite game and I doubt anything could top it for me. Anyway, The soundtrack is excellently made and Toby Fox did an excellent job in putting the right songs into the right moments. This game also teaches many, many important messages such as, love someone else as though they were you, If you look in the mirror you will find your greatest enemy and your best friend, How you need to stay determined to persevere and get through every obstacle and challenge. and of course, dog humor is good humor. Toby Also does a good job with inserting humor into the right places, at the right times. This game has forever changed me, this game makes me want to love and treat everyone as who they are. The charcters are well designed humorous, comassionate, you feel as though you truly know them as friends, You choose to either help them, or slay them. Stereo-typing isn't necessarily a bad thing, nor is it a good thing. Stereo-typing simply is. It serves as a short hand for the human mind to register information and process situation quickly for the ultimate goal of self-preservation. I have an example.
You’re walking to God-knows-where one day and you see a dog walking towards you. You see a collar, tags, leach and someone walking with it. Based on that information you know that this dog is most likely safe to be around. Hell, you may even pet it on the way by.
Same scenario-you're out and you see a dog walking towards you by itself. You don't see a collar, leach or tags. Now, you might be thinking this dog is possibly dangerous. You may try to promptly plan an alternate route.
I'm sure many of you can come up with your own examples. The problem is stereo-typing, as we recognize it, isn't an accurate technique to completely understand another being. It's also not an accurate way to measure every situation, either. The most common form had been systematically taught and culminates into an unhealthy and broken society. Undertale is a clever RPG that uses video game iconography to touch upon the very serious subject of in-grouping and out-grouping. Stereo-typing can be dangerous when it’s dismissing the value and status of a particular group, thus reducing influence within the in-group and creating unnecessary tension that may explode into violence.
What's your immediate reaction when crossing paths with a monster? Undertale challenges the player to overlook personal, taught biases and see the monsters as complete, complex beings. Undertale challenges the player to empathize with the monsters. As you trek through the Underground you'll gain insight into an actualized society with goals. You'll meet characters that may or may not be bad. You're asked to overlook personal bias and see the monsters as individuals and not representatives of where they're from. If you can extend this much, you'll be met with tenfold. You may even begin to understand the motives behind the actions.
Undertale's morality system feels real. Developer Toby Fox stayed true to his word; there is always another way to resolve conflict. What makes the morality feel real is choice. You're given the option to fight, kill and move on. You could also fight for a little while until the monster gives up. Or you can talk, joke, dance, ignore, pet, encourage, taunt, flex, pose for an audience or prove that you bought a pastry. What makes the choice effective is these options are not always obvious. And that's the best way to play Undertale. I personally recommend playing Undertale for the first time based on your needs moment to moment. Do what you gotta do, man.
So what are you doing? It's ten bucks. It's fun and pretty damn charming. I think you'll like it. It's pretty boring at first, but stick with it. Undertale picks up in a big way. You’ll be introduced to a strong memorable cast. You’ll read some hilarious skeleton related jokes. You’ll spend another ten on the soundtrack no doubt. The gameplay itself plays like any arcade game I know y’all played. And, well, you may be moved, too.

The air was cool, the afternoon sun lit the rows of vibrantly colored homes. We walked a stretch of road through the village on alert for signs of life. Zombies were all we could see, mindlessly shuffling about. Suddenly a man brandishing a large rifle and a woodcutter's  axe appeared.

It was the man from before, now holding an axe high above his head in an attempt to deal a killing blow. I was swift, strafing to the left I proceeded to relentlessly deliver gruesome stabs. EDIT:
TL;DR - Enjoyable, feels like a beta but very pretty with an iffy interface, less of a hunting game and more an animal shooting game. Bows are OP. No microtransactions.
After putting more time into this, I feel I can write a proper and serious review. At the time of writing, this game functions like beta. That said, despite being riddled with bugs and occasional crashes (though your mileage may vary on bugginess) this game is a graphically superb and worthy sibling to theHunter Classic, and I don't regret my purchase. My only major complaint is that they somehow managed to be less realistic in this game than Classic with both the general feel of the game and with animal behaviors - I feel I can describe it best in the way that Diablo 3 is not a dungeon crawler like D2, but a very large loot run. Similarly, you are placed in the vast reserve (and I do mean vast, the maps are colossal) with free reign over a never-ending hunt. It doesn't feel like hunting to me, it feels like animal shooting. Veterans of theHunter Classic (or even other hunting games, I suppose) might understand better than someone fresh to the genre.
Animals, particularly female deer, are still dumb as walking rocks with the added bonus of sometimes running you over on accident in their zeal to be the first to stand as close to you as possible. Bright side? They don't seem to magnetize toward you anymore - they go where the call was and stick around the immediate area. You're free to sprint like a madman with (seemingly) little consequence. In fact, it seems rewarding by the warning calls provided by animals, alerting you to their rough location. Just crouch and spam your callers. Move toward them for increased efficiency. Animals also seem to be very nonchalant about gunfire, even within ranges where they would probably reasonably hear it. They also seem to not mind returning to the same area where you butchered several herd members already. That said - the hunting pressure system seems to mostly work. Animals outside the group (if there was one) you killed from are very unlikely to enter the area when attracted to calls or scents. They do, on occasion, wander through to get somewhere else, though.
So far, weapons handle reasonably well and have satisfying sounds and animations, though I personally find the kick-up of recoil to sometimes be laughably extreme as an avid hunter in real life. The .243 is not as woefully pathetic as in Classic, and will absolutely do the work you need it to (until you can get the .270. Get it.). However, I recommend polymer tip bullets when available. They are a pleasant step up from the standard soft points, but certainly not a critical upgrade. Bows, however, seem grossly overpowered at the moment. Flesh wounds will have deer bleeding out in times comparable to decent rifle shots.
The interface is a bit cumbersome and lacks information (e.g. current weapon scores outside of the shop, experience until next level, return to main menu button) that I would like to have access to, although this is more of a personal gripe than a point against the game. Most of the nitpicky issues I have with menus and interface are personal beyond being unrefined. The map also has the tendency to find itself focused on anywhere except where you are when opened.
If I sound harsh on this game, it's not because these are glaring faults that should dissuade you from buying. This is a good game for the state it's in, but realize that it does have issues. I can recommend this to veterans of Classic that want a more streamlined and immediate hunting experience without fussing through menus and launchers or simply want to support Avalanche and Expansive Worlds. It's more of theHunter, what can I say? If you're on the fence or new to this series, perhaps stick with Classic until this game is fleshed out more.

This game in its current state is an 8/10 from me, and well worth the $30, especially if you think this is your cup of tea even in the slightest. I will list a short number of pros and cons and then talk about what I hope they continue to do with the game.
Pros:
Beautiful Open World Graphics
Massive environments to explore
AAA Graphics and World design at Half the price
Weapons feel powerful and fantastic, nice gap in strength between the later weapons and earlier ones (like the 7mm vs the .243). You will have to worry about shot placement a lot at first.
Excellent sound & lighting effects
Lengthy upgrade grind/cycle, plenty of longevity
Addictive gameplay and rewards upon harvesting animals
Great shop and in-game purchases, NO micro-transaction cash shop
Devs have already been responsive in fixing some bugs and early requests
Cons:
Animals are all based on the same few models, there are no differentiated antlers like TruRACS
No competitive system or real sense of accomplishment from the current scoring system
Trophy rating of animals is not explained well
Time cycle is a little too fast and video-gamey feeling. A quick time cycle in video games is always one of the first things to break the immersion for me. I never understood the rush to see a full 24 hour cycle so quick. Although this game is definitely slower than most... 15 minutes real time is 1 hour in game. TheHunter Classic is half that fast.
The graphics feel a little more like Just Cause than theHunter... they are beautiful don't get me wrong but at times have a "video game" feel to them. I think this is in part because of the TAA blur, which brings me to:
No anti aliasing options. It appears there is a default TAA enabled that works on jaggies but also blurs everything.
There is too much rain and fog, including sunny, midday fog which is impossible in nature.
The weapon animations when walking/running are not displayed well, as you can barely see the gun when you walk in the lower left hand corner. There needs to be an option to hold them as in Classic or as in most first person shooters. Because of this, it hardly feels rewarding when you unlock a good gun (other than the shooting of course) since you can barely even see it when moving. I really, really hope they change this if I am going to continue to support the game. The way it is now is ugly and distracting imo.
There's only two reserves and a handful of weapons so far. The bow is glitchy and is not fun to use for me... which is fine because I've been enjoying the rifles too much.
The water reflections are still buggy and glitchy, and not even on par with Just Cause 3 which is an earlier game using this engine.
Suggestions:
What I really hope to see with this game is first of all fixes or changes for some of the cons listed above, and then I would most of all love to see a modern remake of Whitehart Island. I think a reserve in that deep, lush green forest environment in the new Apex engine would be a sight to behold. In addition with this DLC (and I'm hoping they have a number of reserves planned..) I would love to see the return of some classic rifles from theHunter like the K98K and the .30-06 Bolt Action.
Right now though I am more than happy with the purchase of this game having played it for a long time already, and can easily see myself playing for double this easily while waiting for news and updates about upcoming reserves. Great game, 8/10 so far.

I played a bunch of Rogue Legacy and after a while I found it to be a dumb game. It's great for running aroung the same castle every life over and over again. Sure it's not exactly the same rooms but it *is* the same castle. Same zones, same enemy types.
This game is full of broken features. The manor is nice at first but when you realize that every upgrade that you buy makes every other upgrade more expensive (even the unrelated ones, so prioritize !) so frustrating. This is because getting the next much needed upgrade is exponentially slower with each buy. So you need to rely on luck of good drops to have enough money in one life to afford the next upgrade. If you are missing a dime, tough luck, suck it up because you need to flush all your money before entering the castle by paying death : another feature that makes no sense and looks to be added simply to ramp up replayability.
The concept of ancestors is cool at first. But after your hundred brand new familly member it just gets boring. Looking at the family tree is useless, I couldn't care less that my 50x great ancestor was a barbarian. That feature just offers a reroll with the potential to start again with a new class that you are probably not going to like.
Random challenge rooms are nothing else than frustrating. Good concept but the procedural nature of these rooms means that more often than not you will get a room that requires you to use a spell you don't have. Too bad.
Your character equipment and customization is the only good part, trying to optimize a build is a lot of fun. I especially like assasins with life stealing gear, makes it easier to replenish my hp.
Overall, I would like to like this game. But the more I play it the more I feel like I'm not accomplishing anything. I play a good run only to get one shotted and lose all my gold because I can't afford an upgrade, making this life meaningless. If you like doing the same thing for dozens of hours with little result or it's on sale get this game.

"Military shooters don't often rank high on the narrative front, usually favoring gung-ho G.I. Joe antics and flag waving over character development. And, at first, Spec Ops: The Line falls right in line with that stereotype--you take control of Walker, a soldier sent into a sandstorm-ruined Dubai to find a missing Colonel. But as time goes on it becomes more and more obvious that there's something more devious afoot, and the shooter's story transforms from run-of-the-mill to one-of-a-kind.
What unfolds is a damning criticism of shooters themselves, questioning everything that gamers have grown accustom to. Walker's journey sends him marching into the nucleus of the genre, playing with the storytelling in ways no other game has. By the end you might feel anger or sadness, but the important thing is that you'll feel something, and that's pretty rare in military shooters." I strongly urge you to play this game. This has to be one of the greatest stories every written.

I know that there are already a lot of positive reviews of this game, so I will just note some things that I really enjoyed.
𝗛aving played the original only this week, I would say that the continuity is great, and that this episode doesn't feel like something separate or tacked on. The fact that this game is a prequel (eye roll) and has been developed by a different studio did not affect the quality of the story / gameplay for me at all. The game is just as immersive and I would say touching without being overly sentimental. It took me just over four hours to complete this episode (this seems to be the average time for most) and at no point did I feel that I was playing some sort of filler. It may be only one of three episodes but they have certainly packed a lot in here.
𝗘xperiencing the world from Chloe's perspective is refreshing. Five to ten minutes in and you will have done things (or at least had the option to) that Max would certainly give you a hard time over. Now, instead of Max's optional photographs we have Chloe's optional graffiti, with the marker replacing the camera as a spontaneous form of self-expression (or ahem, vandalism). It is a lot more fun than it may seem, although before playing I did imagine it would involve walking around with a not-so-subtle black gym bag full of spray cans.
𝗟osing the ability to rewind time does not make this game any less fun in my opinion. The backtalk feature that replaces it is a lot more enjoyable than I thought it would be. It definitely feels more 'in the moment' when trying to affect an outcome (time even works against you a little bit) as there is no option to revisit. To me, some of the outcomes do not correlate with Chloe's direct approach and seem to play out as follows:
[awkward pause / narrowing of the eyes]
Okay then! It will be interesting to see how this will feature in future episodes as I found it to be very enjoyable, despite its being cringey / unrealistic at times.
𝗟evel of interaction - To those complaining that these games are a strictly linear affair, I would say that they are overlooking the amount of interaction these games actually allow. Yes, it is possible to just speed through to the end but one can still explore the environment and talk to various characters as well. For people that still have reservations, I would say just try the first episode of Life is Strange™. At the time of posting this review it is available to play for free and so I would certainly recommend checking that out to see whether the style appeals.
Note: One form of interaction I would love to see more of would be something similar to the problem-solving mini games of the original episodes. I really enjoyed establishing the connection between the available pieces of evidence and wanted there to be more to do in that regard. If they incorporated more of those elements (even loosely) in future instalments it would increase the enjoyment for me immensely.
𝗔 final thing I would like to comment on is just how overly critical some have been regarding certain characters' actions. On the surface (ie. without playing the game) it is very easy to label a character's actions as selfish, forgetting that they are not only young but fallible just like everyone else. Playing as the characters, we are able to see the factors (both internal and external) that prompt the actions, and also be reminded that they inhabit a world in which they have very limited control over. Chloe may be immature but she certainly isn't stupid, but when family isn't there for us it is only natural to look to our friends - and it is often the case that our friends are just as f*cked up as we are.
10/10 Would definitely marvel at how square David's head is again.

As only the first episode was released for this game, it should be noted my opinion may change with the release of episodes 2 and 3. I really loved the first game, and honestly, this one is no different. now for anyone who may not know, you played as Max in the first game and you had a time travel mechanic allowing you to redo your actions to progress the story, Max makes friends with Chloe, who is the main character of this game and has no time travel abilities. Many people have voiced concerns that the mechanic used instead in this game is less intresting. In this game you "argue" with people to get you to do what you want, but its basically impossible to lose and there isn't any real puzzle solving like the first game. after finishing the first episode, I agree with that argument, I only used that ability maybe 3 times, where as in the first game you are constantly reversing time. the dialog used in these arguments feel oddly out of place, and the word "Hella" (which was used by characters in the first game) feels forced into conversation as a sort of fan service.
But all of this is not to say this game is bad, or that you shouldn't buy it, I just recommend playing the first game before playing this one. In fact I would argue that you SHOULD buy this game, despite the clunky minigame style game mechanics, the story behind this game sheds light on topics of the first game and  allows the player to see the emotional trauma and pain that plays a factor in Chloe's character during the first game. anyone who plays the first game sees Chloe and how she is dealing with
Chloe clearly is not sad but angry, and this game does a wonderful job of showing the extent of Chloes flawed home life, loss of her father, and the hatred she has for the new boyfriend her mother begins to date. This game is a chance to see what was going on with Chloe that caused her to be the way she is in the first game.

Personal Rating: I love driving my truck!
Classic Rating: ★★★★★
ETS2 is an awesome driving simulator, it's got many different features and they fit very well together.
These are some of ETS2's strong points:
● Good playability, easy handling/steering (I'm using an XBOX 360 Controller, but Steering Wheels are also supported)
● Nice gameplay: you don't just drive; you can run your own company, hire drivers, take a loan if you need money to buy a truck or personalize it - the game offers many (unlockable) items for your trucks. You also advance in your driver's career, adding skills every time you gain enough XP; those upgrades are needed to take longer trips, carry fragile/expensive/dangerous cargos which let you earn money faster.
● You can listen to your favourite music in-game, being it a Streaming Radio or MP3 files.
● ETS2 is highly moddable and there is plenty of Mods: I can suggest "ProMods" for Single Player and "ETS2 Multiplayer Mod" which adds a living layer to the game (only human player are in there).
● You can have your favourite avatar and plate, registering at World of Trucks website (they will also give you a free key for a "Metallic Paint Jobs" DLC).
Some downsides too:
● The AI is not the best, sadly. You'll have to pay a lot of attention when driving near crossings or when switching lanes, because the AI drives faster than you and it doesn't care very much about you; a little delay in your maneuver and some car can easily hit you - and yeah, you're the one being fined - always.
● Mods: they're cool but you should chose wisely and do not draw the longbow. Some game breaking is to be expected, so always save your game before adding a new Mod. Another problem with them is that if you want to remove any, you'll have to reload a previously saved game and all of your gameplay with that Mod will be just gone; so, again, pay attention while modding.
● The game is a little "heavy" on Graphic Cards, but I guess that's to be expected.
I've got this game on sale, no DLCs, but I'm enjoying it so much - recommended.

A really engaging game and I highly recommend it.
The prison you design has to operate within a budget so you have to think about keeping it financially viable. There are decisions to be be made between spending money on meeting the prisoners needs (eg food, hygeine, visitation, sleep, entertainment) and cracking down on bad behaviour, which is a product of not meeting those needs to a certain extent.
There is so much detail in all of the various systems its hard to know what to mention but as an attempt to encompass this without being comprehensive:
There are high- medium- and low-secure prisoners, you can design a different daily regime for each category.
Prisoners are all individual with names, rap sheets and personality problems.
Prisoners can have jobs, either replacing staff you would otherwise have to hire (cooks, cleaners) or generating income for the prison (making liscence plates)
Prisoners will steal stuff from the canteen or their workplace to make weapons or dig tunnels, you can place metal detectors, search cells and route sniffer dog patrols to combat this.
Contraband also flows in through the deliveries to the kitchin and for construction as well as being thrown over the prison walls. You can track the history of items you find and work out where the holes in your security are.
You can operate drug and anger management programs.
Prisoners need to train for jobs and can attend education programmes.
There is a whole snitch system for gaining intelligence on prisoners, snitches can be found out by other prisoners  which tends to end badly for the snitch.
Ultimately its a sandbox experience and you could pretty much set your own objectives but if you care you are also judged on your reoffending rate and the public's perception of whether the indivual prisoner was properly punished during his time in prison - these two factors may be in competition with each other as many of the factors which reduce the reoffending chance are also percieved as not amounting to proper punishment. You are also penalised for deaths in your prison.
I really think the developers have done a great job in capturing the different pressures you might have to consider if you were running a prison. I think they manage to steer clear of trivialising the subject matter but at the same time its not depressingly realistic or overly graphic in its portrayal of violence or drugs.

As an Early access game its perfectly playable, content-rich and bugs are very rare in my experience. There have also been regular meaningful updates.

The gameplay is flawed because of linearity and somewhat clunky controls, but it's still enjoyable to play. Plus the graphics are great, scenery looks amazing and the action is just exhilarating. It's even quite challenging at times because AI, although not the brightest, does give quite a resistance. I must also add, it has some of the most upsetting things happening, this is not for the faint of heart. I heard that this game was controversial for its violence, and I can definitely understand that. It's not just the violence, there's a whole sickening atmosphere in this game that can even make the most atmospheric and creepy horror-games seem silly.

I thought this was the sequel to Max and the Magic Marker: The Curse of Brotherhood.
I figured it would be after the impending nuclear war with Russia, and Max's whole family is dead. It was like the ONE THING he couldn't draw himself out of.
So he's pretty mad about that, but he gets to drive and stuff, because there are no cops left or anything. Just crazy psychopaths who torture people. They're A LOT worse than those purple eggplant monsters. He's gonna need all the orange ink he can find.
But he does! And then he uses his magic marker to rebuild the world into a vibrant and colorful place.
I mean.. No one would make a game where you just drive around in an empty desert, doing the same chores a million different times, right? Well, Ubisoft would definitely make that - they don't really do anything else these days - But this is not they.
TURNS OUT!!!
It's actually a reference to the 1970's trilogy, now quadrology, Mad Max.
Silly me. I should've picked up on that.
Sad thing is, it really has nothing to do with those movies either. Max is a silhouette of a person, with nothing psychological going on**, the vehicle physics are ATROCIOUS, and all you get are boring fourwheels, no trucks and no motorcycles.
You don't even get classic chassis, except for the V8 interceptor, and for whatever reason, even though the game contains different skins, there's no Main Force Patrol paintjob available.
There are also no goofy villains with weird European accents.
There is also no Tina Turner.
I mean what the ♥♥♥♥, Avalanche? Did you seriously not watch the movies before making the game, or are you just deliberately ignoring the stuff that made them cool.
Watch Fury Road. Watch Thunderdome. Watch Road Warrior. Take special care to watch Mad Max, because that is an amazing ♥♥♥♥ing B-movie.
The game has none of the qualities of those movies. It's a truly pointless romp through an open world, that is never half as satisfying as Arkham or Mordor. It's pointless fluff - And that can be fine for a slump, in a sale, but then I don't see why you wouldn't just play Darksiders 2, or do another play of Mordor instead. They're vastly better games.
It is really well engineered, it runs beautifully, storms are super gorgeous, but that really does nothing to tell you why you'd want to knock over 40 completely interchangable camps for no reason. ♥♥♥♥ those camps. ♥♥♥♥ this world. It never tries to be anything to you, or the protagonist.
It's not fun, it's just busywork. There's no story to tie it together, there are no characters except a beat up dog, and he's really only cool because he's a dog. Dogs are awesome. Every game should have dogs.
It's sad, though. They should've gone with my Max and the Magic Marker idea. It would've been a lot better than this.
