Jumping straight in from hours upon hours of arma 2 and a few hours of arma 3, I was immediately knowledgable of most of the controls, if not all of them, that DayZ had to offer. Upon finding myself in a lowpop server, I wasted no time scouting out the local area for weaponry and nessecary survival gear. I found no food or drink, but what I did find however was a good condition sporter rifle with a magazine holding two bullets strewn next to it. In the same building, I also chanced upon a sledgehammer and a coat. Upon attempting to equip the coat, I instead held in my hands and used it as some sort of weapon and when I attempted to drag it onto myself to equip it, it fell onto the floor and was uninterractable. A minor bug, but the game is still in alpha.
By chance I stumped across one of the only other players in the server and after a minute or so of carefully strafing around him with my gun up and countless amounts of "I'm friendly my friend!" from the other player, I lowered my gun. He approached and dropped another bullet for my sporter, which I wasted no time hastily clipping into my magazine.
We agreed to team up and loot the town, and that we did until I heard a scream far too unlike a zombie's. With my sledgehammer raised, I entered the small building I last saw my new friend enter and upon reaching the second floor, I saw it. My friend, laying on the ground in a pool of his own blood, a zombie crouched over him eating his corpse. I approached from behind and swung my sledgehammer with unyielding force, intent on putting down this damnable creature for good - however my blow was not enough and it retaliated with a powerful bite that punctured through flesh like jet fuel through steel beams. I was bitten.
I managed to emerge victorious from the battle but for how long remained a mystery to me. I knew a bite was fatal - there was no saving me. It would not matter how far I ran away from the site of my only friend's untimely death, I would still perish and become one of those abominable mutants. So I crouched next to the friend, aiming my rifle. I put a shot through his head to make sure that he was sleeping blissfully and would not wake to find himself craving the flesh of his neighbors, then I pushed the F11 key upon my chosen device of control and watched as I placed myself onto my knees with the barrel of the gun pushed against me chin.
I clicked.
You are dead.

Prison Architect (PA) is a brilliant village management / logistics game with unique game mechanics and an intuitive user interface. A new patch comes out at the end of each month which is accompanied by a humorous and informative YouTube video. The game feels rather polished at this point, though a few bugs persist and some systems could use expansion.
There is a moderate learning curve, but grants (PA’s quest system) point you in the right direction in the early- to mid-game. You can select the order to attempt them (somewhat) and they don’t ever expire, though you can only have 2 or 3 at a time so it’s wise to plan ahead. The menus are easy to navigate and there are several overlays for displaying different types of information. You can pause and accelerate time freely, allowing contemplative or frantic gameplay as the player wishes.
Prison layouts are quite malleable due to clear visual cues which make it simple to understand where the bottlenecks in your system are and correct them. Entirely redesigning sections of your prison is easy and enjoyable to accomplish. I’m not saying it’s a simple game; on the contrary, setting up a successful & profitable prison which is able to reply to situations automatically is quite difficult and rewarding.
The logistics element is very robust. Many types of things arrive or leave via truck and need to be moved around your prison (e.g. prisoners, food, exports, garbage, laundry, etc.) and streamlining these processes is engaging and fun. However, there are some types of things that workers can pull out of their pockets, which is a minor quip that I hope will eventually change. Once you have several hundred prisoners distributed between the three security types (min, med and max), creating separate regimes so that they can utilize your facilities at different times is an interesting and fun challenge. Simply watching your prisoners and staff go about their daily business is engrossing and highly enjoyable.
I started playing it in Alpha 01 (which was a mess compared to now) and have continued to play on and off since. At 200 hours of play time, it’s literally my favorite game. PA is fun at every phase of play; you are never short of projects to work on, even after the grants run out and you start making your own goals. Fans of city-builders & logistics management will enjoy the detailed interacting systems. Since there are no pre-set building / room structures, PA allows the player to be expressive in their layouts. Creative gamers will enjoy making interesting prisons and publishing them on the Workshop, and a recent patch improved Workshop mod support so it will likely blossom with complexity in the near future.
Subscribe to “Fin Lake Correctional” (find it in the Workshop), to play my highly tuned 500 prisoner multi-security facility.

I'm a fan of Mad Max movies but that was not the reason I bought this game. Positive things: Good graphics, nice atmosphere, 64-bit OS/ DX11+ only (dx9 & 32-bit OS not supported), good enough gameplay (console port but a good port nonetheless), lots of content (considering it is an action and not a RPG game), open world and non-linear for the most part, true to the Mad Max lore/movies, good mix of car and character combat, many cool screenshots.
Negative things: A bit repetitive and/or boring for some people at times like most action games, limited car looks customisation, the occasional bug/graphics glitch but nothing too serious, seems there is only 1 story path/ending, some car parts need a lot of grinding/farming to unlock, maybe a bit easy overall.
Definitely recommended.

I don't think I can add anything that the other reviews haven't pointed out so far. There are TONS of positives to this game. Great retro graphics, fast load times despite the huge castle, challenging difficulty and extremely addictive upgrade/unlock system which'll have you coming back for "just one more" hours on end. There are so many elements to the gameplay system but everything is introduced gradually and it never gets overbearing. Excellent pacing.
On the flipside, some of the music is pretty boring and gets old fast, especially the castle theme. Controls are mostly good but not on par with the Japanese-style pixel precise platforming action you might be used to. For instance pressing the opposite direction + attack might result in a front attack while moving backwards, which is not what you normally want. Jumps are a bit floaty, missing a bit of that good ol' gravity. Some of the "bullet hell" sections (mainly a couple bosses) are downright impossible to get out of without taking heavy damage. Finally don't make the same mistake as I did and play Rogue Legacy at the same time as Shovel Knight because the downthrust is a slightly different button combination and you WILL mix them up.
I've been waiting a long time for a game like this. I'm really hoping the devs have a sequel in the works, with more of the same. I'll be there day one, no questions asked.

I should add, I was banned sometime in December of last year, had no idea why. I get that the game and Battleeye doesn't tolerate cheaters, that would have been acceptable... IF I ♥♥♥♥ING CHEATED! However it was explained to me that Battleeye can ban you for detecting cheating software on your PC, which I had. I had a trainer for Dues Ex Human Revolution on my desktop. That was all.
So to sum up or TL:DR: The game is and always has been in early alpha stages, improvements since SA release in Early alpha isn't noteworthy, you can be banned for having any cheating software on your PC, even if it isn't related to DayZ, it is 2017 and the game isn't where it should be. 4 years in early alpha is NOT acceptable to any standard of gaming. I am now looking forward to Escape from Tarkov where a full game is being developed by a dev team actually capable of finishing a game
Shout out to PUBG as well, I may not be in to this game much but at least it's far superior to DayZ.

I had never played the first Borderlands but after seeing gameplay footage I felt confident in purchasing Borderlands 2 and it was money well spent.  The game itself is a blend of FPS and RPG elements that balance the two together without making the gameplay feel awkward.   As with most RPG systems you steadily increase the level of your Vault Hunter and gain access to talent tree builds that change up the many ways you can approach combat in this game.  The FPS element adds another depth of variety on how you handle encounters with its many ranged weapons. (pistols, shotguns, sniper rifles, sub machine guns, etc)  The system is very good at complimenting the pace and tactics that the player enjoys using.  Charge in shoot everything in the face with a shotgun or perform stealthy sniper headshots from complete safety its up to you.  Harder difficulties after completetion add decent replay value and improved weapons and loot for those that want more along with extra DLC classes and content.  Pros - Fluid and smooth controls, plenty of player choice, multiplayer with friends, and memorable characters (TINY TINA!!!) and probably one of the best lead villians I have seen in a game in a long time.  CONS-  Can feel repetitive on consecutive playthroughs, a good friend of mine completed the first Borderlands and found it to be much of the same and similar individuals will probably not enjoy it as much as I did since it was my first introduction to the series.   8.5-9/10  Gameplay this smooth is always a plus even if it closely mirrors its origins.

As only the first episode was released for this game, it should be noted my opinion may change with the release of episodes 2 and 3. I really loved the first game, and honestly, this one is no different. now for anyone who may not know, you played as Max in the first game and you had a time travel mechanic allowing you to redo your actions to progress the story, Max makes friends with Chloe, who is the main character of this game and has no time travel abilities. Many people have voiced concerns that the mechanic used instead in this game is less intresting. In this game you "argue" with people to get you to do what you want, but its basically impossible to lose and there isn't any real puzzle solving like the first game. after finishing the first episode, I agree with that argument, I only used that ability maybe 3 times, where as in the first game you are constantly reversing time. the dialog used in these arguments feel oddly out of place, and the word "Hella" (which was used by characters in the first game) feels forced into conversation as a sort of fan service.
But all of this is not to say this game is bad, or that you shouldn't buy it, I just recommend playing the first game before playing this one. In fact I would argue that you SHOULD buy this game, despite the clunky minigame style game mechanics, the story behind this game sheds light on topics of the first game and  allows the player to see the emotional trauma and pain that plays a factor in Chloe's character during the first game. anyone who plays the first game sees Chloe and how she is dealing with
Chloe clearly is not sad but angry, and this game does a wonderful job of showing the extent of Chloes flawed home life, loss of her father, and the hatred she has for the new boyfriend her mother begins to date. This game is a chance to see what was going on with Chloe that caused her to be the way she is in the first game.
tldr:
-poorly implemented game mechanic
-sometimes awkard dialog
+great voice acting
+wonderful sound track
+allows Player to get some more backround on the first game
+beutiful art style, lots of screenshot worthy scenes

I loved the first Life is Strange game, it's one of my favorite games I've ever played. Mostly because of the relatable characters. the art style, amazing soundtrack and the fact that the people behind the games have taken a big risk by making games about high school girls, even tho those type of games are rarely popular.
It's shame to see people hating the game because of they know what is going to happen to Rachel after all this, but guess what, people die, after every story (Unless it's a story about immortal people or something, I dunno.) I wanna know how that happens in Rachel's case and I wanna know more about her as a character and how she changed Chloe as a person so much. It's not important what's going to happen in the end, the journey how we get there is more important.
Also people who are hating the game, because they hate Chloe as a character. (I don't understand you, but it's okay.) Personally Chloe is a really important character for me, she has tons of flaws for sure, but that's what makes her interesting, more interesting protagonist that Max ever was, even when Max had her time traveling powers. Max's only flaw was basically that she was a shy girl, she didn't have any childhood trauma, she had basically nothing about her to make her interesting in any way. Just like every other Tv-Serie/Movie/Anime protagonist, but that makes her relatable for many people, which makes it okay. But I think it's a good change to get a character with more depth than that for once.
Also people who think Chloe doesn't have big ol' crush on Rachel, what are you even doing here. I think it's ridiculous how after all the billion times that Chloe talked about Rachel in the first game all "You're putting it mildly" when Max said that "[Rachel] was obviously a good friend." Some of you still manage to think they are just some good pair of gal pals.
...Whatever floats your boat, I guess.
If you hate the cringey voice lines... well... I'm not going to say anything. Except for me it really makes the game and makes the game little bit less serious tbh.
But yeah, I'm going to approve this game for now. The first episode was great, I love the new facial animations and lip synch is much better than in the first game. Cons ---

- Admins. Admins really do nothing in this game. If you report a scripter to an admin for using a no recoil script he's most likely using it as well.
Only get this game if the community of a multiplayer survival game does not effect you in any way.

I haven't been this pleased with a game in months.  Rogue Legacy is an instant hit. My love-hate relationship with Roguelikes being as it is (I love them, they hate me) is tempered a bit with this being a Roguelike-"lite". It's more like a Metroidvania that thinks it's a Roguelike.
I still die a whole lot either way. I even die during the final battle as my video confesses to. I suffered 186 deaths over 40 hours which averages to 4.65 deaths an hour.  After so many heirs had died, overall it was persistence, dedication, and a whole lot of self loathing that helped me beat Johannes with Sir Taco V, a stereo blind hokage, son of Sir Cellar, a spelunker with ADHD who in turn was the son of Lady Antoinette the VIII, a useless paladin with flatulence and the propensity to swear a lot, and so forth and so on unto creation with the original heir, who as we learn from the game, is Johannes the legendary, a man with quite the lineage and a very interesting gene pool.
Honestly, by the time I reached the boss, my family line had so many issues from colorblindness, to dwarfism, cataracts and endomorphism that I was lucky to beat ol' pappy the 1st.
The game's genetic traits are a fun and enjoyable twist. Eventually you will whittle it down to a few classes and traits that you are most comfortable with and getting anything other than your set few will probably disappoint you, like getting stuck with three Dragons, re-rolling and getting stuck with three more. (It actually happened to me.)
Graphics, sound, and gameplay are all top notch. The developer, Cellar Door Games, knew what they were doing here as the graphics are colorful in all their HD pixel glory. What more could you ask for from a platformer? Control and handling are very good but not perfect. I found myself, especially during the Neo boss fights, hollering at the screen to turn around while I was attacking and would end up walking backwards into disaster. Unless your character had the rare trait of being flexible, this extra quarter second of attack speed precision was missing. As any hardcore platform gamer can tell you, controls are everything. Music was pretty standard, every song was good, but only two really stood out to me, the Ponce fight and the ending theme. You will not be turning the sound down to run your own music over it with this one.
This is a must-play title for anyone who is a fan of Metroidvania platforming or Roguelikes. Buy it to kill a weekend and giggle as your descendants are left with the genetic blessing of flatulence.

I loved Life is Strange (LiS) and eagerly awaited the prequel from the moment I heard about it. I went ahead and bought the deluxe edition a few hours after its release on 31st August.
First impressions are good, in that despite the new developers, the game definitely has the same feel as the original and I was instantly transported back to Arcadia Bay. The artwork remains true to its predecessor and Edouard Caplain’s impressionistic style can still be seen shining through in Before the Storm. There are some really nice arty long shots during the cut scenes but these were overused and unfortunately started to feel gratuitous and even a bit dull.
The soundtrack could easily be an extension of what we heard in LiS, with an indie, slightly melancholy vibe and an effective mix of diegetic and non-diegetic music. The main addition here is a few heavier tracks that fit well with Chloe’s character and the scenes they are in.
I found Chloe a little on the irritating side during the first game but could see her character’s development and it fitted. In Before the Storm, you play as a younger Chloe, who manages to outdo herself in the teenage angst department. I understand that grief can be ugly, and that her story so far is certainly sad but it wasn’t an emotional Chloe that annoyed me, rather the nonchalant bravado act that she puts on the rest of the time. It felt overdone and at times she seemed nothing more than the same try hard, pseudo-b!tch, cliché that we have all seen a million times before. It was actually in her more vulnerable moments that her character is portrayed best and I can see how Chloe might grow from this into the version we see in LiS but the balance of emotions was achieved much more effectively with Rachel Ambers’ character whose anguish felt believable.
The game ran smoothly, even on my sad, old trusty PC, but I didn’t get achievements for graffiti that I know I did, sometimes twice so wonder if this is a bit buggy? I miss the time mechanic from the first game but did not expect this to be a feature. In BtS this is replaced with back chat, which was fun at times but felt lacking as a substitute and was a little cheesy at times.
The story starts slow, introducing and reintroducing characters and taking you to some familiar settings but tension does start to build towards to end of the episode. Despite my complaints I did enjoy the experience and am intrigued to see what happens I just don’t think the game lives up to its predecessor . . . yet. This is my first ever review, and my own views.
Even though this game is in it's Alpha stage, and  It's been out in alpha for more than a year, It feels and looks like it's at the beta stage, If I'm honest it could be confused as the finished project. There are a few things little things that need adding but they could be released as DLC. At around 110ish MB, it's not noticeable on your tb hardrive.
Prison Architect is such a good game, it can be played by both casual and hardcore gamers. There mod's out for it or could create your own, all of which increase the life time of the game. I brought the game, and have myself kinda in the game. You start the game off with limited money (you can get grant's to create different things) you have to design and build your own prision. (It's in the name) .But It's not as easy as that, there are challenges of planning a prison enviroment. Not to mention the everyday running of a prison too.(Riot's etc) but the user choices do matter. It's managment, strategy and simulation all rolled into one fun game.
My advice to you, don't take my word for it. Try it yourself, I mean you may or may not like the game. Just because I like it doesn't mean you will or won't. But once you get past the learning curve, it will keep you entertained.

NOTE: THIS GAME IS STILL IN ALPHA, AND THIS REVIEW IS WRITTEN AT THE TIME OF ALPHA 24
Prison Architect is one of those rare games, in that it's a proper simulation game (in the veins of Theme Hospital). There are so many features and so many ways to go about things in the game.
You are given an influx of around 8 prisoners each and every day (which can be altered by an option, also you can set the type of prisoner you get to Max, Medium, Low, or a mixture of the three, or even all) who you have to give a home to while they live out their sentence.
Do you want to crowd every prisoner you have into one giant holding cell, patrolled around the clock by guards? You can do that.
Do you want each and every prisoner to have their own cell with comforts for those who behave? You can.
Do you want to be a tyrant and lock everyone in Solitary? There's that option too.
Do you want to have an educational prison where every inmate who wishes to, can work on programs to help the prison maintain its working standards? You get that choice as well.
There is a very steep learning curve though, at this time the tutorial is basically a prologue which allows you to do some basic things, but doesn't give much information on the finer points of the game.
Also, you have to watch that contraband, I've had more than one game where I've had to create a new prison because someone went on a murder spree with a stolen spoon, or where a prisoner let everyone in the prison free by killing a guard with a fork and stealing his keys.
Micro-management is a must here, as you need to ensure everything is right otherwise you could end up with a riot on your hands, though, thankfully, there IS the option to turn off failure conditions if you are trying the game out, so you don't lose the game for having too many riots.
There are always the back up plans in case of emergency, Riot Police, Fire department etc, though in some games this is not an issue, depending on the type of prisoners you let in (Maximum Security prisoners need the most watching, Minumum of course, don't)
And what do you do when you feel bored or finished? You can sell your prison and create another, maybe try a different layout for the prison, or try using different rooms (You can set up programs to educate the prisoners and such)
TL:DR If you were a fan of Theme Hospital and similar games, or just want to try to create a hellhole for prisoners (allowing for knife-fights, guard murders etc), this is an awesome game, which is updated at least once a month, and the £20 price sticker is well worth all the hours of fun you can have. There are some bugs, but more often than not, these are dealt with quickly by the developers, which makes it all the more worth the price.

before reviewing the game, I would like to state that I'm a huge fan of Mad Max series and the post-apocalpytic genre, in books, movies and video games. I bought this blindly based on the fact that it was a Mad Max game and done by the same people who did the Batman Arkham series who I'm also a huge fan of, so continuting on the review, I would like to state the good and the bad of this game, because this game at best, was 50/50 for me.
The story itself is pretty standard for a Mad Max storyline, I'm not sure if this is in any way related to the recent Fury Road movie but it felt like a prequel mainly because the main baddie of the story is one of the sons of Immortal Joe(At least I think he is), and familiar locations are stated in the game as they are in the movie, this could also be very well a totally standalone story with similar parts and not be related to the movie. The storyline itself won't take you as much as a day to get thru if you have the time but there is plenty to do in the massive world to keep you busy.
Exploration in this game for me was the best part, alot of sights to see and roads that lean you to epic settlements across the wasteland, a major point in this game was to raid enemy settlements and disrupt their terrority control, most of your time spent on this game will be sololy on that, but is not really needed to complete the game. The game even has a capturing feature that allows you to get epic shoots of you and the vastness of the wasteland. You'll find shady chracters as you explore that will give you tips on how to raid the bigger enemy settlements and finding hidden loot.
Car customization has a pretty linear build path, you have the ability to build a massive tank(not literally) or a speed machine, but again not alot of options, at the end game, you'll probably have the same car as everyone else. you'll have to collect "scraps" to build upgrades for your car and yourself, you can collect "scraps" by killing enemies and their vehicles or exploring settlements and finding/raiding their loot, pretty much the currency of the game.
Certain settlements are known as "Top Dog" settlements which can be find across the wasteland, includes a boss, which personally was the most disappointing part of the game for me, these "Top Dog" are overally size freaks of nature who look similar to the Lord Humungus in a way but alot of them were pretty much the same model and were retexture to the style of the camp you were raiding, and they all had the exact same weakness and in no way were hard to take down, felt like alot of greatness that Mad Max brought into the real world was its amazing character designs, a total hit and miss for this part of the game.
You'll find side missions and very minor missions across the wasteland, these were pretty similar to the style of Skyrim were you would go to point A and kill said amount of people and/or collect said amount of stuff and were extremely stale after a couple of minutes of doing them, the only good side I found of this was finding the cool sights of the wasteland. You'll also find "Death Races" where you would go to point A to point B  in a certain amount of time and racing NPCS, who you could actually kill to win a race, you'll actually could win awesome rides doing this, I personally didn't dig too deep into this part of the mini-game due to the fact that I have no fun playing racing games.
The combat was also very disappointing as well, it was pretty much a copy and paste version of the Batman Arkham series, now I'm a fan of that game, but felt like that was its best part of it, and to copy and paste it on a different game, was very lazy. The combat also didn't feel as fluid as they were in the Arkham series, it felt extremely similar to Asylum were the controls wouldn't respone in time for you to react, this was fixed in Arkham City which had such a much smoothier combat feel to it. you'll have Max's signature double barrel shotgun but the controls for it was very lackluster and felt frustrating at times to aim with.
Do I recommend this game? Yes, I do especially if you are a Mad Max fan, but would also recommend you wait for it to go on sale, probably in next year time.

Yes... this game:
But you know what? Even after playing just the first episode, I already know Deck 9 has surpassed everyones expectations on this game.
Deck 9 did a stunning job on bringing back the original setting of Arcadia Bay, making it feel almost nostalgic to see. The story Deck 9 wrote for this makes you wonder how much influence DONTNOD had on this prequel. Aside from sometimes the cringey teenager stuff people say, the story is just as intense and fluffy as the first game.
Yes, many voice actors could not return to play their parts in the game due to a union strike, but Deck 9 did an amazing job on finding great subs for a majority of characters. The only ones that bug me is Frank and David, but they are not too bad. Rhianna DeVries did super well for voicing a young Chloe, Ashly Bursh even reappeared to help with the story and help Rhianna with Chloe's personality.
Bringing the unknown character of Life is Strange, Rachel Amber, into a game was probably the toughest thing for Deck 9. There was a lot of room for Deck 9 to experiment to bring Rachel's story to us, and the took an interesting and fluffy way of doing it. Even the toughest "pricefield" fans will rethink that relationship and actually see who Chloe Price and Rachel Amber was when they were together.
Not only this, but Before the Storm completely made me change my view on the ending of Life is Strange.
BtS made me totally rethink the way I played the original game, which says a lot.
Seriously, it is 100% worth it. Deck 9 did a wonderful job with the first episode and I have nothing but excitement for rest of Before the Storm!

Advantages:

Disadvantages:

-if you want to play an extra episode after the first 3 are released, you must pay an extra 9.19 euros, which makes 4 episodes to cost around 25 euros
If you can get past the price-point (my main and only problem with this game), LiS: Before the Storm is a worth to play game.

This is my first ever review, and my own views.
Even though this game is in it's Alpha stage, and  It's been out in alpha for more than a year, It feels and looks like it's at the beta stage, If I'm honest it could be confused as the finished project. There are a few things little things that need adding but they could be released as DLC. At around 110ish MB, it's not noticeable on your tb hardrive.
Prison Architect is such a good game, it can be played by both casual and hardcore gamers. There mod's out for it or could create your own, all of which increase the life time of the game. I brought the game, and have myself kinda in the game. You start the game off with limited money (you can get grant's to create different things) you have to design and build your own prision. (It's in the name) .But It's not as easy as that, there are challenges of planning a prison enviroment. Not to mention the everyday running of a prison too.(Riot's etc) but the user choices do matter. It's managment, strategy and simulation all rolled into one fun game.
My advice to you, don't take my word for it. Try it yourself, I mean you may or may not like the game. Just because I like it doesn't mean you will or won't. But once you get past the learning curve, it will keep you entertained.

NOTE: THIS GAME IS STILL IN ALPHA, AND THIS REVIEW IS WRITTEN AT THE TIME OF ALPHA 24
Prison Architect is one of those rare games, in that it's a proper simulation game (in the veins of Theme Hospital). There are so many features and so many ways to go about things in the game.
You are given an influx of around 8 prisoners each and every day (which can be altered by an option, also you can set the type of prisoner you get to Max, Medium, Low, or a mixture of the three, or even all) who you have to give a home to while they live out their sentence.
Do you want to crowd every prisoner you have into one giant holding cell, patrolled around the clock by guards? You can do that.
Do you want each and every prisoner to have their own cell with comforts for those who behave? You can.
Do you want to be a tyrant and lock everyone in Solitary? There's that option too.
Do you want to have an educational prison where every inmate who wishes to, can work on programs to help the prison maintain its working standards? You get that choice as well.
There is a very steep learning curve though, at this time the tutorial is basically a prologue which allows you to do some basic things, but doesn't give much information on the finer points of the game.
Also, you have to watch that contraband, I've had more than one game where I've had to create a new prison because someone went on a murder spree with a stolen spoon, or where a prisoner let everyone in the prison free by killing a guard with a fork and stealing his keys.
Micro-management is a must here, as you need to ensure everything is right otherwise you could end up with a riot on your hands, though, thankfully, there IS the option to turn off failure conditions if you are trying the game out, so you don't lose the game for having too many riots.
There are always the back up plans in case of emergency, Riot Police, Fire department etc, though in some games this is not an issue, depending on the type of prisoners you let in (Maximum Security prisoners need the most watching, Minumum of course, don't)
And what do you do when you feel bored or finished? You can sell your prison and create another, maybe try a different layout for the prison, or try using different rooms (You can set up programs to educate the prisoners and such)
TL:DR If you were a fan of Theme Hospital and similar games, or just want to try to create a hellhole for prisoners (allowing for knife-fights, guard murders etc), this is an awesome game, which is updated at least once a month, and the £20 price sticker is well worth all the hours of fun you can have. There are some bugs, but more often than not, these are dealt with quickly by the developers, which makes it all the more worth the price.

A 3PS cover based shooter.  Lets break it down into two parts.
The gameplay.  Fairly non-interesting.  Ally and enemy AI is absurdly stupid a lot of the time.  The same button controls sprint / take cover / break cover, leading to control frustration.   Gunplay is acceptable and fairly non-clunky, with a fairly diverse selection.  Nothing is especially spectacular about it either, but as long as it works that's fine.  Environments are fairly decorated and detailed, and progresses well without too much staleness, but your environs mostly consist of sand dunes and upscale hotels.
The story and setting.  This game has been praised a lot for its deep moral dilemmas, but I didn't really find them very problematic, but that's probably because the game forces certain scenarios in how people behave or talk.  I didn't really feel like I was the one making any moral choices, just chosing from which script the actor would follow.  This is a pretty significant distinction.  The game would direct me to choose how to act but the approach to the scenario is forced.  Its like saying 'You're Hitler, you just killed a jewish woman's husband, do you spare the wife or kill her when she attacks you with a knife?'  A silly example, but I didn't get to chose whether or not I was Hitler, or if I would have shot the husband.  Same sort of thing here.   The game would similarly try to make me feel like a decision was tough or the 'good' outcome difficult to determing when to me it was not.  Maybe this is because I have a degree in philosophy and studied ethics as part of my coursework, and can approach these situations in a videogame a little more analytically than most can (esp. with time pressure).
So all in all, this videogame is probably not for me.  Less than interesting combat for someone not greatly enamoured of the genre, and a story made for someone of a less studied background.  Plenty of reviews praise it so while I can't say I took much enjoyment out of it, it's probably something other people will enjoy for those reasons I could not.

I love this game, but I must admit it took me a while to come around to it. I had the game on Xbox360, and for whatever reason, I didn't like it. So I never really played it, until I got onto PC gaming. Even then, it had sat for a year in my library without getting played. I am pretty much only on Linux these days, so I have relatively slim pickings in terms of AAA games in my library, and this was literally the last one that I didn't beat, so I finally revisited it a month or so ago. 100 hours of play time later, I think it is in the pantheon of 'favorite games ever'.
For me, in terms of my personal playing experience, Borderlands 2 has been akin to a hybridization of three of my favorite games of all time: Dark Souls, Red Dead Redemption, and the original NES Legend of Zelda. That may sound a bit strange, but I'll give a bit of an explanation. Dark Souls is a game with deep leveling, varied combat, and it exists in an enchanting displaced purgatory world of heathens, with just enough of a glimpse of a backstory to be intriguing on a cult-like level; same with BL2. Red Dead Redemption has a quality where you can just get lost and marvel at the bleak-yet-captivating landscapes, and it is not a product of graphical fidelity, it is the result of artfully inspired design; BL2, same. And with Zelda, grinding for loot never gets old, despite the very predictable nature of the AI combat, because at the heart of the game Zelda is all about drops and loot; BL2 is the same.
Other great things: drop-in/drop-out co-op. multiplayer, rad DLC, rad skins and customizations, rewards, multi-character reciprocities, and especially the ability to trade loot with other players or friends in-game.
Legit 10 / 10

Spec Ops really is as good as people say it is.  I'm extremely surprised that 2K didn't promote it more, it just popped out of nowhere without much of an explanation.
The game is a third-person cover shooter, which I thought was an odd choice given the type of game it is.  That said, it actually works very well.  While I'm not a particular fan of cover shooters, I actually enjoyed it here.  There's a decent variety of military weapons to work with along with several grenades including a sticky grenade which I'm pretty sure isn't real so I'm not sure why they included it.  It's fun to use though.
Graphics are decent, nothing special.  It was designed as a console game with no special PC features so I was able to get a constant 60 FPS on a GTX 260 at max settings.
The real strength of this game is the story.  It is extremely well written, perhaps one of the best written games I have ever played.  No other military shooter comes even close.  I'm not going to give any spoilers, but it really draws you in and makes you feel part of the story.  It is a lesson to the Call of Dutys and Battlefields how a single player experience should be.
There are a few tweaks you should use to fully enjoy the game.  If you want to use keyboard+mouse like I did, you will need to visit the game forum and download an INI decrypter so you can disable the mouse acceleration (it's REALLY bad.)  Flawless Widescreen also has support for this game so you can increase the FOV.  Once you do that, the game handles very well, though the combo controls can be annoying.
Pick up this game when you can, you won't regret it.

Mad Max is that comfortable old shoe that has its soles coming loose. The friend that over stays their welcome. The game that rehashes what other games already did and uses virtually the same engine while doing it.
By all rights and standards Mad Max is a AAA game. It looks fantastic, plays fantastic (scales very well on PC to boot) and it has very solid design behind it. Yet, here it stands with middling sales and reception. The reason? It's too familiar and does nothing new while at the same time squandering its potential to be different.
Mad Max is an open world game that borrows heavily, often too heavily,  from other WB published titles. It uses the same, too familiar now Arkham combat engine. The same sandbox formula that now countless other games used, (run and gun and collect crap all over the map) and the same and tired narrative that all AAA games use these days.
From the start of the game you're made to feel or assume that this game will give you resources sparingly. A dog is about to get eaten alive, water comes from a dirty dish on the ground, a hunchback sits in front of you all mangled and scarred. Everything has a rusty, windblown look and truly, this is a desolate, barren world. It seems you're being set up for yet another survival-like game, but one that might be still worth playing.
But then you play and all of the sudden, no, water doesn't matter as an independent mechanic- it just heals you just like a health pack and you can carry it and thus use it on demand. Food, which also heals you but only where you locate it, is plentiful as long as you're willing to eat maggots from corpses and cans of dog food. Gasoline, a major tenet of this game and movie, is laughably plentiful and cars barely use it so you almost don't have to refill anyway outside of mission related goals, and you can fast travel anyway. (often a sign of an unnecessary, overly large map) Gathering bullets and shivs are trivial once you complete your first set of side missions. Not to mention that every base you raid has all of these resources. Guaranteed and often more than once. Every resource can be automatically filled once at a stronghold once you collect enough project pieces which lay about the "barren" landscape - which are all too easy to collect. So, no matter what you do, even if you ignore the stronghold resource regenerators, resources are plentiful and easily accessible. Though, yes, regardless, you won't be able to shoot every enemy with your shotgun at most places.
So, what is set up to be a survival-like spin on this familiar genre is just another boring, unimaginative and poorly thought out resource system that gets defeated in the first couple hours of the game if you so choose.
You can upgrade your car, but it also becomes OP far too soon and the upgrades are still rather trivial. The world map is huge but not very fun. Go to various points to raid a stronghold, blow up fuel storage tanks or oil pumps (makes sense in a supposedly resource deprived world) collect scrap, tear down towers, take out snipers, do a race here and there and rinse and repeat in between boring story missions.
The character Max in this game is your typical macho but deep down sensitive white protagonist savior. Even referred to as "The Saint". You know what his story is even before he does. You have your standard sidekicks and story motivators/characters. Basically, everything in this game is so formulaic that unless you're brand new to the genre you've already played it at some point. And even then this game has weird design choices such as sharing the controller Button A to pick up junk and as a finishing move in combat. So it's rather "fun" when you kill an enemy that drops something and then another enemy falls on that item and when you press A to finish him, you try to loot a corpse which leaves you open to attack. Really smart, there. This also leads me to the terribly stupid AI that just bum rushes you but outside of one instance, you can counter them with ease. The combat itself is also rather unrefined and you can't have much fun with it. Just spam Y, X, X, X, X, A and each opponent is dead. If you so choose, you can hold the final X or hold all X's for stronger hits. But you can't combo off multiple opponents or use them against each other. It's a timed button masher, essentially.
Of course, notwithstanding wasted potential, stupid design decisions and formulaic AAA gameplay, Mad Max IS a great game. Especially if you love the themes and movie. (Though it really doesn't add anything to the movie, and you don't need to have seen the movie to appreciate the game) Mad Max just has the unfortunate situation of being much of the same after some very good, genre defining games. So, it's tired and boring to those that are familiar with the genre or aren't sold on the Australian outback theme. One can only hope that with all the shared mechanics (even the menu seems like a direct copy of Shadow of Mordor's) that this game was produced with a very efficient budget to warrant such a tame and familiar game.
Still, if you want more of the same - which isn't an outright bad thing with checked expectations, or if you're new to the genre; Mad Max is a great game that, if it had came first, would have been a GOTY contender.

This is my favourite game and one of the best simulators out there. Fantastic graphics and scenery, lots of places to travel and a wide variety of jobs. A good number of different trucks to choose from too. There is also a logistics element as you manage employees, assigning them to different garages, training them up and so on. This game will not only keep your driving skills sharp, but will also improve your European geography knowledge as you become familiar with the different countries and the locations of major cities in them, as well as specific highways leading to them.
Another thing I really like about this game is the extent to which the developers communicate with users via the SCS Software Blog. They work constantly on the game and provide regular updates. The upcoming Scandanavia DLC looks set to add an exciting new dimension to an already excellent game, with many new road types, job types, more detailed cities and so on. Can't wait!
Of course, no game is perfect, and there are a few minor annoyances with ETS 2. While the performance is generally excellent, sometimes I experience "mini-freezes" where all the action just stops for a couple of seconds before continuing. Another thing I find rather irritating is that it seems to take forever to train employees. You can get your own rating up to 10.0 in next to no time, but I have not yet managed to get a single employee to the top level. My other main complaint is that the AI behaves quite stupidly at times, like pulling out in front of you at a T-junction even when you have the right-of-way, or stopping dead in the middle lane of a German autobahn, or turning in front of you at traffic lights when you have a green light and are going straight ahead. I think the AI has been improved since the game was first launched, but there is more room for improvement yet. One last problem is that some rest stops are not displayed on maps, especially parking lot-type stops in Eastern Europe.
When you first start to play the game, there are a few "traps for young players". Be careful when making a tight turn, or your trailer will get stuck and you'll have a dickens of a job getting it free. Also, if you leave it too long before sleeping, you will "doze" and this will result in disastrous loss of control! I have found it is a good idea to check the map when the "yawning" starts to check for the nearest rest stop. In fact, it's a good idea to look even before your driver starts tiring, because sometimes there are very large gaps between stops, especially in Germany.
But all in all, this is a brilliant game that will give you many enjoyable hours of virtual driving, and with the developer support provided, it is about to get even better still!

Deck Nine did a hella good job.
But seriously I was skeptical coming into this game, with another studio handling Chloe and Rachel Amber, a character that was very interesting because she was so mysterious. They exceeded my expectations and kept the vague nature of Rachel's intentions and feelings as well as showing the damaged emotional state of Chloe very well.
Music is fantastic, and shows an interesting parallel to the calmer more nostalgic music of the first game.
The romantic relationship between Chloe and Rachel is beautiful, and as a result bittersweet. I'd recommend this game to anyone.

After playing the first Life Is Strange, the whole story really "hit home" for me knowing how much of a friendship Max and Chloe had and what we can do in the real world to now with Before the Storm where we dip into Chloe and Rachel's story. Putting in the first 4 hours (that's just episode 1), it makes me want to know more. The LIS games really are a life changer. Going to miss Chloe and Max after the prequel...
As for how the game has done so far, it runs very smooth on my computer. Always locked down at 60 frames (highest you can get). The new backtalk feature I'm still getting used to; but, it's great to see there is sort of a memory challenge. Get this game and the first LIS game, you won't regret it.

If you enjoyed Season 1, you'll probably enjoy the prequel. Chloe unfortunately isn't as interesting of a main character as she is a side character, but I still enjoyed her character arc for the most part. There are plenty of plot holes and rushed storylines, and the writing isn't as engaging as the first season. The Backtalk mechanic is nowhere near as interesting as Rewind, and it just felt like the game was missing that extra layer of intrigue besides the vanilla story. But hell, when it comes to atmosphere, music, worldbuilding, and emotional buildup, DeckNine nailed it. I couldn't believe it when I found out they built Arcadia Bay from scratch on a DIFFERENT GAME ENGINE and recreated the world I loved the first time. Bravo. A modest recommendation from me if you're a fan of the series.

Take notes, Telltale:
THIS (and the original Life is Strange) is what a game where "Choices Matter" should be like.
Every bit as mesmerizing, intriguing, and heartwrenching as the first game. Only downside is that this game doesn't have Max, or the ability to manipulate time.
Still, in this game, you have something just as useful and far more practical than the ability to time travel: witticims and snappy comebacks!
Just completed Chapter 1. Cannot wait for the other two chapters to come out.
Note: Purchased deluxe Pre-Order Edition.

I had never played the first Borderlands but after seeing gameplay footage I felt confident in purchasing Borderlands 2 and it was money well spent.  The game itself is a blend of FPS and RPG elements that balance the two together without making the gameplay feel awkward.   As with most RPG systems you steadily increase the level of your Vault Hunter and gain access to talent tree builds that change up the many ways you can approach combat in this game.  The FPS element adds another depth of variety on how you handle encounters with its many ranged weapons. (pistols, shotguns, sniper rifles, sub machine guns, etc)  The system is very good at complimenting the pace and tactics that the player enjoys using.  Charge in shoot everything in the face with a shotgun or perform stealthy sniper headshots from complete safety its up to you.  Harder difficulties after completetion add decent replay value and improved weapons and loot for those that want more along with extra DLC classes and content.  Pros - Fluid and smooth controls, plenty of player choice, multiplayer with friends, and memorable characters (TINY TINA!!!) and probably one of the best lead villians I have seen in a game in a long time.  CONS-  Can feel repetitive on consecutive playthroughs, a good friend of mine completed the first Borderlands and found it to be much of the same and similar individuals will probably not enjoy it as much as I did since it was my first introduction to the series.   8.5-9/10  Gameplay this smooth is always a plus even if it closely mirrors its origins.

The story, however, is what sets Spec Ops: The Line apart from all other shooters and lifts it to an entirely new level. I've been playing this since Alpha 12 and have watched it become more complex with each update.
While playing a standard game is still harder than it needs to be with the prices of objects versus the amount of money you can make in a day before any of the prisioners get through the class needed for them to work for you in the workshop, playing with a unlimited money map downloaded from the Steam Workshop is a joy.
You can build a prsion however you see fit and allow in whichever of the three custody levels you want (or two or all three levels). You find how you build and how you treat the prisions with the regieme you set and the food levels you set, etc. changes how they act. You can cause riots or prevent them by changing how your prision works.
Currently there are bugs that can be annoying. The reform programs are crippled in the Alpha 23 update for example. Do I think they break the game or make it not worth playing? No, not at all. You can get around most of them. And since the save game you are on will still work with the next update there's no reason not to play while you wait on a patch/update. I loaded up an old prison from Alpha 16 just to see if it'd go in Alpha 23 and it plays fine.
There are a few things I want to see improved or fixed. How kitchens work, making it so the prisioners will sleep in the day if their regeme says to sleep instead of only sleeping from 11pm on, the deployment screen needs revamped to where I can say two custody levels can share a space without saying all three levels can go there, and I'd like to see more two square wide doors. My current pet peeve is that it sometimes takes a prisoner 20 mins to decide what they are doing once they arrive at the canteen to eat and they usually pick another activity than eating even if it is the most critical need they have. I'd like to see prisoners actually use the common room instead of walking past it to go halfway across the prison to use an item that's also in the common room. I'd like to see the cells dropdown tell you how many cells you have desginated in each custody level out behind the prisoners number instead of having to remember what you've marked with what.
At the rate the developers have been going I expect they'll improve on all the things that currently annoy me. Even with the annoyances this is my go-to game to play.
Do I think you should pay full price? Nope. Do I think you should stick this on your wishlist and wait for a sale? Totally.

Now that that's over with I'll tell you what to expect. An alpha game that is more fun to play then countless big budget finished games. My friend bought me this game when it was on sale, and I was pretty hyped because I had seen sjin play it. First, you start off with a bit of cash and a few workers to build the prison which will grow very quickly into something unique. You hire some guards, you get the first few prisoners, build the essentials and wait to get some income from keeping those prisoners. More prisoners, more money. Then come the choices. Do you build massive 5x5 cells for each prisoner with TVs and an en-suite? Or do you cram fifty of them like animals into a small holding cell with only a cold metal bench to sleep on? Not only that, I can choose the exact size of the room, and the exact placement of the bench. Total controll. But there is always the worry of money. The afformentioned 5 star rooms cost a lot, but if you do go the second route, you could risk angering your Prisoners. In a riot, they may break all of your stuff and cost you far more then a single room would have. They could kill someone. The fines could finish your prison off. But these perils make it all the more fun to play. Think minecraft. You want to build something awesome, but you may starve to death. But in creative mode it gets a little boring. Survival gives you that balance. Same in  prison architect, it gives meaning to what you build.

I usually avoid movie related games, as they are almost always quickly pieced together and offer nothing more than a brand name on a mediocre game. But Mad Max is something else.
Similar to the film, the majority of this game revolves around driving through the wastelands of a dystopian Australia. In addition to the stunning scenery and expansive stretches of desert coated highway, are a hive of strongholds, enemy towers and sniper nests you can chose to conquer. Though a few bugs persisted after the first few updates, the game as always run smoothly and is well optimises, even at Max settings.
Vehicle combat is excellent, and is similar to that of older Burnout titles, such as Takedown. You can fine tune your car, the Magum Opus, to suit your playstyle, lightly armoured speedster, or fortified tank. Using either grinding and crashes to destroy enemy cars, or your harpoon gun to rip off their tires or leave the driver exposed by removing his door and shotgunning him.
Melee fighting is taken from Warner Brothers other game franchise, the Arkham series, so is polished and well developed. Max himself can be upgraded with combat maneuvers and armour or damage boosts, and Skills such as increased health and weapon durability.
Though the story is not of particular merit, the one thing Mad Max shines at is fun. You often spend hours driving around the giant open-world, littered with side missions, hunting scrap to upgrade your car. During your 30-40 hours of game time, you will notice the small touches the developers added, which shows you that they really cared about the game and wanted to produce something that stands in line with the Mad Max franchise.
If you enjoy vehicle combat or wasteland based games, Mad Max is a great addition to your games library.

If you love hunting, you will love this game. If there's no hunting season in real life, there's always a hunting season in thehunter. This game is the BEST hunting game that I've EVER played. It's worth your money.

TLDR:
The game is playable and enjoyable but riddled with bugs so much so you might mistake this game for an early access rather than an actual game release. The gameplay itself is simple but even then the AI of the animals is lacking in so many ways with pathfinding issues. I'd say that in my 300 "harvests" of animals that around 1/3 of those were from "bugged animals" which were either standing still, running in place or stuck on the terrain. I didnt buy a hunting game only to be shooting fish in a barrel.
Running the game on Max settings GTX 1080 i7-6500 3.4Ghz 16gig RAM rig runs the game perfectly, suffer from random audio crashes that have yet to be fixed despite many people suffering from it.
Single player missions are a joke, often asking you to take a picture of a deer but the quest itself is bugged and no amount of pictures or the distance you are to the deer will make a difference.
With the latest patch the developers essentially ripped away whatever progression system the game has, the idea is that you hunt animals and gain EXP, weapon experience and money. The developers have made it possible to essentially have end game gear within hours of playing by drastically reducing the amouint of experience needed to unlock these weapons (seriously i'd say they reduced the amount needed by about 80%). So now i have the end game weapons and can kill animals easily from an enormous distance so now what? I could go ahead and try and hunt the biggest trophies in the game for the bragging rights on the global leaderboards like in theHunter classic? WRONG. There is a leaderboards amongst your friend list but thats it and even then it isnt even working right now and doesnt update itself often.
The game is nothing like a hunting game, if you think you are going to be sneaking up on groups of animals, picking out the biggest trophy and taking it down then think again! The game as it is punishes players who just hunt for trophies as far as progression is concerned. It's actually more beneficial for to kill every animal you see no matter what size or gender than going for a trophy, the difference in rewards between a trophy and a crappy female deer is tiny, maybe a third less money and EXP, the game doesnt even punish you for killing an animal with the wrong weapon nor does it punish you for failing to track a wounded animal down and finishing it off. so it gets to a point where you just shoot an animal and if you find that its barely wounded your better off just leaving it and finding some other animal to shoot at.
If the developers want this game to last longer than a few months then they really need to make some major changes to this game, which is a shame because it could be a very good game once they fixed all the bugs and actually made it feel like you were hunting rather than playing some arcade shoot em up with deers instead of zombies.
WIll change this review once game becomes more playable but if anyone is reading this right now please save your money for now, watch this game and keep an eye on its updates and maybe even catch it in a steam sale a few months down the line.

Turn on the European (UK, Czech, French, etc.) radio, pick up a load and let's go crusing past the pretty terrain on my way to delivering that cargo for more money!. Delver that load, pick up another and head elsewhere. Maybe I feel like visiting the Danes today and those canals. Maybe I prefer the curvy roads of the Alps. Or maybe I'd like to visit Scotland.
Either way, it's addictive. After a while you get new trucks, hire drivers and expand your empire to become a shipping tycoon. It's not a particularly well done piece of the game but it does give the player a reason to keep hauling those loads. But overall it's just something you play to relax and enjoy. Now if you'd excuse me, I need to go tour the French countryside and get my hazardous materials bonus!

Ok, devs released a 1.3GB patch today as promised. They seem to be willing to fix all those stupid little bugs. Because of that, thumbs up!
Here is my old negative review. Note that not everything was fixed yet but as long as they keep working on it I am recommending the game:
*********WARNING***********************WARNING****************
Even when this game is supposedly to be considered fully released it has actually still more in common with an easy access title!
The game menu, for once, is extremely amateurish and borderline infuriating! It is not possible, for example, to assume that the game would save changes you made to it like turning toggle scope on. It will work for 5 mintues but then for whatever reason will suddenly go back to default toggle scope off !!?? I think it resets options whenever you score a kill and open the trophy screen. Another example for the ridiculous game menu is the apply button of the graphics options tab which is not even 'clickable'! To top things off the game won't even save your graphics options which is really inconvenient when u restart, cause optimization isn't exactly CotW's strong suit.. But zealots will probably find an excuse here as well, huh?
Once you reach the startup screen you'll be welcomed with the game character's hand, holding a mobile in first person only to see that vanish in a matter of seconds so that the camera can fly up into the air in order to show you the awesome landscape which happens all in the background of your startup screen where you can select options, start game etc.. Another easily visible sign that this game was rushed out of the door or for an early access title..
Once you fought your way through the pain-inducing game menu you will reappear in either the american or european hunting reserve only to get immeditely jumped by hordes of apparently sedated animals which barely care at all about your presence! My first experience was literally spawning in, seeing a deer, killing it, turning around, seeing another one, walking, tracking, harvesting, seeing another one and so on.. You barely get a chance NOT to immedaitely see another animal which is just ludicrous considering that you're blasting through the forest with firearms!
That was my experience in the US reserve the european, however, has way less animals in it. Sadly, such animals there are just as stupid as the American ones.. Like me shooting at one and only a few seconds later some jerk of a deer thinks it's a good idea to pop out of the woodwork right next to me in order to get shot, too instead of being frightened by the shot and running away..
Animals sink halfway through the floor. Sounds animals make sound like they're right next to you even when they are actually way farther away than the sound suggests which is an issue in the hunter one and primal, too, by the way. There are no actual wounds animated on killed animals!
According to other reports is there also no animal variety of the same type or in other words, all deer apparently look alike! Antlers apparently do not vary as well, only size but not the looks of it.. Some calls animals make are apparently incorrect, too.
There's a ton more I could list here if I really wanted to but I think at this point you should have a good idea of what you're getting into!

Rust when it first came out was fantastic. Thew new Rust all in all is a great game, but many features in terms of the community shine a very negative and hard to enjoy experience on the game.
Pros +++
- Nice graphics.
- Very well optimized.
- Great building dynamics.
- Great survival aspects (i.e Hunting, Food etc.)
- Great servers.
- Weekly updates that actually add to the game and are also always small in size.
Cons ---
- Scripts.Scripts.Scripts. 95% of gun fights you get in this game will consist of you being no recoil scripted by someone. Almost everyone uses them.
- The sense of raiding is gone. When Rust Legacy came out raiding would mean going to the enemies base and getting in a big gunfight and blowing through their base. Now everyone just raids you offline.
- Admins. Admins really do nothing in this game. If you report a scripter to an admin for using a no recoil script he's most likely using it as well.
Only get this game if the community of a multiplayer survival game does not effect you in any way.

It is made so that your attention in this game is focused on relationships between members of the squad, how they react on the actions of each other and even more important role here plays the mental state of main hero and how it changes during the game while he makes this or that decision. Spec Ops gives you the choice - to be good or bad guy, to save hostages or to kill them and everything depends on you. This game asks you different questions about the cost of human's life and the horrors of war. Are you ready to do anything for saving civils or will you just follow the orders? Finally, i'd like to say that despite it's straightness i love this game.

I would recommend this to any mature gamer. This is much more than just any Modern Military Shooter, Spec Ops: The Line explores the psyche and the mental elements of being a soldier and being responsible for the deaths of thousands of lives.

This game has been an incredibly fun experience thanks to the Dungeon Crawling fun which is comparable to Castlevania games.  Whenever your character dies you're left with the gold he accumulated in order to unlock equipment, rune bonuses, and stat upgrades for your next characters within his or her family line.  Each incarnation after the first is modified by the existence (or lack thereof) of traits such as Gigantism, ADHD, limited vision or other traits which, despite their initial perceptions as disadvantages, may prove highly beneficial depending on how you make use of them for your chosen playstyle, as well as possibilities of functioning better within the randomized layout for your dungeon: Gigantism, while it makes you a larger target, also increases the reach for your attacks, allowing for attacks onto enemies behind walls; ADHD provides a significant speed boost which may stack with other speed boosts present on your character; and limited or altered vision...the various forms of it may enhance the atmohsphere of your dungeon and may even provide other bonuses should you acquire certain items. : )
The customization system for your characters as a result of the randomized Traits which manifests in your characters' heirs allows a player to alternate playstyles with each incarnation of his heroes, with sginificant advantages or disadvantages depending on how each trait performs within the dungeon.
I have spent many hours within the game on edge while traversing the Castle since, despite drastically increasing the capabilities of my characters, it is rare that I truly feel invinicible for the slightest mistake....perhaps not paying attention to a simple trap or projectile, may easily cause my character to play o nthe defensive while on the search for health restoring equips, all the while cursing at the misforutne of running into much more powerful challenges at the most inopportune times.  :P  It really makes it seem as I'm desparately fighting for my characters' lives while making my way to the final encounter.

I found this a good game to play on the bus or in lulls of productivity. The story is incredibly simple, but the ending is surprisingly deep. The highlight might actually be the soundtrack, which I loved.

There should be no doubt that this game has great potential but currently lacks due to some bugs. Unfortunately, it's not something smallish and not so important stuff. Let me give an example.
I have during my first few hours in the game already encountered numerous bugs where the animals are stuck in trees and rocks and keep running like they were on ecstacy, it might be fun to look at but after some time, you just get really annoyed about it. They might be easy to shoot - but they kill the overall feeling about being on a "real hunt".
Another major flaw is the lack of greater depth in the multiplayer session. If you or your partner is the host of the server you play on, then it would be impossible for the other part to get certain spots on the map. Which again, unfortunately, sucks big time because of the distance between areas and places like "save zone/fast travel". They really need some kind of vehicle to reduce the distance to certain areas like this. Otherwise i think a lot of people would get tired of just walking/running from the other end of the map to another. Also I would like to see some more challenges online, not just those few they have right now, but something which could be a lot more interesting to do.
Graphic wise, I think it look's really good. And the sounds are not bad at all. Small adjustments here and there would make this part of the game to be some of the best with The Hunter: Call of the Wild.
Is it worth buying now? It depends on whether you are willing to invest in a product that possibly should have waited 2-3 months longer to correct some crucial bugs as the game crashes from time to time. (Something the dev's are working on right now).
Even though this review seems negative, I just can't get myself to press the "negative" button. I think if some of those things i have written is going to change, then this game can get really good over time!
At least im exicited to see what the future brings, hopefully more animals, new areas, easier level system, and vehicles.

This is my favourite game and one of the best simulators out there. Fantastic graphics and scenery, lots of places to travel and a wide variety of jobs. A good number of different trucks to choose from too. There is also a logistics element as you manage employees, assigning them to different garages, training them up and so on. This game will not only keep your driving skills sharp, but will also improve your European geography knowledge as you become familiar with the different countries and the locations of major cities in them, as well as specific highways leading to them.
Another thing I really like about this game is the extent to which the developers communicate with users via the SCS Software Blog. They work constantly on the game and provide regular updates. The upcoming Scandanavia DLC looks set to add an exciting new dimension to an already excellent game, with many new road types, job types, more detailed cities and so on. Can't wait!
Of course, no game is perfect, and there are a few minor annoyances with ETS 2. While the performance is generally excellent, sometimes I experience "mini-freezes" where all the action just stops for a couple of seconds before continuing. Another thing I find rather irritating is that it seems to take forever to train employees. You can get your own rating up to 10.0 in next to no time, but I have not yet managed to get a single employee to the top level. My other main complaint is that the AI behaves quite stupidly at times, like pulling out in front of you at a T-junction even when you have the right-of-way, or stopping dead in the middle lane of a German autobahn, or turning in front of you at traffic lights when you have a green light and are going straight ahead. I think the AI has been improved since the game was first launched, but there is more room for improvement yet. One last problem is that some rest stops are not displayed on maps, especially parking lot-type stops in Eastern Europe.
When you first start to play the game, there are a few "traps for young players". Be careful when making a tight turn, or your trailer will get stuck and you'll have a dickens of a job getting it free. Also, if you leave it too long before sleeping, you will "doze" and this will result in disastrous loss of control! I have found it is a good idea to check the map when the "yawning" starts to check for the nearest rest stop. In fact, it's a good idea to look even before your driver starts tiring, because sometimes there are very large gaps between stops, especially in Germany.
But all in all, this is a brilliant game that will give you many enjoyable hours of virtual driving, and with the developer support provided, it is about to get even better still!

Everything is so finely tuned that you can even gently lift off the clutch slipping it while you  feel it "bite," making the truck roll with nothing but the engine's torque at idle.
The truck modeling is in par with big names like Gran Turismo, the maps are massive, light effect... everything. For a car nut, or a simulator enthusiast, this game is a MUST.
Graphics: 10/10
Controls (wheel support): 10/10 (judging as a G27 owner)
Gamplay: 9.5/10 (game is extremely relaxed, and although there isn't much variety, the driving itself completes the experience)
Sounds: 9/10 (some trucks sound okay. Others are simply beautiful)
And best of all, MERCEDES IS FINALLY COMING!! (And the Scandinavia map too!!)

Spec Ops gives you the choice - to be good or bad guy, to save hostages or to kill them and everything depends on you. When you first start the game you are just an average weak adventurer, who enters the castle and meets his demise.
Your child (Glorified Respawn) is then sent in after you.
Here is how it works, when you die you get a choice of 3 children to pick from. Each one of them is different and some have perks and others have disabilities such as being color blind, or clumsy. Which is cool because some of the traits are helpful and make for some good fun.
Whenever you die you keep all of your money from your last life, which you can then spend on upgrading your Manor (Base/Skill Tree) which permantely upgrades your characters from then on. However you have to spend all your money before going back into the castle otherwise the gatekeeper takes it all away for that life. (so you cannot just farm the first few rooms.)
This is great because you have to PLAY good still to buy the more expensive upgrades, but every time you play you can usually upgrade one of your stats or abilities that makes it so you can go even farther into the castle. Every time you play you are a bit stronger than before.
The game is super hard at first but as you play you will get new abilities and powers and stats that will make it easier, but of course it can still be hard. The deeper you go into the castle the harder it gets and the more rooms you go through the enemies get stronger.
This game is punishing and rewarding, it feels amazing to go on a good run and succeed and make enough money for some upgrades. There is a lot of collectable items. Such as Runes and Armor and the game is just really really addicting.
You will always think to yourself... "Next time I will upgrade my health, or maybe my strength.. or maybe my defense, or maybe I should buy some new armor."
You die,  you upgrade, you die, you upgrade.
You keep going farther and farther until you can challenge the bosses and beat them.
It's hard to say in words how good this game is, but the controls are spot on, fluid, and fast. You can double, triple and even quadruple jump, then mid-air dash out of the way of enemies.
The game is really really good and there is so many different classes and strategies and so much replayability.
This could be one of my favorite games of all time. 10/10.
