theHunter Call of the Wild.. what a game. It's the perfect hunting game for people who just want to relax, enjoy the scenery and then take down a nicely lined up buck putting their name on the leaderboards to top their friends!
Seriously this game while it has it's flaws is like one of those games you hate but you keep playing because it's fantastic at the same time. You can lose so many hours in this game just from walking around and finding loads of beautiful location in which you can spam the screenshot key and post all over your steam profile. So into the nitty gritty! The review
-[ Gameplay ]-
The gameplay is awesome, the animal tracking, wind, callers, weapons, clothing and scents. There's a decent amount of equipment to keep you entertained for a while!
Now the wind has to be the biggest feature of this game, simply sneaking up to an animal quietly just won't cut it anymore if you're upwind of an animal. Unless you don't have a scent sprayed all over you.. You're going to struggle to kill it. It will smell you before you even see it. Sometimes they throw a warning call, that could be your saving grace to bag it. If not, reposition so you're no longer upwind, get downwind and call them towards you. The sound you make also can scare animals off, If you're walking through a bush it makes more noise than walking through grass as you would expect, so planning your route whilst getting set-up is essential to get the big scores!
Gun play, while you can shoot any animal with any gun you do lose score by doing this, if you're going for a big buck to try and top the leaderboards, don't go running in with a 7mm unless you getting Bison or something. You have the make sure you using the correct rifle and ensure the 100% Trophy Integrity which adds onto your final score. The sounds of the guns firing are really nice, they sound similar with small differences... but. They sound awesome!
Perk/Skill system, compared the theHunter Classic, CoTW (Call of The Wild) has perks and skills, as you play you gain XP, level up and you can then unlock skills and perks, this helps you hold you breath longer, gain more information about the animal you've spotted - such as weight, potential score and this helps down the line to track your animals too. So you can really tailor how you prefer to hunt and then buy the perks which benefit you.
-[ Sound ]-
Overall the sound of this game such as effects, wind. rain, lightening, animal calls. They're really good. Whilst there are some small bugs where you can't locate a call if you're in a menu and then exit. Also sometime calls don't display so you physically cannot locate them. It's pretty uncommon that this happens. The wind sounds are spot on although sometimes really loud when in a blind/tent and the same goes for the rain. I would love to see a weather sound volume slider so we can keep the sound effects high, just lower the weather sounds.
-[ Multiplayer ]-
The best part! Hunting with your friends is awesome. The multiplayer is pretty stable. Never really had a lot of issues with it either apart from the small desync with animals but changing the time in-game simply seems to sort this out. If you are hunting with a friendas much as you'd love to roll around together and hunt together it's not practical unless you switch rolles, so a caller/spotter and then the shooter. If you're both looking to shoot you'll have to sync your shots. Which when you land two kills, is really cool! Hunting on your own in a MP lobby would be the best way to go, you can still see what they kill and the score they recieve so you can still have competition. Which makes the game that little bit more fun!
The downside to Multiplayer though, If you have any tents placed around a reserve, if you're not the host, they will not be there when you join, only the hosts tents/blinds will show. Which can be slighly annoying but it just means getting your friend to set-up in close/similar locations.
-[ Hunting Pressure ]-
Hunting Pressure is a feature that has been added into this game to stop animals constantly vacating hotspots, so this pressure would deter animals to walk/sleep/feed/rest in these areas due to the recent harvests in that area. The way to remove the pressure from your hunting area is simply to hunt somewhere else. The way the hunting pressure works is that it has a limited amout that can "placed" on the map. Let's say for example the limit is 20. You go around a reserve get 5 harvests, move another 10 and then another 5. You would then have hunting pressure scattered around other areas within the reserve, but your original location would be fine to hunt there again. So it forces you to move about and explore the reserves to benefit you as you gain more XP for exlploring and finding new things with these beautil reserves!
-[ Conclusion ]-
I Highly reccomend this game, it's fun, relaxed and a fun casual game which you and a few friends could easily lose a few hours to. I'm a bit annoyed you have to pay a small amount for the DLC (Tents/Blinds & ATV) I feel like these should have been in the base game but other than that. Great game, loads of fun!

"On the road again, but this time I'm actually enjoying it." 9/10
If you've ever wondered what it was like to be a truck driver, out there on that lonely road, left to your own personal devices, then your opportunity has finally arrived! I mean sure, there have been plenty of truck driving simulators for the PC over the past few decades, but let's be honest here and admit that they all sucked and were basically just one big gigantic tease that all of us truck driving simulator enthusiasts had to endure for what seemed like an eternity, to finally get to the only one worth playing; 'Euro Truck Simulator 2'!
If you like the idea of casually driving down the highway, listening to your favorite music or talk radio stations after a long day of work, then this game is for you. There's just something about using turn signals, adjusting mirrors, and following the general rules of the road that screams relaxing to me, and this game does it all perfectly. Load up your own mp3s or stream from your favorite radio stations as you travel around actual European landscapes all from the comfort of your own living room. This game seems like it would be even more enjoyable with a physical steering wheel and pedal. Well worth the price, and I'm really looking forward to the US version.

I updated this review from negative to positive knowing that mods are available to make the driving and/or economy more realistic.
SUMMARY
This games puts you on command of a truck for delivering goods. You are also the administrator of your own truck company. I would not say it is a terrible game, but I would say that it is only a good game if you are a fan of truck driving. The game could be much better with a higher difficulty mode.
TRUCK MODELLING
There is a nice array of different trucks and cargos, and the landscapes are often pretty. Sounds are decent. Some cabins are so well insulated against noise that it's difficult to hear the engine.
TRUCK DRIVING:
Truck behaviour on road is ok, just a bit too forgiving in rough situations.
Driving sensations are just ok, with a force feedback wheel it feels good. Braking is unfortunately difficult to dose due to (for myself) the unavailablility of a more realistic pedal.
Difficulty: much too easy. There are no surprises except a very few obstacles to avoid.
Driving code is badly enforced. It is possible to drive like crazy on the emergency lane of the motorway blaring the honk for hours and crush the brakes before the cameras just in time.
I think there is no damage to cargo when taking turns too fast or emergency braking, but I'm not so sure. anyway the damage taken is really much too forgiving.
Consequences of a grave accident (I mean turning the entire truck over, which is very difficult to achieve unless you drive like a madman) are only a money penalty: you pay for help, you're late, you have less money, and that's all. This is not enough for a simulator.
Simple collisions with cars are rewarded only with a slight money penalty, it does not even delay your trip.
Truck manoeuvering at the client's companies is interesting for a short while until you have understood how to handle it.
Truck maintenance is very easy and it is sufficient to "repair all" once a while without worrying about anything. I can say that the maintenance of my own car is far more complicated than that....
COMPANY MANAGEMENT
It is limited to buying and enlarging garages, assigning trucks and drivers to your garages and harvest money. The choices you make on the competences of drivers are extremely simple and the trucks you assign to them have no visible impact on the game. The company management part of this game is just incomplete and not sufficient to enjoy it.
CONCLUSION
The game is enjoyable for a few hours and rapidly becomes repetitive, after you have run all the major landscapes of the european roads. It is just too easy. However, I must admit that I still play it after 6 months and bought a DLC. Therefore it is not so bad if you don't mind the lack of challenge. You can also make a nice collection of screenshots with the different landscapes, trucks and cargos, and it has value as a collector tool.

If you enjoy simulators this game is pure FUN! It has a great feeling of European trucking, lots of options to customize your experience depending on what controls do you like, straightforward mechanics and great features to make the game enjoyable whether you're skilled or not (for ex. automatic parking which is a BLESSING here, it's more difficult to control the truck than it was in Haulin or Long Haul or other previous games). The game looks great, gives you easy access to online radios and the world is just perfect. I really like truck customization too!
The only problems that I have in the game are overpriced DLC's (map packs are ok but those paint jobs are ridiculous) and game crashing on Steam (tested on Windows 7 and Windows 8). Save a lot so you don't lose your progress.
Edit 6/28/2017 - I recommend a steering wheel. The game became a true EXPERIENCE. I stopped playing when I got a real car :)

This game is overwhelmingly fun, the single player and missions over all are fun and enjoyable.  There is times where it is a little tough, but the road to finishing some missions can be very interesting.
This game is a really big (better) upgrade from the previous free game.  The best part is that you unlock weapons and buy them with in-game currency, that's a win in my own opinion.  You can now progress and hunt more things without having to pay more money to do so.
I recommend this game and I also recommend bringing a friend along with you, the multiplayer is a great way to have fun with friends and compete to see who can kill the biggest animal.
Lastly, you can expect bugs as it's a new game, but the devs are updating it and making it better, you can wait to buy the game if you want to play a game with ease, but if you don't mind a few bugs and glitches that can give you a laugh at times, I'd recommend picking up this game soon.
Pros
[+] Graphics are amazing
[+] Enjoyable game with a lot of missions
[+] Multiplayer is fun and not laggy [depending on the host ;)]
[+] Loads of places to explore currently
[+] Devs are working hard to make the game better.
[+] A lot of animals to find a kill (they sometimes roam in large groups)
[+] Animals can hurt you (you actually have to fear that now, isn't that cool?!)
[+] Realistic hunting simulator
[+] Skill points and other sorts to make your character a better hunter. (Example; Skill points put towards certain things makes tracking easier)
[+] A lot of other things that you should check out!
Cons
[-] When you play multiplayer you can't interact with monuments, outposts, and outlooks.
[-] Some fps bugs, but you can restart the game and you'll be fine.
[-] Some interface bugs, but easily bypassable.
I can't think of much more cons as this game is really great, I recommend picking it up and bringing a friend along with you! ;)

This isn't an easy review. As the game still has several bugs and a terrible UI. But the UI is manageable if you are somewhat presistent. It takes a bit of fiddling in order to figure it out. My main annoyance was the fact that I couldn't figure out how to replenish my ammo. Highly annoying in a game where bullets play a key role. Yet in the end I managed.
The rest of the game is great. While the scenery is great and the animals behaviour feels realistic, I like the fact that you're not being help by the hand. All hints and tips can be disabled and the game leaves you alone to hunt. That is exactly what I needed on a grey saturday afternoon. Just let me walk and stalk a whitetail deer for 15 minutes, and focus on taking a kill shot. In the same line, the game gives feedback on your shot and hunting skills but again without smashing it in your face. After collecting the kill, you get a type of score board with all the information. Perfectly ignorable, not advisable if you want to become good and are sick of following a blood trail.
All in all, I've decided that I like this game. The required focus and yet the casual manner that you're allowed to play in make this a game for casual players and people that really want to master it. I would recommend this game as one of the better hunting games currently out there. But we'll have to be honest and agree that the competition isn't that steep. Adjust your expectations to average and you'll have an enjoyable experience.

This is an odd game to review because, like Crusader Kings II, it's fun - but a very specific kind of fun that might not be for everyone. This is obviously a driving sim with a healthy mix of logistics and entrepreneurship and it's hard to sell that to people who aren't already interested in it, which is why the trailer to this game looks lost and confused. People like videos that highlight the action and, honestly, this isn't a game that has a lot of it. This game doesn't have explosions, it's relaxing, if anything. You transport objects and make money doing it. For some people, this is boring, but for the target audience, that's a cool concept in and of itself. It's probably the meat of what people describe as being the intangible backbone of what makes this game good.
What makes life in this game tolerable?
Well, the first thing that comes to mind is that an enormous amount of time was spent trying to get the roads and scenery to look convincing. If you're on the M5 and pause the game, go to Google and drop the streetview cam on the approximate spot where your truck is, it's going to be pretty darn similar to what you'll see. Road signs will toned down and simplified, but the traffic cams will not. People without cars will soon learn what a pain in the butt they are for commuters. Road patterns like interstate on/off ramps will be recycled, but that's pretty much what happens in real life as well.
When driving down an interstate, it's obviously not in anyone's interest to make a two hour trip to Bristol actually take two real world hours, so time and distance are abridged. So are cities and the insane traffic patterns and congestion associated with it. This means that, sometimes, it's O.K. to go to London.
The game can be as accurate as you like when it comes to operating your truck, from incomprehensible (how gears work in real life) to arcade (magic transmission - W means go).
Radio stations are real. If you choose, you can have your truck radio stream the actual radio stations of whatever country you want and whatever languages they are broadcast in. This is a pretty fun feature and adds to the immersion in the game.
The biggest downside? Traffic. It's inconsistent and has a few bugs. The most pressing one is that NPC drivers have no concept of their own safety. Honestly, I'm not sure what their pathing is, but they seem to cruse right into you as if you were not there, even with proper signaling. That said, they're better than I expected for AI behavior for the most part. If you signal that you want to turn across an oncoming lane, the cars will ocasionally stop and flash their lights to indicate that they're willing to stop for you to get across.
An unrelated disappointment is that weather is not dynamic to your location, it's a global setting. So, the chance of rain in Glasgow is the same as Paris.
The final remarkable disappointment I can think of is that, like I mentioned earlier, roads and cities are abridged. And while I definitely don't mind avoiding cities for their suicidal traffic AI, they're very unconvincing for the most part. Unless it's is a larger city that they are particularly proud of, like Klagenfurt and Venice, the majority of "cities" are maybe ten blocks? Residential areas and all? It makes the final destination a repetitive anticlimactic end to a long drive.
The game is still being worked on, obviously. Scandinavia will be released at some point and there's already a host of mods for amateur-created areas. At some point, it's possible that the drawbacks I've mentioned will be taken care of. Even if they aren't, there are far worse and game breaking problems that it could have, but doesn't. The devs have put a tremendous amount of time into this unfathomably large and complicated project and it's solid because of that. As far as a truck driving sim goes, this is probably as good as it gets for the foreseeable future.

I recommend this game to anyone that just wants to have a good time.

Euro Truck Simulator 2... Great, another simulator game. This was probably made in a few weeks and is probably terrible.
Well, surprisingly this isn't the case. Euro Truck Simulator 2 is actually quite fun, what makes it fun is that there's a levelling system, so each time you complete a truck run which normally lasts on average 25-40 minutes, (depending what job you take) you gain XP and money for your own truck company. Aside from levelling up, you can accumulate money to purchase new trucks, and upgrades for them. Making your own business / trucking company more reliable and efficient.
That's pretty much all there is to it for the most part. The downsides to this game is that it can be dreadfully boring as there is no music playing whilst you're driving. You can put in .mp3 files into a folder in your documents (much like the GTA games did) and you can play your music whilst driving.
You can also use custom radio station links (e.g real ones) as well which is cool.
Putting your own music into your documents folder is pointless though as there is no special EQ or anything to make it sound as if its coming out of the speakers in your truck etc.
This game also allows a steering wheel, and foot pedals of course as it's a simulator.
ETS 2 is quite fun despite its simple concept of getting from point A to point B. I recommend getting this in a sale for £10, or less.

An updated retelling of Joseph Conrad's Heart of Darkness shackled to an average cover based shooter.
Rating 6/10
If it wasn't for the story propelling the action I doubt the game would have been noticed amongst numerous other 3rd person cover based shooters.
It doesn't do anything particularly well, enemies attack in waves whilst you hide behind waist high cover. This format doesn't change through the game but the enemies get smarter using grenades to try and flush you out and at times they destroy your cover. You have two other members in your squad, a sniper and heavy MG and they should be a help but the AI lets them down and they often become a hindrance especially on tougher difficult levels.
There is a lot of good to be found in the game and it's not all bad, firstly the ruined setting of Dubai is well realised in places, the sand taking over many of the buildings and it's a beautifully eerie place as you make your way through the ruins of what was once a populated city.
As the game progresses it also offers up a few moral choices, tough choices in a tough environment. Sadly though these choices have no effect on the ending, so no matter which path you choose you'll end up in the same place. It continues to ask moral questions throughout about the justification of your actions. If you've read Heart of Darkness or seen Apocalypse Now you'll know what to expect, I won't ruin the story but it has a few nice twists and turns as you discover what's really been happening in Dubai.
So I recommend you buy the game for the story but don't expect much from the actual gameplay.

If you've seen the movie, the game feels different than the movie.  The game goes more along what I would call classic max, instead of fury road max, and to me this is good.  The gameplay mixes combat and gathering. If Bethesda's Rage could have been closer to this formula, it would have had a greater success.  I enjoy playing it, and look forward to turning the pages of the story.
After playing 71 hours in game, I can say I want to finish 100%.  Few games draw this from me, as I typically finish the story then move to another game instead of finishing the "collect them all" process.
To comment about gameplay, I found the camera a bit challenging to work with, and it has a similar issue with the auto adjust when driving that driving does in Sleeping Dogs, where it takes too long to focus on what the car points at.  I stongly prefer games where when you enter a car, the camera moves to the movement view immediately, instead of waiting for you to drive some first before doing this auto adjustment.
The fightning feels similar to batman, except more like Splash Damage / Warner Bros Montreal than what Rocksteady produces.  The fightning feels a bit sluggish with responsiveness when parrying, feeling more like small "quick time" fightning than brawling like with rocksteady's.  Still enjoyable and fun, but if you compare the two, you'll see what I mean.  Upgrading the vehicle, upgrading the strongholds, and max all have a great feel and progression.  The environments feel great, along with the environmental sounds.  The vehicle weapons made me feel powerful, while max became more durable on foot.
I felt a little let down with the engine sounds, but few driving games seem to have, for me, a real feel about engines.  I guess they're not quite mastered the air and ambiance of engine sounds in most games, but that seems more a sound engineer issue to resolve.
Overall, while I've experienced a few detracting cases for Mad Max, the game provided an immersive experience well worth the time I've invested.

Imagine you're playing a board game. You're given infinite lives. However, every time you die you have to reroll all of your character traits.
That is essentially the gimmick behind Rogue Legacy. The only difference is that instead of infintie lives, you have infinite heirs. Each heir is given any of a whole slew of different modifiers that can be useful, harmful, or simply funny. Each heir gets to retain anything their predecessors unlocked and make another go at the pseudo-randomized castle (certain regions of the castle are always in the same general location, but the rooms and layout are randomized).
It is admittedly an exercise in grinding as most runs through the castle early on you can expect to die. And die. And die. But you do get this certain feeling of progress and learning how to cope with the variety of traits you can get. But there's nothing quite like that feeling of seeing a boss for the nth time and finally kicking its♥♥♥♥♥
The story is fairly basic but is entirely fitting for the game. It is, however, somewhat predictable if you can catch on to certain things as you make your way through the game. If you enjoy the gameplay a lot, the replay value is high as each iteration of the game gets progressively more difficult. Plus a patch some time back added special versions of the bosses for added challenge beyond the original game as well.
Overall, I found it a very enjoyable game.

Rust is a classic 'two wrongs don't make a right' lesson. Somebody should make a horror movie about this game. There's theft, extortion, and...rampant hacking with griefing. Rust has all the right components on which to build an amazing story.
I tried, I really tried--like the kind of try one would make to endure a bad relationship. I played Rust religiously and regularly for months. I even upgraded my computer hardware to play Rust. The gaming dynamics are great. That holds true until you face one of the many hackers, then the whole game just goes straight to hell in a handbasket.
We built an epic labyrinth of walls, very many doors, and hidden stairways to confuse would-be raiders in a 10x resource server. We came back the next day to find it raided by an apparent hacker. How do I know? A surgically precise optimal path through our doors was chosen by the raiders to reach our otherwise hidden loot room. Please heed the gravity of my statement when I say we built a veritable labyrinth. We had 48+ doors on the lowest level alone in a regular shape comparable to the facets of an emerald cut diamond. The raiders (read: hackers) wasted no C4 in blasting their direct path to our loot room through over 3 large floors of this labyrinth. In case you're wondering, no, the loot room was not centered and obvious.
After dealing with hackers EVERY, SINGLE, TIME I started Rust. You name it, there were ridiculous pot shots from aimbotters and ESP griefers stalking and taking any reasonable loot. I decided enough is enough, these ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s aren't going anywhere anytime soon. I might as well level my playing field with them. So I bought a hack. Did I ever notice any of the obvious hackers getting game banned? No. Did I get game banned? Absolutely, they caught onto me within hours. 10/10, would do it again, if I wished to continue playing the game.
Now, let's get to this juicy early access matter. Rust has been in early access since December 2013. It might come out of early access--when Facepunch decides to stop developing it. Garry blasted Reddit, saying players got their $20's worth from Rust already.
TL;DR: Play something else until Facepunch decides to move on. I love their games, despise their callow antics.

I bought this game expecting it to be just filler before Fallout 4. It ended up being tons of fun, and actually took me a little by surprise.
Graphics:
For a desolate wasteland, the graphics are superb. The sun rises/sun sets look great. The vast and endless horizon really makes you feel like you are apart of a huge open desert world to explore. The explosions and fire effects are absolutely top notch, and make for some great screenshots with the photo capture mode that is built into the game.
Sound/Music:
The sounds in this game fit perfectly. From little things like footsteps in heavy sand, the crunching sound of melee combat, to the engine rumblings of the Magnum Opus (which change depending on your engine). The music is a little sparse, but it picks up during melee combat as well as vehicular chases/fights. I will however say that during a lot of the repetitive tasks, I threw on some of my own music :P More on that below.
Story:
The story is basically there to string the gameplay and different wasteland environments together. Only during one part at the end did it really wow me in any sort of way. This isn't necessarily a bad thing, but don't go in expecting anything more than a very loose plot with just enough dialogue/cutscenes to push you to the next task/zone/etc.
Gameplay:
This is where the game shines the most, but also stagnates the most. The gameplay is tons of just plain stupid fun, but if you let yourself become a completionist it can get very stale very fast.
Now, this varies from person to person. A lot of people like the "checking things off a checklist" type gameplay, and get major satisfaction from clearing out everything to do on a map they are given. This is important to remember, because all of your car upgrades are tied to at least 1 of 3 different things:
- Scrap (which you will always be collecting throughout the entire game, from start to finish) - You get scrap from pretty much everything. Destroying enemy cars, killing people in hand to hand combat, exploring the wasteland and finding it in marked and unmarked areas on the map, enemy camps, turning in certain vehicles to strongholds, etc.
- "Threat Levels" of each zone (There are 4 main strongholds throughout the game that control their own 'sections' of the wasteland. You need to lower threat in these map sections to unlock different upgrades).
- Main Story missions/Side missions for Stronghold leaders (several of the upgrades are locked behind main/side story mission completion).
Magnum Opus:
The gritty truth of it is this: If you want your Magnum Opus to look like the friggin' awesome death machine in the game promo material/screenshots/trailers, then you're going to be doing A LOT of repetitive tasks. I want to stress again though that in my opinion it never truly became boring. There were a few times while clearing minefields that it started to feel like a grind, but never enough to turn the game off or anything like that.
The Magnum Opus is indeed the most customizable thing in the game. You can make yours unique in terms of not only looks, but what you prefer as priority (speed or armor/ramming power). I won't list the huge amounts of customization or upgrades here as there are many, but I will say that at the end of the game I felt very satisfied with the functionality and looks of the car. It definitely 'grows' with you as you play, and at the end its usefulness really makes you feel like it all paid off and was worth it.
Max Upgrades:
Aside from upgrading the Magnum Opus, there is also vehicles to collect, and you can also upgrade Max himself. The cool thing about upgrading Max is that almost every single thing for him is locked behind a "legend" rank that you need to achieve through completing 'challenges'. However, you achieve these legend rank challenges naturally by just playing through the game. Some of them are things like "Perform 10 perfect parries on enemies" and "Use your shotgun to destroy 15 fuel tanks on cars". Never once did I find myself checking the list of challenges to unlock the next armor/shotgun/handguards/knuckledusters/beard (yes beard) for Max, that's just how naturally they come.
Strongholds:
The 4 different Strongholds themselves in the game can also be upgraded by doing the same tasks in each section of the map. Once upgraded, they appear visually better (more people, better interiors, etc.). But more importantly, they also provide useful benefits for Max such as a full ammo belt/fuel tank/health bar/water canteen upon entering. Also, there are projects to build that will do other things such as collect scrap automatically when you blow up cars (so you don't have to get out each time) and collect scrap when the game is turned off (online connection required). Its questionable whether more than 1 Stronghold truly needs fully upgraded due to the ability to fast travel between them at any time. The only things I would say are a necessity build in each Stronghold are the "clean up crew" projects, which are the ones that collect scrap automatically for cars you destroy.
"Final Verdict", or whatever.
I got the game for about 15 bucks. For that price, it was absolutely-100percent-withoutadoubt worth it. At around 45 hours played, with the main story complete, and a good chunk of everything side activity related done, I can safely say it is a good game that is more than just filler, and took me by surprise with how fun it ended up being. However, I would not say its worth the full $60 price tag. With its simple stupid fun yet repetitive gameplay, its very customizable and visually appealing yet checklist type upgrade system, and its loose story, to me this is a game you play with music/Netflix on in the background. Of course its up to you how much you think that type of game is worth.

I will be vague to avoid spoiling anything. As of writing only episode one is out and it took me roughly 4 hours to finish Episode 1. (I am pretty slow at games so asume 3 hours on average) So far this is just as good as the previous Life is Strange. You care about the characters. They feel like they have depth and, well, character. It sucks you in and gets you interested in what's going on and makes you feel. No there are no time travel mechanics in this one, instead you have a Backtalk mode wherein during a conversation you can trigger backtalk. In Backtalk you are given a few seconds to respond to a previous statement with one of 3 responses. Do this correctly enough times and you will “win” the backtalk. Pick the wrong option to many times and you will “loose” the backtalk.
There are no doover in this game which builds some tension and sense of permanent action that the first game lacked in a lot of places. As far as writing and characters go it is, so far, as good if not better than the first. $17 is, in my opinion, more than fair for this. The small, and major, changes depending on your actions add some replayability to the game but even if you only plan to play this one time through and live with your choices (or look up things you didn't do on youtube) this still gets a glowing recommendation!
I recommend setting aside 4-5 hours to be safe, sitting in a dark room with headphones, and playing each episode in one sitting. Regardless of if you're playing them as they come out (which should be every 2 months or so) or if you are waiting to play them all when they are all out.

Quick Review:  Is it as good as the first one?  No, but it is damn close.  I recommend purchasing.
Longer Review:
The mechanics are all there.  The storyline is really good.  It was nice to see some familiar faces.  There are some really fun side "games" in there (I won't ruin it for you).
We have interesting scenarios to work through.  Some interesting characters.  I found that this game's "secondary" characters are given a lot less emphasis - almost like the developers didn't want to stretch too thin and concentrated on the main couple of characters exclusively.  This could obviously change in the next two episodes, but so far - it's all about Chloe (and 'friend').
I love the fact that the developers are willing to "work outside" some of our social established paradigms.  I'll leave it at that.  I hope that this continues in the next episodes.
If you're worried that the charm of the game is lost because there are new developers; don't.  They a respectful and true to the original game.
If you're worried that the game won't be as fun without the time control mechanic - I can't lie.  I miss it alot.  I have been using the RESTART FROM LAST CHECKPOINT option to sort of deal with the concept of making alternative decisions.
If the developers are reading; please allow us to skip through replays - even if we restart from checkpoint.  The checkpoints seem further between - we need it to get our "rewind" on.
I'm enjoying it tremendously.  Can't wait to keep playing.

has the potential to be the best hunting game out there. It's a great foundation for the perfect hunting game. Unfortunately, that's all the game is at its current state. It's pretty much just a pretty landscape with everything else feeling rushed. When it actually works and you don't encounter one of the many bugs it's a really enjoyable and relaxing experience, but way too often do you find your immersion getting completely ruined by a visual bug or weird AI.
Not only that,
Here are two of the major things I think the game is lacking at the moment, to at least make it a complete hunting game and putting the glitches aside:
1. Birds. You can hear them all around you. There are some oddly placed seagulls (or whatever they are) here and there that flies away by the noise you make. But
. I was really expecting this to be in the game at release, but knowing where the developers are coming from (the microtransaction hell that is theHunter: Classic) I'm guessing it will be a future DLC. Hard to say if the developers ran out of time or if this is an intentional decision. The shotguns are there to tease you though.
2. Any means of transportation. The map is HUGE.
And at the pace the character is running it feels even bigger. Sure, you can fast travel between the outposts but first you'll have to find them, usually by going to a lookout point to reveal them on the map and then walk to them to claim them and just hope that you don't accidentally stumble between two static rocks that somehow magically squishes you to death on your way there. Yes, that happened not only once, but three times. I remember playing Deer Hunter 3 back in the days and thought it was cool that you could get around with ATV's, snowmobiles and such. Guess this might be DLC too, concidering there are achievements for traveling "BY FOOT". Feels weird to state that unless they have some other way of travelling planned.
Now those are just the features I feel that the game is currently lacking. As an addition to that it's
and some of the most
I've seen in a game. Which is a good way to completely ruin your immersion that you otherwise get from the stunning visuals. Squirrels gets stuck humping rocks, rabbits run in circles at the speed of light, deer gets stuck against trees and rocks and I've even seen a group of four different animal types running into eachother in a mess that looked like the queue line to the Noah's ark. I try my best to just ignore these derpy animals and move on but you see them way too often to just simply ignore them. I know it must be hard to code AI and especially animal like behaviour but I still don't expect to see these kind of situations in a full release of a hunting game. I've seen a whole pack of wild boars just running into an invisible wall forever.
There doesn't seem to be any fall damage in the game, yet somehow you sometimes die if you get stuck between two rocks or try to climb them as I mentioned earlier. I even just flat out died walking on a flat surface at one point. The screen has gone completely blurry as if the field of depth was bugged and also completely red after I died once. These were fixed by just clicking ESC twice to bring up the menu interface (which can be a little bit disorienting at times when it comes to equipment and such) and then close it again. The smartphone is visible in some of the cutscenes, just floating there (sometimes upside down). I've found a hunting stand that was not buildable for whatever reason (surely the developers must have had time to test this once they put it down on the map?) and seen some weirdly placed street signs and poles. There was also this one pile of stones which gives you lore that had the trigger 8 meters underground so it was impossible to activate. I've seen some floating 3D sprites and trees that goes through rocks and some terrain deformities (with stretched textures), but usually you have to look really close for these types of minor glitches. The one visual glitch that occurs the most is the one with parts of the scope disappearing after you take a shot.
With all this being said, I really hope the developers listens to the community and addresses these issues. I'm really looking forward to future patches and updates, it can only get better from here and hopefully we'll have our hands on the best hunting experience one can have on a PC. I tried to summarize my experience with the game so far in this review, for the developers and others thinking about buying it, just to let you know what you can expect from it at its current state. I have no complaints about the sounds nor the visuals, but as for now I'll give this game a rating of "Not recommended" until it gets some fixes.

Not sure why but I can honestly say I love this game. After only 7 hours of gameplay I look forward to the next job and spend the day at work waiting to get home to play this. Literally everything about this game, from sound effects, combat, visuals, car driving fighting has been exquisitely done.
Although you will be doing things repetitively, the way that these things are done and the design that has gone into these activities makes it a joy to do it for a long while.
The only negative aspect is that there is no New game mode where you can do it all over again with all of your acquired abilities/ weapons.    But on the other hand, even the beginning when you are just starting out has its charm.  This is not one of those games that start out boring and dull and only get good later on.  From the get go you will be feeling every skull cracking blow, every piece of metal grinding on metal, every blast from the shotgun.
All developers should take a queue from this game if they want to keep selling games at a $50 price point.   Although due to most games being dumbed down to the point that I refuse to paying full price, I have to admit that I think that this game is one of the (very) few that is deserving of being sold as an actual AAA game.
